ثُمَّ اسْتَأْنَفَ الحَدِيثَ عَنْ بَقِيَّةِ حالِهِمْ فَقالَ: ﴿يَكادُ البَرْقُ﴾ أيْ مِن (p-124) قُوَّةِ لَمْعِهِ وشُعاعِهِ وشِدَّةِ حَرَكَتِهِ وإسْراعِهِ ﴿يَخْطَفُ أبْصارَهُمْ﴾ فَهم يَغُضُّونَها عِنْدَ لَمْعِهِ وخَفْضِهِ في تَرائِبِهِ ورَفْعِهِ. ولَمّا كانَ مِنَ المَعْلُومِ أنَّ البَرْقَ يَنْقَضِي لَمَعانُهُ بِسُرْعَةٍ، كانَ كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: ماذا يَصْنَعُونَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ؟ فَقالَ: ﴿كُلَّما﴾، وعَبَّرَ بِها دُونَ "إذا" دَلالَةً عَلى شِدَّةِ حِرْصِهِمْ عَلى إيجادِ المَشْيِ عِنْدَ الإضاءَةِ ﴿أضاءَ لَهم مَشَوْا فِيهِ﴾ مُبادِرِينَ إلى ذَلِكَ حِراصًا عَلَيْهِ، لا يَفْتَرُونَ عَنْهُ في وقْتٍ مِن أوْقاتِ الإضاءَةِ، مَعَ أنَّهم يَغُضُّونَ أبْصارَهم ولا يَمُدُّونَها غايَةَ المَدِّ خَوْفًا عَلَيْهِمْ، ووُقُوفًا مَعَ الأسْبابِ، ووُثُوقًا بِها واعْتِمادًا عَلَيْها، وغَفْلَةً عَنْ رَبِّ الأرْبابِ. وهو مَثَلٌ لِما وجَدُوا مِنَ القُرْآنِ مُوافِقًا لِآرائِهِمْ، وعَطَفَ بِـ"إذا" لِتَحَقُّقِ خُفُوتِهِ بَعْدَ خُفُوقِهِ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وإذا أظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قامُوا﴾ أيْ أوَّلَ حِينِ الإظْلامِ، لا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى التَّقَدُّمِ خُطْوَةً واحِدَةً، إشارَةً إلى أنَّهُ لَيْسَتْ لَهم بَصائِرُ يَسِيرُونَ بِها فِيما كَشَفَ البَرْقُ لِأبْصارِهِمْ مِنَ الأرْضِ قَبْلَ الإظْلامِ (p-125)، بَلْ حالَ انْقِطاعِ اللَّمَعانِ يَقِفُونَ لِعَمى بَصائِرِهِمْ ووَحْشَتِهِمْ وجُبْنِهِمْ وغُرْبَتِهِمْ وشَدَّةِ جَزَعِهِمْ وحَيْرَتِهِمْ. وهَكَذا حالُ هَؤُلاءِ، لا يَقِيسُونَ ما أشْكَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ القُرْآنِ عَلى ما فَهِمُوهُ.

﴿ولَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ الَّذِي لَهُ العَظَمَةُ الباهِرَةُ مَعَ شِدَّةِ حِرْصِهِمْ وتَناهِي جَزَعِهِمْ، ودَلَّ عَلى مَفْعُولِ "شاءَ" بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ﴾ أيْ بِقاصِفِ الرَّعْدِ، ولَمْ يُغْنِهِمْ سَدُّ آذانِهِمْ ﴿وأبْصارِهِمْ﴾ بِخاطِفِ البَرْقِ، ولَمْ يَمْنَعْهُ غَضُّهم لَها. ثُمَّ عَلَّلَ ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أيِ الَّذِي لَهُ جَمِيعُ صِفاتِ الكَمالِ ﴿عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ أيْ مَشِيءٍ، أيْ يَصِحُّ أنْ تَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ المَشِيئَةُ، هَذا المُرادُ، وإنْ كانَ الشَّيْءُ كَما قالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ يَقَعُ عَلى كُلِّ ما أُخْبِرَ عَنْهُ، وهو أعَمُّ العامِّ كَما أنَّ اللَّهَ أخَصُّ الخاصِّ، يَجْرِي عَلى الجِسْمِ والعَرَضِ والقَدِيمِ والمَعْدُومِ والمُحالِ. (p-126) وقَوْلُ الأشاعِرَةِ (أتباع أبي الحسن الأشعري): إنَّ المَعْدُومَ لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ، بِمَعْنى أنَّهُ لَيْسَ بِثابِتٍ في الأعْيانِ مُتَمَيِّزٌ فِيها. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ إعْلامًا بِأنَّ قُدْرَتَهُ لا تَتَقَيَّدُ بِالأسْبابِ. قالَ الحَرالِّيُّ: القُدْرَةُ إظْهارُ الشَّيْءِ مِن غَيْرِ سَبَبٍ ظاهِرٍ. انْتَهى.

ولَعَلَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ قَدَّمَ المَثَلَ الأوَّلَ لِأنَّهُ كالجُزْءِ مِنَ الثّانِي، أوْ لِأنَّهُ مَثَلُ المُنافِقِينَ: جُعِلَتْ مُدَّةُ صِباهم بِنُمُوِّهِمْ وازْدِيادِ عُقُولِهِمُ اسْتِيقادًا، مَعَ جَعْلِ اللَّهِ إيّاهم عَلى الفِطْرَةِ القَوِيمَةِ، وزَمانِ بُلُوغِهِمْ بِتَمامِ العَقْلِ الغَرِيزِيِّ إضاءَةً؛ والثّانِي مَثَلُ المُنافِقِينَ، وهو أبْلَغُ، لِأنَّ الضَّلالَ فِيهِ أشْنَعُ وأفْظَعُ. فالصَّيِّبُ: القُرْآنُ الَّذِي انْقادُوا لَهُ ظاهِرًا، والظُّلُماتُ مُتَشابِهَةٌ، والصَّواعِقُ (p-127) وعِيدُهُ، والبَرْقُ وعْدُهُ. كُلَّما أُنْذِرُوا بِوَعِيدٍ انْقَطَعَتْ قُلُوبُهم خَوْفًا ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [المنافقون: 4]، وكُلَّما بُشِّرُوا انْقادُوا رَجاءً، وإذا عَرَضَ المُتَشابِهُ وقَفُوا تَحَيُّرًا وجَفاءً. وكُلُّ ذَلِكَ وُقُوفًا مَعَ الدُّنْيا وانْقِطاعًا إلَيْها، لا نُفُوذَ لَهم إلى ما وراءَها أصْلًا، بَلْ هم كالأنْعامِ، لا نَظَرَ لَهم إلى ما سِوى الجُزْئِيّاتِ والأُمُورِ المُشاهَداتِ.

﴿فَإنْ كانَ لَكم فَتْحٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ قالُوا ألَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ﴾ [النساء: 141]، ﴿يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهم فَأفُوزَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [النساء: 73]. والكَلامُ الجامِعُ النّافِعُ في ذَلِكَ أنْ يُقالَ: إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ شَبَّهَ في الأوَّلِ مَثَلَهم بِمَثَلِ المُسْتَوْقِدِ لا بِالمُسْتَوْقِدِ، وفي الثّانِي شَبَّهَ مَثَلَهم في خَوْفِهِمُ اللّازِمِ ورَجائِهِمُ المُنْقَطِعِ بِأصْحابِ (p-128) الصَّيِّبِ لا بِمَثَلِهِم. فَتَقْدِيرُ الأوَّلِ: مَثَلُهم في أنَّهم سَمِعُوا أوَّلًا الدُّعاءَ ورَأوُا الآياتِ فَأجابُوا الدّاعِيَ، إمّا بِالفِعْلِ كالمُنافِقِينَ، وإمّا بِالقُوَّةِ في أيّامِ الصِّبا لِما عِنْدَهم مِن سَلامَةِ الفِطَرِ وصِحَّةِ النَّظَرِ، ثُمَّ تَلَذَّذُوا فَرَجَعُوا بِقُلُوبِهِمْ مِن نُورِ ما قالُوهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ مِن كَلِمَةِ التَّقْوى، نُطْقًا أوْ تَقْدِيرًا، إلى ظُلُماتِ الكُفْرِ، فَلَمْ يَنْفَعْهم سَمْعٌ ولا بَصَرٌ ولا عَقْلٌ، فَصارُوا مِثْلَ البَهائِمِ الَّتِي لا تُطِيعُ الرّاعِيَ إلّا بِالزَّجْرِ البَلِيغِ. مَثَلُهم في هَذا يُشْبِهُ مَثَلَ المُسْتَوْقِدِ في أنَّهُ لَمّا أضاءَتْ نارُهُ رَأى ما حَوْلَهُ، فَلَمّا ذَهَبَتْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلى تَقَدُّمٍ ولا تَأخُّرٍ، لِأنَّهُ لا يَنْفَعُ في ذَلِكَ سَمْعٌ ولا كَلامٌ، فَإذًا اسْتَوى وُجُودُهُما وعَدَمُهُما (p-129)، فَصارَ عادِمًا لِلثَّلاثَةِ، فَكانَ مِن هَذِهِ الجِهَةِ مُساوِيًا لِلْأصَمِّ الأبْكَمِ الأعْمى، فَهو مِثْلُهُ لِكَوْنِهِ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى مُرادِهِ إلّا إنْ قادَهُ قائِدٌ حِسِّيٌّ، فَهو حِينَئِذٍ مِثْلُ البَهائِمِ الَّتِي لا تُقادُ لِلْمُرادِ إلّا بِقائِدٍ. فاسْتَوى المَثَلانِ، وسَيَتَّضِحُ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ﴾ [البقرة: 171]. ولِذَلِكَ كانَتِ النَّتِيجَةُ في كُلٍّ مِنها: "صُمٌّ..." إلى آخِرِهِ. و"أوْ" بِمَعْنى الواوِ، ولَعَلَّهُ عَبَّرَ بِها دُونَها، لِأنَّهُ وإنْ كانَ كُلٌّ مِنَ المَثَلَيْنِ صالِحًا لِكُلٍّ مِنَ القِسْمَيْنِ، فَإنَّ احْتِمالَ التَّفْصِيلِ غَيْرُ بَعِيدٍ، لِأنَّ الأوَّلَ أظْهَرُ في الأوَّلِ، والثّانِيَ في الثّانِي.

(p-130) وجَعَلَ الحَرالِّيُّ المَثَلَيْنِ لِلْمُنافِقِينَ فَقالَ: ضَرَبَ لَهم مَثَلَيْنِ، لَمّا كانَ لَهم حالانِ، ولِلْقُرْآنِ عَلَيْهِمْ تَنَزُّلانِ: مِنهُ ما يَرْغَبُونَ فِيهِ لِما فِيهِ مِن مَصْلَحَةِ دُنْياهم، فَضَرَبَ لَهُمُ المَثَلَ الأوَّلَ، وقَدَّمَهُ لِأنَّهُ سَبَبُ دُخُولِهِمْ مَعَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا، لِما رَأوْا مِن مُعاجَلَةِ عِقابِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا في الدُّنْيا؛ ومِنهُ ما يَرْهَبُونَهُ ولا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَماعَهُ، لِما يَتَضَمَّنُهُ مِن أُمُورٍ شاقَّةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ لا يَحْمِلُها إلّا مُؤْمِنٌ حَقًّا، ولا يَتَحَمَّلُها إلّا مَن آمَنَ، ولِما يَلْزَمُ مِنهُ مِن فَضِيحَةِ خِداعِهِمْ، فَضَرَبَ لَهُ المَثَلَ الثّانِيَ؛ فَلَنْ يَخْرُجَ حالُهم عِنْدَ نُزُولِ نُجُومِ القُرْآنِ عَنْ مُقْتَضى هَذَيْنِ المَثَلَيْنِ. انْتَهى.

وضَرْبُ الأمْثالِ المَنهِيُّ إلى الحَمْدِ المُنْتَهِي إلى الإحاطَةِ بِكُلِّ حَدٍّ، لا سِيَّما في أُصُولِ الدِّينِ، الكاشِفُ لِحَقِيقَةِ التَّوْحِيدِ، المُوصِلُ إلى اليَقِينِ في الإيمانِ بِالغَيْبِ، المُحَقِّقُ لِما لِلَّهِ تَعالى مِن صِفاتِ الكَمالِ، الدّافِعُ لِلشُّكُوكِ، الحافِظُ في طَرِيقِ السُّلُوكِ، مِمّا اخْتَصَّ بِهِ القُرْآنُ مِن حَيْثُ كانَ مَنهِيًّا إلى الحَمْدِ ومُفْصِحًا بِهِ، فَكانَ حَرْفُ الحَمْدِ. وذَلِكَ أنَّهُ حَرْفٌ عامٌّ مُحِيطٌ شامِلٌ (p-131) لِجَمِيعِ الأُمُورِ، كافِلٌ بِكُلِّ الشَّرائِعِ في سائِرِ الأزْمانِ؛ فَكانَ أحَقُّ الرُّسُلِ بِهِ مَن كانَتْ رِسالَتُهُ عامَّةً لِجَمِيعِ الخَلْقِ، وكِتابُهُ شامِلًا لِجَمِيعِ الأمْرِ، وهو أحْمَدُ ومُحَمَّدٌ (ﷺ).

قالَ الإمامُ أبُو الحَسَنِ الحَرالِّيُّ في كِتابِهِ "عُرْوَةِ المِفْتاحِ": هَذا الحَرْفُ لِإحاطَتِهِ أُنْزِلَ وِتْرًا، وسائِرُ الحُرُوفِ أشْفاعٌ لِاخْتِصاصِها، ووَجْهُ إنْزالِهِ تَفْهِيمُ ما غَمَضَ مِنَ المُغَيَّباتِ بِضَرْبِ مَثَلٍ مِنَ المَشْهُوداتِ. ولَمّا كانَ لِلْأمْرِ تَنَزُّلاتٌ، ولِلْخَلْقِ تَطَوُّراتٌ، كانَ الأظْهَرُ مِنها مَثَلًا لِما هو دُونَهُ في الظُّهُورِ، وكُلَّما ظَهَرَ مَمْثُولٌ صارَ مَثَلًا لِما هو أخْفى مِنهُ، فَكانَ لِذَلِكَ أمْثالًا عَدَدًا: مِنها مَثَلٌ لَيْسَ بِمَمْثُولٍ لِظُهُورِهِ، ومَمْثُولاتٌ تَصِيرُ أمْثالًا لِما هو أخْفى مِنها، إلى أنْ تَنْتَهِيَ الأمْثالُ إلى غايَةِ مَحْسُوسٍ أوْ مَعْلُومٍ، فَتَكُونُ تِلْكَ الغايَةُ مَثَلًا أعْلى، كالسَّماواتِ والأرْضِ فِيما يُحَسُّ، والعَرْشِ والكُرْسِيِّ فِيما يُعْلَمُ: ﴿ولَهُ المَثَلُ الأعْلى في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [الروم: 27]، ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ (p-132) العَرْشَ ومَن حَوْلَهُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ [غافر: 7]. وذَلِكَ المَثَلُ الأعْلى لِإحاطَتِهِ اسْمُهُ الحَمْدُ: ﴿ولَهُ الحَمْدُ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [الروم: 18]. وأحْمَدُهُ أنْهاهُ وأدْناهُ إلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، بِحَيْثُ لا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ اللَّهِ تَعالى واسِطَةٌ؛ فَلِذَلِكَ ما اسْتَحَقَّ أكْمَلُ الخَلْقِ وأجْمَعُهُ، وأكْمَلُ الأمْرِ وأجْمَعُهُ، الِاخْتِصاصَ بِالحَمْدِ، فَكانَ أكْمَلُ الأُمُورِ سُورَةَ الحَمْدِ، وكانَ أكْمَلُ الخَلْقِ صُورَةَ مُحَمَّدٍ (ﷺ)، كانَ خُلُقُهُ القُرْآنَ: ﴿ولَقَدْ آتَيْناكَ سَبْعًا مِنَ المَثانِي والقُرْآنَ العَظِيمَ﴾ [الحجر: 87]. ودُونَ المَثَلِ الأعْلى الجامِعِ، الأمْثالُ العِلْيَةُ المُفَصَّلَةُ مِنهُ: ﴿ضَرَبَ لَكم مَثَلًا مِن أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ [الروم: 28]. ولِإحاطَةِ أمْرِ اللَّهِ وكَمالِهِ في كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يَصِحُّ أنْ يَضْرِبَهُ مَثَلًا: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَسْتَحْيِي أنْ يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةً فَما فَوْقَها﴾ [البقرة: 26]، ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أوْلِياءَ كَمَثَلِ العَنْكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا﴾ [العنكبوت: 41]. ولِلْمَثَلِ حُكْمٌ مِن مَمْثُولِهِ: إنْ كانَ حَسَنًا حَسُنَ مَثَلُهُ، وإنْ كانَ سَيِّئًا ساءَ مَثَلُهُ؛ ولَمّا كانَ أعْلى الأمْثالِ الحَمْدَ، كانَ أوَّلُ الفاتِحَةِ الحَمْدَ، ولَمّا كانَ أخْفى أمْرِ الخَلْقِ النِّفاقَ، كانَ أوَّلُ مَثَلٍ في التَّرْتِيبِ مَثَلَ النِّفاقِ، وهو أدْنى مَثَلٍ لِما خَفِيَ مِن أمْرِ الخَلْقِ، كَما أنَّ الحَمْدَ أعْلى مَثَلٍ غابَ مِن أمْرِ الحَقِّ؛ (p-133) وبَيْنَ الحَدَّيْنِ أمْثالٌ حَسَنَةٌ وسَيِّئَةٌ: ﴿مَثَلُ الجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ﴾ الآيَتَيْنِ،

﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها﴾ [الجمعة: 5]، ﴿فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ الكَلْبِ﴾ [الأعراف: 176]، الآيَتَيْنِ. وبِقَدْرِ عُلُوِّ المَثَلِ أوْ دُنُوِّهِ أوْ تَوَسُّطِهِ يَتَزايَدُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ الإيمانُ، ولِلْعالِمِ العِلْمُ، ولِلْفاهِمِ الفَهْمُ، وبِضِدِّ ذَلِكَ لِمَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِأضْدادِ تِلْكَ الأوْصافِ:

﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَيَعْلَمُونَ أنَّهُ الحَقُّ مِن رَبِّهِمْ وأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَيَقُولُونَ ماذا أرادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا ويَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيرًا﴾ [البقرة: 26]. ومَعْرِفَةُ أمْثالِ القُرْآنِ، المُعَرِّفَةُ إحاطَةَ مَمْثُولاتِها وعِلْمَ آياتِهِ، المُعْلِمَةُ اخْتِصاصَ مَعْلُوماتِها، هو حَظُّ العَقْلِ واللُّبِّ وحَرْفِهِ مِنَ القُرْآنِ. ولِكُلِّ حَرْفٍ اخْتِصاصٌ بِحَظٍّ مِن تَدَرُّكِ الإنْسانِ وأعْمالِ القُلُوبِ والأنْفُسِ والأبْدانِ، فَمَن يُسِّرَ لَهُ القِراءَةُ والعَمَلُ بِحَرْفٍ مِنهُ اكْتَفى، ومَن جُمِعَ لَهُ قِراءَةُ جَمِيعِ أحْرُفِهِ عِلْمًا وعَمَلًا فَقَدْ أتَمَّ ووَفّى. وبِذَلِكَ يَكُونُ القارِئُ مِنَ القُرّاءِ الَّذِينَ قالَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «إنَّهم أعَزُّ مِنَ الكِبْرِيتِ الأحْمَرِ»، يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَن يَشاءُ، واللَّهُ ذُو الفَضْلِ العَظِيمِ.

ثُمَّ قالَ فِيما بِهِ يَحْصُلُ قِراءَةُ هَذا الحَرْفِ: اعْلَمْ أنَّ قِراءَةَ الأحْرُفِ (p-134) السِّتَّةِ تَمامًا وفاءٌ بِتَفْصِيلِ العِبادَةِ، لِأنَّها أشْفاعٌ: ثَلاثَةٌ لِلتَّخَلُّصِ والتَّخَلِّي، وثَلاثَةٌ لِلْعَمَلِ والتَّحَلِّي، لِأنَّ تَرْكَ الحَرامِ طُهْرَةُ البَدَنِ، وتَرْكَ النَّهْيِ طُهْرَةُ النَّفْسِ، وتَرْكَ التَّعَرُّضِ لِلْمُتَشابِهِ طُهْرَةُ القَلْبِ، ولِأنَّ تَناوُلَ الحَلالِ زَكاءُ البَدَنِ، وطاعَةَ الأمْرِ زَكاءُ النَّفْسِ، وتَحَقُّقَ العُبُودِيَّةِ بِمُقْتَضى حَرْفِ المُحْكَمِ نُورُ القَلْبِ.

وأمّا قِراءَةُ حَرْفِ الأمْثالِ، فَهو وفاءُ العِبادَةِ بِالقَلْبِ جَمْعًا ودَوامًا: ﴿ولَهُ الدِّينُ واصِبًا﴾ [النحل: 52]، و﴿الَّذِينَ هم عَلى صَلاتِهِمْ دائِمُونَ﴾ [المعارج: 23]. فالَّذِي يَحْصُلُ: قِراءَةُ هَذا الحَرْفِ إنَّما هو خاصٌّ بِالقَلْبِ؛ لِأنَّ أعْمالَ الجَوارِحِ وأحْوالَ النَّفْسِ قَدِ اسْتَوْفَتْها الأحْرُفُ السِّتَّةُ التَّفْصِيلِيَّةُ، والَّذِي يَخُصُّ القَلْبَ بِقِراءَةِ هَذا الحَرْفِ هو المَعْرِفَةُ التّامَّةُ المُحِيطَةُ بِأنَّ كُلَّ الخَلْقِ دَقِيقَهُ وجَلِيلَهُ خَلْقُ اللَّهِ وحْدَهُ لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ في شَيْءٍ مِنهُ، وأنَّهُ جَمِيعَهُ مَثَلٌ لِكُلِّيَّةِ أمْرِ اللَّهِ القائِمِ بِكُلِّيَّةِ ذَلِكَ الخَلْقِ، وأنَّ كُلِّيَّةَ ذَلِكَ الأمْرِ الَّذِي هو مَمْثُولٌ لِمَثَلِ الخَلْقِ هو مَثَلٌ لِلَّهِ تَعالى: ﴿ولَهُ المَثَلُ الأعْلى﴾ [الروم: 27]، وأنَّ تَفاصِيلَ ذَلِكَ الخَلْقِ المُحِيطاتِ أمْثالٌ لِقِيامِها مِن تَفاصِيلِ ذَلِكَ الأمْرِ المُحِيطاتِ بِها، وأنَّ تَفاصِيلَ الأمْرِ المُحِيطاتِ أمْثالٌ لِأسْماءِ اللَّهِ تَعالى الحُسْنى بِما هي مُحِيطَةٌ. ولِجَمْعِ هَذا الحَرْفِ لَمْ يَصِحَّ إنْزالُهُ إلّا عَلى الخَلْقِ الجامِعِ الآدَمِيِّ، الَّذِي هو صَفْوَةُ اللَّهِ وفِطْرَتُهُ، وعَلى سَيِّدِ الآدَمِيِّينَ مُحَمَّدٍ خاتَمِ النَّبِيِّينَ، وهو خاصَّتُهُ وخاصَّةُ آلِهِ، وعَنْهُ (p-135) كَمَلَ الدِّينُ بِالإحْسانِ، وصَفا العِلْمُ بِالإيقانِ، وشُوهِدَ في الوَقْتِ الحاضِرِ ما بَيْنَ حَدِّيِ الأزَلِ الماضِي والأبَدِ الغابِرِ، وعَنْ تَمامِ اليَقِينِ والإحْسانِ تَحَقَّقَ الفَناءُ لِكُلِّ فانٍ، وبَقِيَ وجْهُ رَبِّ مُحَمَّدٍ ذِي الجَلالِ والإكْرامِ، وكانَ هَذا الحَرْفُ، بِما اسْمُهُ الحَمْدُ، هو لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ بِداءٌ وخِتامٌ. انْتَهى.

Al-Biqa'i's Commentary (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 2, Verse 21:

When it was established through this clarification of what the disbelievers in both of their categories have of wretchedness, together with the perfection of power and the comprehensiveness of knowledge, which necessitate the oneness (wahdaniyya) of God, it definitively produced the singling out of Him in worship, which entails the happiness contained in "You alone do we worship" (iyyaka na'budu). Thereby, His saying turned toward them directly, after turning away from them at the division, as a notification that by what preceded of the striking of parables and other things, they had come within the scope of those qualified to be addressed directly, without an intermediary, as an encouragement (tansheet) for them in His worship, an incitement and a stirring toward raising their selves through the approach of the Greatest King, away from submission to one who is beneath Him, but rather beneath them. It is also good news for whoever turns toward Him after having turned away from Him, through the continuance of elevation. Thus, what the particle of calling (harf al-nida') indicated is removed, and the one called is described as remaining in distance through heedlessness, inattention, aversion, shortcoming in worship, agitation and wavering: "O mankind (ya ayyuha al-nas)."

Al-Harali said in his tafsir: "Ya" is an alert to one who is within hearing of the one alerting, so that he may turn to the address, and it is an alert within the very self of the one addressed. The middle distance is understood between ayaa (with the long vowel) and ay (with the short vowel). "Ayy" is an indefinite noun whose meaning is the singling out of what falls under it from the requirement of a comprehensive noun. "Ha" is a word whose meaning is an alert to a matter that the one alerting gains. End of quote. And He, glorified is He, emphasized the speech by the indefiniteness, the alert and the clarification by specifying the intended one of the calling, as an alert that what comes after it are important matters that deserve the gathering of skirts and standing upon the leg of earnestness.

Al-Harali also said: Know that just as the Opening of the Book encompasses the whole Qur'an, so too each surah has been given a comprehensive heading that contains all of its oft-repeated verses, and a conclusion that aligns and is organized by its heading. For this reason a surah serves as a heading for several surahs, and the alert to this will occur in its proper place, God willing. Know also that every prophet is one who has been informed (munabba') — pronounced with a hamza — from al-naba', which is news, for he began his call while not knowing the hidden matter of his affair and the news of his people. God, Mighty and Majestic, made His prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) a prophet of elevation (munabbiyan) — from prophethood (nubuwwa) — pronounced without a hamza. Its meaning is elevation of rank and loftiness. Among what God exalted him with is that He sent ahead before his call the knowledge of the hidden matter of his affair and the treasured knowledge of God, Exalted is He, in the secret of decree which has always been concealed in every book. So He informed him that God, Exalted is He, created those being called, who are in the state of wavering, oscillating between being absorbed in the conditions of their own selves and returning to the remembrance of their Lord, in three types: among them is one who was created upon faith and was not sealed upon it (i.e., upon his heart), so he will certainly respond; and among them is one who was sealed upon disbelief, so he will certainly refuse; and among them is one who vacillates between the two extremes, outwardly faith and inwardly disbelief; and that each is made easy for what he was created for. Thereby the expansion of his breast during the time of his call was accomplished, and the constriction of his breast, which he shared with the prophets (with the hamza), was removed. Then he rose after that to the one deserving of his lofty rank. So the first thing with which He opened his Book was to make him know the meaning of what "Alif Lam Mim" contains. Then He explained from it the three conditions of those called by this Book. At that point He began to instruct him in the general call to mankind, so after that He opened the call, the summons and the summons (da'wa) to worship, meaning by this verse. God, Glorified is He, undertook the calling of creation in this general call, which comprises every call in the Qur'an.

Because its opening included a threat against His Messenger, the address of that was not carried out upon his tongue; and because it contains severity, the address of the King, and recompense, while Muhammad (ﷺ) is a mercy to the worlds, it was not fitting to carry it out upon his tongue for that reason. As for the other messengers, the general call of whomever God, Glorified is He, specified the account of his call, it is carried out upon their tongues; and for this reason the opposition of their people and those they called was great.

When the Truth, Exalted is He, carried out this call from before him, there was in it good news of victory and the manifestation of (p-140) His religion, because God, Glorified and Exalted is He, is not overpowered by His creation.

When it reached the good news, which is mercy, He carried the speech over to addressing him, peace be upon him, with His saying: "And give good news" (wa bashshir). Along with the carrying out of the call of the messengers upon their tongues, it was attached to the Name of God with the wording "that worship God" (an u'budu Allah) and the like. So it was difficult for most souls to respond, due to the Name of God escaping the grasp of minds. Yet with God, Glorified is He, undertaking this call by His lofty authority, He carried it out with the Name of Lordship (rububiyya), which is a name closer in example to souls, because they witness His signs in the meaning of nurture (tarbiya) and fostering (rababa). Moreover, the mention of the Name of God in the call of the messengers was not followed by, nor described with, the signs of divinity; and had it been mentioned, the example of its knowledge would not be near, so it is (p-141) like the sun and the moon and the like. And God, Exalted is He, mentioned Lordship in this call followed by its manifest signs, which neither escape reason nor sense, and whose denial is impossible.

The reason souls are distant from submitting at the call by the Name of God is that the signs of Lordship, which are easy for them to submit to from the aspect by which, with a little of them, they submit to kings and benefactors (because they are disposed to love whoever does good to them), remain, at the call by the Name of God, far from awareness of their attribution to the Name of God, and the intellect is perplexed regarding the one to whom worship is directed. Heedless souls attribute the signs of Lordship to what they observe of the nearest causes in customary matters, such as the seasons upon which births and sustenance have been tied according to the wisdom of God, Glorified is He, or to the causes of these causes, such as the stars and the like. So what suits the one called during his subsistence is not harmonious with worship to Him, and hesitation and refusal increase. The ease which (p-142) God intended for this Community required the mention of Lordship attached to its signs. End of quote.

Since worship that is deficient through shirk or otherwise is void, and increasing from the sound and persisting upon it is a new worship for which the command is fitting, He addressed both groups and said: "Worship your Lord" (u'budu rabbakum), that is, the One who has no lord other than Him, with worship of such a kind that the Self-Sufficient accepts it. Then He described Him with what the attribute of Lord indicated of benevolence, as an alert to His existence and to the obligation of worship to Him by the obligation of thanking the benefactor, so He said: "Who created you" (alladhi khalaqakum). Al-Harali said: "Alladhi" is an indefinite noun whose meaning is an essence described by an attribute by which it is followed, which is its necessary relative clause. Creation (khalq) is the determination of the mingled constituents of what is intended to be manifested as a form after mixing and composition. "And those before you" (wa alladhina min qablikum): "qabl" is that toward which, when the one turning returns to the origin of his direction, he turns toward it. End of quote.

Then He explained its outcome with His saying: "So that you may be God-fearing" (la'allakum tattaqun), that is, so that your condition, by worshipping Him, because all of it is goodness and there is no goodness in anything else, becomes the condition of one for whom piety is hoped; and piety is avoiding what is ugly out of fear of God. What comes in His saying "so that you may be thankful" (la'allakum tashkurun) will benefit here. Al-Harali said: "La'alla" is a word of hope for what its cause has preceded. He began from the signs of Lordship with the mention of creation, because it is in their essences, and connected that with the creation of those before them, so that they do not lean in their creation upon those before them. He hoped piety for them, so that they worship their Lord from the standpoint of their view of their creation and the determination of their constituents, for when they ascribe their creation to their Lord, it is more fitting that they ascribe to Him the fruit of that in their attributes and actions, so they refrain from self-sufficiency, and piety arises for them thereby. End of quote.

(p-145) How well it is that the command to worship is placed, when the argument is made for the right to worship through the creation of the first and the last and what follows, immediately after establishing the power of the Caller, which points to a warning against His punishments! This argument for the sole entitlement to worship is also unique, coming after describing those who are farthest from it in their stubbornness, through observable matters that every intelligent person reaches at first glance: the spreading out of the earth and what follows, which sustain their survival, such as dwelling and provision. It is set in a context that reminds of blessing, warns against losing it, and points to God after the indication through the self, since everyone knows necessarily that he came into existence after not having been. So there must be an originator other than people, because of what is observed, that the state of all is like his state. It also points through the horizons, since they are changing, and so they need a changer, who is the one who brought them into being and is not changing, because He is not a body or corporeal. It is in a context that reminds of great blessings, which require love for the Benefactor, abandoning dispute, and obtaining submission. So He said: ﴿Who made﴾. Al-Harrali said: from making (ja'l), which is the manifestation of a matter from a cause and making it into something. ﴿for you the earth﴾, meaning the place that gathers the growth of every plant, whether apparent or hidden. The apparent is like births and everything whose origin is water, and the hidden is like deeds, character, and everything whose origin is water, whose sign is guidance, knowledge, and the like. Because the meaning of its name is realized in this sense, its description came from the word of its name, so it was said: ardun ariḍah (a fertile, productive earth), meaning the generous one that causes growth. Its original meaning is what is lowest, in contrast to the meaning of heaven, which is what is high, over the lower part of the earth, as if it were the tablet of His pen on which His book appears. End of quote.

(p-146) ﴿a bed﴾, which is a carpet whose ceiling is the sky, and it is the resting place of living creatures, both the living and the dead. Its origin, as al-Harrali said, is a carpet on which one lies down for rest and the like.

﴿and the sky as a structure﴾, meaning a tent that encloses the suitability of the dwelling place. By my life, it is indeed a structure of lofty worth, firmly ordered, pleasing to behold, and great in what it reveals.

These blessings, which indicate the Creator and call to thank Him, are arranged in the most wise order. He put people first, because a person knows himself best, and blessing upon him calls more to gratitude. He placed the second after the one before it, because he knows his own kind best. He made the earth third, because it is his dwelling which he cannot do without. He made the sky fourth, because it is his roof. He made water fifth, because it is like the effect and benefit that comes out of them, and what comes out of their cause of provision, such as offspring produced between them. So He said: ﴿and sent down﴾. Al-Harrali said: from sending down (inzal), which is the hurling of a command from high to low. End of quote.

(p-147) ﴿from the sky﴾, meaning by stirring up the winds that drive the clouds carrying the water, ﴿water﴾, meaning a fine substance that cools the thirst's burning, by which every growing thing lives. Al-Harrali said: it is the first thing visible to the eye of the forms of creation. ﴿and brought forth﴾ from bringing forth (ikhraj), which is the manifestation of something from a veil. Putting it after with the letter fa' (so) confirms the causation in the water. End of quote.

He used the plural of paucity for fruits and left provision indefinite, though it is observed, because both are extremely abundant to a degree that cannot be counted. This is to belittle them in comparison with His power, out of honor for Him. So He said, (p-148) ﴿by it, fruits as provision for you﴾. Bringing out things behind the veil of causes is more fitting to the obligation of belief in the unseen, because, as it is said: "Were it not for causes, the doubter would not doubt." Fruit, as al-Harrali said, is the food of the palm and tree, and it is upon them. He expressed it with min (of), because not every fruit is provision, due to what is on it and in it of husk, shell, and pit. Nor is every fruit provision, for some of it is for medicine and some is poison and other things. In His saying ﴿for you﴾ there is an indication that provision is a completion of their selves and a passage toward their return with recompense from them.

This Lord has been described in this verse with two relative clauses. He mentioned the connection of the second with the word (p-149) "making", because the state of sustaining is ordered upon the state of creation and derived from it. So no person of intellect doubts the entitlement to submission to the One who undertook creating him and established his composition. Nor does any person of sense doubt, when he wakes from sleep or heedlessness and finds a carpet spread out for him, a tent pitched over him, and food and drink prepared and offered to him, that his soul moves by itself to honor the One who did this for him and to bear His blessing and magnify Him. So, for the revelation of this call in this clarification, which compels the soul to submit, and in which knowledge of its requirements enters the rank of necessity and immediate perception, this call is an Arabic call, running according to the states of the Arabs. The Arabs do not go beyond necessary knowledge by themselves, and it is not their nature to force thoughts or to take the path toward the theoretical sciences drawn from indicators and proofs. So they were addressed in what they were created upon. It descends to them so that (p-150) its transfer is from one natural disposition to another natural disposition, and from intuitive knowledge to lofty intuitive knowledge, in order that the rank of i'rab (grammatical inflection) and clarity be preserved for them, by not forcing them into a path that introduces doubt into their knowledge. For every acquired knowledge requires forced causation through signs, markers, and proofs that are remote from sense and the first assaults of intellect, whose proofs conflict with one another and doubt becomes habitual. So this Arabic call was protected from artificiality and was carried out according to what the opening of the surah decided in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2].

Know that the state of the created being in his provision is parallel to his state in his existence. So it is known, through consideration and the proportion whose nature is that unknown things are learned through it, that water is the seed of human existence, just as water is the root of his provision. For this reason, peace be upon him, when he was asked by one who said "Who are you?" and did not want to name himself, said: "We are from water." It is also known (p-151) that the earth and the sky have an entry into the mixture of man, and his provision's coming into being is arranged upon it. In mentioning the earth in the definite form, there is a taking of the earth to its end and completeness. For this reason, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever usurps a span of land, will have it hung around his neck from seven earths." Likewise, mentioning the sky is a taking of it to its end and completeness. He put the earth first, because the gaze of souls toward what is beneath them comes before their gaze toward what is above them. Then he said: Because the sign of lordship is clear, most people accepted it, and they only hesitated over prophethood. For this reason the mention of prophethood is connected with the threat. End of quote.

When He commanded worship of Himself and reminded them, glorified is He, of what they know He alone does, it was fitting to forbid associating with Him anything that has no effect at all in any of that. This is through the fa' of causation from both matters together. He said, expressing by the divine name what is most fitting for rebuke over the deification of others: ﴿So do not set up rivals to Allah﴾, meaning what His encompassing attributes of perfection are. It is also possible (p-152) that it is caused by the hoped-for piety, so that the particle lā is negating and the verb is in the subjunctive. ﴿rivals﴾, meaning according to your assumption that they do what you wish. Al-Harrali said: the plural of nid, which is the one who opposes in the attribute of standing and enduring. He expressed it with making (ja'l) because through making and moving from one state to a lower state, heedlessness coats the hearts, until they witness in blessings and afflictions only the creation, whether a king, a holder of command, or whoever holds the higher hand. When they witnessed that from them, their hope and fear became attached to them, and their Lord punished them for that by their own hands. So the driver of their hope for them and the driver of their fear of them grew strong, and they humbled themselves and submitted to them. So they became worshippers of the tāghūt (false object of worship) and made them rivals to Allah. End of quote.

How excellent is His saying in rebuking them and reminding them of what they have done against themselves: ﴿while you know﴾, meaning while the state is that you are people of knowledge according to what you claim (p-153). It hints that whoever associates with Him while these proofs exist is not one from whom knowledge can be valid, so he is counted among the beasts. In it, as al-Harrali said, there is an announcement of the manifestation of signs of what prevents making a rival for what one sees: that all creation, lowest and highest, stands in the sky and on the earth and from water. So whoever makes a rival to Allah from what the sky and earth contain, and draws support from water, has contradicted the necessary knowledge by which he was obligated to humble himself to lordship within himself. If he judges by that about others whose state is like his state, he is more entitled in knowledge. End of quote.

In its following what came before it is the utmost rebuke (p-154) of the one who abandoned this Capable One over all things and worshipped what has no power over anything.

This verse is among the muhkam (clear, decisive verses) upon which the sharia agree and the scriptures unite, and it is the pillar of humility, and upon it turns the axis of lowliness and submission. The Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in al-'Urwa: The purpose of the revelation of this letter (verse) is to establish the servant's attribution of what is fitting for him in the sincerity of his direction toward the Truth, by severing himself from his own self and disavowing it, seeking refuge in his Lord with submission, striving in serving Him with reverence, leaning on Him with reliance, and being at peace with Him in tranquility: ﴿O soul at peace﴾ [al-Fajr 89:27] ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 89:28]. The servant's adornment with the attributes that befit him is reinforced by reciting this letter and acting upon it, in accordance with his freedom from exposure to its ambiguous counterpart, because following the mutashabih (ambiguous verses) is deviation, due to the shortcoming of intellect and understanding in attaining it, and it is obligatory to limit oneself to belief in it without weighing what Allah addressed to His servants for knowing against what He made for the servant for reflection. Glorified is He, who made no path to knowing Him except through incapacity to know Him.

The comprehensive scope of the revealed muhkam is what the revelation opened with in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾ [al-'Alaq 96:1] and the verses, and what He put first in the order in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O people, worship your Lord﴾ (p-155) [al-Baqarah 2:21], up to what is included with that of mentioning the worship of the heart, which is knowledge: ﴿I did not create jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:56]. So let the first thing you call them to be the worship of Allah, and when they know Allah, then the worship of the self, which is general patience and good recompense: ﴿Restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord﴾ [al-Kahf 18:28], ﴿and they repel evil with good﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:22], ﴿those who are humble in their prayer﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:2], "If this one's heart were humbled, his limbs would be humbled..." up to the rest of the servant's states by which he is realized in turning toward the Lord. The two letters of the lawful and unlawful are for reforming this world, and the two letters of command and prohibition are for reforming the Hereafter, dealing with His Book. Acting upon this letter is a joy in servitude and a refuge from freedom. For this reason it is the first of specialization and the beginning of selection, and it is the singling out of loyalty to Allah alone without associating anything with Him in self or other. For this reason, His servant and prophet, peace be upon him, was first sent down with it. It is the fruit of what came before and the foundation of what comes after (p-156). For the servant it is a set of realized states in which no one who shows off or is hypocritical shares. It shares with the four previously mentioned, meaning the prohibition, the command, the lawful, and the unlawful, because those are outward deeds, so the hypocrite adorns himself with them. Yet with his hypocrisy he cannot adorn himself with knowledge, nor with humility, nor with submission, nor with longing for meeting, nor with grief over delay, nor with contentment with decree, nor with the attracting love that clings to remaining on the path of passing away, nor with anything of what the verses of the clear muhkam revealed in the Qur'an include, and its hadiths revealed for clarification. This letter is characteristic only of the servants of the Merciful: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth humbly, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [al-Furqan 25:63], those over whom Satan has no authority: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority﴾ [al-Hijr 15:42].

Since the letter of the muhkam (ḥarf al-muḥkam, the aspect of the clear, unambiguous verses) is the servant's due toward the Lord in the natural disposition (fiṭrah) upon which He created him, it is constant in every religion (milla) and every law (sharʿah). Therefore its verses are the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitāb), which comprises the four letters (al-aḥruf al-arbaʿah), because the other letters change, are abrogated and replaced (tabaddul, tanāsukh), and vary in their fitness for the law and the religions, and differ according to the doctrines of the Imams regarding the all-encompassing religion (al-milla al-jāmiʿah), while the religions agree on the letter of the muhkam. So it is their mother and their constant pillar amid their changes, and it is the letter of guidance (ḥarf al-hudā), by which Allah guides whom He wills. Those who read it and act upon it are the rightly guided, the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa’l-Jamāʿah). Just as those who follow the letter of the mutashābih (the ambiguous aspect) are those who scatter among the religions, namely the People of innovation (bidʿah) and of desires (ahwāʾ), who occupy themselves with what does not concern them. And by this ambiguous letter Allah leads astray whom He wills. Thus the letter of the muhkam is for unity and guidance, and the letter of the mutashābih is for division and misguidance. ﴿And Allah speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 4]

Then he said: Know that the recitation of the four letters that preceded is the portion of the common people of the Ummah, who work for their Lord seeking reward, and who deal with Him by seeking multiplication of recompense. The recitation of this letter in its completeness is the portion of those who are truly realized in servitude (al-mutaḥaqqiqīn bi’l-ʿubūdiyyah), who worship through sincere states, who are fearful of the illusion of transaction (wahm al-muʿāmalah), because they perceive that the servant, toward his master, is disposed in whatever and however He wills. He has no right or ruling of his own, and no argument against his master regarding whatever form of happiness or wretchedness He has placed him in. ﴿In whatever form He willed, He fashioned you﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 8]. ﴿On the basis that We replace your likes and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah: 61].

The means by which the recitation of this letter is attained is either from the side of the heart: knowledge of the servitude of creation to the Real is the bondage of creation, provision, and disposal in whatever He wills, both in what lies between him and his Lord, what lies between him and himself, and what lies between him and his peers among the rest of the servants. He possesses for himself no harm, no benefit, no death, no life, and no resurrection. He takes only what his master has given him, and he guards against only what his master has protected him from, and no one removes evil from him except Him. So he surrenders to Him the keys of his affair, outwardly and inwardly. This is the religion with Allah that accepts nothing else. ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 19]. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 85]. It is the religion of the Prophet, the servant, and what is realized for the servant of this, through the consideration of reason and the purity of the core, is the Ḥanīfiyyah, the religion of the Prophet, the Friend (Khalīl) of Allah. This is from the side of the heart.

As for the side of the state of the soul (nafs): all the states of the servant who is wholly owned, the utter slave, are: "I am only a servant who eats as a servant eats." The sum of this and its root is: humility through brokenness, humility through tenderness, freedom from exalting oneself or boasting over the rest of creation, and realizing lowliness before them through the description of the self. By this the goodness of conduct with creation and the sincerity of worship toward the Real are perfected.

As for the side of action: the limbs are directed, and submitted to Allah, in speech, deed, and giving; and in peaceful dealing with creation through tongue and hand. This is the completion of Islam and its firmness. "None of you is written among the Muslims until people are safe from his tongue and his hand."

What is specific to outward form among this is what is most fitting to the forms of servants, such as that upon which the form of prayer is built: lowering the gaze while standing and placing the right hand over the left opposite the chest, the form of the servant who is courteous and awaits what he does not know of his master's command. And like the form of sitting in it, which is the sitting of servants. Thus the Prophet ﷺ used to sit for his meal, so that the state of his worship in matters of his worldly life and his next life would be equal, and he would say: "I am only a servant who eats as a servant eats." And all that belongs to the form of servants influences his worship, his food, his drink, his clothing, his mount, his travel, and his residence. ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me, and Allah will love you﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 31]. Thus, through these matters, namely the realization of servitude in the heart, the humbling of the self, and the breaking of the limbs, the recitation of the letter of the muhkam is attained. And Allah is the Protector, the Praiseworthy. End.

(p-160) When these proofs were established, obedience to what they call for became obligatory, and no stubborn person was left with any excuse except to say, "I will not act until I know that this Book, which was described earlier as guidance, is the speech of God." He said, clarifying that it is from Him in its composition just as it is from Him in its meaning, and confirming what He concluded the previous verse with: whoever refrains from what He calls to, such as monotheism and other things, has no knowledge of any kind. He used the particle of doubt, may He be glorified, although He knows their state, to alert that it is very far-fetched for Him to assert their doubt after this clarification. ﴿And if﴾, i.e., if you are among those with pure insight and bright consciences, who know through the reality of these meanings, the sublimity of these methods and the eloquence of these structures, that this is (p-160) My speech, then hasten to obey what He commanded and refrain from what He forbade.

﴿And if you are in doubt﴾, i.e., in a doubt that encompasses you, about the Book that I have said, and who is more truthful than Me in speech, that ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [2:2].

(p-161) Here He also indicated His greatness and the greatness of the one it was sent down upon, by using the first-person plural, shifting from the third person to the first person, so He said: ﴿what We have sent down﴾. Al-Harali said: from tanzil (sending down), which is bringing near to understanding through detail, translation and the like. End.

﴿upon Our servant﴾, i.e., one purely devoted to Us, who never worshipped anything other than Us. Therefore he deserved to be singled out over the great men of the two cities and others. Yet you doubted that it is Our speech, sent down by Our command, and you claimed that Our servant Muhammad brought it from himself, because you imagined that among the speech you had heard there is something like it, (p-162) or because of the manner in which he brought it, in installments, or other aspects of his circumstances.

﴿Then produce﴾, i.e., in the manner of installments or otherwise. Al-Harali said: one who brings a matter does so from capacity and strength. ﴿a surah﴾, i.e., one single installment. Al-Harali said: a surah is a complete unit of what is heard, encompassing a complete meaning, like the walls encircling a city. End. The Qur'an is divided into surahs and verses because when a thing is a genus and types are made for it, and its types include categories, it is better, more majestic in its status, and nobler. This is especially so when forms follow one another in striking order, similar parts respond with fine coherence, and examples embrace one another in resemblance in the completeness of rulings and their beauty. It is also more stimulating to the reader and greater in his estimation, for what he takes from it when it is named by counted verses, a known surah, and so on. ﴿like it﴾, i.e., from the speech which you may claim is like what We have sent down, as He said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce its like﴾ [17:88]. For Our servant is one of you and grew up among you; he cannot bring what you cannot match except with Our support.

Since they found lying repugnant, He said: ﴿And call your witnesses﴾, i.e., whoever among those present in your town or nearby you can summon. (p-164) The witness, as al-Harali said, is one with whom presence is frequent and whose insight into what he has witnessed is deep. End.

﴿besides God﴾, i.e., so that they may look between the two speeches and bear witness to what their knowledge leads them to regarding similarity or difference, so that doubt disappears and the unseen becomes evident as testimony; or so that they may help you produce a piece like the encompassing portion you wish to oppose. Al-Harali said: "dun" denotes the station of nearness, the near being from the lower direction. The Arabs understood that the name of God is not applied to what the intellect can grasp, let alone what the senses perceive. They therefore realized that everything their senses perceive and their intellects reach is "besides God." End.

(p-165) In the expression "besides Him" there is a rebuke to them, for they did not accept His testimony, may He be glorified.

The wisdom in using the partitive "min" in this surah, but not in the rest of the Qur'an, is this: since He imposed on them a doubt which necessarily entails their claim that they had found a parallel to it or heard that someone had found a likeness to it, the situation required the use of "min," to indicate that what is demanded of them in the challenge is a piece of that supposed likeness: wise in its meanings, harmonious in its structures, its beginning joined to its end, like the walls of a city in soundness of arrangement, goodness of coherence, encompassing structures that are like meanings, and meeting of the two ends, until one cannot tell its beginning from its end. Whether the piece brought forth matches a verse or more than that, the challenge applies to a verse at the first consideration and to what exceeds it at the second, because the verses of the Qur'an are like a surah: its end is known from its beginning, and its beginning leads to its completion.

The meaning of "surah" here is its linguistic sense, because the thing being challenged is the supposed likeness (p-166), which does not exist outside the mind. Hence there is no established technical sense for cutting it into parts. Moreover, knowledge of the technical meaning was restricted to believers. Had the challenge been with a surah of the Qur'an, He would have said, "bring a surah like one of its surahs." Since this is not what was intended, the calling of witnesses was restricted to those present with them. What completes this discussion, God willing, will come in Surah Yunus, peace be upon him, and in the remaining surahs mentioned there that address this same meaning.

In His saying ﴿if you are truthful﴾ there is an allusion to their lying in claiming doubt about it. Al-Harali said: the truthful one is one whose tongue's speech and limbs' action agree with what his heart contains of a firmly established reality. He also said: the verse on the sending down of revelation is consistent with the verse on the sending down of provision, since the descent of what was sent down upon the Messenger, singled out for it, should be considered in comparison with the descent of provision. For these are two provisions: one outward, common to the disbeliever in its descent, and the other, revelation, is an inward provision (p-167) that specifically belongs to the elite by its descent, and is determined for whoever is most complete in natural disposition and most perfect in essence. It was not suitable for this inward provision to be general as the outward one is, for then the wisdom of singling out in the two provisions would be void. If doubt disputes with them about the singling out, they assume it is general and attempt to oppose it. Just as they testify through their senses to their ability when they attempt to challenge its generality, so they must testify to their inability to produce a surah like it, confirming the singling out of the one upon whom it was sent down. He mentioned him by the name of servanthood, informing of his fulfilment of all forms of humility, and showing the excellence of his being singled out for it over them, so that the cause of the singling out becomes apparent.

The "nun" in "nazzalna" encompasses one who descends with revelation from the Holy Spirit, the Trustworthy Spirit, and the like, because it implies a following. The "nun" in "Our servant" expresses the submission and following the Prophet (ﷺ) displays toward them, and what his great character requires of lowering the wing, to the extent that he agrees with whoever among his community (ﷺ) is correct in a matter, and to the extent that he takes on the attributes of a servant in his eating, as he said: "I eat as a servant eats." End.

The challenge with a surah includes the shortest surah, such as al-Kawthar. What is equivalent to it in the challenge (p-168) is an independent verse that matches it, and verses. This was stated by the Imam Jalal al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahalli in his commentary on Jam' al-Jawami' (a work of usul al-fiqh). The Imam Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Abd al-Da'im al-Barmawi preceded him, versifying it in his Alfiyya on usul, and transmitting it in its commentary from the apparent statement of Imam al-Haramayn in al-Shamil, and from the jurists' discussion of dower, where a man makes the teaching of a surah her dower and then teaches her part of a verse. The scholar Sa'd al-Din Mas'ud ibn Umar al-Taftazani preceded both of them. He said in his Talwih on the Tawdih of Sadr al-Shari'a: "The miraculous (mu'jiz) is the surah or its quantity." Thus those who spoke on i'jaz (inimitability) among the usulis and others mentioned that the challenge was with a surah of the Qur'an, whereas the correct view is that it was with a piece of a verse or more, because "surah" here means its linguistic meaning, not the technical one, as already explained.

The summary: since the verses concerning the hypocrites mention parables, and they found some of the Qur'an's parables strange and made them a place of doubt, though they were a place of certainty, they said, "If this were from God, He would not have mentioned such parables in it." He is greater than to mention in this Medinan surah what calls them to opposition by every means available to them, and to inform them that they are incapable of it and that their incapacity is permanent, establishing that in that state they were obstinate, not doubters. (p-169)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 24 (part 1 of 2):

(p-170) Since He, glory be to Him, knew that the proud souls and the lofty, zealous noses, which had adhered to something and been trained upon it until it became a disposition for them, finding it difficult to be separated from it and hard to be freed from it, He expressed this information by the phrase of incapacity, threatening them in a context that compels them to do justice by acknowledgment, or to have their hearts split by their inability to attain what is sought. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if you do not do it﴾, came with the particle of doubt, as a relief for them and a mockery of them in reality, and a making them appear foolish. Then He did not complete that relief, but struck them with a blow (p-170) that broke their backs and cut their hearts. So He said, so that the verse would ensure the soundness of the attribution of the composition (nazm) and the meaning, something firmer and more emphatic against their claim to ability, with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and you will never do it﴾. Thus He imposed upon them the disgrace of what had been decreed against them, of incapacity. They had no course of action except to hasten to confirm this by holding back, so they were like one who has been made to swallow a stone, and had no choice but silence. This confirmation continued for them and for their likes across the course of time, in every age, where its caller calls out and necks submit to it, and its muezzin proclaims and heads are bowed (p-171). The expression with the more general verb (fi'l), rather than with the verb of coming (ita'), is more eloquent, because negating the general verb is negating the more specific one and something more.

Al-Harrali said: al-fi'l (the act) is what arises from a motive from one who is capable, whether with knowledge or without knowledge, for the sake of religion or for other than it, as has been mentioned repeatedly before. End of quotation.

It has thus been established that this Book, which He stated is the guide to the straight path, is the greatest proof of the singling out of Him for worship and His being exclusively the object of the vigilance (muraqabah) to which He guided us with His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], and so on, by what has been established in it of the proofs of His unique divinity, through what has been established of their incapacity to oppose it, and the incapacity of all the Arabs, who were the most eloquent of creation, and likewise all who were born in their lands and whose tongues were shaped by theirs, from the Jews and Christians, who had from eloquence and knowledge what is well known. For the Jews of the Children of Israel who were in the Blessed City (Madinah), Khaybar, Yemen and elsewhere, and those of the Arabs who entered their religion, had eloquence, rhetoric and knowledge such that whoever reads the Sirah about them does not need to pause. The Christians of the Children of Israel, and those of the Arabs who adhered to their religion, were numerous, like the people of al-Mundhir ibn Ma' al-Sama, and those close to them among Abd al-Qays, Tanukh, their governor, and Ghassan. All of them were eloquent and articulate. Many of them added to that knowledge, and among them were the outstanding poets. Yet with all that, none of them was able to find fault in this Qur'an, nor did any of them oppose it, except what Musaylimah and al-Aswad al-Ansi said, by which they were disgraced, and God refuted them in it, and their disgrace travelled with the caravans, so they became a proverb throughout all the lands. (p-173)

Amr ibn Bahr al-Jahiz said in his book "al-Hujjah fi Tathbit Khabar al-Wahid" (The Proof in Establishing the Report of a Single Narrator): Indeed God, blessed and exalted is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) when the Arabs were at their most abundant in poetry and oratory, at their most judicious in language, and at their most equipped. He called the far and the near of them to the unity of God and to confirming His message. He called them to their share of proof. When he had cut off excuse, removed doubt, and what prevented them from acknowledgment became caprice and zeal rather than ignorance and bewilderment, He drove them to their share by the sword. He set war against them and they set war against him. He killed of their elite, their notables, their paternal uncles, their cousins, and they killed his paternal uncles, his cousins, the elite of his companions and the notables of his household. In all of that, he argued against them with the Qur'an and other things, calling them morning and evening (p-174) to oppose it, if he was a liar, with a single surah or a few easy verses. Whenever he increased his challenge to them with it, and their rebuke for their incapacity regarding it, there was revealed of their deficiency what had been hidden, and there appeared of it what had been obscure. When they found no stratagem and no argument, they said to him: "You know of the reports of the nations what we do not know, so you can do what we cannot." He said: "Then bring forth your fabricated ones." None of their orators could attempt it, no poet was tempted by it, and it did not take shape for them because of its artifice. Had they forced it, it would have appeared, and had it appeared, someone would have found it good, defended it, persisted in it, and claimed that he had opposed, matched and refuted it. Thus the intelligent man deduces the incapacity of the people despite the abundance of their speech, the breadth of their language, the ease of that for them, the multitude of their poets, and the multitude of those among them who satirised him (p-175) and opposed the poets of his companions and the orators of his community. For a single surah and a few easy verses would have been more damaging to his saying, more corrupting to his affair, more effective in refuting him, and swifter in dispersing his followers than surrendering lives, leaving homelands and spending wealth. This is from the sublime planning that is not hidden from one who is below Quraysh and the Arabs in intellect and judgment by many levels. They have the marvellous qasidah, the excellent rajaz, the long eloquent speeches and the short concise ones. They have rhymed prose (saj'), paired prose (muzdawaj), and loose speech (manthur). Then he challenged them with it, the farthest of them after the incapacity of the nearest had become clear. So it is impossible, may God honour you, that all these people should agree upon error in a manifest matter and a plainly exposed mistake, along with rebuke for deficiency and being made to stand over incapacity, while they are the most disdainful of creation and the most boastful of them, and speech is the master of their knowledge, and they needed it. Need prompts the search for a stratagem in an obscure matter, so how much more in an evident one! Just as it is impossible for them to agree for twenty-three years upon error in a matter of great benefit, so also it is impossible that they would leave it while they know it and find the way to it while they would expend more than that. End of quotation.

Thus their incapacity is established, and their eloquence and their signals were definitely silenced, and their pride and their might were humbled in humiliation. How can a created being, though firmly rooted in the marks of deficiency and the depths of need and weakness, oppose the one who is singled out with the attributes of perfection (p-177), exalted above equals, likes and forms?

People have differed about the cause of the inimitability (i'jaz). The best I have come across concerning that is what Imam Badr al-Din al-Zarkashi al-Shafi'i transmitted in his book "al-Burhan" from Imam Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi. He said, and to this most of the scholars of rational inquiry (ahl al-nazar) went: the aspect of the inimitability in it is from the side of eloquence (balaghah), but it was difficult for them to detail it, and they referred it to the judgment of taste (dhawq). He said: The truth is that the kinds of speech differ, and their levels in the degrees of expression vary. Among them is the eloquent, firm and robust; among them is the eloquent, near and easy; and among them is the permissible, free and flowing. (p-178) These divisions constitute praiseworthy excellent speech. The first division is its highest, the second its middle, and the third its lowest and nearest. The eloquences of the Qur'an took a share from each of these divisions and took a portion from each kind. Thus there was arranged for it, by the arrangement of these qualities, a pattern of speech that combines the two attributes of majesty (fakhamah) and sweetness (udhubah). These two, taken individually in their descriptions, are like opposites, because sweetness is the product of ease, and firmness and robustness treat a kind of harshness. So the combination of the two matters in its composition, with each of them remote from the other, was a virtue specific to the Qur'an, so that it would be a clear sign for its Prophet (ﷺ). The inability of all of mankind to bring the like of it was for several reasons. Among them: their knowledge does not encompass all the names of the Arabic language and its conventions, which are the containers of meanings. Their understandings do not grasp all the meanings of the things carried by those words, and their knowledge is not complete in fulfilling all the aspects of composition by which their harmony and the connection of parts to one another occur, so that they could arrive, (p-179) by choosing the best of the most excellent of its aspects, at producing speech like it. Speech is sustained by three things: a carrying word, a meaning that subsists in it, and a binding that composes both. When you reflect upon the Qur'an, you find these matters in it at the utmost nobility and excellence, to the point that you do not see any words more eloquent, more firm or sweeter than its words, nor any composition more beautiful in its formation or more firmly harmonious and fitting together than its composition. As for its meanings, every person of intellect bears witness to its precedence in its chapters and its ascent to the highest of its degrees. These three excellences may be found dispersed among kinds of speech, but that they be found gathered together in one kind was not found except in the speech of the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful. It follows from this that the Qur'an became inimitable only because it came with the most eloquent words, in the most excellent composition, containing the most correct meanings: the unity of God, exalted is He, His transcendence in His attributes, a call to His obedience, an explanation of the way of His worship, in matters of lawful and unlawful, prohibition and permission, admonition and correction, commanding right and forbidding wrong, guidance to noble morals and restraint from their opposites. It places each thing in its proper place, such that no place is seen as better for it, and in the image of reason no matter is imagined as more fitting for it. It deposits the reports of past generations and what descended of God's punishments upon those who passed away and opposed. It informs of the events to come in the future ages of time. In all of that it combines the proof and what it argues for, and the evidence and what it indicates, so that this would be more emphatic in binding one to what it calls to, and it declares the obligation of what it commands and forbids. It is known that bringing the like of these matters, and gathering their scattered parts until they are arranged and in harmony, is something the powers of man cannot reach and his capacity cannot attain. So creation was cut off short of it, and they were incapable of opposing it with its like or contradicting it in its form. Then those who were hostile to it kept saying at one time: "It is poetry", because they saw it arranged, and at another: "It is magic", because they saw it to be beyond their ability and not within their power. They found in it an effect on hearts and a dread in souls that troubled and bewildered them, so they could not restrain themselves from acknowledging it in some measure. For this reason they said: "Indeed it has sweetness, and upon it is (p-181) a radiance." At times, out of their ignorance, they would say: "It is the fables of the ancients which he has had written down, so they are dictated to him morning and evening" [al-Furqan: 5], although they knew that its bearer was unlettered and there was no one present to dictate or write anything of that sort, which obstinacy, ignorance and incapacity had made them say. End of quotation.

The beginning of his words leans toward the inimitability being by the composition alone, without regard to the meaning, while the end of his words leans toward its being by regard to both composition and meaning together, from the aspect he mentioned. This is what ought to be believed. However, in the challenge with a single surah; as for the challenge with ten, it is by regard to eloquence in composition only. Al-Baghawi transmitted this in his tafsir of Surah Hud from al-Mubarrad, and something like it has already passed a little earlier in the words of al-Jahiz.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 24 (part 2 of 2):

[p-181]

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in *Miftah al-Bab al-Muqfal* (The Key to the Locked Door): The first chapter concerns the superiority of the Qur'an's exposition over human exposition. Know that the eloquence of exposition rises in proportion to the loftiness of the one who expounds. Thus the exposition of God is superior to the exposition of His creatures in proportion to God's loftiness above His creation. The exposition of every expounder is proportionate to the comprehensiveness of his knowledge. When a human being describes what exists, he describes it only to the extent of what he perceives of it, and his knowledge does not encompass it, so his exposition does not reach the utmost eloquence concerning it. When he reports on the past, his exposition is in proportion to what remains of his deficient knowledge of it, existing in his memory, because of what human beings are bound to forget. When he wishes to report on the future, all exposition fails him except what he estimates or fabricates. So his exposition of the present is deficient, his exposition of the past is more deficient, and his exposition of the future is void. ﴿Rather, man desires to deny what lies ahead of him﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 5]. The exposition of God, glory be to Him, concerning what exists reaches the utmost extent of what His knowledge encompasses. ﴿Say: Knowledge is only with God﴾ [al-Mulk: 26]. Concerning the past, His exposition is according to His encompassing of what exists, and He, glory be to Him, is free of forgetting: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha: 52]. Concerning the future, He expounds the truth that will occur: ﴿We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾ [al-A'raf: 7]. ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth﴾ [al-A'raf: 8]. The true exposition is that whose expression does not weaken by suggesting any attribution of deficiency to it. A human being suspects himself in exposition and fears being attributed with incapacity, so he seeks to exhaust the exposition, and the conception of his exposition weakens to a degree of weakness from his limitation. The conception of the Qur'an's exposition is manifold, manifold upon manifold, of its reports, and say: it is not less than its counterpart. End.

Al-Imam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Murrakushi al-Akmah said in his commentary on his versification of *Misbah* of Ibn Malik on the sciences of ma'ani (semantics) and bayan (rhetoric), [p-183] what is suitable to be a base text and a sentence, and what precedes it as an explanation and elaboration. He said: The miraculous aspect of the Qur'an is known through reflection on the science of bayan (the science of rhetoric), which, as a group has chosen to define it, is that by which one is protected from error in conveying meaning and from its obscurity, and by which are known the aspects of beautifying speech after observing its application to the requirement of the situation. This is because the aspect of its inimitability is not its individual words, for otherwise they would have been miraculous before its revelation; nor is it merely their composition, for otherwise every composition would be miraculous; nor is it their i'rab (grammatical inflection), for otherwise every inflected speech would be miraculous; nor is it merely its uslub (style), for otherwise beginning with the style of poetry would be miraculous, and the babbling of Musaylima would be miraculous (uslub being the manner or method). Moreover, inimitability exists without that style, as in ﴿When they despaired of him, they withdrew to consult privately﴾ [Yusuf: 80] and ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾ [al-Hijr: 94]. Nor is it by diverting people from opposing it, for their wonder was at its eloquence. Moreover, Musaylima, Ibn al-Muqaffa', al-Ma'arri and others attempted it, but they produced only what the ears reject [p-184] and what human natures recoil from, and what is mocked in the circumstances of its composition and disgraced by those circumstances. It defeated the eloquent and silenced the articulate. So upon its inimitability there is a general proof, which is that the Arabs were unable to produce its like, though it is in their own tongue, so others are even less able. And there is a detailed proof, whose premise is reflection upon the distinctive properties of its composition, and whose conclusion is the knowledge that it is a revelation from the One who encompasses everything in knowledge. End. What will benefit here will come, God willing, at the end of al-'Ankabut. In His threat, He alluded with His words: ﴿Then fear the Fire﴾. So said al-Harrali. It is a subtle substance which, because of its extreme subtlety, is excessive in burning those who are frozen by intense heat, and in freezing those who enjoy intense cold. [p-185] Others said: it is a subtle, luminous, hot body whose nature is to burn. ﴿Whose fuel is﴾, that is, that which is kindled and set aflame by it, ﴿men and stones﴾, which are more general than their idols with which they associated themselves in this world, [implying] that they were unable to oppose it and persisted in denial. They were obstinate, and whoever is obstinate deserves the Fire. [It also implies] that when they are burned therein, it is kindled against them with their idols, as an allusion that these, although in this world they neither harm nor benefit by reason of their own essence, in the Hereafter are a harm to them with no benefit, neither by intercession nor otherwise. The definiteness of "the Fire" and the relative clause are because the reports of the Qur'an, after it is established that it is from God, are known and definitively certain. Thus this is of the category of treating the ignorant as if he were knowing, as a warning that what he is ignorant of, no one is ignorant of.

[p-186] Al-Harrali said: "Stones" (al-hijarah) are that which has become hardened, that is, whose parts have become firmly compacted from water and earth. "And guard yourselves" [wa-ttaqu] means: stop this distinction between God and His Messenger, where you submit to His lordship but doubt His Messenger. The Fire is prepared for punishment by the most severe separation, against the most subtle parts, which is the meaning of burning, for those who separated and severed what ought to be joined. That is, since you missed taqwa (piety/God-consciousness) through the motive of knowledge, let not taqwa escape you through the driving of the specific painful punishment appropriate to your deeds. For it is a fire whose nourishment and kindling is by the entire created order, whatever its kind, and its people are those compatible with its fire by its variety, its rarity, and its solidity, which are the stones. Thus there are nine categories between these, by way of a fortiori reasoning. In this [p-187] is an indication of its might and its strength, and that by this capacity it is ready to cling to a creation, meaning [people]. It is not like the fire of this world, whose nourishment is from weak sources, namely plants, and which acts on both ends only through an intermediary. Its nourishment and fuel was plants, since it was kindled from them, as He said: ﴿He who made for you fire from the green tree﴾ [Ya-Sin: 80]. The Arabs say: "There is fire in every tree," and al-Markh and al-'Affar were rubbed for fire. This is according to the principle that the nourishment of a thing is from that from which its origin of existence comes. He said "its fuel" because fire's action is most intense on its fuel, since through it it acts upon what is other than it. So when its fuel is that which it burns, it acts most intensely upon it, as it strengthens itself against it. Its consideration [in the Hereafter] by the fire of this world [p-188] implies the kindling of it from the deeds of those who are recompensed by it, and from their nature, since they are created from it and nourished by it, except that it is extinguished outwardly in this world and blazing on the Day of Recompense. The likeness of every person recompensed by it is according to the measure of what in his nature is from its substance.

I say: It is supported by ﴿Indeed the squanderers were brothers of the devils﴾ [al-Isra': 27], that is, in that the predominant element in them is the destructive fiery element, as He said: ﴿Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?﴾ [Maryam: 83]. He said: In the mention of stones is an indication of the generality of resurrection and recompense to what the heaven and earth contain, and that every thing, not the two weights (humans and jinn) alone, is included in the division between Paradise and Hell, just as it is included in the division between the wicked and the good. But in the basic creed of faith, he limited himself to belief in the resurrection of the two weights and their recompense, for ease and as an opening. Whatever is beyond that is from the increase of faith and its completion, as He said: ﴿That they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾ [al-Fath: 4]. Among the scholars are those who restricted their faith to the resurrection of the two weights and their recompense, to the point that some of them deny the recompense of anything other than these two, and strain to interpret such as the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Retribution will be exacted for the hornless sheep from the horned sheep." End.

When that was complete, and since "people" (al-nas) is general, including the disbeliever and others, it was as if it were said: For whom is this Fire? So it was said: ﴿is prepared﴾, that is, readied and completed before the time of its use [p-189], and it is in the passive voice because the one who inflicts the harm, when unknown, is more terrifying. ﴿for the disbelievers﴾. Thus it was clarified that it exists, readied for them and for everyone who is described by their description, which is concealing the signs of God that have become manifest. Al-Harrali said: It is the promise of the King, the Judge, to them, like the sword of a king among the kings of this world. End.

[p. 190] When he had mentioned their state as a warning, he followed it with what is for the believers as encouragement. So He said, turning the address of mercy toward the Prophet of mercy (ﷺ), and joining it to what its implied sense is: "So warn them of that." But He left that out, because the context is one of tenderness: ﴿And give good news﴾. Al-Harrālī said: al-bushrā (good news) is the manifestation of the unseen joy through speech. ﴿to those who believe﴾, that is, who affirmed the messengers, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾. Al-Harrālī said: ʿamal (deed) is an act built upon knowledge or upon the assumption of it. ﴿righteous﴾ refers to words and actions. Al-Harrālī said: it is the plural of ṣāliḥa, which is the deed that is guarded against the entrances of defect. If good news is for these, then the believers are more deserving of what is above good news. Good news is given only to one who is in danger, and the believer is at peace, so how much more so is what lies beyond that of the rank of excellence, of what no eye has seen and no ear has heard, and what no soul's knowledge reaches and no human heart has imagined.

When he had mentioned the one given good news, he followed it with the thing announced: ﴿that for them are gardens﴾, that is, many. Al-Harrālī said: because of the multiplicity of the ranks of their deeds, to which the reward corresponds in its gradation and multiplicity, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the woman who asked about her son: "They are gardens, and your son has attained al-Firdaws al-Aʿlā (the highest paradise)." In the expression "for them" there is an indication that what is for them should join their very selves, so that through it there is obtained, from the perfection of their affair and the soundness of their state, something like what is obtained through the perfection of their creation and proportioning. The gardens are delights for the souls, gathering the pleasures of all their senses; they conceal (tujinnu) the one who moves within them, that is, they hide him, and they conceal behind their bliss an enduring increase. End of quotation.

Then He described them: ﴿flowing﴾. Al-Harrālī said: from jarī, which is the swift and continuous motion of a thing,

﴿beneath them﴾, that is, beneath their chambers. Taḥt is what is below the level,

﴿the rivers﴾, the plural of nahr, which is the wide course for water. End of quotation. The attribution of flowing to them is a figurative usage (majāz). The definiteness is for what the hearer already knows of the kind. It may be that the meaning is: their ground is the source of the rivers, so beneath every tree and chamber is a source of a river, and they are ever fresh and flourishing, with blossom and fruit continuously joined, not like water that is brought to them, which may sometimes be cut off, so that some part of their affair is disturbed. Al-Harrālī said: when the state of the doer is known from the description of his reward, it becomes clear that their deeds were founded on sincerity, which is the portion of the doers from the generation whose sign is water. End of quotation.

Since the gardens are known for their fruits, He brought their description in that manner, as something beyond doubt, unlike the flowing of the rivers. So He said: ﴿Whenever﴾, a word that conveys the recurrence of the matter across all times, ﴿they are provided with fruit from them﴾, whatever fruit it was, as provision, ﴿they say﴾, because it is in the form of what is in this world, ﴿This is what we were provided with before﴾, that is, in the world. Since the provision was known and no purpose depended on knowing who brings the provision, the verb was put in the passive, so He said, the Exalted, joining it to what its implied sense is: because We created it in the form of what was before, so that they would rejoice in it more, know its distinction more, be more inclined to it and more drawn to it, ﴿and they are given it﴾, that is, this kind of provision is brought to them in the two abodes, in Paradise, without seeking and longing, ﴿similar﴾ in the general color and kind, so that it might be thought to be similar in taste, and then its excellence in that would become, through tasting, another blessing. The similarity intended here is a sharing in outward form. The use of the particle of repetition indicates that the resemblance grows greater each time, so the wonder increases. Al-Harrālī made this specific to the fruits of Paradise and said: "from before" is an announcement that the individual fruits of Paradise and their units do not differ, because they are at the highest form and do not vary between higher and lower, nor does the time of their return delay.
