So they replace what is plucked at the very moment of plucking, and the forms of what is picked do not differ from the successor, so that the picker thinks the replacement is the same as the first. Thus the state of the fruit of Paradise is like the state of water, which is its origin, and from the swiftness of the succession of the fruit of Paradise, and that it is a continuous flow of existence. The Prophet (ﷺ), peace be upon him, said about a cluster of its fruit: "If I took it, you would eat from it as long as the world endures." This suggests, when considering the deed in it, that their intentions in deeds are righteous, firm and steadfast, until they brought about this continuity and perfection of form in the provision. From this is the marfūʿ (traced to the Prophet) hadith related by al-Ṭabarānī from Sahl ibn Saʿd: "The intention of the believer is better than his deed."

﴿and they are given it similar﴾ explains their excuse in supposing the fruit to be one, and it informs of their safety from hardship, because if it varied, dislike of the lesser would follow and striving for the choice of the better would be required, and that is fitting only for the snares of this world, not for the bliss of Paradise. Some scholars have mentioned that this similarity is consistent in the fruit of Paradise even though its kinds differ, but this is weakened by what it entails of complete agreement in meaning and form, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿In them is fruit and palm trees and pomegranates﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 68] and what goes in its direction. End of quotation.

When He had mentioned the dwelling, which is the place of pleasure, and followed it with the food that is intended in itself, and the pleasure of the abode is not complete except through the companionship of a spouse, especially one who is enjoyed, He said: ﴿And for them therein﴾, that is, in addition to that, ﴿are spouses﴾. Since they are of one creation without defect, He indicated this by the singularity of the attribute, and confirmed that with the form taʿhīr (intensive form), indicating that they have been worked upon to the utmost, so that there is no hope for increase, and so He said: ﴿purified﴾. Al-Harrālī said: the zawj (spouse) is that without which the intended purpose of a thing is not completed except with it, in a certain kind of partnership and cooperation. Taṭhīr is the repeated removal of one blemish after another from a thing. When the Exalted mentioned the provision accrued from the deeds of those who believe, He joined to it the mention of the spouses accrued from the state of their souls, from the goodness of their characters and the beauty of their inner form in this world, and the woman is the spouse of the man, since his affair is not complete in offspring and tranquility without her. End of quotation.

Since fear of loss or of transfer to a lower state is troubling, and pleasure does not truly delight except with stability, and since this description is general across all the high and other gardens, He said, putting the prepositional phrase first to indicate that they will not be in any garden except that this is its attribute, and that their bliss has no end: ﴿And they therein﴾. Since the fronting of the adverbial phrase conveys the restriction of their being to it and not being in any other, and since that is the meaning of khulūd (abiding), which is sometimes applied to lasting a very long time even if it has an end, He clarified it so that the intended meaning is that which has no end, otherwise it would convey nothing new, and so He said: ﴿abiding﴾. Khulūd is a long stay with settled residence, and the context of favor is sufficient to dispense with restricting it by perpetuity and permanence.

[p-199] Since their inability to produce an equal to it established that this speech is the speech of Allah, glorified is He, it follows that the parables it contains are His sayings. In this Madinan surah He therefore threatened them for their obstinacy, and He followed this with the verse in which He reported that the fruits of this world and its spouses, though they resemble what is in Paradise in name and in some form, differ from it greatly in taste and purity and in what none knows in its true reality except Allah, the Exalted. Their likeness to it thus vanishes. The closing of the verse with "khalidun" (abiding) indicates that the parables which are the best of human speech, though they resemble His parables in name and in the permanence of their remembrance, bear no comparison to them, for reasons not hidden from the fair-minded. Only their objection remained: that because these parables concern lowly things, they are not fitting for His majesty. So He explained their excellence, the obligation to take account of them, and the value of reflecting upon them, by indicating that one should not be shy of coining them, since they are the truth. This is because all things, however great, are lowly in comparison to His majesty, His greatness and His perfection. Had He abandoned the use of parables for this reason, [p-199] that door, which is among the most wondrous of wonders, would have been closed. Therefore He, exalted is He, said, by way of inference from premises that are accepted, and He emphasised it, glorified is He, to repel the suspicion that He would abandon, because of what they used to confuse matters, the parables, which are the most revealing of things for forms and the clearest in all states.

Al-Harrali said: Since the call requires, along with the one who hesitates in it and the one who refuses it, an approximation to understanding through the coining of parables, and since this call comprises all calls, He connected to it this comprehensive verse establishing the proof through the coining of parables, and that this is of the truth, glorified is He: ﴿And Allah is not shy of the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53]. He thus concluded the mention of what the opening of the surah contained of the letters by which the Qur'an was revealed, with its seventh, which is the letter of the parable (mathal). He, exalted is He, also explained that the measure of wisdom which witnesses to the one who coins the parable lies in a gnat and in what is more apparent to the senses and more potent for knowledge. Attention should be paid to the rank (qadr), not to the measure (miqdar), and to the effect of the parable on the one it illustrates, whether small or great, near or high. Thus He, exalted is He, is far removed from what creatures find when there arises from their inner selves the illusion that they should reveal a matter, and then they imagine a deficiency in it, which turns them back from revealing it, whether by speech or deed. End of quotation.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing everything in majesty and greatness [p-201] and perfection, ﴿is not shy﴾, that is, He does not do what one who is shy does, which is to refrain from what he is shy of.

Al-Harrali said: Shyness (ḥayā') is the contraction of the self from its habit of expansion in the outward body, in confronting what it sees as deficient, where it finds it impossible to flee with the body. The word "an" (that), whose signification belongs to the one upon whom the reality of an inner state is brought, and whose knowledge is connected to what makes it apparent, Sibawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, regards as a noun, while most grammarians, because its meaning is inconsistent for them, regard it as a particle. ﴿yadrib﴾ (strike, coin) is from "daraba al-mathal" (he coined a parable), which is the effect of the parable upon what it illustrates, [p-202] because the basic sense of striking is the falling of one thing upon another. The meaning is that the striking should exist renewed and continuous, and this is not equivalent to saying "min darbihi mathalan" (from his coining a parable), for that applies to a single parable, past or future. The verification of this is that the verbal noun (maṣdar) refers only to the complete reality, without regard to time or anything else, whereas with a verb it is understood that the reality is brought about, also without regard to time. By understanding it with regard to time, along with renewal and continuity, and along with the complete reality and before its completion at the beginning of the act, and to this last qualification refers the statement of al-Harrali: shyness of coining a parable is shyness of its effect in the inner self, and shyness of striking the parable is shyness of making it apparent by speech. He thus negated the more eloquent principle, by negating which the negation of striking becomes more fitting. So let this meaning be reviewed alongside the repetition of the word "inna" (indeed), for it recurs often in the Qur'an and its meaning is weighty in its positions. What the grammarians say about the meaning of approximation (taqrib) proceeds [p-203] from neglecting attention to the position of its meaning: that "an" with the verb is in the sense of a verbal noun. What is required in i'rab (grammatical analysis) and bayan (clarification) is to make clear the ordering of their meanings. At this point "an" must be a noun, with the verb as its relative clause, like "man" and "ma." ﴿mathalan ma﴾ (a parable, whatever it may be): "mathal" is a matter apparent to the senses and the like, by which a hidden matter that corresponds to it is considered, so that its meaning is understood through that consideration. "Ma" in this position is for generality, so here it is for the inclusion of the lowest and the highest of parables. End of quotation.

Then He explained this by His saying: ﴿a gnat﴾.

Al-Harrali said: Since striking a parable involves a likeness and a thing illustrated, the striking falls upon both, so it is transitive to two objects: "mathalan ma" and "ba'udatan" (a gnat). The gnat (ba'ud) is a well-known genus of the smallest flying animals in size, and it has independence and complete creation, which the meaning of "ba'd" (part), from which its word derives, suggests, because in a part all the parts of the whole exist, [p-204] so it is, in that respect, a whole.

﴿So what is above it﴾, that is, of a meaning that would be more apparent than it. The "fa" (so) indicates a connection of some sort, either succession and attachment or causation. So here there is an indication of what is nearest to it in attachment and gradation up to the furthest extent. End of quotation. The meaning is that if that is considered in relation to Him, glorified is He, then He and you and others are of one rank in lowliness; and if it is considered in relation to you, the two groups are of one rank in that it is a lowly, weak, small creation of dust. As for the nobility of one part of it over another, that is only by Allah's honouring it; and had He willed, He would have reversed the situation.

Then He mentioned the condition of the two groups of believers and disbelievers, with the two sub-groups of each, in accepting His parables. He said, emphasising by the division, because the condition of each of the two groups is that of one who denies what happened to the other: ﴿As for﴾. Al-Harrali said: It is as though it were composed of "inna" [p-205], which indicates the inner reality of an essence, and "ma," which indicates an obscure outward, used for division. End of quotation.

﴿Those who believed﴾, that is, in what we mentioned at the beginning of the surah. Since "amma" includes the sense of a condition, as Sibawayh explained it, "whatever may be the case," it is answered with the "fa" in His saying: ﴿they will know that it﴾, that is, the striking of the parable, ﴿is the truth﴾, being ﴿from their Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to them in every kind of good, and that He did not intend for them anything but their nurture through goodness, by striking through the customs of His bounty. As for the parables of others, if there is no element of falsehood in them, there must still be a kind of indulgence, by which they are unworthy of the name of truth and not firmly rooted in it.

Al-Harrali said: Since those who believed are among those who hastened to respond, and since the striking of a parable is an emphasis of call and admonition for whoever has hesitated, those who believed attained insight by the light of faith in the striking of the parable, so they came to know the place of truth in it. And just as those who believed gained insight into it, its meaning became obscure to those who disbelieved, and they were ignorant of it [p-206], so they asked about it in the manner of one who denies its fitness. End of quotation. Therefore He said: ﴿And as for those who disbelieved﴾, that is, the open and the concealed among them, ﴿they say﴾, that is, in continuous speech, ﴿What﴾, that is, what ﴿did Allah intend﴾, who is the Most Majestic of the majestic, ﴿by this﴾, the lowly thing, that is, by His striking it ﴿as a parable﴾, that is, as a likeness, in mockery, ignorance, obstinacy and rudeness. Then He connected to that the mention of its fruit for both groups, as an answer to the question of the one who asked [p-207] among them. He said: ﴿By it He leads many astray﴾, that is, of them, by not making them understand the intended meaning, so that they entertain thereby the thoughts they entertain. Al-Harrali said: It was a misguiding of them, because in striking a parable with what precedes them, such as the fly and the spider, which they consider too trivial for a parable, there is a path for them to ignorance, so that was misguidance. He placed the answer "misguidance" first, because it is what the questioner deserves. And misguidance is the path that leads one off the straight and saving way. End of quotation.

﴿And by it He guides many﴾, that is, through the blessing of their belief in good and their submission to Him in the matter, their Lord guides them through their faith. He makes them understand the intended meaning and expands their breasts to what it contains of knowledge, so that it increases them in faith, tranquillity and certainty. The guided are many in reality, though few in comparison to the astray. And since the context is one of warning, as passed in His saying: ﴿So beware of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24], He was content, regarding the guided, with what preceded of their good tidings, and He spoke in condemnation of the other group and in warning against it: ﴿and He does not lead astray by it except﴾. Al-Harrali said: It is as though it were composed [p-208] of "in" and "la," whose signification is the negation of the reality of an essence from the judgement of what precedes it. End of quotation.

﴿the defiant ones (al-fasiqin)﴾, that is, those who go outside justice and goodness. Al-Harrali said: Those who went outside the encompassing of insight, the avenues of receiving the primordial nature, the binding covenant and good care, because defiance (fisq) is going outside an enclosure, like the husk for the fruit or the burrow for the mouse. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 27:

Then He described them by His saying: ﴿Those who break﴾, from al-naqd (breaking), which is the untying of the parts of a thing from one another, ﴿the covenant of Allah﴾, i.e., that which He took from them, given His greatness, through the intellects He placed in them and the proofs He set up for them. Al-'ahd (covenant) is a prior commitment regarding a matter, as said by al-Harrali.

(p-209) Since the intended covenant was a specific one, namely the sending of the Messengers, peace be upon them, He affirmed the report, saying: ﴿after its pledge﴾, i.e., through the indication of the Books upon the tongues of the Messengers, together with its nearness to the innate nature (fitar) and its facilitation for reflection. Al-wathaq is the intensity of binding and the strength of that by which something is bound, as said by al-Harrali. ﴿And they sever what Allah has commanded﴾, i.e., the Most Great King. Since explanation after generality is more delightful to the soul, He said: "with it" (bihi), then explained it by His saying: ﴿that it be joined﴾, i.e., of goodness. Al-Harrali said: qat' (severing) is separation within a single thing, and wasl (joining) is becoming one thing together with what completes it, with the completed, as is observed in the conveying of water and the like. It is an informing that they sever the connected nature of the innate disposition and the like, so they fall away from its level, while Allah has commanded that it be joined with increasing knowledge connected to it, until its growth reaches its most complete end. Likewise is their state in every matter (p-210) that must be joined: they come, in what is required to be complete, with the opposite of the complete, the deficient. End.

﴿And they cause corruption﴾. Since He restricted the verb to make it more general, He said: ﴿in the earth﴾, i.e., by deviating from the path of truth. Al-Harrali said: Since the earth is laid out for growth from it and in it, and as the place where the general forms of corporeal, lasting shapes appear, and the locus of the growth of the soul's form through deeds and character, and since corruption is the breaking of forms, as He, exalted, said: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the earth to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and progeny, and Allah does not like corruption﴾ [al-Baqarah: 205], their action in it was of the same kind as placing the evil opposite in the position of its more complete opposite, and falling short in what is meant for completion, so it was corruption of that. End.

Since it was as if it were said: "The conduct of these people is extremely ugly, so what is their state?" He said: ﴿Those are﴾, i.e., the far removed from righteousness, ﴿they are the losers﴾, i.e., those for whom loss has been confined to themselves. Khusran (loss) is deficiency in what is meant for increase, as said by al-Harrali. It is known that this is the result of the attributes previously mentioned. Al-Harrali said: Since the loser is one who has capital prepared for growth and increase, and his deficiency comes from poor management, and since their affair in the three successive states was the state of one who diminishes what is meant for growth, they were thereby losers; for this reason the verse ends with this. They were indicated by the distal demonstrative to place them at the furthest positions from the locus of good. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 28:

When Allah, glory be to Him, called to tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) and pointed to it, warned those who turned away, gave good news to those who turned toward Him, and mentioned the condition of the two groups in their acceptance of the proofs, whose essence is the parables and whose refusal is their rejection, He turned to rebuking the Manager (of affairs) so that he might gain insight. Allah, glory be to Him, continued with the proofs of tawhid until they stood like banners and pierced like arrows, until they penetrated the marrow of the bones. They have become manifest, so none is hidden from anyone except a blind person who cannot see the moon, in a style that alludes to the Resurrection and alerts to escaping loss. How excellent is the opening of this after "the losers," with His saying, in the manner of a turning of one who is angered, who beseeches compassion, and who is amazed! ﴿How﴾ (p-213). Al-Harali said: When the call was made to the people, one hastened to respond, another hesitated, and parables were struck, so one recovered and believed, while another persisted in his disbelief. He turned the direction of address away from direct confrontation with the Truth, may He be exalted, and spoke through the tongue of baseness and denial. So this interrogative comes to clarify the severing of excuse for persisting in disbelief. It came with the word "how" because their vision is confined to sensible modes, for "how" (kayf) is a word whose meaning is an inquiry about the general states that are perceived by the senses. It is as if it is said to them by one who perceives: "By what sense have you persisted in disbelief in Allah?", as required by the form of the verb in the continuous present in ﴿you disbelieve﴾. End.

He said: "In Allah" means together with the manifestation of His greatness and exaltedness. The denial that necessitates the negation of what is denied, as in your saying: "Would you fly without wings?", indicates that disbelief should have been among the impossible, because of the proofs that refute it and establish tawhid, which are beyond counting. Denying its condition is denying its existence by way of demonstration, for if it is impossible for it to exist in any state (p-214) of its states, then its existence is impossible absolutely.

Al-Harali said: This address has been made remote from ease by mentioning the name "Allah," because they were not among those who accept descent by claiming the name of Lordship, since they were not among those who responded promptly or followed, as the verse on the confirmation of the striking of parables indicates. When this address came with the mention of the name Allah, it was followed by mention of the divine acts, which are the ends of death and of life, the well-known two, whose matter the disbelievers do not deny. End.

﴿And you were﴾, meaning, while the state is that you know that you were ﴿dead﴾, rather lifeless, dust, then drops of semen. Al-Harali said: From death, which is a state of concealment and hiddenness, attributed to the manifest world that precedes or follows it, in which are observed the manifest qualities of that manifestation. End. Applying the word death to what has not been touched by life is a metaphor, and the secret of expressing it with that word is to alert that the return which they deny is most like the beginning, so there is no basis at all for denying it while acknowledging the beginning. How much more so, when the return is less than that. ﴿Then He gave you life﴾, so you became possessors of sense, strength and intellect. Al-Harali said: (p-215) He used the "fa" (then/so), which indicates immediate succession, because they had no knowledge of the interval of death that precedes birth-life. Life is the perfection of a being whose lowest degree is the life of plants, by growth and movement, up to the life of what crawls by its motion and sense, up to the ultimate life of a human in his disposition and management, and beyond that is further perfection. End.

﴿Then He causes you to die﴾, after lengthening lifespans and turning through stages. So when you are bodies like pottery, as though life had never dwelt in them for a moment, and after your intimacy with them they are replaced by estrangement, and after love of nearness to you, by aversion. The illustration of death with what we know: just as the summons of a king produces terror that nearly destroys, and sometimes destroys, so the summons of the King of kings is bound to produce death. Al-Harali said: These three states, namely death, which is expressed by non-existence, then life, then death, are known to them, and they cannot deny them. When they admit to a life after death, they are obliged to admit to another life after death, by the necessity of judging the validity of the existence of what has previously had a like. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth (p-216) able to create their likeness?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. From this knowledge it follows that death and life are paired and mutually implicating. When the first death is followed by its life, then the second death must also be followed by its life, for if there were no receiving of life, it would not be death but rather nullity, loss and dissolution. For the reality of death is a state of hiddenness, before which is manifestation, while life is a fixed end, and death is the beginning of a passing hiddenness. So the whole genus of death is ending and terminus, and life is firm and everlasting. This is why what is authentically reported from him, upon him be prayer and peace, is that death will be slaughtered, which informs that its genus has ended and life is permanent. Hence it is mentioned first and followed by life, where the article "al" in the saying ﴿He created death and life﴾ [al-Mulk: 2] (p-217) encompasses both, and the address stands on the affirmation of life and perfection, as was reported from him, (ﷺ), in his saying: "The bliss of Paradise has no end." Thus it is required, by the apparent sense that the disbelievers perceived and the inner sense that this kind of knowledge implies, beyond it, the spreading of a second life after the death of this world. End.

Since the proofs for the Resurrection and the Gathering are such that they render them like the perceptible, he counted them within the domain of what is known to them, like the first giving of life and death. So He said: ﴿Then He will give you life﴾, so He will raise you after your being folded up, and resurrect you after your being held in the barzakh (intermediate realm), so you will be as you were the first time, possessors of ability to spread out by that same power by which He originated you and caused you to die (p-218). This does not negate that they have some perception in the barzakh apart from this complete form.

﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾, so He will gather you after a long standing for recompense of reward and punishment. In this, as al-Harali said: there is information that if they do not return to Allah, may He be exalted, by the call of knowledge in the world, then after an interval from the second life they will return to Him by compulsion, when they witness the severing of their means from those they had attached themselves to, and those they worshipped besides Allah will disown them. This interval came after the resurrection only because they still retain hope in their associates, when they call upon them and those do not respond. Then the severing of their means compels them to return to Allah, so they return by force and driving. Then He recompenses them for what they earned in their worldly life, as He, may He be exalted, said in an address encompassing all the people of recompense: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281]. This is the last address of turning toward them from the call of Allah to them and the tongue of rebuke against them. For this reason the verse ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281] was the last verse revealed in the Qur'an, because it is an end beyond which there is no word encompassing the people of recompense. And "al-raj'" (return) is the return of a thing, when its end is reached, to its beginning. End. (p-219)

When He, glorified is He, had summarized at the beginning of this verse their situation, its beginning, middle, and end, in the manner already mentioned, which alerts that disbelief should be among what is impossible given the overwhelming evidences it faces, He began to explain it in a way that calls them to Him by bestowing upon them kinds of favor, with a matter higher in conveying the intended meaning than what came before it, following the Qur'an's custom of ascending from the lofty to the loftier. So He, glorified is He, presented the origination of creation, which is among the greatest proofs of His oneness, in the manner of bestowing blessings upon His servants through the benefits they contain, so that it would call them to His monotheism for two reasons: that it indicates a sublime, effective greatness and perfect power, and that it is a kindness to His servants and gentleness toward them. Hearts are naturally inclined to love one who does good to them. So He said: ﴿He﴾. Al-Harrali (d. 637 AH, a Qur'an commentator) said: it is a word whose meaning is the Most High, the hidden essence of divinity, which sustains everything and is not manifest to anything. Its essence is forever hidden, and its outward manifestation is the manifest Names, from the height of the encompassing of the Name Allah down to the descent of the Name the King, and what lies between them of manifest Names. He then said: When the address concluded with mention of their being returned to Allah, and this was a specific address to one who persists in his disbelief, He followed, upon his turning away and retreat, with this decisive statement as a threat, cast upon their shoulders, and as a causation attached to them, extended for them like a rope let out for one who is to be pulled by it: either that gentle grace will overtake him and he will return willingly, or it will be applied to him by force when the span of his retreat ends. The closing of the verse of the call was thereby arranged in a manner resembling its beginning, except that this one is at the end of the cutting off between its two ends, while that one is in the clearest coherence. So in this verse they were removed to the utmost distance, by attributing the matter to a name which is the hidden one, the Name Allah, and by attributing to Him the creation of what was made for them on earth, which is the most evident thing to the senses. End of quotation.

﴿He who created for you﴾ religious and worldly benefit, out of kindness to you, ﴿all that is in the earth﴾. That is, after He had made them seven. Al-Harrali said: His saying ﴿all﴾ informs that the need of man is not met by one thing without another, but is met only by the totality of what is in the earth, such that if any part of it were lost, the rest would collapse. End of quotation. The verse is evidence that the basic principle regarding things is permissibility, so nothing is prohibited except by evidence.

Since the heaven is nobler in terms of the height that cannot be reached, the substance perfect in its construction, the beautiful adornment of its order, founded upon great benefits, and the abundance of its advantages and signs, He expressed its matter with ﴿then﴾, and said: ﴿Then He rose over the heaven﴾. That is, He honored that direction of height with its own direction, with its beauty, purity, and abundance of benefits. Then He linked His will and purpose to its ordering without the slightest turning or consideration toward anything else. He magnified its matter by mentioning it first in an ambiguous form and then explaining it, and by the singular form suitable for the direction of height, as an alert to its nobility, and by the collective noun suitable for multiplicity. For this reason He returned the pronoun in the plural. Thus the creation of the earth and its preparation for what is intended from it came before the creation of the heaven, and its spreading out came after the creation of the heaven. Moreover, ﴿then﴾ here expresses magnification, not sequence, so there is no difficulty. The earth is mentioned first here because it is more indicative, owing to its intense closeness and direct contact with us. Al-Harrali said: He raised the address by mentioning the rising toward the heaven, which is the place of fear for them, since the frightening things descend upon them from it. So it was said to them: this place of which you are afraid is the one He rose toward. The usage of the word "rising" in rank and station deserves its meaning more than its placement in place and visibility. In sum, the most worthy usage of speech is that it is a report about the First, the Real; then a report about what is in His command and dominion; then a report about what is in His possession and manifestation. Therefore, the true meaning of the word is not fit to be restricted to the perceptible things apparent in the kingdom, to the exclusion of the realities behind them from the world of dominion. What makes kingdom and dominion manifest is Allah's report about Himself, such as rising and the like, and this report about Himself is more truly real. Then the report about the soul, for example, and its rising over the body, then over the head, for example, and its rising over the trunk, does not merit that outward appearances be the true meanings of words over their inner realities; rather, the inner realities are more deserving of the application of words. By this, much confusion in the address is dispelled for those who limit the realities of words to their sensible forms. ﴿So He made them﴾ ﴿seven heavens﴾. Equalizing (taswiyah) means giving each part of a thing its due for the perfection of that thing's form. He gave each one of them its due. ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾ [Fussilat: 12]. End of quotation. He created all that is in them for you. So the verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are each omitted from one half and left implied by the other). It omitted first that the lands are seven, which is indicated by the second, and second that what is in the heaven is for us, which is indicated by the first. This is a rare and precious art, and I have compiled a good book on it, in which I mentioned its definition, its linguistic derivation, and the examples I recalled from the Mighty Book and the speech of the jurists, and I named it "Al-Idrak li-Fann al-Ihtibak."

Since the creation in this manner clearly indicates, by immediate perception, the most perfect power of its Maker, and since knowing that this structure rests upon knowledge requires reflection, He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾. That is, He is, over every thing, Powerful.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 30 (part 1 of 2):

When [God] mentioned the life and death that are witnessed, as a reminder of the power to do what He follows them with, namely resurrection, and then also indicated that power through the creation of this whole cosmos in this wondrous order, and concluded that by the attribute of knowledge, He mentioned the beginning of the creation of this human species, in which the attribute of knowledge is deposited, showing its excellence, with His words, exalted is He, [in a passage] coordinated with His words ﴿Worship your Lord﴾ [2:21] and explaining His words ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ [1:2], since from the beginning the return is known to one who reflects. Or it may be coordinated with something whose implied meaning is: "Recount this to them." That is because, when He, glorified is He, addressed them with this interrogative, which among its meanings is rebuke, mentioning the Greatest Name, which is the highest of names and the most hidden in unseen meaning, and the pronoun "He" is more hidden than it, and followed it with some of what they deny or are ignorant of, and indicated with His words "for you" by stating it where it is apparent to them and by omitting it where it is hidden from them, as He drew attention to in the *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are mentioned in one place and omitted in another), [He indicated] that He did not create this human species for annihilation but for permanence. By this He made clear that He created all [p. 227] that is in these existences for their sake. Some of it is provision for them, some of it is means to them, and some of it He caused to prostrate before their father, while they were in his loins, and He entrusted them with the guarding of their deeds, the distribution of their provisions, the breathing of their spirits, and other things of their nurture and reform. They were not fit to understand this address in its true understanding, receiving it directly from God, because of His exaltedness, glorified is He, and the exaltedness of this address through the hidden names and the meanings arranged by them that are suited to them, in exaltedness and unseenness. So He made known, glorified is He, by coordinating with "when" (*idh*) something not apparent, that it is coordinated with [p. 228] something like: "Recount to them, O Messenger, this," because none understands it in its true understanding from Us except you, and they are closer to understanding it from you. "And when" means: and recount what occurred when. This coordinated element was omitted because the one commanded to recount it may be [the subject of] denial, while the context is for conveying kindness and good tidings on his tongue, ﷺ, to win them to him and make him beloved to them. In omitting it and indicating it by the coordinating particle there is also an urging to reflect on what precedes it, as an alert to the greatness of its rank and the subtlety of its secrets. When the indication was known, but only to people of insight, He followed it with the story of Adam, peace be upon him, as clear evidence and a manifest example of the essence of what was intended by these sentences, of what He drew attention to by the coordinating particle: that the Adamic species is the primary object of this existence, and that it is not permissible in wisdom that it be left after its death without a revival by which it is returned to an abode in which no aspect of its affairs contains any flaw from anyone, and in which wisdom will be very manifest, with no concealment at all. Thus praise appears in its fullest manifestation. For this reason He mentioned the preference of Adam, peace be upon him, [p. 229] by knowledge, then by the prostration of the angels to him, then by settling him in the Garden, then by receiving the means of repentance when a lapse occurred.

Al-Bayhaqi related at the end of *al-Dala'il*, and al-Harith ibn Abi Usama, and al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak*, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from Abdullah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Indeed the most honoured of Allah's creation with Allah is Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ)." I said: "May Allah have mercy on you! Then where are the angels?" He looked at me, smiled, and said: "O my nephew! Do you know what the angels are? The angels are a creation like the creation of the earth, the creation of the heavens, the creation of the clouds, the creation of the mountains, the creation of the winds, and the rest of the creatures that do not disobey Allah in anything. And indeed the most honoured of creatures with Allah is Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ)."

Al-Bayhaqi said: "It is not a *mawquf* report (one ending at a Companion) but its ruling is that of a *marfu'* report (one traced to the Prophet, ﷺ)."

Al-Harali said: When Allah, exalted is He, made the light of the intellect a guide to the signs of what appears in the cosmos, and among creatures there were those guided by it and those who turned away from it, Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news to whoever was guided by the light of the intellect according to the requirements of the sensible signs, and that is the *hanifiyyah* (the pure monotheistic disposition) and the Abrahamic creed; and as warners to whoever turned away from that and was occupied by the desires of his worldly life. [p. 230] Therefore the address of the Book was arranged between what it addresses to the most exalted who are guided, and what it addresses to the lowest who turn away. Likewise the address varied between what it addresses to the guiding imams and those who follow them. The highest address was what turns toward the imam of the imams, the lord of lords, and the most favoured of Allah's creatures with Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ). Thus the first address was with ﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ [2:1] ﴿That is the Book﴾ [2:2], turning toward him and bestowing upon him from the First Reminder, as he, peace be upon him, said: "I was given al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran from the First Reminder." It is the first thing written when Allah was and nothing was with Him, and everything was written in the First Reminder. So Allah, mighty and majestic, addressed him with what is in the First Reminder and sent it down as a Qur'an, so that it would be the last of what is revealed, the seal, which is the first of the preceding Reminder, so that it would be the last-first in His Book as it is in its essence. Since the first address is from the highest address of Allah to Muhammad (ﷺ), there was included within it what is the lowest address of the verses of the call, as an alert to whoever turned away from being illumined by the light of the intellect, because of the correspondence of contrasts between the two extremes. Then the direction of the address returned to him (ﷺ) with what is an informing about the unseen past from the present time, concerning the beginning of God's consultation with His angels about the creation of Adam, so that this would be an encouragement for those given good tidings to ascend in the ranks toward completion, just as the verse of the call was an alert to those who turned away so that they would return to turning toward Him. The specific descent is only in the informing about the unseen of existence from His kingdom, and the unseen of Allah's past days and the awaited days of Allah to come. That is what pertains to those guided by the light of the intellect, so that they may rise from the level of faith to the rank of certainty. The alert and the revelation with what the guidance of the light of the intellect contains only come for the sake of those who turn away. Thus what the revelation included in this was four matters. The first: the alerting to the signs according to the requirements of Allah's names, from His name the King, to His name the Merciful, the Compassionate, to His name Lord of the worlds, to His name the Mighty, which is Allah. The second: the alerting to the unseen awaited to which creation is returning, as encouragement and warning. The third: the informing about the past command of Allah, gathering the aspirations to earnestness and diligence in the worship of Allah. The fourth: the enlightening about the inner realities of the present time, whose outward appearance is its informing. So the first revelation in this surah was the command of the first day of the remembrance of Allah, which is the writing of the requirement of knowledge and power in His division of His servants among believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites. Then He sent down the address to the verse of the call from behind the veil of concealment with the prior decree, so that He generalized it to people and alerted them [p. 232] to the signs of His lordship, as a revelation that Allah revealed from Himself to him. Then He coordinated upon that, as an informing about the beginning of the consultation about the creation of Adam, a coordination with that which its understanding of this clarity gives. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: "And when," for the *waw* (the coordinating particle) is a letter that joins what follows it with something before it, either explicitly in utterance or implicitly in meaning, and this only occurs for one whose address is elevated and who has no doubt about its conveying. *Idh* is a vague noun for what has passed of matter and time. *Qala* (said) is from speech, and speech is the manifesting of forms of words in arrangement, in the way that the sensible forms are brought together in composition. Speech is therefore what the heart witnesses by means of the ear, just as the sensible is what the heart witnesses by means of the eye and other faculties.

Then he said: When Allah, mighty and majestic, informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what is in the Reminder of the decree, which is the hidden treasure of the law, and arranged by it what He revealed of the call of creation to His rule, and that combined two ranks of command, He, exalted is He, arranged by that the sending down of the mention of one creation coordinated upon the mention of a creation of higher rank than it, whose relation to it is like the relation of the call to its hidden treasure. So He mentioned the creation of Adam as the apparent treasure of what is coordinated upon it, and that, and Allah knows best, is the mention of the creation of Muhammad (ﷺ), which is the hidden treasure of the creation of Adam. It was as if He, exalted is He, informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of the matter of his creation as the beginning of a secret revelation, and then declared, through what He coordinated upon it, [p. 233] the mention of the creation of Adam as an open revelation, so that the matter of the creation of Muhammad (ﷺ) would be understood by the elite, just as the matter of the creation of Adam was clear to the common people. The meaning understood was: "Recount, O Muhammad, when your creation was thus..." ﴿And when your Lord said﴾, that is, the one who is good to you by the mercy of His servants through you, who concealed you in the manifestation of the creation of Adam, ﴿to the angels﴾ what He sent down. The interpretation of "angels" according to the people of Arabic grammar is that it is the plural of *malak*, transposed from *ma'lak*, from *al-alk*, which is the message. In that case the *mim* is extra, and its pattern is *ma'afilah*. And *malak* is from *al-mulk*, which is the firm establishing of that from which the forming comes, as in "he kneaded (*malakat*) the dough," and its plural is *amlak*, in which the *mim* is original. So let the name *malā'ikah* be a comprehensive term combining both meanings, carved from both roots. Such is often found in names of beings that are comprehensive, like the word *insan* (human), in which it appears that it derives from both *al-uns* (intimacy) and *al-nisyan* (forgetfulness). This is a formation of words toward a purpose more eloquent and elevated than what the term specifically signifies as a single meaning. Speech therefore has two ranks: a general rank and a special rank, the latter being more eloquent and elevated in words and speech.

He said: And in it, that is, in this address, together with that, there is a drawing out of the inner states of people of discernment, that the attachment of their inner states to anyone other than Him, when He showed them His singling Himself out for their manifestation as a creation apart from His noble angels, [is forbidden], so that their hearts are not attached to anything other than Him among the chosen ones. How then of one who is in a place of distance and remoteness! This is a preparation for the abominable matter that befalls some of them of following the footsteps of Satan. That is because in every verse there is a meaning by which it is joined to what precedes it, and a meaning by which it is prepared for joining with what follows it. By this [p. 235] the joining of verses falls within the meaning of inimitability, which no creature can produce the like of, even if some of them were helpers to others.

*Inni* (indeed I): *inna* is a particle conveying emphasis arising from the essence of the one emphasizing and his knowledge, and the *ya'* is an exalted pronoun specific to the speaker who attributes things to himself.

﴿Placing in the earth﴾. Since Adam's vicegerency was complete in all the earth, through himself and through his offspring, He used the singular for it, although it is possible that it be intended as a collective noun, so He said: ﴿a khalifah (vicegerent)﴾. The *khalifah* is a being that stands by what the one who appointed him stands by, according to the rank of that vicegerent with respect to him. So he is the vicegerent of Allah in His existence, His kingdom and His dominion, and some of them are also vicegerents of others. Thus he is a vicegerent in both senses. End of quotation.

He, glorified is He, made this reminder occur in a context that calls to His worship and leads to His love, in that He conferred upon this Adamic species His blessings and His beneficence toward them [p. 236] before bringing them into existence. So He mentioned to them what He argued with His angels concerning them, and what He honoured their father Adam with, namely knowledge and the command to the angels brought near to prostrate to him, then what befell Iblis with him, though they were two of His servants. He accepted the repentance of Adam but did not accept the repentance of Iblis, despite Iblis's prior worship, but rather He made his expulsion obligatory and made his distance perpetual. Then He, exalted is He, said, relating the words of the angels as an answer to a questioner who seemed to ask what they said when He, glorified is He, informed them of that: ﴿They said﴾, seeking certainty about the wisdom in creating one from whom evil will proceed: ﴿Will You place in it﴾, that is, in the earth, ﴿one who will cause corruption in it﴾, that is, by kinds of sins, through the appetitive faculty.

﴿Wa-yasfiku﴾ (and [he] sheds) is from *al-safk* (shedding). Al-Harrali said: it is pouring out with force, ﴿al-dima'a﴾ (the blood), that is, without right, by the irascible faculty (*al-quwwa al-ghadabiyya*), because they are not protected from sin, and because they were created as hollow beings who cannot restrain themselves, and possessors of desires for which they are ruined. It is as if, when they saw the form of Adam, they perceived this in it. Had they asked about the benefits of his limbs and what was deposited in them of powers and meanings, the Exalted would have informed them of what they had perceived from him, namely that. Al-Harrali said: blood is the nearest provision of the body, the one protected within it. ﴿Wa-nahnu﴾ (while we), that is, while the state is that We are. This pronoun, as al-Harrali said, is the speaker's name that implies one who is under His command and does not oppose Him. ﴿Nusabbihu﴾ (we glorify) means we perform *tasbih* (glorification), that is, *tanzih* (declaring Him free of imperfection) for You and distancing You from what is unfitting for You, while being engaged in the glorification ﴿bi-hamdika﴾ (with Your praise). The sum is: we declare You free of attributes of deficiency while affirming for You attributes of perfection. The object is omitted for generality. Al-Harrali also said: *tasbih* is declaring the Truth, the Exalted, free of any apparent deficiency in creation or rank, and *hamd* (praise) of God is the evenness of His command in height and lowness, the erasure of blame from Him and of deficiency from Him, and that too is a glorification in the exaltedness of God's command. None glorified with praise except the people of praise, from Adam and Muhammad (ﷺ), so the end of the one who glorifies is praise, and praise is a glorification for the one whose end lies beyond that evenness. End of quote.

﴿Wa-nuqaddisu﴾ (and we sanctify) means we purify everything we are able to purify, from our own souls and others, ﴿laka﴾ (for You), that is, not for other than You, because of our being protected by You. Or the meaning is: we perform *taqdis* (sanctification), that is, purification, for You, in the sense that You are at the utmost of purity and exaltedness in every attribute. Al-Harrali said: *al-quds* is a lasting purity that no apparent impurity or hidden filth reaches, and the *lam* (in *laka*) indicates the reason for which that which is attributed was so. End of quote.

Since their perception included their attributing to themselves knowledge that produces goodness, and attributing to the vicegerent ignorance that produces evil, He, glorified be He, informed us, so that we would thank Him, that He disputed with His angels on our behalf. So He made clear to them that the matter is contrary to what they supposed, by His saying, as a resumption: ﴿Qala innI a'lamu ma la ta'lamun﴾ (He said: Indeed I know what you do not know). That is, of that and other things. Al-Harrali said: The Exalted informed of what He has imposed upon His creation of judgment by what is manifest and ruling upon what comes by what has passed. He reported about His angels that they passed judgment on the vicegerent on earth by the condition of those who preceded them on earth, the earlier jinn, of whom He left Azazil and others, so that it would be established that God's command is new, and that He is every day in a matter, not judging any future time by a ruling of what is in it, nor by what preceded it. End of quote. The more evident view (p-240) is what I have mentioned: that they only said that by perceiving, based on what appeared to them of his form and the like, from their knowledge that he combines in himself desire and intellect, and it is known that desire leads to corruption. The Glorified knew what was hidden from them, that He grants success to whoever of them He wills to act according to the requirement of intellect while the opponent of desire and passion remains, so he attains the utmost perfection, which is above the rank of one who acts according to the requirement of intellect without any opponent to it, and thus He manifests complete power. And God knows best.

Once He, glory be to Him, had informed the angels that the matter was contrary to what they had supposed, He began to establish the proof for it. He said, linking it by "wa-" (and) to His saying "He said" ("qala"): "﴿And He taught﴾," meaning, in order to establish the proof of that. Ta'lim (teaching) is the repetition of knowledge so that it becomes firmly fixed, because of the forgetfulness inherent in the nature of the one taught.

﴿Adam﴾: from adam, which comes from adim, meaning the skin of the earth, from which his body was made. The share of the earth's skin in him is his name, which the word Adam points to.

﴿the names﴾ (p-242) namely those belonging to things, ﴿all of them﴾. It is the plural of ism (name), which combines two derivations: from simah (mark) and from sumuw (elevation). In terms of the word, it is a mark (wasm), and in terms of its share of the thing's own essence, it is an elevation (sumuw). That elevation is the meaning signified by ism, which is the mark that is synonymous with tasmiya (naming). So said al-Harrali. He also said in a book of his on usul al-fiqh (principles of jurisprudence): "The term ism is applied to the word of naming, and it is applied to a share and portion of the essences of things. Those are what was presented to the angels. The name of naming is the means by which the named matches its known thing, the named thing which is the presented name. For Adam it is knowledge, and for the angels and whoever does not know the reality of the presented name it is tawqif (divine instruction) and information." End of quotation.

(p-243) Since the presentation to the angels was profound in its purpose, He indicated its magnitude by the particle of delay, so He said: ﴿Then He presented them﴾, namely the things. Al-Harrali said: He made them manifest from a side, which is the presentation and the direction, ﴿before the angels﴾, who had made that statement. Al-Harrali also said: When He, exalted is He, mentioned the angels' objection concerning the creation of this vicegerent, He mentioned His disclosing to them the wisdom of a lofty purpose, by which He elevated this vicegerent through His teaching him the realities of all the essences witnessed by them, despite their encompassing knowledge of God's dominion and kingdom through witnessing. He showed them the comprehensiveness of Adam's knowledge of what they had witnessed in form but had not witnessed in the reality of what its naming signifies. He taught him the wisdom of what lies between those names, which are a share of the essences, and their namings in speech, so that in his knowledge the creation of every thing in form and its command in word would be gathered, and his knowledge would be perfected in his heart by way of his hearing and seeing. He made him a vicegerent in the knowledge of what belongs to him of creation and command, and that was at the beginning of his existence. How then could one judge God's wisdom in what reaches, through the perfection of His creation, to the end of His command, to where the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) arrives, what is ambiguous in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He taught you what you did not know, and the grace of God upon you has been great﴾ [al-Nisa': 113]? Thus God, mighty and majestic, showed them by this the aspect of a vicegerency in knowledge and action in (p-244) naming, exalting him in their eyes. God, mighty and majestic, made them submissive and obedient, so they complied at once, by the excellence of Adam over all creation, and there became evident to them the knowledge that God elevates whomever He wills, by what He wills, of the vicegerency of His command and creation. Those names, which are shares of the forms of existing things, are the presented things, which the pronoun in His saying ﴿Then He presented them﴾ covers. He indicated them by "these" (hā'ulā') when the presentation was complete, and He applied the pronoun "them" (hum) to all of them, because those created things include rational beings and others. In truth, every created speaking being, when the Truth makes it speak, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Today We seal their mouths, and their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65]. Muteness and inanimateness are only relative to the differences between some creatures and others. End of quotation.

Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi said in Kitab al-Zina: "It is said that the word ism is derived from sumuw, which means height and elevation, and that the name was made a means of signalling the meaning of the name, because the meaning lies beneath the name (this is the statement of the grammarians). The mark (simah) indicates its bearer, because they are two letters, sin and mim: the sin is from sana' (radiance), and the mim is from majd (glory), which is the core of a thing. So it was called ism because it illuminates for you the core of a thing and translates its hidden essence. There is nothing except that God has marked it with a mark indicating what it contains of substance. So the names contain all knowledge of things, and God taught them to Adam and displayed his excellence over the angels, peace be upon them." End of quotation.

﴿He said﴾, challenging them: ﴿Inform Me﴾, that is, tell Me with a great and decisive information, ﴿of the names of these﴾, that is, of the existing things, by your own discernment (tafarrus) of them, ﴿if you are truthful﴾, that is, in what you discerned concerning the vicegerent and his offspring. Al-Harrali said: These names which correspond to naming, from the mark, and the first names are the shares of essences, whose possessor is the named. Nevertheless, between naming and name there is a relation, a wisdom-ordained connection between them according to the command of the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 32:

﴿They said﴾, disclaiming knowledge (p-246) ﴿"Glory be to You"﴾, meaning: we declare You far above any description, exalting You beyond attributing to You any deficiency in knowledge or in creating, and we disavow before You what our statement would entail of claiming knowledge for anyone other than You.

Al-Harrali (al-Harrālī) said: In this meaning is a display of their excellence, their submission, and their acquiescence, as a preface to what is connected to it of Iblis's refusal. End of quote. The gist is that this is an explicit declaration of God Most High's transcendence above deficiency, and an allusion to attributing it to themselves, as an apology from them for what they had fallen into. For this reason they said: ﴿"We have no knowledge"﴾, meaning none at all, ﴿"except what You have taught us"﴾. This is evidence that there is no path (p-247) to knowledge of any thing among things except through God's teaching. Al-Harrali said: as a refutation of the beginning of the matter for the One to whom the beginning belongs. For this reason it has been transmitted in the narration "Athara min 'ilm" (a remnant of knowledge): "Whoever does not seal his knowledge with ignorance does not know," and that ignorance is the disavowal of knowledge except what God has taught. End of quote.

Then they restricted it to Him by what they had negated of themselves, saying: ﴿"Indeed, You are"﴾, meaning You alone, ﴿"the All-Knowing"﴾, meaning the One who knows all known things, ﴿"the All-Wise"﴾, meaning that no corruption can enter Your creation in any way (p-248), so there is no objection at all. Al-Harrali said: an affirmation, a purification, and a sincere dedication of knowledge and wisdom to God alone, and that is among the highest forms of Islam, for it is the Islam of hearts, adorned by the Truth, glorified be He, with it. Knowledge and wisdom are the light of hearts by which they live, just as water is the sustenance of bodies by which they live; and wisdom is making a causal connection between two matters, in which an appearance of necessity from the antecedent and support from the consequent becomes apparent. End of quote. Its root in the language is prevention from corruption, and that is only achieved through complete knowledge.

فَلَمّا قالُوا ذَلِكَ، وأرادَ إشْهادَهم على فَضْلِ آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، اسْتَأْنَفَ في جَوابِ (p-٢٤٩) مَن كَأنَّهُ قالَ: ما قالَ لَهم عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ؟ قَوْلُهُ: "﴿قالَ﴾"، مُظْهِرًا لِفَضِيلَةِ العِلْمِ المُوجِبَةِ لِشَرَفِ العالِمِ: ﴿يا آدَمُ أنْبِئْهُمْ﴾، أي لِيَزْدادُوا بَصِيرَةً في أنَّ العالِمَ مَن عَلَّمْتُهُ، والسَّعِيدَ مَن أسْعَدْتُهُ، في أيِّ صُورَةٍ رَكَّبْتُهُ: ﴿بِأسْمائِهِمْ﴾، فَأنْبَأهم بِها. قالَ الحَرالِّيُّ: ولَمْ يَقُلْ: عَلِّمْهم، فَكانَ آدَمُ عَلِيمًا بِالأسْماءِ، وكانُوا هم مُخْبَرِينَ بِها لا مُعَلَّمِيها، لِأنَّهُ لا يَتَعَلَّمُها مِن آدَمَ إلّا مَن خَلْقُهُ مُحِيطٌ كَخَلْقِ آدَمَ، لِيَكُونَ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، ومِنهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ، فَإذا عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِمّا مِنهُ آنَسَ عِلْمَهُ عِنْدَهُ؛ فَلِذَلِكَ اخْتُصُّوا بِالإنْباءِ دُونَ التَّعْلِيمِ، فَلِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَ آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ بِما عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ وأظْهَرَ لَهُ عَلاماتِهِ في اسْتِبْصارِهِ (p-٢٥٠)، والشَّيْءُ اسْمانِ جامِعانِ: اسْمٌ يُبَصِّرُهُ مِن مَوْجُودِ الشَّيْءِ، واسْمٌ يُذَكِّرُهُ لِإبْداءِ مَعْنى ذَلِكَ الشَّيْءِ إلى غايَةِ حَقِيقَتِهِ، ولِكُلِّ اسْمٍ جامِعٍ عِنْدَهُ وُجُوهٌ مُتَعَدِّدَةٌ، يُحاذِي كُلَّ وجْهٍ مِنها بِتَسْمِيَةٍ تَخُصُّهُ، وبِحَسَبِ تِلْكَ الوُجُوهِ تَكَثَّرَتْ عِنْدَهُ الألْسِنَةُ، وتَكَثَّرَتِ الألْسُنُ الأعْجَمِيَّةُ، فَأفْصَحُها وأعْرَبُها الِاسْمُ الجامِعُ، وذَلِكَ الِاسْمُ هو العَرَبِيُّ الَّذِي بِهِ أنْزَلَ خاتَمَ الكُتُبِ عَلى خاتَمِ المُرْسَلِينَ، وأبْقى دائِمًا في مُخاطَبَةِ أهْلِ الجَنَّةِ، لِمُطابَقَةِ الخاتِمَةِ إحاطَةَ البادِئَةِ: ﴿حم﴾ [الزخرف: ١] ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ [الزخرف: ٢] ﴿إنّا جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكم تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [الزخرف: ٣] ﴿وإنَّهُ في أُمِّ الكِتابِ لَدَيْنا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [الزخرف: ٤]، وطابَقَ الخَتْمُ البَدْءَ إحاطَةً لِإحاطَةٍ. انْتَهى. وهَذا كَما كانَ ولَدُهُ مُحَمَّدٌ خاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ (ﷺ) يُكَلِّمُ كُلَّ إنْسانٍ بِلُغَتِهِ، مِن قَبائِلِ العَرَبِ ومِنَ العَجَمِ، بَلْ ومِنَ البَهائِمِ العُجْمِ، لَكانَ عِلْمُهُ لِبَعْضِ اللُّغاتِ مِن غَيْرِ مُخالَطَةٍ لِأهْلِها ولا إلْمامٍ بِلِسانِهِمْ (p-٢٥١) دَلِيلًا عَلى عِلْمِ سائِرِ اللُّغاتِ، لِأنَّهُ لا مُعَلِّمَ لَهُ إلّا العالِمُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ.

﴿فَلَمّا أنْبَأهُمْ﴾، أي أخْبَرَهم إخْبارًا عَظِيمًا يَأْخُذُ بِالأَلْبابِ. و"لَمّا" كَلِمَةٌ تُفْهِمُ وُجُوبَ أمْرٍ لِأمْرٍ في حِينٍ، فَتَجْمَعُ مَعْنى الشَّرْطِ والظَّرْفِ، قالَهُ الحَرالِّيُّ. ﴿بِأسْمائِهِمْ﴾ عَلى ما هي عَلَيْهِ.

قالَ الحَرالِّيُّ في التَّفْسِيرِ، وفي كِتابٍ لَهُ في أُصُولِ الفِقْهِ (usul al-fiqh، أي أصول الفقه، أي مبادئ الفقه الإسلامي): هَذِهِ التَّسْمِياتُ لَيْسَتِ الأسْماءَ الَّتِي هي مَوْجُودَةٌ مِنَ الذَّواتِ، لِأنَّ تِلْكَ لا يَنالُها إلّا العَلَمُ (p-٢٥٢) وشُهُودُ البَصِيرَةِ، وقَدْ جَرى ذَلِكَ في وِراثَةٍ في وَلَدِ آدَمَ، حَتّى كانَ رُؤْبَةُ وأبُوهُ العَجّاجُ يَرْتَجِلانِ اللُّغَةَ ارْتِجالًا، ويَتَعَلَّمُها مِنهم مَن سِواهم مِنَ العَرَبِ، لِأنَّ التَّسْمِيَةَ الَّتِي يَنالُها الإنْباءُ لِلِاسْمِ الَّذِي يَنالُهُ العِلْمُ كالمِثْلِ لَهُ، المُبْدِي لِصُورَةِ مَعْناهُ لِلْأُذُنِ، لِمُناسَبَةٍ ومُواصَلَةٍ بَيْنَ خُصُوصِ التَّسْمِيَةِ واسْمِها مِنَ الذّاتِ، فَيَعْلَمُ ما يُحاذِي الشَّيْءَ المُفْرَدَ مِن مُنْتَظِمِ الحُرُوفِ، كَما يَعْلَمُ الواصِفُ ما يُحاذِي الشَّيْءَ ويُحاكِيهِ مِن مُنْتَظِمِ الكَلِمِ، فَيُحاذِيهِ ويُحاكِيهِ الواصِفُ بِكَلامٍ، ويُحاذِيهِ ويُسَمِّيهِ المُسَمّى لَهُ بِكَلِمَةٍ واحِدَةٍ. وكَما أنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِكُلِّ أحَدٍ مِنَّةٌ أنْ يَصِفَ، فَكَذَلِكَ لَيْسَ لِكُلِّ أحَدٍ مِنَّةٌ أنْ يُسَمِّيَ، ومِنهُ ما يَجْرِي مِن أَلْسِنَةِ العامَّةِ مِنَ النَّبْزِ والأَلْقابِ. وقَدْ كانَ يَجِبُ الِاكْتِفاءُ بِما في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ مِنَ العِلْمِ بِبَدْءِ أمْرِ المُسَمَّياتِ، عَمّا وقَعَ فِيها مِنَ الِاخْتِلافِ بَيْنَ التَّوْقِيفِ (tawqif، أي التلقين الإلهي للأسماء) والاصْطِلاحِ (istilah، أي الاتفاق والتواضع)، فَقَدْ تَبَيَّنَ أنَّها عَنْ عِلْمٍ عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ آدَمَ، لا عَنْ تَوْقِيفٍ كَما هو عِنْدَ المَلائِكَةِ مِن آدَمَ، ولا عَنِ اصْطِلاحٍ كَما قِيلَ. انْتَهى.

(p-٢٥٣) ﴿قالَ﴾، أي اللَّهُ تَعالى، مُثْبِتًا مَدْخُولَ النَّفْيِ، كَما هو شَأْنُ هَمْزَةِ التَّقْرِيرِ: ﴿ألَمْ أقُلْ لَكُمْ﴾ يا مَلائِكَتِي! ولَمّا كانَ هَذا خَبَرًا جَسِيمًا، نَبَّهَ عَلى بُلُوغِهِ النِّهايَةَ في العَظَمَةِ، وأنَّهُ مِمّا يَسْتَغْرِبُهُ بَعْضُ الخَلْقِ، بِالتَّأْكِيدِ فَقالَ: ﴿إنِّي أعْلَمُ﴾ عِلْمًا مُسْتَمِرًّا لا انْقِضاءَ لَهُ ﴿غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾، فَمَن أرَدْتُ تَعْلِيمَهُ شَيْئًا مِن ذَلِكَ كانَ عالِمًا بِهِ، وأمّا غَيْرِي فَلا طَرِيقَ لَهُ إلى مَعْرِفَةِ المُسْتَقْبَلِ إلّا الفِراسَةُ، وقَدْ تُخْطِئُ. قالَ الحَرالِّيُّ: قَرَّرَهم حَتّى لا يَكُونَ لَهم ثانِيَةٌ، وأعْلَمَ بِذَلِكَ عِبادَهُ مِن وَلَدِ آدَمَ، حَتّى يَسْتَنُّوا بِحُكْمِ التَّسْلِيمِ لِلَّهِ فِيما يُبْدِيهِ مِن غَيْرِ تَعَرُّضٍ ولا اعْتِراضٍ، فَمِنهم مَن آمَنَ ومِنهم مَن كَفَرَ. انْتَهى.

(p-٢٥٤) ﴿وأعْلَمُ ما تُبْدُونَ﴾ في كُلِّ حِينٍ، ﴿وما كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ فِيما مَضى وفِيما يَأْتِي. قالَ الحَرالِّيُّ: وفي صِيغَةِ "تَكْتُمُونَ" مِنَ الدَّلالَةِ عَلى تَمادِي ذَلِكَ في كِيانِهِمْ، ما في صِيغَةِ "تُبْدُونَ" مِن تَمادِي بادي ذَلِكَ مِنهم. انْتَهى.

When Allah, glorified is He, informed us of this blessing bestowed upon our father, He added to it the favour of the angels' prostration before him while we were in his loins. He said, connecting it by the conjunction (ʿataf) to the first "idh" (when), and shifting from the third person to the first person, and then to the state of His being in the place of manifestation of greatness, to indicate that this is a decisive matter in which there is no room for reconsideration.

Al-Harrali said: When He, exalted is He, informed us of the matter of the angels' consultation, of their claim (to knowledge), and of their submission of the affair to Allah and to the one whom Allah taught, who is Adam, peace be upon him, He arranged along with it the report of their submission to Adam in action, just as they had submitted to him in knowledge, in perfection of their state in submission, both in knowledge and in deed. Then He said, exalted is He. End of quotation.

﴿وإذْ قُلْنا﴾ means: upon Our greatness, ﴿لِلْمَلائِكَةِ﴾ meaning those whom We honoured with nearness to Us, ﴿اسْجُدُوا لآدَمَ﴾ "Prostrate to Adam," Our servant, in acknowledgment of his excellence, since We preferred him.

Al-Harrali said: So He made him a gate to Him and a Kaʿba, which they venerate with His majesty, exalted is He, and a prayer niche (miḥrab) and a qibla. Their prostration to him is a prostration to Allah, facing Adam, just as Adam's prostration was facing the Kaʿba. Through this it became evident how wrong was Iblis's refusal to prostrate when he disagreed with them regarding the nature of their constitution, because the angels were created from light, and light is obedient and is not confined by any place, nor is it restricted to any direction; and because the jinn were created from fire, and fire is confined by a place and restricted to a direction, and does not turn away from it except by compulsion and force. So he did not descend from the rank of his standing in his nature before a creature of clay, since he did not perceive the encompassing of Adam's creation, as the angels had perceived it. End of quotation. So they hastened to comply, ﴿فَسَجَدُوا﴾ meaning all of them prostrated to him as Allah, exalted is He, commanded them, ﴿إلا إبْلِيسَ﴾ "except Iblis."

Al-Harrali said: It is from "ibla's" (being reduced to despair), which is the cutting off of the cause of hope, from which despair arises, by way of severing that cause. End of quotation.

It is as if it were said: What did he do? So it was said: ﴿أبى﴾ "he refused," from ibaʾ (refusal), which is abstaining from what it is due to respond to, as al-Harrali stated.

﴿واسْتَكْبَرَ﴾ "and he was arrogant" regarding prostrating to him, from istikbar (arrogance), which is seeking out pride. Pride is rejection of the truth and contempt for people and disdain of them. Its consequence is belittling others in one respect and perfecting oneself in that same respect, as al-Harrali stated. ﴿وكانَ﴾ "and he was," meaning in the origin of his nature, as what arrogance conveys of attributing to Us the abandonment of wisdom, either out of ignorance or injustice in Our command to him to prostrate to Adam, while in his assumption he was better than him. ﴿مِن﴾ "from" is a word conveying the derivation of a thing from that from which it was made, as al-Harrali stated.

﴿الكافِرِينَ﴾ "the disbelievers," meaning those whose wretchedness was foreknown to Us. Nothing new became known to Us through this, of what We had not known.

In the three verses, ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ﴾ [2:21], ﴿كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾ [2:28] and ﴿إذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ﴾ [38:71], there is also an indication of the difference in state in address by the attribute of lordship (rubūbiyya) with the sincere ones and with those beneath them, and in address by the attributes of His essence. That is because, when He, exalted is He, made clear that those who go astray in the goodness of His examples are the losers, He marvelled at the one who disbelieves in Him, indicating the intensity of His manifestation and the spread of His light in His examples and in all His sayings and deeds, and that witnessing Him in every consideration is clearer than the light of day, since there is nothing there except His essence, His acts and His attributes:

"And in everything there is for Him a sign indicating that He is One."

Manifesting Himself to them by the name of divinity (ulūhiyya) in His acts, which they behold and by which they know Him. So He said: ﴿كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وكُنْتُمْ أمْواتًا فَأحْياكُمْ﴾ "How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life" [2:28], up to His saying: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ لَكم ما في الأرْضِ جَمِيعًا﴾ "It is He who created for you all that is on the earth" [2:29], and He included within that the matter of resurrection with His saying ﴿ثُمَّ إلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ "then to Him you will be returned" [2:28], to alert to its sharing in the remaining manifestations of the verse, because of what He had previously presented as evidence for it through the bringing forth of fruits, when He made Himself known to them through the attribute of lordship, which looks toward compassion, bounty, nurturing and beneficence, as in such acts of His here that are apparent and His wondrous effects. So He said: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ "O mankind, worship your Lord who created you" [2:21], to the end of the verse. He concluded this verse with the attribute of all-encompassing knowledge, concerning what was established upon it of the proof within this marvel, indicating the proof for the perfection of the examples, and determining that whoever persists in disbelief after this clarification is within His sight and hearing in every state. When He finished addressing them with matters that are apparent according to the measure of their understanding and the extent of their knowledge, the address ascended to the rank of His Prophet, peace be upon him, to elevate the exposition to the unseen dialogue He had with His angels, so He said: ﴿وإذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ إنِّي جاعِلٌ﴾ "And when your Lord said to the angels, Indeed, I will make" [2:30], to the end of the verse. For every station there is a discourse, and for every addressee there is a limit of understanding and a state.

Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in al-Miftah: The seventh chapter: on the attribution of lordship and the description of divinity in the Qur'an. Know that lordship is the sustaining of the one who is nurtured in that for which he was created and for which he is intended. The lord of each thing sustains it according to what its existence has manifested. So the lord of the believer is his Lord, who nurtures him for faith; the lord of the disbeliever is his lord, who nurtures him for disbelief; the lord of Muhammad is his Lord, who nurtures him for praise: "My Lord has disciplined me, and He has perfected my discipline." The Lord of the worlds nurtures every world for what it was created for: ﴿أعْطى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدى﴾ "He gave everything its form, then guided it" [20:50]. So lordship has an explanation at every rank according to what the sign of its nurtured one has revealed. Whoever knows himself knows his Lord. ﴿سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلى﴾ "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High" [87:1]. ﴿فَأرادَ رَبُّكَ أنْ يَبْلُغا أشُدَّهُما ويَسْتَخْرِجا كَنْـزَهُما رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ "So your Lord wished that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord" [18:82]. ﴿اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ "Worship your Lord who created you" [2:21]. ﴿لَهم أجْرُهم عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ "For them is their reward with their Lord" [2:262].

He also said in the chapter that follows: The address of turning toward the Prophet ﷺ is the greatest understanding in the Qur'an: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ﴾ "Have you not considered your Lord, how He extends the shade?" [25:45], to the end of the verse, ﴿وهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِباسًا﴾ "And it is He who made the night a covering for you" [25:47], to the end of the verse. The difference between the two addresses corresponds to the difference between the addressees. Just as the stages of explanation become clear to the people of recognition according to the attribution of the Lord's name, so the aspects of the encompassing of explanation become verified for the people of understanding according to the descriptions and clarifications of the name of Allah: hidden in the manifest signs for the believer, a direct eye for the perfectly certain one, and a comprehensive encompassing from the beginning of permanence for the verifier who is the One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal. ﴿وكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ وأنْتُمْ تُتْلى عَلَيْكم آياتُ اللَّهِ وفِيكم رَسُولُهُ ومَن يَعْتَصِمْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ "And how can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has been guided to a straight path" [3:101]. ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ "Say: He is Allah, the One" [112:1]. Reflection upon the stages of explanation in the occurrences of this kind of address in the Qur'an is among the keys to understanding and the beginnings of increased knowledge. End of quotation.

Allah, glorified is He, has placed the mention of the beginning of creation in the order of its bringing into existence. Muslim in his Sahih and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan, in the book of Tafsir, narrated from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took my hand and said: "Allah created the clay on Saturday, and He created the mountains in it on Sunday, and He created the trees on Monday, and He created the disliked things on Tuesday, and He created light on Wednesday, and He dispersed the living creatures in it on Thursday, and He created Adam, peace be upon him, after the afternoon prayer on Friday, at the last of creation, at the last hour of the hours of Friday, between the afternoon and the night."

Al-Mizzi said in al-Atraf: Al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh: Some of them said: Abu Hurayra from Ka'b, and it is more correct. End of quotation.

As for what is said, that before Adam, peace be upon him, there were creatures on the earth who disobeyed, and that the angels, peace be upon them, measured Adam's state by theirs, this is a statement without basis. What this hadith of Muslim indicates, as you see, is that he was the first inhabitant of the earth. What appears from his name, beginning with the hamza which is the first of the letters, and ending with the mim which is the last of them and its seal, is that he was the first of its inhabitants in person, just as he is its last with his descendants, upon whom the Hour will arise.

I have seen in a translation of the Torah, which is its first part: "Allah created the very heaven and the very earth, and the darkness was there, and Allah said: Let there be light, and there was light. He wished to separate light from the gloom, so He called the light day and the gloom night. Then He said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, to separate water from water, and it was so. Allah created a firmament and separated by it the water beneath the firmament from the water above it, and Allah named the firmament heaven. Allah said: Let the waters beneath the heaven gather into one place, and let the dry land appear, and it was so, and Allah named the dry land earth, and He named the gatherings of the waters seas. He said: Let the earth bring forth the grass of the herb, yielding seed for its kind, and the trees bearing fruit, each bearing fruit for its kind, planted upon the earth. And the earth brought forth grass of the herb, yielding seed for its essence, and trees bearing fruit for its essence. Allah said: Let there be two lights in the firmament of heaven, to shine upon the earth, and to separate the day from the night, and to be for signs, seasons, days and years. Allah created two great lights: the greater light for the rule of the day and the lesser light for the rule of the night, and He created the stars. And there was evening and morning, the fourth day. Allah said: Let the waters bring forth abundantly the living creatures that have life, and let birds fly above the earth in the open firmament. It was so. And He created great sea monsters, and every living creature that moves, each according to its kind, and every winged bird according to its kind, and He blessed them and said: Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the waters of the seas, and let the birds multiply upon the earth. Allah said: Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds, cattle and beasts of the earth according to their kinds. It was so. Allah made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and the cattle according to their kinds, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their essences."

Then Allah wished to create a creature who would have dominion over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heaven, the cattle, and all the beasts, and over the creeping things that crawl upon the earth. So He created Adam in His image, male and female, and blessed them, and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply, and have dominion over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heaven, the cattle and all the beasts. And He said: Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed that is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree bearing fruit that is planted in it, to be food for you, and for all the beasts of the field, the birds of the heaven, and everything that creeps upon the earth in which there is a living soul. It was so. The heaven and the earth and all that is in them were completed on the sixth day. No grass of the earth had yet appeared upon it, because Allah had not yet sent rain upon the face of the earth, and there was no man yet to till the earth.
