A spring used to rise from the depths of Eden and water the whole face of the earth.

Then Allah, the LORD, formed Adam from the dust of the ground and breathed into his face the breath of life, and Adam became a living soul. The LORD God planted a garden in Eden from of old, and placed there Adam. And the LORD God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight and good for food, the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. A river went out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads. The name of the first is Pishon, which encompasses the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold, and the gold of that land is good; there is bdellium and the onyx stone. The name of the second river is Gihon, which encompasses the whole land of Cush. The name of the third is Hiddekel, which flows east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates. Then the LORD God commanded Adam, saying: Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat, but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 34 (part 2 of 3):

God said: It is not fitting for Adam to be alone, so let Us create for him a helper like him. So the Lord gathered from the earth all the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky, and brought them to Adam to see what he would name them. Whatever name Adam gave to every living soul, that became its name, and he named them all. Then God cast a deep sleep (sabat) upon Adam, and he slept. He took one of his ribs and replaced it with flesh, and God fashioned from the rib that He had taken from Adam a woman, and brought her to Adam. He said: "This one now is the one who has been joined to me! She is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh! Let her be called 'woman' (imra'a), for she was taken from man." For this reason a man leaves his father and mother and clings to his wife, and the two become one flesh. Both Adam and his wife were naked and were not ashamed.

The serpent was the most honored of all the beasts of the field. The serpent said to the woman: "Is it true that God said to you both: 'Do not eat from any tree of the Garden'?" The woman said: "We may eat from every fruit of the Garden, but as for the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the Garden, God has said to us: 'Do not eat from it, nor even touch it, lest you die.'" The serpent said: "You will not surely die, but God knows that on the day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil." The woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasant to the eye, and she took of its fruit and ate, and gave to her husband with her and he ate. Then their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, so they sewed together fig leaves and made themselves loincloths.

Then he (the narrator) mentioned that God, may He be exalted, asked him about that. Adam said: "The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me from the tree and I ate." God the Lord said to the woman: "What is this that you have done?" The woman said: "The serpent deceived me and I ate." He said to the serpent: "Cursed are you above all the beasts and all the livestock of the field; upon your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life. I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; her offspring shall bruise your head, and you shall strike at their heels!" To the woman he said: "I will greatly multiply your pains and your conceptions; in pain you shall bring forth children, and your desire shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you!" To Adam he said: "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, the ground is cursed because of you; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life. Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the herb of the field. By the sweat of your brow you shall eat your bread until you return to the ground from which you were taken, for you are dust and to dust you shall return."

Adam named his wife Hawwa' (Eve) because she was the mother of all the living. The Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skins and clothed them. He sent him out from the Garden of Eden to till the ground from which he was taken. God our Lord drove him out, and at the east of the Garden of Eden He stationed a cherub (malak min al-Karubiyyin) with a flaming sword in his hand, which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life. Then he said after that: "All the days of Adam's life were nine hundred and thirty years, and then he died, peace be upon him." This is the text of the Torah. The word karub, in the pattern of zabur, in the language of the Hebrews, means a small being (al-shakhs al-saghir). The Karubiyyun were the angels attributed to mixing with people through revelation, taken from the two cherubim (al-karubayn), the dual of karub, two figures in the tent of meeting (qubbat al-zaman) from between which the speech of God was heard, as will come shortly.

If someone denies citing the Torah or the Gospel, and is blind to the fact that the better approach in the matter of inquiry is to respond to a person with what he believes, I recite to him God's words, as evidence against the Jews' lies: "Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful" (Qur'an 3:93), and His words: "And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what is before it of the Book and as a watcher over it" (Qur'an 5:48), along with many similar verses. I also remind him of the Prophet ﷺ citing the Torah in the story of the adulterer, as will come in full, God willing, in Surat al-Ma'ida. Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "On the Day of Resurrection the earth will be one loaf of bread, a provision for the people of Paradise." A man from the Jews came and said: "May the Merciful bless you, O Abu al-Qasim! Shall I not tell you of the provision of the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Yes." He said: "The earth will be one [single] loaf of bread, as the Prophet ﷺ said." The Prophet ﷺ looked at us and then laughed until his back teeth showed. Similar to this is the hadith of the Jassasa and its like. This is in what our Book confirms.

As for what it neither confirms nor denies, al-Bukhari narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm." Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, and it has the same meaning as what is in the Sahih from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and interpret it in Arabic for the people of Islam, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do not believe the People of the Book nor disbelieve them, but say: "We believe in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you" (Qur'an 29:46).'" The indication of this regarding the sunnah of mentioning such matters is closer than any other indication, and therefore many of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, took from the People of the Book.

If one of the Shafi'is understands the prohibition of their imams on reading any of the ancient books, relying on the words of Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Rafi'i in his commentary: "The books of the Torah and the Gospel are among what is not permissible to benefit from, because they altered and changed them," and similarly said others among the companions (al-Ashab); it is said to him: this is restricted to what is known to have been altered, by evidence that everyone who said that gave the reason as "alteration," so the ruling revolves around it. The text of al-Shafi'i is clear on this. Al-Muzani said in his Mukhtasar, in the chapter on the general conduct of war (jami' al-siyar): "Whatever of their books (i.e., of the unbelievers) contains medicine or nothing objectionable is sold; and whatever contains shirk is nullified, and its containers may be benefited from." And in al-Umm, in the chapter on al-Waqidi's Siyar, in the section on his translation of the books of the non-Arabs, al-Shafi'i said: "Whatever of their books is found is entirely booty, and it is fitting for the imam to summon someone to translate it. If it is knowledge of medicine or other matters with nothing objectionable in it, he sells it as he sells the rest of the booty; and if it is a book of shirk, they split the book and benefit from its containers and its materials, and sell them. There is no basis for burning it or burying it before knowing what it is." End. So his words in al-Umm, "a book of shirk," imply that it is entirely shirk; and for this reason al-Muzani expressed it as "whatever contained shirk," meaning in its chapters and sections. Even clearer is their statement in the chapter on minor ritual impurity (al-ahdath) that its ruling regarding touching by one in a state of minor impurity is the ruling for what has had its recitation abrogated from the Qur'an, according to the more correct of the two opinions. The use of "more correct" according to their terminology indicates that the opinion holding the prohibition of touching and carrying them by one in a state of minor impurity is strong. Clearer still is what the author of the school, Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in questions he appended at the end of the chapter on minor impurity in his commentary on al-Muhadhdhab, and approved, that al-Mutawalli said: "If he thinks that there is in them something not altered, touching it is disliked." End. So the dislike of touching is out of reverence, and reverence is a branch of the permissibility of keeping and benefiting from reading them. Clearer than all of that is the statement of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him: "Whatever has nothing objectionable in it is sold." Likewise is the statement of al-Baghawi in his Tahdhib at the end of the chapter on ablution: "Likewise, if the one in major impurity (al-junub) speaks a word that matches the arrangement of the Qur'an, or recites a verse whose recitation has been abrogated, or recites the Torah and the Gospel, or mentions God, glorified is He, or invokes blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, it is permissible." 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The Prophet ﷺ used to mention Allah in all his states." It is not conceivable that what is permissible for one in major impurity would be impermissible for one in minor impurity; rather, whatever one in major impurity may recite without a compelling necessity, one in minor impurity may also, and not the reverse. His justification for this with the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, indicates that this refers to the remembrance of God, the Exalted, and the ruling cannot be taken as general, especially when one considers the statement of Qadi al-Husayn: that it is permissible to use both of them for istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself), because it is based on the view that all of them have been altered; and this is weak, or is to be understood as referring to the altered portions of them. For it is not hidden from anyone that a Muslim, let alone a scholar, would not say that one may cleanse oneself with something like His words in the Ten Words with which the Tablets began: God said, all these verses: "I am the Lord your God who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, out of bondage and slavery. You shall have no other gods before Me. You shall not make for yourself any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above or that is in the earth beneath or that is in the water under the earth. You shall not bow down to them or worship them, for I the Lord your God am a jealous God. You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not hold guiltless anyone who takes His name in vain. Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God is giving you. You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor."

Our shaykh, the hafiz of his age, Abu al-Fadl ibn Hajar, has fully expounded the matter at the end of his commentary on al-Bukhari. The final point he settled on is the distinction between one whose foot is firmly planted in the religious sciences, for whom it is permissible to consider these matters, since he can extract from them what the guided benefit from, and others, for whom it is not permissible. He supported this with the practice of the imams regarding both in former and recent times, and with refuting the People of the Two Books by what they extract from them; for were it not permissible, they would not have undertaken it. And God is the one who grants success. I have written about the matter in the section on the raised (marfu') hadith in my glosses on the commentary of Shaykh Zayn al-Din al-Iraqi on his Alfiyya, so consult it if you wish. And God is the guide. Then I composed on this a good treatise which I named "al-Aqwal al-Qawima fi Hukm al-Naql min al-Kutub al-Qadima" (The Upright Statements on the Ruling on Transmitting from Ancient Books).

Notice: Know that the Torah exists in three versions, differing in wording but close in meaning, except for a few points. The first is called the Torah of the Seventy (Septuagint), which was agreed upon by seventy-two of their rabbis. The story is that one of the Greek kings of Egypt asked one of the kings of the Jews in Jerusalem to send him a number of those who had memorized the Torah, so he sent him seventy-two rabbis. He housed every two of them in a separate house and appointed scribes and translators for them, and they wrote the Torah in the Greek language. Then he compared their six and thirty copies, and they differed in wording but agreed in meaning, so he knew that they had been truthful and sincere. This version was later translated into Syriac, then into Arabic, and it is in the hands of the Christians. The second version is the copy of the Jews, of the Rabbanites and the Karaites. The third version is the copy of the Samaritans. Imam al-Samarqandi drew attention to something similar in al-Sahaif, and cited many texts of the Torah in support of many issues of the principles of religion; likewise Shaykh Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani in his commentary on al-Maqasid, Qadi 'Iyad in his book al-Shifa', and others.

Then know that most of what I have cited in this book comes from a copy that came into my hands. I did not know the name of its translator. In the margins of its sections are the times at which they are read. The apparent conclusion is that it is a Jewish copy, and it is very old. On the first leaf of it, there was erasure at the edges of the lines, so I completed it from the Septuagint copy. Then I compared my entire copy with some of the Rabbanite Jews, using the translation of Sa'id al-Fayyumi, which they consider the best of translations, if he were the reader. I found my copy closer to the actual meanings of the Hebrew wording, and its translator more competent than Sa'id in the Arabic language. This is what I have. The apparent sense of the Qur'an, in His saying, ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him﴾ [al-Hijr: 29], is that the command to prostrate to him came before the completion of his creation, and that the prostration came immediately after the breathing. Al-Baghawi stated this explicitly in his tafsir (exegesis). He answered His saying in Surat al-A'raf, ﴿And We certainly created you and then fashioned you; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾ [al-A'raf: 11], with several answers. Among them: the creating and fashioning were for Adam alone, and He mentioned it with the plural pronoun because he is the father of humankind, so his creation is their creation and his fashioning is their fashioning. Among them also: "thumma" (then) here means "wa" (and), and does not indicate sequence. End of quotation. Fashioning (al-taswir) is the cutting of the hearing, the sight and the fingers, as stated by Yaman. Proportioning (al-taswiyah) is the balancing of the creation, its completion and its preparation for the breathing of the spirit. It is possible that "We created you" and what follows it mean "We decreed that, a decree close to bringing out from non-existence." By this, His saying in the Torah becomes clear: "He created Adam in His image, male and female," then he said after that, "For Adam had not yet been created," then he related his creation and the creation of his spouse from him. So this "creating" means bringing into existence, and that "decreeing" means a decree close to it, and the preparation for receiving the ends. And God knows best.

Al-Baydawi followed the view that the command to prostrate came after the announcement of the names, and he did not mention any evidence that turns away from this apparent sense. Still, following it is preferable in terms of meaning, because the prostration of the angels, peace be upon them, before that would be faith in the unseen according to the principle of legal obligations (taklif). But after the manifestation of the virtue of knowledge, the veil has been removed and the aspect of superiority has become a matter of the certainty of direct witnessing (ʿayn al-yaqin). As for the order of mention here in this manner, namely placing the prostration after the announcement, it is for a wonderful subtle point: since He, exalted is He, was explaining the blessings which necessitate thanking Him by singling Him out for worship, because He is the Bestower, He first explained His blessing upon every soul in its own particular case, by creating it and bestowing provision upon it.

Then He reminded them all of a blessing that encompasses them, namely His addressing their nearest creation to Himself at that time, our father Adam, before his creation. The wise method required that He clarify for them the proof of this vicegerent's excellence, so He mentioned the knowledge He had given him. When He had finished disputing with them in a way that compelled their submission, He reminded his descendants of the blessing of prostrating to him [p. 281]. Putting forward the manifestation of the excellence of knowledge was only to preserve the good order of the context in arranging the proof along the most upright path and the clearest way. When He had finished with the blessing of preference in essential attributes, He explained the blessing through the nobility of the dwelling, together with the subjugation of a spouse of the same kind for complete intimacy, and what follows from that. So He, exalted is He, said:

Al-Harali said: When Allah, glorified is He, manifested Adam's excellence in what He exalted him by among the angels, namely his knowledge, his vicegerency, the command to prostrate to him, and Iblis's refusal of it, Allah, exalted is He, then manifested what corresponds to Adam's states at the time when the angels became aware of him, with what he had in it of a share of disobedience, by which he participates in the excess of refusal found in Satan. [This is] because the creation of Adam encompasses the whole cosmos, high and low. And so that Adam's excellence would appear in his state of disobedience, in contrast to Iblis's state of refusal, through what appears in Adam of returning in repentance, like the angels' return in submission. Thus the union of the two extremes appears in him, and the excellence lies in both states: the state of his knowledge and the state of his repentance after his disobedience. So Allah, exalted is He, made the settling in the Garden a preparation (tawṭiʾa) for the manifestation of this matter. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We said: O Adam, dwell﴾. The word "sakan" comes from "sakan," which is calm in a thing within which there is disturbance. The "anta" in His words "anta" (you) is a proper name of the inner essence, the part shared in "ana" (I), "anta" (you, masculine), "anti" (you, feminine), and "an taf'ala kadhā" (that you do such-and-such). The alif in "ana" indicates the essence of the speaker, and in contrast to it the tā' indicates the essence of the one addressed, male or female. ﴿And your spouse, the Garden﴾. So she (Eve) concealed for Adam what was in it of hidden matter, drawing out the matter of his disobedience, so that this would be a preparation for the perfection of his inner self, by informing him of one of the secrets of his Lord in the knowledge of decree, as faith. Perfection in its outward aspect would be a preparation for the excellence of his repentance, as submission. There is no repentance for his descendants after sin, in opposition to Iblis's persistence after his refusal, and as a testimony against him for his ignorance in his claim. This was given to Adam in what descends from the rank of his knowledge, so no trial afflicted him in it, a protective guard over his vicegerency. His disobedience was lowered to the place of his eating, which is the particular state of a person in terms of the hollowness of his creation, so that the deficiency of the hollow would appear, and that would manifest the magnification of the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who feeds and is not fed. So that act of his was a glorification with the praise of his Lord. Allah does not decree for a believer a decree except that it is good for him. End of quotation.

Since the context here is merely to mention the blessings, to incline toward harmony, the conjunction of eating with the particle "wa" (and) in His words ﴿and eat from it﴾ was sufficient for that. And the explicit mention of "raghadan" (abundantly), which is among the greatest blessings, has a great position, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿raghadan﴾, that is, [p. 284] wide, comfortable, good, and pleasant. ﴿Wherever﴾, that is, in whatever place, ﴿you both wish﴾. This differs from the context of al-A'raf, where what was intended, along with reminding of the blessings, was to make known the increase of establishment and that it did not prevent the expulsion, as a warning to those established on the earth who expand in livelihoods against bringing down severe punishments and sending down calamities, as will come, Allah willing. Then the purpose of narrating the stories in the Qur'an is only the meanings. So variation in wording does no harm when it conveys all or part of the meaning and there is no contradiction, for the story at the time of its occurrence was in the fullest of the meanings reported. Then Allah, exalted is He, expresses to us in every surah in which the story is mentioned what suits that context in wording, expressing what befits the meanings, and leaves aside what that context does not require. I will explain what Allah makes me aware of in this regard in its places, Allah willing.

When He, glorified is He, permitted them all of that, He followed it with a prohibition against one tree. Al-Harali said: He granted him abundance without restriction, and He made the prohibition a conjunction rather than an exception, so that Adam would have a stronger excuse for forgetting, because the exception is more important in address than specification. He said: ﴿And do not approach﴾ and did not say "do not eat," forbidding its vicinity [p. 285], so that this would be stronger in the prohibition. End of quotation. "Hadhihi" (this): since the demonstrative has no indication of the essence of the thing, it required clarification of the identity of the thing indicated, so He said: ﴿the tree﴾. That is, if you approach it, you will eat from it, ﴿and thus you will be﴾, that is, by that, ﴿among the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who place a thing in other than its place, like one who walks in darkness [p. 286]. In this prohibition is evidence that this dwelling does not last, because one who is eternal is not suited to being exposed to restriction, by having something forbidden to him or being commanded and forbidden. For this reason Satan entered upon him through the matter of eternity. There is no need to explain the kind of tree, because the context is to explain the evil of disobedience and the blessing of repentance, not to specify what was forbidden. So explaining it at that point is not wise.

Then he explained that they hastened into intercourse, by the decree of their creation with natures inclined to desire, for what they had been forbidden. So He said: ﴿Then Satan caused them to slip from it﴾. Al-Harrali said: From zalal (slipping), which is the sliding of a thing that cannot hold firm on a thing that offers no hold, like the slipping of the zulal (drops of dew) from the leaves, which is what gathers from the dew so that it becomes what is on the leaves and flowers. And azalahuma is from zawal (removal), which is moving them away from a place or a position, namely causing them to go to one side of it. ﴿Satan﴾ is derived from two roots: from shatn (distance), from which the long rope is named, and from shayt (rapid burning and fattening). So it is derived from both meanings, like the words insan (human) and malaika (angels). ﴿From it﴾, meaning from intercourse with the tree. ʿAn (from) is a word that requires going beyond a fixed cause, as in their saying: "I shot from the bow." End of quotation.

Its verification: Satan thus caused their slip, or their removal from it, ﴿and so he brought them out﴾, meaning that as a consequence of causing them to slip into the lapse arising from that intercourse, he brought them out ﴿from what they were in﴾, from the great blessing that is too exalted to describe. Al-Harrali said: fi (in) is a word that requires the container of a place or a position. Then he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed of what was in the hidden matter of His command, which is beyond the knowledge of the angels concerning what He had manifested of the affair of Adam, peace be upon him, and beyond Adam's knowledge of what Satan revealed of his condition in causing Adam to slip, through Adam's good opinion of Allah's servants absolutely when Satan swore to them both that he was giving sincere advice. There is an order in this in some respect, through the angels' hesitation regarding the creation of Adam, so the angels warned to the utmost. There came from behind their caution a praise which Allah manifested from Adam, and there came from behind Adam's good opinion a sin which Allah manifested from Satan in the manner of the dwelling of the Garden, so He cast them both out of its dwelling by what He showed him of the love of the tree he had looked upon. Then he said: The wisdom in this, that is, attributing this sin to Satan through his causing it, is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives His servants good both through an intermediary and without one, and evil reaches them only through a self, as occurred with the refusal of Iblis. So his sin was either from his own self or through another devil, as Adam's disobedience was. His sin was not from his own self but an accident upon him from an enemy who caused him to slip from his closest refuge, through his spouse, who is the nearest of his creation. So repentance erased the accidental sin of Adam, and persistence established the self-born refusal of Satan. The Real, exalted is He, mentioned the slipping from him by his name Satan and not by his name Iblis, because of what is in the meaning of shaytana (being distant and swift) which accepts remedy, and because of what is in the meaning of iblas (despair) of cutting off hope. So in that there was a glad tiding of Adam's recovery through repentance. End of quotation.

When he had explained that He deceived them and harmed them, he distinguished between the descent of the deceiver and the deceived, and that He showed favour to the deceived rather than the deceiver, given what had preceded for him of persistence in worship and long perseverance in service. In this there is an amplification of the blessing, to incline toward sincerity in worship. So He said, linking to what the context guides to, such as saying: then We reconciled them with mercy and remedied their error with pardon, since it was an accident from them through an external cause, and We made the deceiver's remedy a perpetual wretchedness, since he disobeyed by misguidance and misleading deliberately, so he was one upon whom wrath is cast. ﴿And We said﴾, meaning to him and to the deceived: ﴿Go down﴾. In this there is a kindness to his offspring by deterring them from error, a severe warning against his crime, and a great encouragement, should they fall into it, toward repentance and descent.

Al-Harrali said: He strove toward a descent (daraka), and daraka is what comes down from a level. So He held fast their reality, that is Adam, within His enclosure, protection and granting of success for his supplication, his weeping, and the secret of the repentance deposited in him. And He caused his form to descend so that in this would appear the difference between Adam's descent and the descent of Iblis, according to what was shown of it: the speed of Adam's return in repentance and death to his place of familiar intimacy and his known closeness with his Lord, and the respite of Iblis on earth, persisting and cut off from the like of Adam's return, because of the curse which Iblis received, which is the opposite of repentance. ﴿Some of you to others﴾. The "some" is what is cut off from a whole and contains what that whole contains. ﴿Enemy﴾ is from ʿadaʾ (enmity), that is transgressing the bounds of the ruling of peaceful coexistence, which is the least of what is due between those who are independent in the right of mutual aid. End of quotation. So the meaning is: let each one of you beware of his enemy by following the commands and avoiding the prohibitions.

Al-Harrali said: In this is a notice of how the enmity of Satan has extended over a portion of Adam's offspring until they became of his party. In this also is a glad tiding for the righteous among Adam's offspring, that they will confront the portion of Iblis, so they will join them in faith, Islam and repentance, and be guided by his guidance from the point where enmity became general. The one of good intent transgresses, so his enmity against the people of evil becomes good; and the one of devilry transgresses, so his enmity against the people of good becomes evil.

﴿And for you on the earth there is a settlement﴾ in which you will dwell, from qarar (settling), which is a thing's being in that where it has growth, manifestation and agreeable living. ﴿And enjoyment﴾, which you will enjoy. Matāʿ (enjoyment) is benefiting from what is benefited from for a limited time, whose deficiency is recognized by what is better than it. That is, in it is a notice that the enjoyment in this world is cut off, and that what is benefited from is deficient compared with the place where they were. Since the word mutaʿ was used in the Arabic language for carrion, which is the provision of the one compelled and the sustenance of wild beasts and dogs, so too the world is a carcass with which those compelled by descent were given enjoyment, and He made it the portion of one who has no share in the Hereafter. ﴿Until a time﴾, meaning it will neither advance nor delay. In the indefiniteness of "time" is a notice of the difference of lifespans among the two groups: some of them reach the term young, and some of them reach it old. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 37:

(p-293) Since the consequence of Adam's punishment, peace be upon him, through the descent (al-ihbat), which was an expiation for him, was that he was inspired to make the supplication by which he was shown mercy, he expressed this by His saying: "﴿Then Adam received﴾," meaning: so they descended, and then "﴿Adam received﴾" after the descent. Talaqqi (receiving) is what the heart accepts inwardly as revelation, or what is like revelation, taken inwardly from the instruction (talaqqun) that one receives verbally and as outward knowledge, or what is like the outward. So said al-Harali: "﴿from his Lord﴾," that is, the One who is good to him in every state, "﴿words﴾," that is, words that please Him, the Glorified, by what the expression "receiving" conveys. Kalimat (word) is the plural kalimat, and it is a supplication that he made to his Lord, or a praise with which he praised Him. The word (kalimah) is also applied to the execution of God's command without (p-294) causing a wisdom or arranging a judgment, so said al-Harali. Then he said: The conjunction with "fa" (then) in this verse indicates what the receiving rested upon: the alerting of Adam's heart and his being granted success in what the keeping of his reality with his Lord had established for him. Its meaning is supported by the raising of the words and their receiving of Adam in one of the two readings. So it is as if he received the words with what was in his inner self, and the words received him with what they turned toward him, so he deserved them. Thus they were receiving him with what the two readings combined of meaning. "﴿So He turned in forgiveness﴾" (fataba), from tawb, which is a return with an outward aspect, whose inward aspect is inabah, and which is a return with knowledge, whose inward aspect is awbah, and which is a return with the piety of the heart. End of quotation.

"﴿Upon him﴾" because of his mention of Him by the words, sincere in his intention. Then he gave the reason by His saying: "﴿Indeed He, He﴾," that is, specifically (p-295) "﴿is the Oft-Returning﴾," that is, the one who is abundant in turning in forgiveness and repeating it. And since He had made it incumbent upon His Holy Self to bestow favor upon the one who does good, He said: "﴿the Most Merciful﴾," that is, to whoever returns to Him in the best manner and qualifies him for His nearness.

Al-Harali said: His acknowledgment with his tongue was a matter of courtesy and submission to the establishment of God's proof over His servants by what He informed of in His saying: "﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾" [al-A'raf: 23], and so on. This is a repentance of heart and action that no specific state of the heart undoes by a breaker, and it is the sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh) that frees one from sin by realizing the oneness of the heart and requires the expiation of outward faults that have no root in the heart, from the veil of claiming in actions and associating partners in God's command. So, by what was in his inner self, His Name the Most Merciful (al-Rahim) became manifest in him, which is from mercy, namely the specific favor of Him toward the believer, and by what became manifest upon him of humility and acknowledgment, the requirement of His Name the Oft-Returning (al-Tawwab) became manifest in him; thus his repentance combined the two matters. End of quotation.

When they were informed of the enmity that is inherent (in their situation), it was as if it were said: "What is the way of escape from it?" So it was said: following Our Law which is prescribed for repentance and mercy. For We ﴿said﴾, as has preceded, ﴿Go down﴾. Since the earlier descent could be understood as from a place in (p-296) the Garden to a lower place in it without their having left it, He repeated it here for emphasis, portraying the evil of disobedience and denouncing it. He said: ﴿from it﴾, i.e., from the Garden, ﴿all of you﴾, i.e., none of you shall remain behind, whether that occurs at one time or in succession. And We made a covenant with them at the descent into the abode of obligation that We would come to them with guidance, so that it would lead them back to the Garden a second time, promising those who follow and warning those who refuse. Thus We said: ﴿Whenever there comes to you﴾ (p-297).

Al-Harrali said: The mention of this verse without a conjunction indicates that its outward meaning is an opening that was not preceded by an inward intimation, as occurred in the previous (verse). The two descents are repeated because the first descent is a descent to the meaning of settling in this world, seeking sustenance in it, the propagation of offspring, and the carrying out of the matter of the enmity that became firmly established between the two creations, Adam and Iblis. This second descent is a descent from the station of the religious commanding rank, which was hidden in the case of Adam and manifest in the case of Iblis. The word ﴿all﴾ in His saying indicates the multiplicity of the offspring of the two creations and the multiplicity of innovations in religious matters from the two transmitted sources. End of quotation.

(p-298) He singled out the pronoun in its emphatic form with pure singularity, without attaching it to the manifestation of majesty, to distance it from the illusion (of plurality), so He said: ﴿From Me there will come guidance﴾, i.e., through the Books and the Messengers. Since guidance, which is clarification, does not necessarily entail being guided, He said: ﴿Whoever follows﴾, i.e., at least the minimal following that is considered valid. For this reason, in its recompense He was content with the negation of fear, which may arise from repentance from error, unlike what is in Ta-Ha, as will come, God willing. Following (al-tabaʿ) is striving in the wake of knowledge of guidance, as al-Harrali said. ﴿My guidance﴾, i.e., that which is transmitted (p-299) or that which is rationally apprehended; the second is more general than the first, because it is more general than being transmitted from the Messengers, or being rationally apprehended by analogy with what is transmitted from them, or by pure reason alone, as happened to Waraqa ibn Nawfal, Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, and their likes, who are alluded to with the word "few" in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few﴾ [al-Nisa: 83]. The gnostic Shihab al-Din ʿUmar ibn Muhammad al-Suhrawardi said in his book "Rashf al-Nasa'ih al-Imaniyya": Reason is the hidden proof of God, and the Qur'an is the manifest proof of God. Al-Harrali said: "My guidance" came indefinite so that it would encompass the removal of fear and grief from whoever holds fast to some truth of the comprehensive Truth, and the least of it is one who believes in God and the Last Day and does righteous deeds in what is between himself and the Truth and in what is between himself and the creation. End of quotation.

Since fear is more severe, because it increases with the passage of time, whereas grief lightens, He placed it first and said: ﴿There shall be no fear for them﴾, i.e., of something coming, for fear is the agitation of the soul from anticipating a harmful act, as al-Harrali said.

﴿Nor shall they grieve﴾, i.e., over something lost, because they will be saved from the Fire and enter the Garden. Grief, as al-Harrali said, is the aching of the heart for an absent one with whom there was relief in union, and nearness to whom is ease (p-300). The word "they" was used with grief to indicate its being hidden inwardly, and the verb was used because it manifests from the inner depths of their reflection on what they have lost. The negation of fear was detached from their action because it is fear that manifests upon them from others. End of quotation.

[p. 301]

When He had given good news to the believers who followed the guidance, He followed it with a warning to the disbelievers who rejected it, by His saying: ﴿But those who disbelieve﴾. Al-Harrali said: This is among the worst kinds of disbelief, because it is disbelief in the signs (āyāt) which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made as knowledge of the unseen of His covenant. These signs are what all the senses perceive of the heavens, the earth, and what is between them, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and of the living creatures He has dispersed through them﴾ [al-Shura: 29]. This is because the Truth, Exalted, made the cosmos manifest as writing indicating His command, and placed in the intellect a light by which His Book is read. Whoever has no light is among the companions of the Fire. He is either a follower of guidance through the light of reason and the awakening of faith, or a companion of the Fire. Then He said: ﴿and they denied Our signs﴾, because whoever was among those who disbelieved in the Book of creation, refusing to accept faith through the descent of the command, the word of punishment is specifically applied to those whose disbelief is confirmed by the visible signs, through their denial of the revealed signs. So they disbelieved in what they saw, and thus were blind, and they denied what they heard, and thus were deaf. End of quotation.

The meaning is that by disbelief and denial they combined the denial of the hearts [p. 302] and the tongues. ﴿Those﴾, that is, the distant and the hateful, ﴿are the companions of the Fire﴾. He clarified their particular connection with eternal abiding by His saying: ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾. Upon them is constant fear of what is coming from its shackles, and constant grief over the loss of Paradise. So the verse uses ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one term is omitted from each of two parallel clauses, and each clause implies the omitted term of the other): the negation of fear and grief in the first clause indicates their presence in the second, and the presence of the Fire in the second indicates its absence in the first, and the presence of Paradise in the first. It is known from this, together with His saying ﴿a dwelling place and enjoyment for a time﴾ [al-Baqarah: 36], that there must be their return to that abode, and how their dwellings will be there. It is as if this is an answer to a questioner who said: Is there any ascent after this descent? Al-Harrali said: His saying ﴿they﴾ contains an indication that punishment is soaked into their inner selves and reaches their souls with the torment of distress, grief, despair, and other things, [p. 303] including the burning of the Fire inwardly. It also contains an indication that they are in it now, in the present time, without their perceiving it. The one who drinks from vessels of gold only swallows the fire of Hell into his belly, and the Fire is nearer to each of them than the thong of his sandal. ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾, even if they did not feel its reality in this world, just as the guided ones are in Paradise in this world, even if they do not witness its direct vision. Every one who abides in something, abides in it in this world unseen, in the Hereafter directly seen, and in the grave as exposure, ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾ [al-Takathur: 6], ﴿Then you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾ [al-Takathur: 7], ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir: 46]. Here ends the address of the Furqan (the Qur'an) which is specific to the call to the Arabs, who are the head of the people of the Muhammadan call (ﷺ): "All people are followers of Quraysh; their believers follow their believers, and their disbelievers follow their disbelievers." End of quotation. [p. 304] That is, they are the primary intended audience, and the address includes others, but those others are intended secondarily. Here ends the verses specific to the general blessings for all the children of Adam, indicating the Oneness of God in that they are created things, so they have a Creator; and indicating prophethood in that he (ﷺ) informed of them in agreement with what is in the Torah and the Gospel without having learned it; and indicating the Return in that He who is able to create them at the beginning is able to restore them. Al-Isfahani related this from the Imam. The verse also contains an allusion to the Book, which is guidance for the God-fearing, containing the seven ahruf (modes of recitation), that whoever attends to one of them with full attention is sufficed by it, and whoever is occupied away from it by the lower enjoyment loses both his worldly life and his Hereafter.

Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in the Tamhid (Introduction) on the condition for attaining recitation of its seven letters, its knowledge, and acting upon it: Know that Allah, Glorified, created Adam with His hand, breathed into him from His spirit, and provided him with light from His light. Because He created him with His hand, he was in the best stature of creation. Because He breathed into him from His spirit, he had the most perfect life in contraction and expansion. Because He provided him with light from His light, he had the purest intellect, the sincerest mind, the clearest speech, and the most expressive explanation in joining and separating. He made him aware of what He wrote of the letters of His creatures by perception and sense, and made him understand what He established of His command by comprehension and knowledge, [p. 305] and alerted him to what He deposited in his essence by gnosis and ecstatic experience. Then He placed for him, among what He subjected to him of His creation, enjoyment and comfort, so he became familiar with them, and turned him between advance and retreat, acceptance and aversion. Whoever is occupied with lower enjoyment away from the higher perception is foolish, and whoever is occupied with the higher perception away from lower enjoyment is a ḥanīf (one who turns to the pure monotheism). ﴿Those whose eyes were under a veil from My remembrance﴾ [al-Kahf: 101]. ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself﴾ [al-Baqarah: 130]. ﴿Indeed Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, ḥanīf﴾ [al-Nahl: 120]. Since the enjoyment of creation on earth is for a time, and their eating and enjoying preoccupied most of them, and their hopes distracted them from their share of the ḥanīfiyya (pure monotheism) with what the intellect was given of conveying from Allah by reflection and consideration, Allah, Glorified, chose from among the ḥanīfs, alerting to the reflection which those who turned away were preoccupied with, and which those who turned their backs were disdainful of and arrogant about. They reinforced their alerting by what they made them hear of the news of what lies beyond the day of this world, of the command of Allah on the Last Day, and what the days of Allah extend to, and they reminded them of what passed of the days of Allah. Allah, Glorified, sent with them Books which they recited to them and explained to them in knowledge, action, and state. So the ḥanīfs accepted what they brought, affirmed it, and rejoiced in it, and those who turned their backs and those who turned away were warned by it. Some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. Whoever became aware of reflection and consideration believed, and cast the hearing while being a witness, [p. 306] and whoever preferred his enjoyment in the immediate, which the eyes see, over the promise and threat of Allah in the deferred, which only the heart comprehends and the ear hears, disbelieved. Just as the disbelief and worldly concerns of those invited to Islam preoccupied them, so too the heedlessness and worldly concerns of those born into Islam preoccupied them: their play in childhood, their frivolity in youth, their multiplication of wealth in old age, and their multiplication of children in their elderly years. So the one invited to Islam and the one born into Islam who is heedless share in non-attention and non-acceptance, in neglecting concern for the deferred and limiting themselves to concern for the immediate. Both made the Qur'an behind their backs: the one invited, verbally and in knowledge, and the one born into Islam, heedless, in knowledge and action. The invited one did not hear it, and the heedless one did not understand it, so in reality each made it behind his back. Whoever makes the Qur'an behind him drives him to the Fire. Only one who reads it in knowledge, state, and action places it before him. Whoever places the Qur'an before him leads him to Paradise. When the proof was established against them by their recitation of it, since it did not pass beyond their throats, they became the most severely punished of the disbelievers in the Fire. "Most of the hypocrites of my community are its reciters." ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ [al-Nisa': 145]. So it is necessary, in reciting the Qur'an, to renew attention, readiness to accept, and the realization of taqwa, because it is only guidance for the God-fearing, and unanimous concern. Just as the affairs of this world are not attained by their people except in proportion to their resolve and concern, it is more fitting that the affair of the Hereafter is not attained except with the strongest resolve and the most complete concern. So one should not recite the Qur'an unless he turns to it with the entirety of his outward self, and gathers his concern for it with the entirety of his inward self. ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ [al-A'raf: 145]. So take it with strength. ﴿O Yahya, take the Book with strength﴾ [Maryam: 12]. ﴿So remain upright as you have been commanded, and those who turn with you﴾ [Hud: 112]. The condition for attaining its recitation is the heart's concern in understanding it, and the senses' attention in listening to it and reflecting upon it. For each letter there is a condition specific to it. End of quotation.

When He, Glorified, had established the proofs of Oneness, prophethood, and the Return first, and followed them with mention of the general blessings, calling people in general, especially the Children of Isma'il, the Arabs, who are the people of the Caller (ﷺ), and most deserving of being called after the relatives, and most entitled to precedence were the people of knowledge who had been upon the truth but deviated from it, especially if they had kinship, because they are most worthy of hastening to the response with the least explanation and the easiest reminder. If they returned, the ignorant would follow them, so his matter became easy and his evil was cut off. If they did not return, their disputation would lengthen, and the ignorant would see their error, and he would be more fitting to return and refrain from his error and turn away. The rulings were recognized from the continuation of speech with them, and the lawful and the unlawful became clear. Therefore, when He finished with the call to the Arabs, which encompasses others in brief, and concluded by promising for [p. 308] following the guidance and threatening, He, Glorified, began to single out the scholars among the hypocrites for mention. These were those among the People of the Book who had outwardly professed Islam, in a way that implied the generality of those who openly declared disbelief, since they were among the greatest who were especially given what He had indicated of guidance and clarification, with what contains healing. Their Book, which contains guidance, was among the greatest, most famous, and most comprehensive books. So He related to them what, like it, softens iron and humbles the hard rocks. He said, Exalted, reminding them of His special blessings for them: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾ [al-Baqarah: 40]. It is also permissible to establish the connections from the beginning of the surah in another way, saying: Since [p. 309] the disbelievers were two kinds: one kind purely disbelieved, and another kind resembled them with hypocrisy and deception. The pure ones were of two kinds: one kind had no knowledge from a previous Book, which are the polytheists of the Arabs, and another kind had a Book by which they knew the truth. He, Exalted, mentioned the pure kind with what encompasses both kinds, the knowledgeable and the ignorant, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6], to the end. Then He followed it with the kind of hypocrite, because it is more important due to the intensity of mixing with the believers and their showing that they are among them, so that the believers would be wary of their deception. He said: ﴿And among the people are those who say: We believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 8], to the end. When He finished with that, and with what it entailed of commanding Oneness and establishing its proofs and pouring out its virtues, and with marveling at those who disbelieved despite the presence of proofs, and warning against those calamities, and winning over with mention of blessings, He began to mention a kind of the pure disbelievers who resemble the hypocrite in that they know the truth and conceal it. [p. 310] The hypocrite was once acquainted with disbelief, then ceased it, and displayed being clothed in Islam, while continuing in disbelief inwardly. This kind was upon faith in this Prophet before his call. When he called them, they erased the faith they had been clothed with, and displayed disbelief, and their state continued to display disbelief and conceal the knowledge which is the origin of faith. So their state, as you see, is most like the state of the hypocrites. For this reason you find them mentioned alongside them in many places in the Qur'an. He delayed them because of the length of their account and what in it are indications of prophethood and signs of the message, by what they showed of what they had concealed of the subtleties of their knowledge. The disputation of the scholar sends forth the steeds of thought in the fields of knowledge, and they hasten in the regions of aims until they become like birds, and bring wondrous secrets. Indeed, He, Glorified, spread within their disputations, their debates, and their discussions, among the comprehensive sentences on the laws of religion, which contain the desire of the guided, what establishes the proof that it is a guidance for the worlds. This is the summary of the matter. In its details, as you will see, there are wondrous descriptions which are too great to describe, tasted through the beauty of instruction, and the ignorance of its ignorant is healed through gentle speech. And Allah is the Giver of success and the Guide to the most upright path.

[p-311] Al-Harrali said: Then the address turned to the Children of Israel, aligned with the beginning of the address to the Arabs in His words: ﴿O mankind﴾ [2:21]. Likewise, the coherence of the Qur'an is such that the opening of one address aligns with the opening of another address that suits it in its overall meaning, and its details align with its details. So the Children of Israel were the first and most fitting to be addressed after the Arabs, who are the seal, while the Children of Israel are the beginning, in that they were the first to whom the first Book was sent down, the Torah, with which God opened His books, following His scrolls and tablets.

Then he said: When the address to the Arabs was aligned, the Arabs having had no prior guidance from the address that preceded them to the Prophet (ﷺ), the address to the Children of Israel was aligned with the address to the Arabs, through the guidance that had preceded them in their own time: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light﴾ [5:44]. [p-312] It was also aligned through what was covenanted to them concerning the multiplication of guidance, through what had preceded them in its ascent to the perfection of guidance in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in this Qur'an. For this reason it was most fitting that they hasten to it, so that the Arabs would be guided by them, and so that they would be the first believers in what they already possessed of its earlier knowledge. End of quotation.

He, glory be to Him, began by reminding them of the blessings with which He had singled them out from the rest of humankind. They met these blessings with ingratitude. He also reminded them of how He dealt with them: He granted them respite for their transgressions and treated them with pardon and remission, which shows the vastness of His mercy and the greatness of His forbearance. Among the commands He gave them, He began with fulfilling covenants (ʿahd), the greatest of which is following this noble Prophet and believing in his Book, which has removed all doubt. So He said: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾, meaning, the one whom I ennobled [Israel], and I ennobled his sons on account of him. ﴿Remember﴾, from dhikr (remembrance). The two readings, with kasra and with ḍamma, have the same meaning and both can be by the tongue and by the heart. Al-Kisa'i said: with kasra it is by the tongue, and with ḍamma it is by the heart. The opposite of what is by the heart is forgetfulness, and the opposite of what is by the tongue is silence. This was transmitted by al-Asfahani. Al-Harrali said: it is from dhikr, which is the recalling of what forgetfulness has preceded.

﴿My blessing﴾: a blessing (niʿma) is granting a person what suits his soul and body. For the discerning, it is what suits his inner and outer self, of what lies between his heart and his kin and household. ﴿Which﴾ (allatī): the form tī in it indicates a hidden, imagined, ambiguous inner matter, which its relative clause explains, by the status of [dhī], and the ʾal in it indicates that same meaning by an imagined indication. End of quote. ﴿I bestowed﴾, that is, with it, and I showed its nobility by attributing it to ﴿upon you﴾. That noble blessing is the bringing of guidance through the Books and the Messengers, by which I rescued you from the humiliation of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And fulfil﴾, from wafāʾ (fulfilment), which is an action that follows from prior knowledge that has already been established. This was said by al-Harrali.

﴿My covenant﴾, that is, the covenant I took from you to adhere to what was sent down to you, to follow your Prophet, and to follow whomever I command you to follow after him. ʿahd (covenant) is advancing toward a matter secretly, specifically for the one to whom it is advanced. This was said by al-Harrali. Al-Asfahani said: it is preserving a thing and observing it moment by moment. Al-Khalil said: its root is keeping a thing safe and renewing the agreement concerning it.

﴿I will fulfil your covenant﴾, that is, by making you among those for whom there is no fear, nor will they grieve, through abundance of livelihood and victory over enemies, as is stated in the text of the Torah in its appropriate places within this Book. ﴿And Me﴾, that is, specifically ﴿so fear Me﴾, that is, and do not slip; I will place you in the fate of the disbelievers after being struck with kinds of humiliation in this world. Ruhb (fear) is the soul's caution about what it naturally flees from, due to a harm it expects. They were addressed with fear because it is latent in them regarding what concerns the violation of knowledge. Al-Harrali said: Glory be to Him, He extended His argumentation against them, following the method of reasoning in disputation with the learned denier and in addressing the stubborn rejecter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 41:

And in His saying, ﴿And believe in what I have sent down﴾ (p-316), meaning: I have caused its sending down, ﴿confirming what you have﴾, is an affirmation of "That is the Book about which there is no doubt." They were commanded, as al-Harali said, to renew their faith in the Qur'an, because of what it contains of reports about unseen matters that were not in their Book, such as the details of the matters of the Hereafter which the Qur'an fully covered, for it is the Seal, with no Book after it awaited for further clarification. It has left for every Book before it a remainder in which it refers to what comes after it, so that the clarification extends to the final point of what the Qur'an was revealed with, since they had not been bound to anything except its basic principles in general terms. End of quotation. And in His saying: ﴿And do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾ there is a subtle meaning in rebuking them and a weighty matter of reproaching them. That is because the intended meaning of "first" is not its apparent meaning that comes immediately to the mind, for the Arabs (p-317) often use "first" without intending its literal sense, but rather exaggeration in precedence, as Miqyas ibn Subaba said, when he had killed a man of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who had killed his brother by mistake, and he returned to Makkah as an apostate:

"I have settled my blood-debt with him and attained my vengeance, and I was the first to return to the idols."

This is in the affirmative form. When you negate with a prohibition, saying: "Do not be the first to do such-and-such," its meaning is that if you do that, your attribute will be nothing but that, so it comes out in the manner of exaggeration in blame, by means of what is the attribute of the one prohibited, and so it has no implied restriction. He expressed it this way as an alert that when they abandoned following this Book, [they were] because of the knowledge they had of its truth, in utmost obstinacy, so their action in their disbelief was like the action of one who races another person to something, even if it is delayed (p-318). Or the meaning is that neither ignorance of reasoning nor lack of acquaintance with what their prophets, who were human, brought prevented them from believing in it, but rather mere envy of the Arabs that a prophet should come from among them, which necessarily entails envy of this very Prophet, because a judgment upon the more general implies a judgment upon the more specific, by being one of its instances. Thus the rank of their disbelief became prior to the rank of the disbelief of the ignorant Arabs or those who envied him ﷺ specifically, not that of the Arabs in general. So the People of the Book were "the first to disbelieve in it," and their disbelief could only occur in this manner, which is the worst of manners. Thus the meaning is: do not disbelieve in it, for if disbelief in it occurs from you, it would be the first disbelief, because its rank is the first rank of disbelief occurring from others than you, so you would be the first disbelievers, and you would have fallen into the worst forms of disbelief. For this reason it was given in the singular and not "disbelievers." And Allah knows best.

When He forbade them from disbelieving in the signs, He forbade them from what drives them to it, by His saying: ﴿And do not exchange﴾ (p-319), meaning: do not strain or insist on substituting ﴿My signs﴾, that is, those you know concerning the command to follow this noble Prophet, ﴿for a small price﴾, which is the leadership of your people and what you take from kings and others in return for carrying the Law. And "qillah" (smallness) is what falls short of sufficiency, as al-Harali said.

﴿And Me alone﴾, meaning exclusively, ﴿so fear Me﴾, meaning: make for yourselves a shield against the descent of My wrath. Thus taqwa is the result of awe, just as these actions are the result of what is in the verse of awe,

[p. 320] **﴿And do not mix﴾**. *Al-labs* is presenting a thing in a form other than its own, and from it comes *al-libas* (clothing), because it conceals the limbs so that their shape does not show. This is said by al-Harrali (Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali). **﴿the truth﴾**, that is, what you acknowledge of the Torah and the Gospel as it actually is, that which you have no purpose in altering. **﴿with falsehood﴾**, that is, what you distort from them. Al-Harrali said: *al-haqq* (the truth) is that which remains and endures until its opposite perishes. So for every pair, the one that is established is the truth, and the one that is removed is falsehood. The falsehood is that whose period of replacement is short in comparison with the long duration of its enduring counterpart. End of quotation.

Since *al-labs* may be distinct from concealment, in that a person is asked about something and presents it mixed with something else, or conceals it while knowing it, He said: **﴿and conceal the truth﴾**, that is, from those who do not know it. **﴿while you know﴾**, that is, while you are responsible. Al-Harrali took it at its outward meaning and said: When He required them to fulfil the covenant, He forbade them from evil conduct and from what they mixed up in the matter before their followers from among their community and before those among the Arabs who sought guidance from them. So by following them, they mixed the true faith in Moses (peace be upon him) and the Torah with the falsehood of what they had taken from their book concerning the affirmation of faith in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. Thus they concealed the complete and comprehensive truth [p. 321] and mixed the established, known truth with the most ancient and extreme falsehood. The falsehood of a perfect truth is an extreme and excessive falsehood in proportion to its opposite. He informed them that this was from them the concealment of a testimony against them, by their knowledge of it, as an indication. Then He followed it with testimony against them concerning their knowledge, explicitly. End of quotation.

In this verse there is a great deterrent for the People of the Book from the stubbornness they displayed. And from the kindness of Allah, the Exalted, is the deterrence of the hard-hearted who are far off, and the prohibition of the disobedient and restless, down to what is less than that, such as alerting the heedless and increasing the perfect. Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in *Kitab al-'Urwah*: The purpose of the revelation of this particle, meaning the particle of prohibition, is to restrain creatures from what would destroy them in their hereafter, and from what would take them out of safety in their death and resurrection, from what they are content with, feel at rest with, and prefer of their worldly life. So its direction toward the one who is at rest in his worldly life and turns away from its summoner, calling him to abandon what he is upon, is called *zajr* (deterrence). Its direction toward the one who looks around and senses some defect in what he is upon is called *nahy* (prohibition). The two come together in one meaning and one intent, though they differ in degree. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) repeated both over the comprehensive meaning in this hadith, meaning the one mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqarah. The first of the two in revelation was *zajr*, because the Prophet (ﷺ) [p. 322] was sent when manifest error had reached its height among creatures. Allah, glory be to Him, looked upon all the people of the earth and despised them, Arabs and non-Arabs, except remnants of the People of the Book, as related in the authentic hadith both in its chain and its text. For this reason the first thing revealed of the message was the surah **﴿O you wrapped in garments﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 1] **﴿arise and warn﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 2] **﴿and magnify your Lord﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 3] **﴿and purify your garments﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 4] **﴿and abandon uncleanness﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 5]. It is the first of the striking matters of the command, just as the sudden arrival of the Hour is the first of the striking matters for creatures. For this reason their thought is united in His words, exalted is He: **﴿when the trumpet is sounded﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 8] **﴿that will be a difficult day﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 9] **﴿for the disbelievers, not easy﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 10]. The one who is deterred has two states. Either he flees at the deterrence in wild dread, as He, exalted is He, said: **﴿as if they were startled donkeys﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 50] **﴿fleeing from a lion﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 51]. Or he turns his back after thinking, out of arrogance, as He, exalted is He, said: **﴿then he looked﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 21] **﴿then he frowned and scowled﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 22] **﴿then he turned away and was arrogant﴾** [al-Muddaththir: 23]. Sometimes he comes close to seeing, but then turns away. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "But these are minds that their Creator has outwitted." **﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right; and even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾** [al-A'raf: 146]. They are turned away from the heavenly signs of truth, despite their manifestness, as a punishment for the sin of their arrogance over creatures, while perceiving the sign of the joining of the ties of kinship in its clarity. Every striking matter is for both kinds of disbelievers, the ones who flee and the ones who turn away, from this particle. The completion of this meaning forbids the one who is comfortable and confined from gross and hidden indecencies that harm him in the next world, even if they harm him by abandoning them in this world, such as His saying, **﴿do not draw near﴾** (regarding) consuming the property of orphans, adultery, and approaching a menstruating woman. It goes down to what is less than that, the prohibition of what they regard as shrewdness in their worldly life, such as His saying: **﴿and do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾** [al-Baqarah: 188], and **﴿do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied﴾** [Al 'Imran: 130], **﴿do not spy, and do not backbite one another﴾** [al-Hujurat: 12], and **﴿let not a people ridicule another people﴾** [al-Hujurat: 11], and what joins this pattern, down to what is less than that, in a continuous gradation of the prohibition of bad interpretation resulting from a hidden purpose of the self [p. 324], such as His saying, **﴿do not say to one who offers you peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of the worldly life﴾** [al-Nisa': 94]. It goes down to what is less than that, the prohibition of what detracts from excellence even if it is within the judgement of justice, such as His saying, **﴿let not those of virtue and abundance among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah﴾** [al-Nur: 22]. It goes on to the completion of what safety cannot be achieved without, the prohibition of what exceeds sufficiency and subsistence in this world, by which right action in wisdom is valid, such as His saying, **﴿and do not walk on the earth exultantly﴾** [al-Isra': 37], down to His saying, **﴿that is part of the wisdom which your Lord has revealed to you﴾** [al-Isra': 39]. And such as His saying, **﴿do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them, the splendour of the worldly life, that We may test them therein﴾** [Ta-Ha: 131], because everything beyond sufficiency is a trial. This is the foundation by which the degrees of knowledge in this world and the ranks of Paradise in the hereafter differ. The aspects and particles that come after it, that is, all the other particles, are not sound in knowledge, action, steadfastness, or acceptance at the test except in proportion to the firmness in the recitation of this particle, its collection, and its explanation [p. 325], because it is the manifestation of what follows it from the connections of the particle of command. The shortcoming of tens of sects of the community in the prohibition particle lies in the fact that the upright religion is built upon contenting oneself with a little of the commanded things and striving intensely from the general body of the infinite prohibited things, because of the multiplicity of the entrances of calamities from them upon creatures after death. This particle is difficult for creatures, because it has become fixed in their imaginations that their worldly life can only be set right by persisting in various kinds of prohibited things, as they look to their benefit in this world and are blind to their harm in the next. Discipline, training, and refinement are preserved only by the fulfilment of protective diet from them, and protective diet is the root of medicine. Whoever does not protect himself from prohibited things will not benefit from treating himself with commanded things. He is like one who treats himself but does not observe diet: he loses the medicine and his disease multiplies. **﴿Shall We inform you of those most lost in their deeds?﴾** [al-Kahf: 103] **﴿Those whose effort is lost in the worldly life while they think they are doing good work﴾** [al-Kahf: 104]. They came with good deeds like mountains, and they used to fast, pray, and rise a part of the night, but that is treatment without diet. Because they did not protect themselves from the world, whose splendour they were forbidden, whenever it appeared to them they pounced upon it, obtaining its desires and committing sins, so the treatment did not benefit them. Whoever observes protective diet has recited this particle, and that is sufficient for him. So recite of it what is easy. The most beloved acts of worship to Allah are abandoning the world and restraining the self from the desire for its status and wealth. "Rather a servant and prophet" [hadith]. "I fast one day and break my fast another day" [hadith]. "Whoever turns away from my sunnah is not of me" [hadith]. The Qur'an is a proof for the one who acts by it, so it becomes his imam, leading him to Paradise. And it is a proof against the one who does not act by it, so it becomes behind him, driving him to the fire of the pit, which is in the well of the valley of Hell, from which Hell seeks refuge, and the valley and the well seven times every day. **﴿But We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾** [al-Shura: 52]. **﴿He misleads many by it and guides many by it﴾** [al-Baqarah: 26]. **﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾** [al-Isra': 82]. "I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in Your good pleasure from Your wrath, and in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself" [hadith]. [p. 327]

Then he said, concerning what is achieved by reciting the particle of prohibition: Know that the one who completes the recitation of the two particles of the lawful and the unlawful, which were revealed to set right the affairs of this world and to improve the condition of body and soul, acquires a habit of goodness that makes easy for him the recitation of the two particles of the hereafter's welfare, the command and the prohibition. Since wisdom and knowledge required establishing the affairs of this world by reciting the two particles of its welfare in full, faith in the unseen and belief in the promise and the threat required the trade of purchasing the promised unseen, with the great portion of the hereafter, using what the servant possesses of the currency of worldly goods. So all lawful things beyond sufficiency, according to the Sunnah, are a trade for the servant. If he spends it, he profits and keeps it, and arrives with it. If he enjoys it, he consumes it and regrets it. **﴿So you enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you have enjoyed your portion as they enjoyed theirs﴾** [al-Tawbah: 69]. **﴿Why did You not delay me to a near term, so that I might give charity and be among the righteous﴾** [al-Munafiqun: 10]. **﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾** [Al 'Imran: 92]. That is profitable wealth, that is profitable wealth. Just as the particle of the lawful is broad, so that gratitude may be achieved through it, the particle of prohibition is narrowing, so that the breadth of the particle of the lawful is limited, and patience may be achieved through it, so that the servant may be grateful and patient. Whatever is achieved by reciting the two particles of prohibition [p. 328] is either from the heart and the vision of the inner self, which is the witnessing of the insight of the promised reward, as though he sees it, so that the soul is at rest with its good and dismayed by its evil, as Harithah said: "It is as if I am looking at the people of Paradise in Paradise, enjoying its bounties, and at the people of the Fire in the Fire, being punished." This produced in him what he reported about himself in his saying: "My soul turned away from the world, so its gold and its clay are equal to me." Especially for one who has been strengthened by the good tidings of true dreams and sincere unveiling, so that he abandons the perishing for the enduring, with certainty and witnessing. Or it is from the state of the soul, and patience is by restraining it from what it desires by nature, even if it is lawful for it by the Law. "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he pitied his condition: 'Are you not content that they should have this world and we should have the hereafter?'" **﴿And seek help through patience﴾** [al-Baqarah: 45]. Restraining the self from its desires, even when they are lawful, is the reality of its purification, and killing it by weakening it from them is its life. [p. 329] Letting it loose to graze in its desires is its corruption.

﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams: 9] ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 10]. The soul is a mount: wearing it down strengthens it, and indulging it weakens it. Restraining it from indulgence is common across all the permissible ways of enjoyment, except in two things. The first is women, by the word of God, because they are of the very self of men and are not other than them: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find rest in her﴾ [al-A'raf: 189], and ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take from it anything﴾ [al-Nisa': 20]. The second is good scent, because it is nourishment for the spirit, a strengthening of the senses, and a breath from the inner realm of the Dominion to the outer realm of the kingdom. As for everything else, enjoying it and following the soul's desire in it is a sign of denying the promise of the Most Merciful and affirming the promise of Satan: ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them and barred them from the way, so they are not guided﴾ [al-Naml: 24]; ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, and Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾ [al-Nisa': 120].

This is in regard to the soul. As for the matter of action and the reach of the hand, it consists of lifting it from what exceeds sufficiency and leaving that surplus to those in need, so that they may take it as a livelihood. It also consists of acquiring wealth beyond sustenance only through trade of transport, travel in the land, and setting aside for a time of need, not through hoarding and constriction. Taking more than two garments, one for work and one for Friday, is a sign of weak faith, contrary to the Sunnah, a severance from the traces of prophethood, a departure from the practice of the Caliphs, and an abandoning of the emblem of the righteous. Likewise, refining the matter of food, seeking what is pleasing in appearance rather than what is pleasing in knowledge, preferring good food over good piety, and multiplying condiments and varying dishes. Likewise, taking more than one dwelling and more than one sufficient farm, raising buildings, and aspiring through structures.

The Prophet ﷺ refused to return the greeting to a man who had built a dome in Medina, until he demolished it and leveled it with the houses of the people of Medina.
