Al-Harrali said: The greatest of sins is that the punishment of Allah Most High for them is to be bound to sins even worse than them. So their arrogance was followed by the curse, as was the case with Iblis regarding Adam, peace be upon him. Thus the opening of this surah contains the manifestation of the two satanic forces, of jinn and of humankind, with which the Qur'an concludes in His words: ﴿from among the jinn and mankind﴾ [al-Nas: 6], so that its two ends connect, making it a conclusion with neither a beginning nor an end. (p-35) The Fatihah encompasses it; it cannot be said that it is its beginning or its end. For this reason some reciters joined its end to its beginning so that no end can be discerned. This is like the Arabs' saying when they were asked about their sons: they are like a hollow ring, whose end cannot be known.

When He informed of their being cursed, He made His next words a consequence of it: ﴿so little is it that they believe﴾. He described their belief as scant and emphasized it with the particle "ma", as an indication that they are overwhelmed by disbelief and have no benefit in them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 89:

When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the coarseness of their conduct and concluded it with their being cursed, and He had previously mentioned their Book several times, and had alluded to the Injil (Gospel) by Allah's giving 'Isa, peace be upon him, the clear proofs, He then mentioned their disbelief in this Book, whose main theme in the surah is described as guidance, and in this Messenger who brought it, as evidence of how deeply they were immersed in disbelief. For although they sought victory through him ﷺ before his mission, against those who opposed them, rejoiced at him, and called on themselves to witness their joy at his coming, they were the furthest of people from his call, persisting in disbelief [p. 36] and bound to error. Thus this proof was clearer than the first to the people of that age. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when there came to them a Book﴾, i.e., one comprising all guidance because of its greatness, in that it is ﴿from Allah﴾, who comprises all the attributes of perfection. Then He mentioned, among the things that make them love following it, His saying: ﴿confirming what they already have﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91], through the tongue of a prophet whose truthfulness they recognise by matters their own Book testifies to, and by this Book's confirmation of him through the inimitability of its composition and its confirmation of his message by agreeing with their Book. The answer (jawab) is omitted, and what follows indicates that they disbelieved in it. In this there is a crushing blow to them, because their Book would be a witness against their disbelief. When he had shown the testimony of their Book, he followed it with their own testimony, lest they distort the meaning of that, so He said: ﴿And they had been﴾, i.e., and the situation was that they had been, and since their seeking victory happened at some time, He affirmed the preposition, so He said: ﴿before﴾, i.e., before his coming,

﴿seeking victory﴾, i.e., asking Allah for victory through the Name (the Prophet) who was to come, seeking blessing by mentioning him,

﴿over those who disbelieved﴾. This means that they were not heedless of him; rather they were the most knowledgeable of people about him, and they had prepared themselves [p. 37] to believe in him. Yet despite all of this, ﴿when there came to them﴾ with the mission of Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿what they recognised﴾, i.e., of his truthfulness, through the descriptions of him mentioned in their Book,

﴿they disbelieved in it﴾, making excuses with kinds of pretexts that are clearly false. Among them was their claim that Jibril, peace be upon him, is their enemy, though he is the one who brings it. Al-Tha'labi and al-Wahidi said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated that "'Abd Allah ibn Suriya argued with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about several matters, and when the proof was made manifest against him, he said: 'What angel comes to you from the sky?' He said: 'Jibril.' He said: 'Allah has never sent a prophet except that he is his ally' (and in another narration: he asked him about the one who descends upon him with the revelation, and he said: Jibril). He said: 'He is our enemy; had it been someone else, we would have believed in you.'"

Ibn Ishaq said in the Sirah: "'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn al-Makki narrated to me, from Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari, that a group of Jewish rabbis came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'Tell us about four things that we ask you about. If you do, we will follow you, confirm you, and believe in you.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: 'You must give me the covenant and pact of Allah that if I inform you of them, you will confirm me.' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Ask whatever you wish!' [p. 38] They said: 'Tell us: how does a child resemble its mother, when the seed is only from the man?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I adjure you by Allah and by His days among the Children of Israel: do you know that the man's seed is white and thick, and the woman's seed is yellow and thin, and whichever of them prevails over the other, the resemblance is to that one?' They said: 'By Allah, yes.' They said: 'Tell us about how you sleep.' He said: 'I adjure you by Allah and by His days among the Children of Israel: do you know that the one you claim I am not, his eye sleeps while his heart is awake?' They said: 'By Allah, yes.' He said: 'So too is my sleep: my eye sleeps while my heart is awake.' They said: 'Tell us about what Israel forbade for himself.' He said: 'I adjure you by Allah and by His days among the Children of Israel: do you know that the food and drink he loved most were the milk and meat of camels, and that he fell ill with an ailment from which Allah healed him, so he forbade himself what he loved most in food and drink, out of gratitude to Allah, so he forbade himself the meat and milk of camels?' They said: 'By Allah, yes.' They said: 'Tell us about the Spirit.' He said: 'I adjure you by Allah and by His days: do you know Jibril, who comes to me?' They said: 'By Allah, yes, but he, O Muhammad, is our enemy. He is an angel who brings only hardship and the shedding of blood. Were it not for that, we would have followed you.' So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril – for indeed, he has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart by permission of Allah, confirming what was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97], up to His saying: ﴿Was it not that every time they make a covenant, a party of them discards it? Rather, most of them do not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 100]."

The origin of this is in al-Bukhari, in the chapters on the Creation of Adam, the Hijrah (migration to Madinah), and Tafsir, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from several narrations whose wording has been combined. He said: "The Prophet of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, i.e., during the Hijrah..." until he said: "He continued traveling until he alighted beside the house of Abu Ayyub, may Allah be pleased with him. He was speaking to his family when 'Abd Allah ibn Salam heard of him while he was in a palm grove belonging to his family, gathering dates for them. He hastened to put down what he was gathering for them in it, and came with it in his hand, [p. 40] and listened to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, then returned to his family. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: 'Which of our households is nearest?' Then he mentioned his alighting at Abu Ayyub's, may Allah be pleased with him. Then he said: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him, came and said: 'I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah and that you have come with the truth! The Jews know that I am their chief, the son of their chief, their most knowledgeable, and the son of their most knowledgeable. Call them and ask them about me before they know that I have become Muslim, for if they know I have become Muslim, they will say about me what is not in me.'" (In another narration: news of the arrival of the Prophet ﷺ reached 'Abd Allah ibn Salam while he was in land gathering dates, so he came to him and said: "I am asking you about three things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise will eat? And why does the child resemble its father, or why does it resemble its mother?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Jibril has just informed me of them." 'Abd Allah said: "He is the enemy of the Jews among the angels." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril – for indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by permission of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97]. "As for the first sign of the Hour: it is a fire that will gather people from the east to the west. As for the first food the people of Paradise will eat: it is the extra piece of the liver of a fish (in another narration: the fish). As for the resemblance in the child: when a man has intercourse with a woman and his water precedes hers, the child resembles him, and when hers precedes, it resembles her." (In another narration: "When the man's water precedes the woman's, the child is drawn to him, and when the woman's water precedes, she draws it.") He said: "I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." Then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander. If they know of my Islam before you ask them, they will slander me before you." So the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sent for them, and they entered upon him (in another narration: the Jews came and 'Abd Allah entered the house), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "O assembly of Jews! Woe to you! Fear Allah! By Allah, other than whom there is no god, you indeed know that I am the Messenger of Allah and that I have come to you with the truth, so submit!" They said: "We do not know that." They said this to the Prophet ﷺ three times. He said: "What sort of man among you is 'Abd Allah ibn Salam?" They said: "He is our chief, the son of our chief, our most knowledgeable, the son of our most knowledgeable, our most virtuous, and the son of our most virtuous." He said: "What do you think if he becomes Muslim?" They said: "Far be it from Allah! He would never become Muslim!" (In another narration: "May Allah protect him from that.") He said: "O Ibn Salam, go out to them!" He went out and said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. O assembly of Jews, fear Allah! By Allah, other than whom there is no god, you indeed know that he is the Messenger of Allah and that he has come with the truth." They said: "You are lying!" and they said: "Our worst and the son of our worst!" and they attacked him and belittled him. He said: "This is what I was afraid of, O Messenger of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had them removed.

Al-Wahidi, in Asbab al-Nuzul (occasions of revelation), narrated: "'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'I used to visit the Jews during their study of the Torah, and I was amazed at the agreement of the Qur'an with the Torah and of the Torah with the Qur'an. They said: "O 'Umar, no one is more beloved to us than you." I said: "Why?" They said: "Because you come to us and sit with us." I said: "I only come to be amazed at how the Book of Allah confirms itself, part by part, and at the agreement of the Torah with the Qur'an and of the Qur'an with the Torah." While I was with them one day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed behind my back. They said: "This is your companion, so go to him!" I turned and saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had entered a small door of Madinah. I turned to them and said: "I adjure you by Allah, and by what Allah has sent down to you of Scripture: do you know that he is the Messenger of Allah?" Their chief said: "You have adjured us by Allah, so inform him." They said: "You are our chief, so inform him." Their chief said: "We know that he is the Messenger of Allah." I said: "Then I will destroy you if you know that he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and yet do not follow him." They said: "We have an enemy among the angels and a friend among the angels." I said: "Who is your enemy and who is your friend?" They said: "Our enemy is Jibril." I said: "And who is your friend?" They said: "Mika'il." I said: "I testify that it is not permissible for Jibril to be hostile to the friend of Mika'il, nor for Mika'il to make peace with the enemy of Jibril. They and those with them are enemies to whoever opposes them and friends to whoever makes peace with them." Then I rose, and he (meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) met me and said: "O son of al-Khattab, shall I recite to you some verses?" Then he recited: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril – for indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97], until he reached ﴿And none disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 99]. I said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I came to you only to inform you of what the Jews said, and behold, the Subtle, the All-Aware had already preceded me with the news!" 'Umar said: "I found myself in the religion of Allah harder than a stone."' End of quotation.

I asked some of the learned Jews living in our time about their enmity toward Jibril, peace be upon him, and he would not permit himself to state it explicitly, and said: "That is not given (to be disclosed)."

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also narrated this hadith in his Musnad, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Our shaykh al-Busayri said: It is mursal (a report whose chain omits a Companion) with a sound chain, and in it: He said to them: "And what is their position with their Lord?" They said: "One of them is on His right and the other on the other side." And I testify that they and their Lord are peace for those who make peace with them and war for those who wage war against them.

When He, glory be to Him, had made clear by this that they were the most obstinate of people and the most adept at deceit, falsehood, lying and corruption, they were most deserving of the description of disbelief. He therefore made the following a consequence of that: ﴿So the curse of God﴾ [2:89], meaning He to whom all command belongs,

﴿is upon the disbelievers﴾ [2:89]. He placed the apparent noun where a pronoun would have been, to attach the judgment to the description so that it would be general, and to indicate that some of them might be righteous, if God wills.

Since they deserved by this all the aspects of blame, he joined to it His words ﴿Wretched is﴾ [2:90]. He used the comprehensive word of blame, which is the opposite of the comprehensive word of praise, meaning: (p. 44) a wretched thing ﴿is that for which they sold their souls﴾ [2:90], meaning their own portions (of worldly gain). They preferred them and chose them over (the truth), and that was the very essence (of their loss). He then reported the opposite of what the believers did, who sold their souls (to God) and gave them up by worshipping God, preferring what pleases Him over the desires of their souls. Thus that was the very essence of attaining and advancing them.

Then he explained the pronoun referring to the ambiguous term that is used in preserving the self, saying: ﴿that they disbelieve﴾ [2:90], meaning that they conceal, in a renewed and continuous manner, what they know,

﴿in what God has sent down﴾ [2:90], Who has no equal. That is, they sold their souls and so kept them for themselves, according to their claim, by disbelieving, and did not make them subordinate. It is also permissible that "sold" (ishtaraw) means "they sold" (baa'u), because they gave them up to Satan by disbelief, just as the believers gave up themselves to God by faith.

Then he gave the reason for their disbelief by His words: ﴿out of envy﴾ [2:90], meaning out of jealousy and injustice, that prophethood should be among the children of Isma'il, peace be upon him. Al-Harrali said: it is an intensification (p. 45) in seeking something, ended quote.

Its root meaning is simply seeking and wanting, as if a human being, since he is inclined toward deficiency and naturally disposed to evil and disobedience, except those whom God protects and helps, is blamed for mere wanting, because it is his duty not to have any choice or desire of his own, but rather his desire should follow the desire of his Master, as is the state of the servant. And God is the Giver of success.

Then he gave the reason for their envy by His words: ﴿that God should send down﴾ [2:90], the Lord of majesty and generosity, ﴿of His bounty﴾ [2:90]. The form "yunazzilu" (sends down) indicates that what angers them will continue in the future, and it is glad tidings to the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [2:90], namely the Arabs whom they envied. Then he made the following a consequence of that: ﴿So they returned﴾ [2:90], meaning they came back because of that,

﴿with anger﴾ [2:90] for their envy of this Prophet (ﷺ) because he was from the Arabs,

﴿upon anger﴾ [2:90] which they had deserved through their disbelief in their prophets, out of obstinacy. Then he attached the judgment they deserved to their description, in a general way (p. 46) and as an indication that some of them would believe, saying: ﴿And for the disbelievers﴾ [2:90], meaning those who are firmly established in this description, among them and among others,

﴿is a humiliating punishment﴾ [2:90]. "Muhin" (humiliating) derives from ihanah, which is casting down by way of abasement and contempt.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 91:

When Allah (glorified is He) had established the proof that they deserve to abide forever in the Fire because of their disbelief in the Book by which they used to seek victory (through the one who brought it), He established another proof for this, clearer than the first, namely their disbelief in their own Book. So He said: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾, that is, to those who violated the covenants of their Book,

﴿"Believe in what Allah has sent down,"﴾ that is, the King to whom all affairs belong absolutely, and in the general sense, [believe] in the Books and scrolls.

When He had raised their status by calling them to belief in what was attributed to this Greatest Name,

﴿they say﴾, debasing themselves,

﴿"We believe in what was sent down to us,"﴾ so they dropped the name of the One by whose mention one is honored and by whose name one seeks blessing, and they singled out only part of what He sent down. Then He marveled at their claim with His words: ﴿"and they disbelieve in what is beyond it"﴾, that is, they said that, while in fact they disbelieve in what is beyond what was sent down to them, of what Allah sent down to His messengers. This includes what came before the Torah and what came after it, because *warā'* (وراء, "beyond/behind") is sometimes meant as "behind" and sometimes as "in front." When you say, "Zayd is behind me (warā'ī)," it is correct to mean the place that I conceal from one who is behind me, in which case it is in front of me, and it is correct to mean the place that is hidden from me, in which case it is behind me. Al-Harrali said: *warā'* is what the senses and knowledge do not reach, wherever the place may be; so it may happen that a thing is *warā'* in that it is not known, and yet is *amām* (in front) in place. End of quote.

﴿"while it is the truth"﴾, that is, while that which is beyond it is the Truth that has reached its furthest end by what the definite article *al-* (ال) indicates. Al-Harrali said: He made it the ultimate of truth by the word *al-*, because what is established and has no cessation, since it has reached its end, is *al-ḥaqq* (الحق, "the Truth"), whereas what is established for a time and then is followed by completion, or admits increase, is only *ḥaqq* (حق, an indefinite "a truth"). Between what is definite by *al-* and what is indefinite there is the greatest difference in meaning. End of quote.

﴿"confirming what is with them"﴾. Thus it is established that they disbelieve in what they have, because one who denies what confirms a thing denies that thing itself.

Then He uncovered the veil of their statement with the clearest refutation, saying: ﴿"Say, 'Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah"﴾, the King, the Greatest. That is, as a consequence of your claim, it is said to you: why ﴿"do you kill the prophets of Allah"﴾, even though your Book forbids killing in general, so how about killing the prophets! Then He made clear that their disbelief in this killing is only by way of consenting to the killing of their forefathers, with His words, affirming the preposition [*min qabl*] because that came from them in some past times: ﴿"before"﴾. The use of the present tense depicts the abomination of this killing in that horrible state, and indicates that if they were able now, they would do what they did, because the implied meaning is: "and you would persist in killing them afterward." In this there is a hint of their eagerness to kill the Prophet (ﷺ), as a warning from them, and this hinted-at matter came true: the Banu al-Nadir resolved to drop a rock upon him, and the people of Khaybar poisoned him. Then He stated the substance of their claim with the particle of doubt, saying: ﴿"if you are believers"﴾, indicating that such conduct does not proceed from one who is clothed in faith.

Having shown their falsehood in claiming belief through what they did after Moses, for which they deserved eternal abiding in the Fire, He established another proof, stronger than all that preceded it. For in the Torah there was not laid down for them what was laid down for them regarding tawhid (the oneness of God) and distance from shirk (associating partners with God), and that is in the extant copies that are now among them. Yet they broke all of that by taking the calf in the days of Moses and in the presence of Harun, peace be upon them both, as is now explicitly stated in what is before them of those texts. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And certainly Moses came to you with the clear proofs﴾ from the signs.

Since their disbelief in spite of that was extremely far-fetched, He expressed it with its particle, depicting the increase of its ugliness by its being consequent upon the clearest of clarifications, and rebuking them. So He said: ﴿Then you took﴾, that is, despite the treatment of your original natural disposition and your sound intellects, ﴿the calf﴾. He indicated by the prepositional phrase (p-51) that the taking occurred during a part of the period of absence, so He said: ﴿after him﴾, that is, after Moses departed from you to the Mount, as in the other verse: ﴿We have tempted your people after you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 85]. ﴿And you were﴾, that is, while you were, ﴿wrongdoers﴾, meaning: you did not claim that it was your god out of ignorance on your part; rather, after the clear proofs had come to you that your God is only Allah, who rescued you from bondage and showed you wondrous extraordinary signs admitting no doubt, and you heard His speech and thus knew that He is not a body nor resembles a body. You did not do that except because wrongdoing (zulm) — which is walking without order, like a blind camel's stumbling (khabt 'ashwa') — is a necessary attribute of yours.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 93:

(p-52) Then he mentioned another matter, which is clearer in demonstrating their obstinacy and that they are only following their desires. So he turned to address them directly, for that is more severe in rebuke, saying: ﴿And when We took your covenant﴾, and He made it manifest in the mode of greatness, portraying the increase in their audacity;

﴿your covenant﴾ concerning faith and obedience;

﴿and We raised above you the Mount﴾: the great mountain which We made as a deterrent to you from being content to dwell in the lowland of ignorance, and as an elevation to the summit of knowledge. And We said to you, while it was above you: ﴿Take what We have given you﴾ of the fundamentals and the derivative rulings in this great Book ﴿with strength﴾.

Since the benefit of hearing is acceptance, and whoever hears but does not accept is like one who has not heard, He said: ﴿And listen﴾, otherwise We will bury you under it. This is like where raising the whip and the rod over someone suffices for others in discipline, so that he is stirred to learning, which noble souls endure severe hardships for, because of its nobility and the pride it brings them. (p-53) When they went astray after this great sign, quickly, although it required steadfastness in faith after taking the covenant, which no person of honour breaks, their straying after it indicated that obstinacy was a binding disposition for them. So it was as though they were disobedient at the moment of giving the pledge. He spoke, translating the general state of most of them throughout their times, which he expressed in the previous verse with His saying: ﴿Then you turned away﴾ [al-Baqarah: 64], signalling anger against them by turning away from addressing them after confounding them with direct rebuke, since they contradicted what was said to them of the beneficial hearing, and thus they declared that they had made it harmful.

﴿They said: We hear﴾, meaning: with our ears.

﴿and we disobey﴾, meaning: and we act contrary to what we heard. He presented it, because of its strangeness, in the manner of an answer to a questioner, as if he had said: the Mount was raised above them, a tremendously awesome matter (p-54) requiring haste in giving the covenant outwardly and inwardly and steadfastness in it. So what did they do? It was said: they hastened to the opposite of that.

﴿And they were made to drink﴾: he magnified the matter by attributing the verb to them, then to their hearts. It is from al-ishraab, which is a penetrating, smooth interpenetration like a drink, and water is what penetrates the whole body because of its fineness and its pervasiveness. So said al-Harali.

And al-Kashshaf said: a mixing of one colour with another. ﴿into their hearts the calf﴾, meaning: its love, and He omitted it to indicate the intensity of their firm entrenchment, to the point that the annexed became the annexee. ﴿because of their disbelief﴾. In this is an indication that whoever turns away from complying with the command deserves being distanced from the station of intimacy.

The Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harali said in al-Miftah, the eighth chapter, on the aspects of explaining turning towards and turning away in the Qur'an: Know that every created being is addressed according to what is within its capacity to grasp, and what is beyond its capacity to grasp is negated from it. So for every age of the ages of hearts there is an address of turning toward it according to its capacity to grasp. Perhaps it has an aversion to some of that, so turning away befalls it according to the initial degree of that aversion. Perhaps grace repairs it, and turning toward it returns in some manner, short of the purity of the first turning. Perhaps the turnings align in sequence, so that clarification and comprehension rise according to the rank of the one toward whom turning is directed, and aversion intensifies according to the initial aversion. Perhaps the wording of clarification in them returns, some upon others. So the address of turning toward the Prophet ﷺ is the greatest comprehension in the Qur'an.

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord extended the shade?﴾ [al-Furqan: 45], to the end of the verse;

﴿And He it is who made the night for you as a garment﴾ [al-Furqan: 47], to the end of the verse; the difference between the two addresses corresponds to the difference of those addressed.

﴿Have those who disbelieved not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We parted them?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30]. He turned the address away from them and negated from them what was not in their state to see.

﴿Take what We have given you with strength, and listen.﴾ They said: We hear and we disobey, and the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief. Say: Evil is what your faith commands you.﴾ He addressed them and commanded them. When they disobeyed, the direction of address turned away from them, then He repaired them by addressing them through the tongue of the Prophet of mercy, and His own turning away from them continued in the persistence of the address:

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [al-Talaq: 1]. The address descended on both levels, to make clear to the higher what it makes clear to the lower.

﴿That is better for you and purer﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 12]. (p-56) This chapter is of great benefit in understanding for one who seeks clarification of it and the interweaving of its sources in the Qur'an. End of quotation.

The existential proof of their being made to drink in love of the calf is their hastening to worship what resembles it in lacking harm and benefit and in form. In the Fourth Book of the Torah, in the story of Balaq, king of the Amorites, who sought help from Balaam son of Beor, its text is: "And Israel dwelt in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, and they called the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods, and Israel joined himself to Baal-peor, and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel." End of quotation.

When He, glory be to Him, had shown the greatness of their disbelief and obstinacy together with their impudence in claiming faith and special favour with the Gardens, He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say to them, in mockery of them, emphasizing their blame by using the expression set for the totality of blame, so He said: (p-57) ﴿Say: Evil is what﴾, meaning: evil is the thing which ﴿your faith commands you﴾ to, namely the disbelief, this faith which you claimed. He clarified this mockery by His saying, as a supposition and doubt: ﴿if you are believers﴾ as you assert. From this it results that they are either liars in their claim, or they are the most ignorant of the ignorant, in that they did what faith does not combine with, and they do not know.

[p. 58] When the proofs established that they have no share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and this contradicts their claim that it belongs to them alone, as in their saying, ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:80], and their interpretation of that as seven days, and that we will succeed them in it, the Exalted concluded this with a decisive, self-evident proof. He said, ﴿Say: If the Last Abode﴾, and He placed the prepositional phrase first to indicate exclusivity, saying, ﴿is yours with God﴾, meaning, as you claim. He distinguished it by His words ﴿with God﴾, to whom belongs all perfection. He explained the intended meaning by His words ﴿exclusively﴾. When He mentioned exclusivity, for emphasis of the meaning, He reinforced it with His words ﴿apart from the rest of mankind﴾, meaning, none of them shares it with you. Al-khulus (exclusivity) is the purifying of a thing from what mixes with it in its making, from what is lower than it. So said al-Harrali.

﴿Then wish for death﴾, because that is a sign of the servant's good standing with his Lord, of the cultivation of what is between him and his Lord, and of his hope for meeting Him.

Al-Harrali said: In proportion to the soul's aversion to death, the soul's attainment (of the knowledge that comes with it) is weakened, together with the knowledge by which it finds intimacy with its Lord. So it wishes to meet Him and loves Him. Whoever loves to meet God, God loves to meet him; whoever dislikes to meet God, God dislikes to meet him. This happens to the common believers at the unveiling at the time of the death-rattle (al-gharghara), and to the elite believers during the respite of life, because if the veil were lifted from them they would not increase in certainty. Therefore what the believer after the unveiling has of love for meeting God is what the certain one has in his life and wakefulness, because the unveiling is complete for him while the veil of the outward King remains. For this reason no prophet died until he was given the choice, and he chose meeting God, so that his coming to God would be the coming of a lover who hastens. And because the believer falls short of the certainty of the prophet, God takes charge of choosing for him in his meeting, since He is his Protector. From this is what was reported: "I have not hesitated over anything as I hesitate over seizing the soul of My believing servant, who dislikes death, and I dislike to cause him distress, yet he must have it." So within this is God's choosing for the believer his meeting, since He is his Protector, choosing for him in what his perception cannot reach. End of quotation.

[p. 60] Then He recorded their lying against them, saying, ﴿If you are truthful﴾, meaning, if you believe in the truth of your claim that it is exclusively yours. Since the implied sense was, "He said to them, then what did you wish for?", He joined to it His words, as a definitive report of the unseen, to cut off obstinacy and as emphasis, because their claim of exclusivity is greater than their claim of being God's friends, as in Surat al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And they will never wish for it, ever﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 62:7]. Then He mentioned the cause of their not wishing, saying, ﴿because of what their hands have sent ahead﴾. The word qaddama (sent ahead) is from taqdima, which is placing a thing in front, the direction of the foot, which is the goal and the aim, meaning opposite the face. So said al-Harrali. He expressed it by the hand, with which most actions are done, indicating that their deeds, because of their ugliness, are as if empty of intention. So He said ﴿their hands﴾, meaning, of wrongdoing. To this His words point, joined to what is implied as: "Then God knows that?" ﴿And God﴾, to whom none is equal, ﴿is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning all of them, where He made clear the attribute that necessitates the ruling, with generality and warning.

[p. 58] When the proofs established that they have no share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and this contradicts their claim that it belongs to them alone, as in their saying, ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:80], and their interpretation of that as seven days, and that we will succeed them in it, the Exalted concluded this with a decisive, self-evident proof. He said, ﴿Say: If the Last Abode﴾, and He placed the prepositional phrase first to indicate exclusivity, saying, ﴿is yours with God﴾, meaning, as you claim. He distinguished it by His words ﴿with God﴾, to whom belongs all perfection. He explained the intended meaning by His words ﴿exclusively﴾. When He mentioned exclusivity, for emphasis of the meaning, He reinforced it with His words ﴿apart from the rest of mankind﴾, meaning, none of them shares it with you. Al-khulus (exclusivity) is the purifying of a thing from what mixes with it in its making, from what is lower than it. So said al-Harrali.

﴿Then wish for death﴾, because that is a sign of the servant's good standing with his Lord, of the cultivation of what is between him and his Lord, and of his hope for meeting Him.

Al-Harrali said: In proportion to the soul's aversion to death, the soul's attainment (of the knowledge that comes with it) is weakened, together with the knowledge by which it finds intimacy with its Lord. So it wishes to meet Him and loves Him. Whoever loves to meet God, God loves to meet him; whoever dislikes to meet God, God dislikes to meet him. This happens to the common believers at the unveiling at the time of the death-rattle (al-gharghara), and to the elite believers during the respite of life, because if the veil were lifted from them they would not increase in certainty. Therefore what the believer after the unveiling has of love for meeting God is what the certain one has in his life and wakefulness, because the unveiling is complete for him while the veil of the outward King remains. For this reason no prophet died until he was given the choice, and he chose meeting God, so that his coming to God would be the coming of a lover who hastens. And because the believer falls short of the certainty of the prophet, God takes charge of choosing for him in his meeting, since He is his Protector. From this is what was reported: "I have not hesitated over anything as I hesitate over seizing the soul of My believing servant, who dislikes death, and I dislike to cause him distress, yet he must have it." So within this is God's choosing for the believer his meeting, since He is his Protector, choosing for him in what his perception cannot reach. End of quotation.

[p. 60] Then He recorded their lying against them, saying, ﴿If you are truthful﴾, meaning, if you believe in the truth of your claim that it is exclusively yours. Since the implied sense was, "He said to them, then what did you wish for?", He joined to it His words, as a definitive report of the unseen, to cut off obstinacy and as emphasis, because their claim of exclusivity is greater than their claim of being God's friends, as in Surat al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And they will never wish for it, ever﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 62:7]. Then He mentioned the cause of their not wishing, saying, ﴿because of what their hands have sent ahead﴾. The word qaddama (sent ahead) is from taqdima, which is placing a thing in front, the direction of the foot, which is the goal and the aim, meaning opposite the face. So said al-Harrali. He expressed it by the hand, with which most actions are done, indicating that their deeds, because of their ugliness, are as if empty of intention. So He said ﴿their hands﴾, meaning, of wrongdoing. To this His words point, joined to what is implied as: "Then God knows that?" ﴿And God﴾, to whom none is equal, ﴿is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning all of them, where He made clear the attribute that necessitates the ruling, with generality and warning.

When he had made clear that they would not wish for death, he affirmed for them something beyond that: wishing for the opposite, which shows their knowledge of the evil end awaiting them. So he said: ﴿You will surely find them﴾, meaning, by what you know of their conditions, which is what is attained by *wijdan* (finding), namely the inner perception of one's state, and also the reaching of what has an inner connection, as if it were within them: ﴿most eager﴾. This is an intensive form from *al-hirs* (eagerness), which is the seeking of total absorption in whatever one's share is concerned with, as stated by al-Harrali.

﴿of mankind for life﴾, in whatever condition it may be. They are certain that no day passes without some turmoil, yet they know that this life, however miserable, is better for them than what follows death. ﴿And more than﴾, meaning: and more eager than ﴿those who associated partners﴾, who have no impulse toward life, knowing that they are headed for the lasting punishment because of their evil deeds that encompass them and their shirk. Al-Harrali said: attributing a matter specific to one person to someone who has no authority over it, ends.

Then he specified the extent of what they wish for, saying: ﴿wishes﴾, from *al-widd* (desire), which is the genuine inclination of the soul toward a thing that deserves that inclination, as stated by al-Harrali.

﴿one of them﴾, meaning: one of those who came before, from among the Jews and the polytheists in all their categories; or from the Jews specifically, in which case the Jews' desire is included a fortiori. Al-Harrali said: this is a kind of Qur'anic address that the reach of creatures' communication does not attain.

﴿were given long life﴾, from *al-ta'mir* (granting long life), which is the prolonging of lifespan, as if it were repeated. *Al-'umur* (lifespan) is the duration between the appearance of a thing and its cessation, as stated by al-Harrali.

﴿a thousand years﴾, out of fear of death or what follows it. The *alf* (thousand) is the completion of number with the completion of the third rank; and the *sana* (year) is the period in which the sun completes one cycle and the moon completes twelve cycles, as stated by al-Harrali. Although this meaning exists in *al-hawl*, *al-'am* and *al-hajja* as well, the etymological root of each term is still taken into account in general. For the eloquence of the Qur'an, none of these words is used except in what suits the context derived from the original root of these words. Since this context aims to censure them for their clinging to remaining in this world in whatever condition, knowing that any state of it, even the worst, is better for them than what follows death, given the certainty of their wretchedness, he expressed it with what carries the sense of drought and hardship (*al-isnat*), or what carries the sense of circling, which involves toil and fatigue, if its origin is from *sana yasnu*, meaning it circled around the well. Al-Suhayli said in al-Rawd: the year is sometimes called *dar* (a turn). In a report: between Adam and Nuh there are a thousand *dar*, meaning years. Then he said: reflect on this, for knowledge of the placement of speech and the setting of words in their fitting positions opens a door to knowledge of the inimitability of the Qur'an, and Allah is the One sought for help.

﴿and it is not﴾, meaning: his being granted long life,

﴿one to remove him﴾. *Al-zahzaha* (removal) is the distancing of a heavy thing, pushing it away from what it is far from, as stated by al-Harrali.

﴿from punishment﴾ (p-64), meaning: a removal that begins from punishment. He used *min* rather than *'an* to inform that they have not separated from punishment either in this world or the next, even if they do not feel it in this world. Then he explained the pronoun with his words: ﴿that he be given long life﴾. Only obedience joined with sound faith, which admits no division, removes him from it. Since the implied sense is: because they perform in their lifetimes the evil deeds that encompass them, he followed it with his words: ﴿and Allah﴾, to whom all command belongs, ﴿is Seeing of what they do﴾.

[p. 65] When He mentioned their enmity towards the most distinguished of mankind, and their audacity against him by denying and killing, and concluded that by their enmity towards the most perfect and most distinguished of creation, out of envy at the descent of this Reminder upon him, expressed first explicitly and then allusively through what He hinted at, namely their plotting to kill him, and ended that by saying there is no escape for them from the punishment, because He is All-Seeing of their deeds which necessitate it, He mentioned what is among the subtle aspects of their deeds in their deep-rootedness in disbelief, in their enmity towards the chosen angels who are pure good, with no cause at all for hating them except disbelief. He began with mention of the One who sent down the Qur'an, because their enmity towards the one upon whom it was sent down, on account of what was sent down upon him, is enmity towards the One who sent it down, since he is the cause for which the enmity exists. So He said, commanding him (ﷺ), informing him of what He had perceived of their hidden scheming which called for their harm: ﴿Say﴾. Or it is said (and this is better, clearer and firmer): when He commanded him (ﷺ) with what indicated their lie in their claim that the Hereafter is exclusively theirs, and informed that they must surely be punished, He commanded him with another proof for both matters. So, if it is a proof for the first, it is linked to the first ﴿Say﴾ [al-Baqarah: 94] without a conjunction, which signals that each of the two proofs suffices for what it was brought for. And if it is a proof for the second, which He specified, it is an answer to someone as if he had said: Why does the extension of life not keep them away from the punishment? ﴿Say﴾ [p. 66] i.e., to these people who claimed that the abode of dominion is exclusively theirs while they are enemies of His chosen angels.

﴿Whoever﴾: it is an indefinite noun which includes rational beings, singly, in groups, and in totality, as said by al-Harrali.

﴿is an enemy to Jibril﴾: i.e., he harms only himself, for his harm cannot reach Him in any way. And his enmity is by his enmity towards him for the sake of God, who singled him out with nearness and chose him for His message. So this one who is hostile to him disbelieves at that point in all the Books of God and His messengers. Jibril: al-Harrali said: it is said that it is a name of servanthood, because "Il" is one of the names of God, Mighty and Majestic, in the Highest Assembly, and he is a hand of extension of God's Spirit into hearts, by which God gives them life from the Spirit of His command, returning them to Him in this abode before the return of the spirit of life by the hand of seizing from ʿIzrāʾīl, peace be upon him. End of quote.

Then He gave a reason for this omitted predicate by what pointed to it, saying: ﴿for he﴾, i.e., Jibril,

﴿has sent it down﴾, i.e., the Qur'an which they disbelieved in, out of their envy of the one upon whom it was sent down, after they used to seek victory through it; bringing what benefits them, calling to what sets them right [p. 67] and raises them up. Since the intent was to establish that it is the speech of God and that He commanded its delivery, He combined ﴿Say﴾ with ﴿upon your heart﴾, i.e., and it is the most perfect of hearts, rather than saying "upon my heart", which would correspond to "Say". The particle of elevation indicates that what was sent down settled in the heart, so its receptacles became submerged in it, and so it was manifest through him ﴿by the permission of God﴾, the Sovereign, the Greatest, to whom all command belongs. So no one has the right to deny what He has permitted, and the one who brought it did not transgress anything of what he was commanded. Permission is the removal of prohibition and the granting of capacity, by way of creation and bringing into being, as long as no decree of disposition prevents it, as said by al-Harrali.

﴿confirming what is before it﴾ of the Books of God, the greatest of which is their own Book. So they were the most entitled of people to believe in it, and Jibril, peace be upon him, was the most entitled of the angels to their love [p. 68] for bringing it down. Their disbelief in it was disbelief in what they themselves possessed, so there is no ground for their enmity towards him. Al-bayn is a dividing boundary, in sense or in meaning, as said by al-Harrali.

﴿and guidance﴾ to every good, because it clarifies what the obligations concerning the actions of the hearts and the limbs are about,

﴿and good news﴾, i.e., by clarifying the reward,

﴿for the believers﴾, i.e., those for whom faith is a constant attribute, so they do not distinguish between God's Books nor between His messengers, but wherever the truth leads them they submit. This does not include those who believed with their tongues. Nor does it include the one whom God knows would be such, even if he came before his (ﷺ) mission; God knows best what they were doing. Had they been believers, they would not have been hostile to the one through whom good news came to them, but they are disbelievers, so they are in punishment, and the Hereafter is not theirs, but rather against them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 98:

Since the enmity of one member of a group, by virtue of his belonging to that group, is enmity toward the whole group, He followed it with His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah﴾, the Possessor of Majesty and Honour, by his enmity toward one of His friends, by virtue of that person being among His friends,

﴿and His angels﴾ (p-69) who descend by His command,

﴿and His messengers﴾ from among humankind and others. Among them He singled out for mention those whom He favoured with grace, saying: ﴿and Gabriel and Michael﴾, for he [the enemy] has disbelieved and destroyed himself by his disbelief. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, the Supreme King, ﴿is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾, where He stated it openly and did not conceal it. He expressed it with a permanent attribute, turning the address away from those among them who take heed and return, so that enmity does not reach them for that reason. As for Michael, it is said that he is also a name of servitude, and that he is the hand of provision that extends the sustenance that sustains bodies, just as Israfil is the hand of extension for the spirits by which there is life. This was said by al-Harrali.

When he had finished encouraging them toward the Qur'an, by stating that it is from God and that it confirms their own Scripture, and (encouraging them) toward Gabriel, by stating that he is the one who brought it by God's leave, and when he had warned them against enmity toward him, he followed this with praise of this Qur'an, and that its matter is clear to whoever seeks the truth, even if some of them or others disbelieve in it. "Fasiq" means: one who goes outside what is known of the truth, for it is of such a nature that it is not hidden from anyone. So God, the Exalted, said, in continuation of His saying ﴿Indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by God's leave﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97], or of His saying ﴿And Moses had certainly come to you with clear proofs﴾ [al-Baqarah: 92], or with an implied meaning: "Thus it has become clear through this which Gabriel, peace be upon him, sent down that the Hereafter is not exclusively theirs, and that they are (p-70) among those whose sin has encompassed them because of their disbelief": ﴿And We have certainly sent down﴾: by Our greatness in this and in other things,

﴿to you﴾, while you are the greatest of creation,

﴿clear signs﴾ in showing your truthfulness and the soundness of your message. And "bayyinah" (clear proof) is the decisive evidence that distinguishes the true account from the false, so they transgressed by their disbelief in them,

﴿And none disbelieve in them﴾ among them or among others ﴿except the defiantly disobedient﴾, those for whom defiance (fisq) is a constant attribute. It is reported from al-Hasan that when "fisq" is used for a type of sin, it applies to its greatest form, such as disbelief and other things. (p-71) In this there is a return to the description of the Book, which is the aim of the surah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 100:

When He first denounced them for rejecting the Messengers, because they opposed their commands by following their desires, saying: ﴿Whenever a Messenger came to you, did you [not] follow your desires?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87], and followed it with what is suited to it, until He concluded that the signs of this Messenger are among the clear matters which their own Scripture attests, and that He had taken their covenant to follow him, as He guided to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then if guidance comes to you from Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 38], and so on, He now denounced them a second time for their disbelief in what the Messengers brought, saying: ﴿Whenever they make a covenant, a party of them throws it aside﴾. That is, it casts it away, treating it with contempt.

﴿A party of them﴾: that is, people whose concern is to cause division. Since this was open to two readings, a reading of minimization and a reading of maximization, because the tanwin (nunation, the "-n" suffix on the noun) is ambiguous between magnifying and belittling, He removed the possibility of minimization by saying: ﴿Rather﴾. That is, the disbelieving party that threw it aside is not the smallest of them; rather ﴿most of them do not believe﴾, neither now nor in the future.

Then he followed this denial with a mention of the Book and the Messenger, as he had done in the first denial, except that here he stated explicitly what he had concealed there. He said: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger﴾, i.e., great, whose call is all-encompassing, with what the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam, "the Greatest Name" of God) indicated in His words ﴿from God﴾, i.e., the King to whom belongs all sovereignty and command,

﴿confirming what was with them﴾, because he came with a Book whose being from God is verified by the inimitability (i'jaz) of its composition and by its confirmation of the meaning of their Book,

﴿a party of those who were given the Scripture threw away﴾, i.e., cast away with a casting of contempt, the first (party),

﴿the Book of God﴾, the Supreme King, concerning which He took their covenant through the tongue of their prophet to follow the Unlettered Prophet (ummi, "unlettered"). It was the worst casting away, by making it an object of their contempt,

﴿behind their backs﴾, by abandoning acting upon it, even if they adorned it with gold and placed it on chairs before them. He indicated their obstinacy by His words: ﴿as if they did not know﴾.

(p-73) Since it is a established practice of God that whoever extinguishes a sunnah (prophetic practice) is increased in abandonment, in that a bid'ah (innovation) is revived at his hands, the consequence for them was that they cast aside the Speech of God, the first of allies, and turned instead to the speech of the devils, who are the most hostile of enemies. So He, exalted, said: ﴿And they followed what they recited﴾. That is, what they recited or followed. He expressed it in the present tense to indicate its abundance, its spread, (p-73) and its continuance.

﴿The devils [recited] over the kingdom﴾, that is, at the time of the kingdom of ﴿Solomon﴾, ﴿of sorcery, which is disbelief﴾. Al-Harrali (al-Harallī) said: "Because its reality is a matter that is nullified by the mention of the name of God, and its effect appears in what it is restricted to, in imagination, insinuation and the like, by relying on it without the name of God, which is disbelief." End of quote. It seems that sorcery was in those days prominent and dominant, as the expression "over" (ʿalā) suggests. Better than this is that "tatlū" (recite) be understood as implying "takdhibu" (lie), so the meaning is: they recited falsehood concerning his kingdom, as indicated by what al-Baghawi and others narrated from al-Kalbi, and likewise what was related from al-Suddi. Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi said in the book Kitab al-Zinah: "It is related in a hadith: 'When Solomon, peace be upon him, died, the devils set about writing the kinds of sorcery: whoever wishes to attain such-and-such, let him do such-and-such. They put it in a book, then sealed it with Solomon's seal, and they wrote on its cover: This is the book of Asaf ibn Barkhiya the truthful, for Solomon ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, from the treasures of the stores of knowledge. Then they buried it beneath his throne. Afterwards, the remnants of the Children of Israel extracted it when they introduced what they introduced. When they discovered it, they said: The kingdom of Solomon was only by this. So they spread sorcery among the people; and it is found in no one more than in the Jews.'" End of quote.

(p-74) Solomon, according to what is mentioned at the beginning of the Gospel of Matthew, within the Gospel of Luke, is the son of David, son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Naasson, son of Amminadab, son of Ram, son of Joram, son of Azariah, son of Phares, son of Judah, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, peace be upon them all. The sum is that they, despite abandoning the Books which confirm what is with them, which are sufficient for every guidance and blessing, coming from God, who is loving toward His servants with every kindness, through the tongues of His messengers who are the most truthful, the most sincere and the most guided of people, and especially this inimitable Book, whose coming they used to rejoice in the nearness of the time of its bearer, they followed sorcery, which is the most harmful and most hideous of things, brought by the devils, who are the most hostile and most atrocious of enemies. And most astonishing of all in this is that they attributed sorcery to Solomon, peace be upon him, falsely and wickedly, and declared him an unbeliever because of it; then they were themselves the most eager of people to seek it, to associate with it in knowledge and practice, and it was found most among them. Thus they became witnesses against themselves with disbelief. Also among the subtle points: since His saying ﴿And We gave Moses the Book, and We followed him up with messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:87], and what follows it concerning the Books, the prophets and the messengers, from humans and angels, was its summation, the disbelievers among the People of the Book cast all of that aside and rejected it, and turned to sorcery, whose refutation was among the first and greatest miracles of their Prophet. So it is the most contrary thing to their law, while knowing that it harms them in both abodes and does not benefit them.

When the People of the Book believed, after the death of Solomon, peace be upon him, that sorcery was from him, and that the ordering of his kingdom over humans, jinn, birds, beasts and the wind was only by it, God, exalted, negated that about him by His saying: ﴿But Solomon did not disbelieve﴾. Al-Harrali said: "It is said that it is from salāmah (soundness/safety), for he was safe in his heart from attachment to what God, exalted, had granted him of his kingdom ﴿This is of the favor of my Lord, to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Naml 27:40], and it is one perfection in the kingdom of the visible world, of the four elements and what is among the created things." End of quote. That is: nothing of disbelief occurred from him, let alone by sorcery, which is the furthest of things from the signs of the prophets.

(p-75) ﴿But the devils disbelieved﴾.

Then He clarified their disbelief by His saying: ﴿teaching people﴾, that is, those who are compelled, who had not reached the age of those who believed, ﴿sorcery﴾, that is, that which they themselves produced, adorning it with its condition so that it would be believed to be effective in itself and the like, just as the prophets and their followers teach people the truth by clarifying its affair. And sorcery: al-Harrali said: it is the turning of the senses in what they perceive away from the customary aspect proper to them in their soundness, by a false cause, which is not established in the presence of the mention of God over it. And al-Karmani said: it is a matter that breaks habit, issuing from an evil soul, which cannot be unfailingly opposed. And al-Asfahani said: they differed about learning it in three ways: first, that it is forbidden; second, that it is disliked; third, that it is permissible. The truth is that if learning it is for practice, then it is forbidden, and if it is for guarding against it and not being deceived by it, then it is permissible. He said: What is meant by sorcery is that which is sought in its attainment through drawing near to the devil, of what a human cannot accomplish on his own; and that is not established except for one who is suited to it in wickedness and corruption of soul, for suitability is a condition of mutual support and cooperation. By this the sorcerer is distinguished from the saint and the prophet. As for what is marveled at, such as what the people of tricks do by means of instruments and medicines, or what the one with sleight of hand shows, it is not forbidden; and calling it sorcery is figurative, because of its subtlety, since in origin it is what its cause is hidden from.

His saying: ﴿and what﴾, that is, and they followed or they taught what,

﴿was sent down to the two angels﴾. Al-Harrali said: "In it is an indication that this imagining is of two kinds: one deposited in the cosmos, which is the affair of the devils, and one sent down from the unseen, which is what is learned from the two angels." He said: ﴿at Babylon﴾, to affirm their descent to the earth.

﴿Harut and Marut﴾ are a substitution for the two angels. As if they, when they were with the need for them, did not need anyone, (p-78) they were also described as two kings (malakayn), with a kasra on the lam. Al-Harrali's expression: "Two angels made into two kings on the earth." The verse is from God's showing the angels the excellence of the vicegerent. Then He clarified the counsel of the two angels by His saying: ﴿And not﴾, whereby He indicated that the sense is: and the two angels did not disbelieve as the devils disbelieved, for they did not teach ﴿anyone﴾, the addition of "min" in ﴿min aḥad﴾ being for emphasis of the comprehensiveness of the negation ﴿until they say: We are only a trial﴾, that is, in the form of a test from God to His servants, for He knows the news of him who chooses sorcery because of the immediate benefit it has over the matter of prophethood and so disbelieves, and of him who knows its reality lest he fall into it while not perceiving, and then leaves it, turning to the religion of God. And he used the singular for the one reported about, though they are two, because the word is a verbal noun (maṣdar), which is not dualized or pluralized. Al-Harrali said: The root of its meaning is from fatn al-dhahab (testing of gold), which is subjecting it to fire so that its essence appears and its good is separated from its bad. End of quote.

﴿So do not disbelieve﴾ by acting on what we teach you, for acting upon it is disbelief, or by believing that it is true and self-sufficient, dispensing with what has come from God, or that it is effective in itself,

﴿so they learn from the two of them what they cause division by﴾, in opposition to the two angels regarding the prohibition of that. He mentioned the division in its strongest connection so that what is less than it would be understood from it, and so He said: ﴿between a man and his wife﴾. And "al-mar'" (the man) is the name of one of the ages of (p-79) nature, by which a man shares with a woman and in which he has some superiority; its meaning is called al-marwah (manliness), as al-Harrali said.

When He mentioned the near cause of the harm, He returned it to that, to elevate the sharp mind to the highest ranks and to preserve it from believing what is not fitting. So He said: ﴿And they are not harmers﴾. It is from ḍarr (harm) – with fatḥah and ḍammah – which is what pains the outward body and what is connected to its sensible aspect, in contrast to adha (injury), which is the pain of the soul and what is connected to its states. The ḍammah in ḍurr indicates that it is from height and domination, and the fatḥah indicates that it is what comes from an equal or the like, and it rarely comes from one below except as injury. From it: ﴿They will not harm you except with injury﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:111]. Al-Harrali said so.

﴿with it, from anyone﴾. When He emphasized its comprehensiveness with kinds of emphasis, He followed it with a criterion of generality, so He said: ﴿except by the permission of God﴾, who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, with no equal to Him. In this is an announcement to them that the harm of it to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that weak harm when Labid ibn al-A'sam bewitched him, is only like the harm of other causes which may be hidden, so the affair of their harm is attributed to God, exalted; and which may be known, so the harm is attributed to them, as occurred to others among his brothers the prophets, from among them and from others. The knowledge is that the one who is effective in all of it in reality is God, exalted. What comes at His saying, exalted: ﴿And it is He who made for you the stars that you may be guided by them﴾ [al-An'am 6:97] in Surat al-An'am is of benefit to recall here.

Since what has preceded, though there is benefit for its practitioner according to his claim, its harm is greater than its benefit, He followed it with another category which the practitioner gains nothing from except harm. So the only thing that drives one to learn it is preferring to join Iblis and his party. So He said: ﴿And they learn﴾, that is, from the sorcery which the devils produced, not from the two angels,

﴿what harms them﴾, because mere practice of it is disbelief or disobedience. Then He established that it is entirely harm, with no admixture of benefit in it, by His saying: ﴿and does not benefit them﴾, (p-81) because it has no effect at all. Benefit is the arrival of what agrees with the outward body and what is connected to it, in contrast to harm. For this reason the disbelievers are often addressed with it, since both of its meanings occur in the outward, which is their aim from the outward of the life of this world. Al-Harrali said so.

Then He followed it with what is known that they committed knowingly, so He said, establishing and emphasizing: ﴿And they had certainly known﴾, as a clarification that they are the most foolish of people,

﴿that whoever purchased it﴾, that is, preferred it over what he knows to be beneficial of faith,

﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾, the enduring whose benefit endures,

﴿of any portion﴾, that is, any suitable share at all. Khalāq means the fitting portion for one to whom a share of a thing is allotted, as if it balances with his own created self and his created body. Al-Harrali said so.

Then He gathered for them the blameworthy qualities by way of emphasis, so He said: ﴿And wretched is that for which they sold themselves﴾, that is, they sold them out of obstinacy,

﴿with it, their souls﴾. This is an indication that it is among what has encompassed them, so their souls were uprooted from their origin, and so this necessitated for them eternal abiding in the Fire. Then He said, after establishing knowledge for them: ﴿If only they had known﴾, that is, if they had had the capacity to receive the arrivals of (p-82) the truth, indicating that this is not undertaken by one who has even the least knowledge; so their knowledge which led them to this boldness is in fact ignorance, rather ignorance is better than it.

When he had explained the harms they incurred by what they committed, he followed it with the benefits of turning away from it, and said: ﴿And if they had believed﴾, that is, in what they were called to from this Qur'an, and in the belief that the Agent in everything is none other than God, not magic,

﴿and had been mindful of God﴾, that is, of what would corrupt faith: adhering to what had been true but was then abrogated (naskh) from the Torah and so became false, and proceeding to what was never true at all, such as magic. They would have been rewarded with something better than what they gave up, for whoever abandons something, God compensates him with something better than it. This is the answer, but He expressed it in a way that implies permanence, continuance, nobility, and other qualities that minds fall short of comprehending in the eloquence of the Qur'an. So He said: ﴿Indeed, a reward﴾. The form *mathubah* is the pattern *maf'alah* from *thawab*, which is recompense with good. The form itself conveys elevation and stability, as al-Harrali said. He ennobled it by saying ﴿from God﴾, to whom belong all the attributes of perfection, and He increased its nobility by saying ﴿better﴾, with the comparative omitted.

Al-Harrali said: He equated this reward with the content of the message in both being from God, to honour this reward and to link it with the lofty order of His knowledge, wisdom, and the execution of His decree. End of quote. This reward is general, encompassing the goods of this world and the Hereafter, among which is what God gives to His righteous servants of the disposal of His Most Beautiful Names (*asma' husna*), according to what their meanings yield of benefits. Among this are the transmitted effects, such as the Opening Chapter being a cure, the Verse of the Throne being a protection from Satan, and similar benefits of the Qur'an, of invocations (*adhkar*), and of seeking blessing from the traces of the righteous, and the like.

Then He confirmed the report by saying that their knowledge was ignorance, with ﴿if only they knew﴾ [al-Baqarah: 102]. Al-Harrali said: In it is an indication of a rank of knowledge higher and more noble than the rank that was diverting them from taking up magic, because that rank makes one indifferent to knowing what is evil, while this one inspires desire to attain what is good. In it is also good news for this community, given what is in its constitution of acceptance of this knowledge, which is the knowledge of the Names and the benefits of the Qur'an, and which will be for them a substitute for the knowledge of *sīmiyā'* (a kind of occult science), which is a branch of magic. It may be of the kind revealed to the two angels. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever acquires knowledge from the stars has acquired a branch of magic, and the more he acquires, the more he has acquired."

The reality of *sīmiyā'* is a matter from God's affair which manifests its effects in the terrestrial world by means of names and evil spirits, from the places of trials in the heavenly realms, among the luminaries, the stars, and the figures. Whatever of it is presented in sciences and practices, nothing of it is established along with the Name of God Most High. Rather, its soundness requires that it be free of the Name of God, of His remembrance, of fulfilling His right, and of directing devotion and turning toward other than Him. Therefore it is unbelief, placed as a trial from God Most High for whomever He wills to test with it. Indeed the trial of the name *sīmiyā'* is, in the position of guiding the Name, like the names al-Lat and al-Uzza in relation to the guidance of the Name al-'Aziz. To God belongs the totality of creation and command, guidance and misguidance, to manifest His Word, which comprehends all paired opposites, whose ultimate end is division into two abodes: the abode of light, of the merciful kind, from His Name al-'Aziz al-Rahim, and the abode of fire, of the vengeful kind, from His Name al-Jabbar al-Muntaqim.

﴿And on the day the Hour arises, on that day they shall be divided﴾ [al-Rum: 14].

When He made harm in magic and the like, there was, as a reward for whoever among this community believed and was mindful of God, the Chapter of the Daybreak (al-Falaq) and the Chapter of Mankind (al-Nas), the two protective chapters, as a safeguard, an annulment, and a swallowing up of what the deceiving sorceresses' magic fabricates. They are a lasting, permanent substitute for this community, from the staff of Moses, so these two are the staff of this community, which swallows up what the sorceresses' magic fabricates, as a permanent substitute, through the charm they contain, which encompasses protection from the evil of the Daybreak, from a glimpse of which magic is scattered. These two are protective charms from beyond what lies beyond magic and the like. This is part of the reward of protection, together with what they were given of the reward of benefit. Hardly does anyone who has been granted this verse for this community stop at any limit of attaining good things and aspects of honour. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 104:

Since, as al-Harrali said, it is part of the truth that matters are carried out according to the judgment of what the Truth has affirmed, because by this they become truth, which is an example of the clear Truth, while diverting them to someone whom the Truth has not affirmed in its domain is falsehood and a turning away from its direction. It is then a baseless fancy in matters of opinion, in the same way as magic is to the senses. It is a fancy, for its attribution is not sound, and it is an example. He followed the verses that condemn genuine magic with a warning against metaphorical magic, by which they deceived the good and intended harm, so that the prohibition against it would be a prohibition against the first by way of priority. So He said, turning away from mention of them to address the believers, which is more specific than "O Children of Israel," which is itself more specific than ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21], ﴿O you who (p-٨٦) believe﴾, that is: you who have professed faith, affirm your profession of it, by ﴿not saying﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿"Ra'ina"﴾, which you intend as "watch over us" and "observe us" for the purpose of good and humility. The Jews seized upon it, because it matched a bad word in their language, and they began to twist their tongues with it, intending by it ruin (ru'una), which is extreme ignorance. So He forbade them from agreeing with them in speech, to prevent the correct word that matches in form from resembling the ugly one, and He replaced it for them with something that no corruption can reach, so He said: ﴿but say "Unzurna"﴾. Thus He preserved the meaning and changed the wording. Al-Harrali said: In this there is a requirement to correct the forms so that they match the correction of the intentions, and so that the difference between the two forms becomes as clear as the difference between the two meanings. Hence it is a verse of distinction specific to the Arabs. Al-Isfahani said: (p-٨٧) This prohibition was specific to that time. Al-Wahidi said: because of the consensus (ijma') of the Community that it is permissible to address with this expression now. He said: ﴿and listen﴾, that is: say what I have commanded you and obey all my commands, and do not be like the Jews in taking hearing in its literal sense, and their saying ﴿"We heard and we disobeyed"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 93]. The conjunction of ﴿and for the disbelievers﴾ with something not previously mentioned to be conjoined to it guides to the meaning that the implied sense is: indeed hearing, that is acceptance, is faith, and for those who listen there is a generous bounty, while turning away is disbelief, and for the disbelievers among the Jews and others there is ﴿a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 105:

When he had given guidance, he concluded the verse with the reason that moves one to comply. He gave another reason, saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book﴾ absolutely, namely the Jews and the Christians,

﴿nor the polytheists﴾ of any kind of polytheism (p-88), ﴿desire that there should be sent down to you﴾ out of hatred for you and envy of you, ﴿any good from your Lord﴾. He emphasized the comprehensiveness with his words ﴿any good from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to you. It is as if it were said: there are two reasons that drive one to listen and that impel him to it. The first is otherworldly, namely bliss for the obedient and punishment for the disobedient. The second is worldly, namely opposing the enemies, for they do not desire that anything good for you be sent down upon you, let alone that you should comply with it. Opposing the enemies is among the great aims for those firmly established in noble character, possessing complete faculties. He did not join ﴿desire﴾ with a conjunction because, together with that, it is a reason for the reason. It is as if it were said: for them is a painful punishment, because they desire good for you; so your hearing it is part of their punishment, since it occurs contrary to their wish, together with what is stored up for them in the Hereafter because of their disbelief and their wishing your disbelief. What incitement there is in these words and in those that follow toward the Book in which there is no doubt is not hidden.

When He, glorified be He, had explained what they desire, He followed it with the declaration that He has complete disposal, (that) whoever is pleased is pleased and whoever is angered is angered. So He said, attaching the matter to the all-comprehensive Greatest Name (p-89): ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., while they desire otherwise, and the state is that He, Possessor of the Most Beautiful Names, ﴿singles out﴾. Since the One who sends down is the most complete in mercy, He expressed it with His words: ﴿with His mercy﴾, which encompasses everything of guidance, knowledge and other than that,

﴿whomever He wills﴾, i.e., He makes him specially chosen, that is, singled out from among people by it, even if he is, in the estimation of others, of low standing, as the Arabs were in the eyes of the Children of Israel, given what they saw of their ignorance, misguidance, harshness and disordered conditions. "Ikhtisas" (specialization) is a care that enables the one singled out for a rank in which he stands apart from others. "Rahmah" (mercy) is the bestowal of what suits the one shown mercy in his outward and inward state; its lowest level is the removal of harm and the warding off of hurt, and its highest is being singled out by the lifting of the veil, as al-Harrali said. Since that might give the impression that when He does this, nothing of His mercy remains sufficient for anyone other than the one singled out, He negated it with His words, again prefacing it with the Greatest Name, conjoining it to what the specialization conveys, in a manner like saying (p-90), alluding to the Jews: ﴿So Allah is Knowing of whom He withholds mercy from,﴾

﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, to whom belongs all greatness and mercy, so there is no equal to Him,

﴿is Possessor of great bounty﴾, i.e., the One who cannot be confined by any limit and cannot be enclosed by any counting.

When Allah, glorified is He, prohibited the saying ﴿Raina﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:104] after having permitted it, and this was a case of *naskh* (abrogation, the replacement of a ruling by a later one), and He concluded what relates to it by describing Himself with great bounty, after the particularization which by its nature involves the transfer of benefits, whether dominion, religion, strength or knowledge, from one people to another, and the Jews held that their religion could not be abrogated, abrogation was for that reason among their objections to this religion and to this Book being a guidance for the God-fearing, because, in their claim, it is not permissible for God. They said: it entails *bada'* (the notion that something becomes apparent after it was not, a change of mind), with the *ba'* pronounced with a fatha and in its shortened form, which means that a thing appears, that is, becomes manifest after it was not, and this is not permissible for God, the Exalted. This is in addition to the fact that abrogation exists in their own Book which is among them, for in it God commanded them to enter the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis) after fighting the tyrants, and when they refused, He forbade them to enter it and prevented them from it and from fighting by power and command, as you will see from the text of the Torah in Surah al-Ma'idah, God willing [p. 91]. He also commanded them regarding Friday, and they differed about it, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, and it will come in His saying: ﴿The Sabbath was only prescribed for those who differed about it﴾ [al-Nahl 16:124]; they chose Saturday, so it was made obligatory for them and made strict upon them, and all meats and fats were made lawful for them. Then when they took the calf, He forbade them the fats.
