So He said, emphasizing the statement because it is on the tongue of the followers, who have more right to emphasis: ﴿and what was given to the prophets﴾, meaning all of them, those who came before and others, from what was sent down, in a book or otherwise, ﴿from their Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 136], the One who bestowed favour upon them with that, ﴿We make no distinction between any one of them﴾ in the matter of faith, despite the direction of commands to them, ﴿and to Him we are submitting﴾, meaning to their Lord, the One who favoured us by His favour to them, alone, ﴿Muslims﴾, meaning obedient outwardly after obedience inwardly, with no command of our own in it at all. Al-Harrali said: So He made to flow upon the tongues of those who believed from this Ummah, as a teaching for them, what He made to flow upon the tongues of the Tribes as speech from them. Thus the Arabs had more right to them than the Children of Israel, in that they are equal in religion even if they differ in Israelite lineage. End.

"Al-Asbat" is the plural of "sibt". Al-Qamus says: "al-sibt" (with kasra) is a son's son, and a tribe among the Jews, and its plural is "asbat". Al-Baydawi said: "al-asbat" is the plural of "sibt", which is the grandson, meaning the grandchildren of Ya'qub, his sons, and their offspring, for they are grandchildren of Ibrahim and Ishaq.

Al-Isfahani said: It has been said that the original meaning of "sibt" in the language is an intertwined tree with many branches from a single tree. Al-Baghawi said: "al-asbat" means the sons of Ya'qub, whose singular is "sibt". They are twelve tribes, and the sibt of a man is his grandson. From this it was said of al-Hasan and al-Husayn: "the two grandsons of the Messenger of Allah" (ﷺ). The asbat among the Children of Israel are like the tribes among the Arabs from the sons of Isma'il, and the peoples among the non-Arabs. Among the asbat there were prophets, so He said: "and what was sent down to them". It has also been said: they are the sons of Ya'qub from his loins, all of whom became prophets. End.

I say: This is what appears when you reflect on this verse together with the one after it and the verse of al-Nisa'. The asbat, meaning the tribes, included those who went astray, and Allah denied those who said they were Jews or Christians. In the verse of al-Nisa' He reported that He revealed to them. The asbat, meaning the sons of Ya'qub, have been counted as a group, and their expressions differed concerning them. What I have verified myself from the Torah, from several copies that are more authentic, is that it counted them at the end of its first book, then said at the beginning of its second book: "These are the names of the Children of Israel who entered Egypt with Ya'qub their father; each man entered with his household: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin, Dan, Naphtali, Gad and Asher; and Yusuf was in Egypt." End.

I say: Binyamin is the full brother of Yusuf, peace be upon them both. It is sometimes said of him "Binman"; of Reuben "Ruwbal"; of Simeon "Sham'an"; of Issachar "Iysakhar"; and of Zebulun "Zabulun" and "Zabulun". And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 2, verses 137–138:

When God Most High had mentioned what He had commanded them, and it was the very essence of guidance, what follows was its consequence. He expressed it with the particle of doubt (in), *fa-in*, to indicate that their faith, given the extreme coarseness, harshness, and boorishness they possess, is in the furthest degree of unlikelihood: ﴿Then if they believe﴾, that is, the People of the Book who wanted to make you their followers, ﴿in the like of﴾, that is, in the very same essence and reality ﴿what you believe in﴾, as its explanation will come in ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11] from al-Shura, so they would be followers of you. ﴿Then they are guided﴾, contrary to what they said: "Be guided like us." He used the reflexive form (*ihtadaw*, from *al-muta'awa'a*) because faith, when its proofs appear, agrees with the original natural disposition (*fitra*). As for disbelief, since it is contrary to the manifestation of faith and its impression upon the heart, being far from temperament, it does not occur except through a kind of treatment between desire and reason. And since it does not occur except after turning away from faith and its absence from clear sight, He expressed the commission of it with a form that indicates this, the *tafa''ul* pattern, and said: ﴿But if they turn away﴾. Al-Harrali said: In it is an indication of a believer among them and of a turning away by one who turns away among them, because when God Most High classifies the address, it is a report about the classification of the existence; He does not bring out His report about something that does not exist, so that it would be a report without existence. That is only the lowest of the attributes of some of the creation. ﴿Then they are only in opposition﴾, that is, they want to be on a side other than your side, because they know that guidance is in nothing other than it, as the particle *innama* (only) requires.

Since the necessary consequence of their opposition in this state is plotting and warfare, and this was on the basis of obstinacy, God, glorified is He, did not leave the sufficiency of His allies to anyone else, so this caused His saying: ﴿So God will suffice you against them﴾, that is, by a promise with no failure in it at all, even if it is delayed somewhat, by His power and His other attributes of perfection which the noble Name conveys. Sufficiency (*al-kifaya*) is making the one who resists independent of resisting his enemy, in a way that does not require him to repel it. Thus said al-Harrali. Since the one who opposes a person may plot against him either by speech or by action, and action is preceded by forming an intention in the heart, and since the one who suffices a person's sufficiency depends on knowledge of what is good for him, He said: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾, that is, of what your enemies say, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, of what they conceal. So He causes for every word and intention of theirs something that turns back its harm upon them. Your share from them is limited to harm in speech and ill will in the heart, while their share from you is subjugation, enslavement, and seizure of their lands and property.

Al-Harrali took ﴿the dye of God﴾ (*sibghat Allah*), that is, the form of the dyeing of the Sovereign on High, which is the adornment of the Muslim and his natural disposition, just as the dye is the adornment of what is dyed, as a state required by the meaning of the speech. He reproached the grammarians for knowing a state (*hal*) only from single words and hardly understanding states from a whole sentence. He said: *al-siyigha* is a rapid transformation by the swiftness of its revelation. He also said: Since this instruction was a revealed instruction, swift in transforming from the state of manifest error in which the Arabs were in their ignorance to the state of manifest guidance in which the prophets were in their guidance, without any period of time, He, exalted is He, made it a dye, as cloth is dyed in the moment, changing from one colour to another, in contrast to what the People of the Book dye their followers with, following their desires, such as what they call the *ghitas* (baptism by immersion). ﴿And who is better than God﴾, that is, He to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿in dye﴾, because it is a dye of the heart which does not fade, since it is steadfast by the One who protects it, the All-Knowing; whereas that is a dye of the body which does not benefit. In it is conveyed what is particular to those who believe of the transformation of their essence into light, as peace be upon him said: "O God, make me light." So what the essence of the imams was transformed into, the hearts of the community were dyed with. ﴿And to Him we are worshippers﴾, that is, exclusively, as a completion of the response to the address of the covenant of the Children of Israel, where He said: ﴿What will you worship after me?﴾ [al-Baqara: 133]. However, worship in the time of the Children of Israel preceded, and submission (*Islam*) is a definitive obligation, and submission in this instruction is a beginning, so that worship may occur as gratitude. He specifically chooses by His mercy whom He wills. He brought it with the attribute that is established and permanent, so in it is an indication that none of them will turn away from his religion out of displeasure with Him after faith has mingled with the brightness of his heart. This is a general share of protection, whose particular share is established for the Prophet (ﷺ) in the highest of his affairs. End.
