Given the instruction to translate exactly and not add notes, I should correct my previous output. Here is the faithful translation of the full passage:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 152:

Since it is known that this good, from which the person of insight turns away and which no one of even the least resolve falls short of, is something that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, mentioned to the Arabs as a favour from Him to them, after a long period of hardship, persistent ignorance, toil and weariness, He encouraged them to sustain it, linking it to what preceded it, and so He said: ﴿So remember Me﴾, that is, for the sake of My bounty upon you in this and in other things, ﴿I will remember you﴾, so I will open to you from the knowledge what does not fall under any limit, and I will ward off from you from the fears what does not fall under any limit. ﴿And be grateful to Me﴾ alone, without any partner [you associate with Me], I will increase you; and he emphasised this indication with his saying [...] ﴿And do not deny Me﴾, that is, I will strip you [of My favours]. Al-Harrali said: Since the Arabs had a great fondness for mentioning their fathers, their battles and their days, Allah, glorified and exalted be He, made His remembrance of them a substitute for what they used to mention, just as He made His Book a substitute for their poetry and for the lamentations of their mourning, by what delights them from His remembrance of them. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 153:

When He had concluded the verses commanding the turning toward the House (the Ka'bah) in prayer with the command to give thanks and to keep away from disbelief, and since that is the head of worship and its performer is in great need of help, He turned to His saying, exalted is He, in the Mother of the Book: ﴿You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], and so He commanded them with what this includes of patience (sabr) and prayer (salah), ﴿Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 45], knowing that they would comply, whereas the Children of Israel disobeyed when He commanded them with the like of this at the beginning of their stories, with His saying: ﴿And establish prayer, and give zakah, and bow with those who bow﴾ [al-Baqarah: 43], up to His saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult except for the humble (khashi'un)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45]. Thus there was in that an indication that they [the Muslims] are the humble ones. The placement of this verse was fitting, being after the harm the People of the Book inflicted upon them by attributing to them the invalidity of the religion through altering the rulings and similar speech, as in the other verse: ﴿You will surely hear much hurt from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah. But if you are patient and fear Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Al 'Imran: 186]. And its coming after the command to remember and give thanks is an allusion that the essence of each of them is patience and prayer. It is as if it were said: Do not turn your attention to the taunts of those who taunt concerning the matter of the qiblah, lest that occupy you from remembering Me and thanking Me; rather, be patient and pray to Me, facing the qiblah which I have commanded you, knowing that patience and prayer are an excellent help in every matter that befalls you, of religion and of worldly life. And more elegant than this is to say: When it was known from these verses that what lay between them and the foolish was a severe entanglement, and He commanded them with the effective remedy of turning away from them and turning toward His remembrance and thanks, He followed that to indicate that the matter reaches something more severe than they had imagined, so He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, addressing them in a manner that includes the perfect one (ﷺ), and perhaps He turned the address away from him because of what the context contains that protects his lofty station (ﷺ): ﴿Seek help through patience﴾, that is, in what you encounter from them and in turning toward Me, so that I may suffice you in every concern, ﴿and prayer﴾, for it is the greatest helper, since it is the most comprehensive of the acts of worship. Whoever turns to his Master with it, He will encompass him and suffice him, by his turning away from everything other than Him, for that is the way of every great matter with whoever turns wholly toward Him.

Since prayer cannot stand except with patience, He limited Himself to giving the reason with it and said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, He to whom belongs all perfection, ﴿is with the patient﴾, that is, and it is known that whoever Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is with, succeeds. Al-Harali (al-Harrali) said: The easiest form of patience is the soul's patience against its laziness, by compelling it toward energy in what it has been charged with: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾ [al-Talaq: 7], and ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. So when Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, eases for it diligence and resolve, He makes for it in what it was patient upon at the beginning a sweetness in it, and the duty of patience lightens for it. But when it does not endure against its laziness and in its diligence, it becomes defiled, and it is struck by punishments, upon which patience becomes harder than the first patience, just as whoever has patience against sweet food does not need to be patient against the bitterness of medicine. If it bears patience against the punishments of losing the first patience, a salvation from the intensifying of punishment upon it overtakes it; but if it does not show patience against those punishments, it falls into the destructions of severe torment, and it is said to its people: ﴿Be patient or do not be patient; it is all the same for you﴾ [al-Tur: 16]. Then he said: The beginning of religion is patience and its conclusion is ease, for whoever Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is with, He lifts from him the bitterness of patience by placing the sweetness of companionship, which the word [ma'a] (with) signals. Ended.

When the Exalted pointed them to what they would face from those who attacked their religion, and raised them step by step in that matter, He followed it with what indicates that the affair would reach killing, and what is close to it, so that they would prepare for it and make ready its equipment.

Al-Ḥarrālī said: Since patience for God is essentially the soul's bearing of what it dislikes, to which it is accustomed, the Truth, exalted is He, informed them that patience for Him is not in the accustomed sense, and that it is found in it when one endures, along with the sweetness of the pleasure of life. Although this is something that the sense of those who believe does not reach, because it is hidden from the grasp of the intellect, He informed them of what would move them to endure the hardship of patience in jihad in the way of God. So He said: ﴿And do not say﴾, coordinated with (p-249) what goes beyond matters that the blessing of jihad requires. End of quotation. That is: and fight them so that you may kill them and they may kill you, and so that you may plunder them and they may plunder you; and do not say [etc.].

Or it may be said: Since patience applies to matters the hardest of which is jihad, then the Ḥajj, then fasting, and since some of the Companions (may God be pleased with them all) had asked about those among them who had died facing the qibla of Bayt al-Maqdis, He explained to them their destination by His saying: ﴿And God would never let your faith be lost﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], immediately after the verse of patience, by clarifying the state of the martyrs among the believers who were slain in jihad, to repel the assumption that they were dead, and as a turning to what He had indicated concerning the affair moving toward war, where He censured those who prevent access to the Mosque, and informed that disgrace in this world through killing and captivity would befall them, and a great punishment in the Hereafter through the Fire and wrath. It also hints that He would permit them to confront those who had commanded them to be patient under their harm from the People of the Book, until the sword destroys them and abasement and fear settle upon them. So the meaning is: Be patient against all that the People of the Book and others say concerning the qibla and other matters, and against all that Satan attacks against the face of faith. Pray toward the House to which I have turned you, and fight everyone who opposes you until religion belongs to God, being patient against all that befalls you in that from killing, plundering and other things. And do not say, when you fight the disbelievers (p-250) who are hostile to you, from among the Arabs and others, and from the People of the Book and others, ﴿concerning those who are killed﴾ from among you ﴿in the way of God﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, by fighting so that the Word of God may be the highest, and not for anything else of worldly gain or tribal partisanship. For We will surely write jihad upon you, and We will take some of you as martyrs. Indeed they are ﴿dead﴾. Rather, say: they are martyrs, for they are not dead; ﴿rather﴾ they are ﴿alive﴾. And it will come in Āl ʿImrān that this is the meaning of the martyr.

Al-Ḥarrālī said: It is as if the Exalted negates for the warrior every likeness of what is disliked in every respect, even to the point of his being described as dead. So He protected him from the speech that, in their view, is among the most hated things to their souls, because their souls are attached to good remembrance. Then he said: He left their affair unspecified in this surah and negated the saying about them, because this is the surah of the Book to which creation is called, and He explicitly specified it in Āl ʿImrān, because it is the surah of God's standing (qiyām), through which the Truth became manifest; so He revealed the hidden aspect of His command in the surah of the manifestation of His command, and concealed it in the surah of the outward call to them. End of quotation.

Since the senses fall short of what the Glorified and Exalted has informed of, He said, drawing attention to this: ﴿But you do not perceive﴾ that they are alive, just as you see sleepers lying still (p-251) who do not move, and you have no awareness of those among them who are watching, dreaming from something other than them. So there is no greater honor than this in this world, and no more pleasant life than it in the Hereafter. As for the one slain from among your enemies, he has in this world only disgrace and humiliation through subjugation, abasement, shame and punishment, which has no end in the Hereafter. Al-Ḥarrālī said: He stated this by negation with the word "lā" and the form of permanence, so this informs that those who believe do not, by their rank, have awareness of it at all, unless God elevates them through the growth of the hearts' purity and the souls' clarity to what is above that, from the purity of the believers to the purity of the doers of good, who witness from the unseen what one at the rank of those who believe does not witness. End of quotation. In this there is an indication that God's being with them does not prevent that some of them be taken as martyrs; rather, that is among the fruits of God's being with them, for whoever is martyred among them attains the happiness of the Hereafter, and whoever remains attains the happiness of both abodes. The summary of this is that, since the essential point of what preceded in this surah (p-252) is that all the people of the earth, near and far, idolaters and People of the Book, are united in enmity toward the people of this religion, and since He often commanded them to be patient against their harm, the souls became greatly eager to know whether there would be any action after this restraint. So He indicated that after patience against the harm of the tongue, He would command patience against the blows of the sword and the spear, as a general command. So He said, joining this prohibition to the command of patience: that is, be patient now against this harm, then be patient when I command you to jihad against the impact of swords and the plunging into deaths, and the loss of those among you who are killed; and do not describe them as dead. Perhaps He surprised them with what this verse contains, to prepare them for being killed in His way, since their longing for war had greatly increased. He gave them the good news that the one slain in it is alive, even if seen as dead, as a consolation for them concerning this great event and this grave calamity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 155:

Since the nature of the clay from which humankind and its offspring are made is that it cannot be purified of impurities except after severe effort, do you not see that gold, though refined, is never free of adulteration and is not cleansed of the filth mixed with it except through the test of intense fire? (p-253) God, the Exalted, said, teaching them through the discipline by which purification is achieved, namely the hardship that comes from confronting the disbelievers and contending with the people of the abode of ruin: ﴿And We will surely test you﴾. It is coordinated with what the context implies, such as His words: "So We will command you to fight everyone whom We previously commanded you to treat with courtesy, and the people of the earth will surely band together against you. And We will surely test you," that is, He will afflict you with things in a way that resembles the act of one who tests your conditions, so that the patient may be distinguished from the one who panics. Al-Harrali said: The first patience, that is in ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ (2:153), is patience against laziness and for action, and the second patience, that is in ﴿And give good tidings to the patient﴾, is patience over the calamities of this world. Therefore this verse, ﴿And We will surely test you﴾, is strung together with these verses by way of coordination and transition to matters taken up by those who do not strive in the way of God out of weakness in restraining the self from the dislike of fighting: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, though it is hateful to you﴾ (2:216). Whoever does not bear the first patience by striving, is seized by matters that are afflictions (p-254) within his inner self, which the address passed over and then turned to, saying: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear﴾, which is the self's apprehension of visible matters that harm it, ﴿and hunger﴾, which is the overwhelming of the self by the need for food, to the point that it is driven toward it without considering its consequences. If it occurs without such overwhelming need, it is called al-gharath (a mild hunger), so there is a certain affliction in hunger, and al-gharath is a customary occurrence. He also said: Hunger is the emptying of the body of what sustains it, just as the emptying of the self of security, which is a kind of sustenance for it, deprives it of both sustaining factors: in its own essence through fear, and in its body through hunger, when it does not endure the dislike of striving. For those who endure it, this was easier than enduring fear and hunger. Whichever of these came first to them in this trial, the fear, when they feared the enemy for their own selves and he came to their dwellings, or the hunger, the one who does not walk to his physician in order to rest will have the physician come to his destruction. There is a vast difference between the fear of the warrior facing the enemy in his own territory and the fear of one besieged among his family. Likewise, there is a vast difference between the provisions of the warrior and the provision of the one who strives, and the best provision is taqwa (God-consciousness) on His path for his striving, and between the hunger of the one who stayed behind in his household. End of quotation. The word "a thing" (shay') and what follows it are indefinite, to urge gratitude, indicating that whatever afflicts them of these (p-255) is within the power of God to inflict something greater, so that not being struck by it is a blessing.

Since hunger may come from voluntary discipline, He clarified that it comes from need by His words: ﴿and loss﴾, which is falling short of sufficiency, ﴿of wealth﴾, that is, the bounties from which their food came. Al-Harrali said: Because that is the customary usage of the word "wealth" among them. He also said: [and wealth] is what belongs to the one who possesses it, and it is to him like a part of himself, so the one who owns it has that as a part of him. Thus God, the Exalted, multiplied the examples of affliction in their very selves and bodies, in order to cut off from them the ease of expecting sufficiency from wealth, in exchange for what the warrior attains of booty, provision and spoils. The warrior is secure among his army, provided for on his journey, and enriched by taking from his enemy, while the one who stays behind is afraid among his family, hungry in his household, and lacking in wealth in his possession. End of quotation.

Since that might arise from excessive abundance, He said: ﴿and lives﴾. Al-Harrali said: In this there is an indication that whoever strives, his numbers increase and his offspring multiply, and whoever is lazy, his numbers decrease and his descendants pass away. Implicit in this is an indication that the one who is lazy (p-256) will be reaped by the scourges of death, such as plague and pestilence, and others. End of quotation. He also said: ﴿and fruits﴾, which are the trees themselves, by which the self and the body are sustained, singled out for mention because they are the greatest wealth of the Ansar (the Helpers of Medina), who are among the people most especially addressed by this mention, particularly at the time these verses were revealed, which was the very beginning of the Hijrah (emigration).

Since the context guides toward the implied meaning, "So warn the one who does not endure," but this was omitted out of reverence for those who believed, lest there be among them one who does not endure, He linked it to that as guidance toward it and as an exhortation to patience. Then He mentioned the things that make victory necessary by His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the patient﴾. Al-Harrali said: Since this affliction arises from laziness in the first patience, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ (13:11), and since patience in it is among the things that can make up for it, God, the Exalted, made up for this rank with the good tidings for the patient, saving them from the ruin that befalls the one who does not endure this calamity (p-257) and who becomes distressed, complains, and grows resentful over it. Thus the first patient one has the companionship expressed in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ (2:153).

When the reward for the second group of patient ones was good news of safety from the punishment of the Hereafter, and their attainment of what He bestowed upon them, and the difference is vast between one who has God with him and one to whom it was said to His Prophet, "Give him good news of his patience through the trial of being left behind," and since human souls had no role in bearing patience out of nobility and jealous protection of lineage and worldly rank, the Exalted One singled out from among the patient those who are patient for Him alone, by natural disposition and by compelling themselves. He said: ﴿Those who, when a misfortune strikes them﴾. "Iṣāba" (striking) means the arrow hitting the target at the point it was aimed at, whether that is in accordance with the self's desire or contrary to it. "Muṣība" (misfortune) is a term whose usage has become restricted to what is disagreeable, due to the specific mention of it. End of quotation. The intended meaning is any misfortune whatsoever, even if small and weak, as indicated by the feminine form of the verb. ﴿They say: "Indeed we belong to God"﴾, that is, to the King who encompasses everything, submitting themselves to their Lord. So He does with us, through this misfortune and others, what He wills, and He is the one asked to make that the better course for us.

Since "belonging to God" was an explanation of their being His, establishing submission to Him, meaning "we are His initiators," He followed it with ﴿and indeed to Him we are returning﴾, that is, not to anyone else, meaning that none of our affairs happens except by Him, and as a reckoning for the resurrection and the manifestation of that afterward, a complete manifestation. Al-Ḥarrālī said: so that this be a culmination in the submission of their fruits, their wealth, and what they lost of themselves. Since they did not strive in the way of God, and misfortunes struck them, their making up for it was to surrender their affair to God, to remember their return to Him, and to feel that what was taken from their selves and what accompanied it is a store with Him. That would be a witness to their faith and their hope in meeting Him, so their striving against their own selves in this matter takes the place of their striving in the way of God that they missed. He made it comprehensive and unrestricted for everyone who is struck by a misfortune and then says "to God we belong," so that his reward for what he was afflicted with is confirmed, and God meets him with guidance to what that statement fell short of. He said: ﴿Those﴾, addressing His Prophet and bringing them to mind at a position of distance from His nearness and an absence from His attention toward them. He said: ﴿Upon them are blessings﴾. The blessing of God upon His servants is His turning toward them with His kindness, bringing them out of a state of darkness into the elevation of light. He said: ﴿It is He who blesses you, and His angels, to bring you out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 43]. So by their blessings upon them is their being brought out from the aspects of those tribulations that had befallen them. For this reason it was expressed in the plural, "ṣalawāt," and not in the singular, to enumerate what befell them according to the number of those tribulations. In His saying ﴿from their Lord﴾ is an indication of their gradual progression in that, by the rule of nurture and the remedying of the states that befell them. He said: ﴿And mercy﴾, singular, indicating its attainment by them after the preceding blessings upon them. Mercy reached them collectively when the blessings brought them out individually. He said: ﴿And those﴾, a reference to those whom the blessings and mercy reached, and He kept them, together with that, at a position of distance in the presence and in an absence in the address ﴿they are the guided ones﴾. He came with the word "hum" (they) to indicate the soundness of their inner selves from what the trial had drawn out of their souls. End of quotation.

What appears to me is that the particle of distance in ﴿those﴾ indicates the loftiness of their station and the honour of their aims. For this reason He expressed their guidance by the nominal sentence in a way that conveys restriction. Ṣalāh is bestowal of favour with what calls for honouring, and raḥmah is bestowal of favour with what calls for tenderness and compassion. God, glorified and exalted, is the one who grants success. In this is an indication of the command to turn away from the People of the Book in what they attack them with by their tongues, and to leave them be until the time of permission to confront them with spears and to clash against them with white swords, as in the other verse: ﴿You will surely be tested in your wealth and your selves﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 186] to its end. It is possible that "fear" is intended to mean "jihād," "hunger" to mean "fasting," the "loss of wealth" to mean the zakāt on silver and money, "the selves" to mean the zakāt on animals, and "the fruits" to mean their zakāt. However, the most fitting interpretation for the opening and closing of the verse and for what precedes and follows it is that it be restricted to jihād.

(p-262) When he had finished with what he intended concerning the states of those who censured the qiblah, which is "a means of standing for the people," and what followed from that, namely the disputes and combats in which they engaged in establishing the religion, and when he had concluded that with guidance, he began to mention the sacred sites through which the House was "a means of standing for the people." These sites lead to every good and protect against every harm, and their stations were made signs of the Hour. This is especially so because the Hajj is the brother of jihad in hardship and in leaving one's homeland. The Prophet ﷺ called it one of the two jihads, although it is among the greatest aims of the House mentioned in these verses. Its virtues are recited, its merits are established, and its rites, which are in reality its pillars, are: i'tikaf (retreat in the mosque), prayer, and circumambulation. [The reference] to its Hajj and 'Umrah is indicated by His words: ﴿a place of return for the people and a sanctuary﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125]. After that allusion, He made it clear to some extent, since none of its great distinctions remained except this. He joined to it the 'Umrah, the lesser Hajj, because it shares with the Hajj in displaying its glory and raising its beacon. So He said: ﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah﴾. This is like a justification for the House's deserving to be (p-263) a qiblah. He defined them because they are two well-known mountains facing the Ka'bah. The name Safa comes from ṣafwah (purity), which is what is cleared of turbidity, and the name Marwah comes from marw, which is stone that has been shaped. So said al-Harralli. He singled them out here to indicate that the blessing of turning to them, in accordance with what Allah the Glorified and Exalted has legislated, brings life to hearts through what was sent down to this Messenger ﷺ of the Book and the Wisdom, which remain until the end of time, as a healing for hearts and a purification for souls, increasing blessing through the attribute of gratitude and instructing through the attribute of knowledge. Just as turning to the sa'y (running) between them was a submission to the command of Allah, it was also a means of giving life to their father Isma'il, peace be upon him, and benefiting those after him through the water of Zamzam that gushed forth for him, which remains until the Hour arrives, as food for the eater and a cure for the sick. In this, along with mentioning Safa first, there is an indication for the perceptive among the people of hearts that the one who is patient for Allah, the one given glad tidings in what precedes, should have a heart that combines firmness and purity. Thus, by its stony firmness it prevents the satanic interruptions, and by its glassy tenderness it gathers the divine lights, far from a heart that is watery in its firmness, and far from a stony one in its clarity and luminosity. Among the greatest connections also is that (p-264) the route of the Hajj at that time was blocked by the enemies of war. So it is as if it were a cause for what precedes it, and as if it were said: "We will surely test you with what has been mentioned, because the Hajj is among the greatest rites of this House, which you were commanded to face, and it is among what is made obligatory upon you, and its route is blocked by those whom you know. So We will surely test you by fighting them, to remove the obstacle to the Hajj, and by fighting others among the People of the Book and others, to complete the favor through the perfection of the religion and its dominance over every religion." Among its excellent aspects also is this: when He, the Exalted, mentioned the afflictions of loss of wealth because of sins, ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is for what your hands have earned﴾ [al-Shura: 30], He followed it with the remedy that repairs that loss, in religion and in worldly affairs. "Indeed, the Hajj and 'Umrah remove poverty and sins, as the bellows removes the impurity of gold and silver." This was narrated by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Hibban in their Sahihs, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ. It was also narrated from a number of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, as I have explained in my book al-Ittila' 'ala Hujjat al-Wada' (Awareness of the Farewell Pilgrimage).

Al-Harralli said: When mention had preceded of a comprehensive matter concerning the Hajj in His words, the Glorified and Exalted, ﴿and that I may complete My favor upon you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 150], inasmuch as the favor attributed to Him is more deserving of the favor of religion, and within it is the favor of this world, which the Hajj could not have been arranged without: conquest, victory, and dominance over all of the Arabs. As He said concerning what He sent down on the day of completion of the Hajj, which is (p-265) the Day of 'Arafah: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3]. This was through what Allah the Glorified and Exalted completed for them of the favor of the complete landmarks of the religion and the establishment of conquest, through the conquest of Umm al-Qura, in whose conquest is the conquest of the whole earth, because it is the means of standing for the people. He, the Exalted, arranged through what He recited after it of address, a detail from the details of the command of the Hajj, in harmony with the command of those who believed, inasmuch as in the cause of its revelation there was the scruple of those who had been informed that the sin was lifted from them. They were a group of the Ansar who used to assume the state of ihram for Manat, which was situated at Qudayd, so they felt scruples about circumambulating between Safa and Marwah. Another group also feared that the practices they had carried out in the Jahiliyyah would, after they became Muslims, constitute a deficiency in their Islamic acts. So Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, informed them that this was lifted from them because of the varying intentions, for actions are by intentions. Whatever was intended for Allah was for Allah, and it was not tainted by conformity with their customs from the Jahiliyyah. In its jurisprudence is the validity of prostrating to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, for one who is compelled to prostrate to an idol. Within that is also the validity of worshipping Allah with a word of disbelief for one who is compelled to say it. He ﷺ permitted, more than once, that a speaker say about him something that agrees with the disbelievers, with good intention on the part of the speaker and to fulfill a need of his worldly affairs among the disbelievers. Thus it became clear that he ﷺ was (p-266) a mercy to the worlds, accepting the inner intentions and not minding the outward appearances in cases of necessity. So Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, lifted the sin from them because of the goodness of their intentions and their sincerity to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, in their deeds. Thus, through this kind of shortcoming in this rank, the opening of this address was connected to what preceded it concerning the states of those who believed among those tested by what has been mentioned. End of quotation.

﴿Among the symbols of Allah﴾, that is, among the markers of the religion of the Supreme King, before whose majesty everything submits. Al-Harralli said: The symbols are what hearts perceive of His right, and he said: The sha'irah (symbol) is what hearts perceive of inward matters. ﴿That is so. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾ [al-Hajj: 32]. He mentioned them, the Exalted, by the term "symbols," and their practice is among the markers of Islam (p-267) and a sacred thing among the sacred things of Allah. Since He had judged concerning the matter of the hearts, in which their scruple was lodged, from the point of view that He reminded them through the sha'irah, sincerity and intention made it correct. ﴿So whoever performs Hajj﴾, from the Hajj, which is the repeated intention toward what is desired for its goodness and righteousness. Al-Isfahani said: Its root is the increase of something you magnify. End of quotation.

﴿the House﴾. He mentioned the House in connection with the Hajj and the Masjid al-Haram in connection with turning, because the circumambulation ends at the House, and the praying place extends from the limit of the Maqam to what is beyond it, since the one circumambulating reaches the House, and the one praying stands in a place of courtesy that keeps him, at the end of the circumambulator's route, from being near the House. He mentioned it, the Exalted, with the word "whoever," which is unrestricted and covers those of understanding, avoiding the address being limited to those who felt scruples. So in its generality there is an indication that the Hajj is not prevented by anything that occurs in its places of the blameworthy matters of the religion, because the pilgrim is occupied with what he is in, away from everything else. Thus, in its hidden jurisprudence is the pilgrim's turning away from the evil practices of those places, which appear there according to the times and eras. This is confirmed by the fact that the Hajj is a sign of the Gathering and of the people of the Gathering: ﴿For every person among them, that Day, there will be a matter that occupies him﴾ [Abasa: 37]. Likewise (p-268) is the ruling for what is its sign. The Hajj to the House, which is the coming to it at the end of the year of months, namely the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, is that it concludes one's life, just as the Prophet ﷺ, whom Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, concluded his life with the act of Hajj. He, the Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿or performs 'Umrah﴾. He mentioned 'Umrah together with Hajj because circumambulation between Safa and Marwah is among the symbols of both acts. ﴿there is no blame﴾, and blame is accountability for leaning away, and leaning is deviation from the main road of intention. End of quotation.

﴿upon him to go around﴾, that is, to go around with determination, intention, and vigor, ﴿between them﴾, beginning with what Allah began with. Al-Harralli said: Lifting blame from an act is a ruling in which the permissible, the obligatory, the required, and the optional all share, to the extent that it is correct to say: "There is no blame upon you for praying Dhuhr," just as one says: "There is no blame upon you for eating if you are hungry." What indicates permissibility and optionality is the negation of blame regarding abandoning the act, not regarding doing it. As the Prophet ﷺ said, peace be upon him, to those who asked him about 'azl (withdrawal during intercourse): "There is no blame upon you if you do not do it," meaning: if you do not ejaculate outside, because the act is a metaphor for affirmation, not for abandonment, which is the meaning of 'azl. This is what 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, established when 'Urwah said: (p-269) "I do not see any blame on anyone for not circumambulating between them." She said: "If it were as you say, it would be: 'There is no blame upon him for not circumambulating between them,'" and she related the hadith. I say: Perhaps the expression by negation was chosen to indicate the negation of what they had imagined, by direct correspondence. The indication of obligation occurs through the implication of the consequence, because whoever performs Hajj or 'Umrah and does not circumambulate between them would incur difficulty. It also occurs through the Sunnah that explained it, in his ﷺ saying: "Perform the sa'y, for Allah has prescribed for you the sa'y," and through his ﷺ action together with his saying: "Take your rites from me," and through those who counted them among the symbols, and the like. Al-Harralli said: As for what has been narrated of the recitation of those who read "that he not circumambulate between them," the "lā" there is not a negation in the same sense as what 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, negated. Rather, it is emphatic for the affirmation, like His words: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ [al-A'raf: 12] and ﴿so that the People of the Scripture may know﴾ [al-Hadid: 29]. This is because a feature of the ambiguous is its use in opposites of negation and affirmation, just as "mā" is used for negation and affirmation, and likewise "lā" came in the language of the Arabs with the same function in usage, though less well known. The Qur'an's wording is to be taken according to the highest level of the Arabic language and its most eloquent form, and no one can reach the correction of its Arabic who limits himself, in grammar and literature, to what falls short of the utmost degree, because of its loftiness in the rank of Arabic: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an, that you may understand﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 3]. End of quotation. Those who read with the addition of "lā" were 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas (with a difference of report from him), Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Mas'ud, Anas ibn Malik, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Muhammad ibn Sirin, [and Maymun ibn Mihran, as Abu al-Fath 'Uthman ibn Jinni related in his book al-Muhtasab fi Tawjih al-Qira'at (The Reasoned Account of the Justification of Irregular Readings)], which are irregular readings. The meaning of 'A'ishah's statement, "it would have been that he not circumambulate," is specifically that he not circumambulate, and no reading with the affirmative has come down. As for the affirmative reading, the meaning guides to the conclusion that the reading of negation is like it, because their being among the symbols requires circumambulating them, not neglecting them. And Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, knows best. Al-Harralli said: And His mention (p-271) the Exalted of circumambulating, which is the form tafa''ul, meaning an assimilation to circumambulation, and His connection of the House with circumambulation in His words: ﴿that you purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125], because the sa'y is a going back and forth over a long distance, while the intended sense is encompassing both of them. So in meaning it was like circumambulation, though not in form, so He made it a tatawwuf for this reason, meaning an assimilation to circumambulation. End of quotation.

Since the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, intended by abandoning the sa'i between them nothing but obedience, they were informed that the sa'i between them is an act of obedience. He therefore expressed it in terms that convey their praise, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾. Al-Harrali said: that is, he burdens himself with maintaining righteousness and goodness without being solicited to it. ﴿Good﴾ here indicates the excellence of spending on the Hajj and 'Umrah, through the offering (al-hady) and the various kinds of provisions for the companions, by what the word "good" conveys, because its customary usage is for good provision and spending, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And indeed he is intense in his love of good﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 8], and ﴿if he leaves behind good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 180]. And since lifting the blame (raf' al-junah) is a form of abandonment, He balanced it in the address by affirming a deed of good, so that in the address there would occur an affirmation that conveys action, since the first only conveyed abandonment. Thus, whoever is truly established in faith lavishes his expenses on his journey (wifadah) to his Lord and economizes on the aims of his own self, whereas whoever is deprived of the fair share of his worldly life limits his expenses on his journey to his Lord and lavishes his expenses on the aims of his self and the desires of his dependents. That is among the signs of believers and the signs of the ignorant. Whoever visits a king lavishes what he presents before him; he has in truth presented it for himself, not for his Lord. Whoever thanks Allah's blessing by displaying it at the time of the visit, upon him in the sign of sending to Him and meeting Him, Allah will thank him for that on the day he meets Him. So Allah's gifts to him on the Day of Resurrection will be greater than his gift to Him on the day of visiting Him in his Hajj and 'Umrah. ﴿Then indeed Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿is Shakir﴾, that is, He rewards deeds, with multiplication of their reward. Al-Harrali said: His saying ﴿All-Knowing﴾ contains a warning against the entryways of showing-off (riya') and reputation-seeking in lavishing expenses, because of what dominates the self of vanity in displaying goodness. End.

When it had already been established that some of the People of the Book conceal what they know of this, he followed it with what was appended to it, concluding with the two attributes of *Shukr* (gratitude) and *ʿIlm* (knowledge), as encouragement and warning: He is grateful to whoever does what He has prescribed for him, and He knows whoever conceals it, however subtle his action is. (p. 273) Since their concealment went to great lengths, the discourse turned to rebuking the hypocrites among them, and to cursing those who openly declared their curse for their concealing of the truth they know. All of this, in reality, concerns their stories, and moving on to other matters is merely *istitrad* (digression), in the wise and clear style. This is because this Book is guidance, and the context indicates that the implied meaning after ﴿Grateful, All-Knowing﴾ [2:158] is: "and whoever introduces evil, then Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful." So he joined to it, as a new sentence, a statement in a manner that encompasses them and others: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal﴾ as an explanation of their recompense, ﴿what We have sent down﴾, that is, by Our greatness. Al-Harrali said: this verse thus unites, in its conclusion, this address with what passed at its beginning, the saying: ﴿And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know﴾ [2:42]. So the beginning was specific and the conclusion general, so that what is in the Book of Allah is a command in the same manner as the command of Muhammad ﷺ and of the messengers before him was addressed to creation, so that the command applies to creation at the beginning and the end in one uniform application. Thus it covers every concealer among the earlier and later generations. — End of quote. ﴿from the clear proofs﴾, that is, those which the listener free of desire does not need anything beside them to understand. (p. 274) Al-Harrali said: in its clarity, then, is a warning against concealing what is hidden of knowledge from minds that have not reached it. — End of quote.

﴿And the guidance﴾, that is, that which by its nature leads whoever loves it to a straight path.

Since the intended warning concerns concealment at any time, however brief, he affirmed the preposition and said ﴿after what We have made clear﴾, that is, by Our greatness, ﴿to the people﴾, that is, those who are at the lowest levels of those addressed. In this there is a great rebuke to the Children of Israel, for they are among the foremost intended by this because of their concealing what they possess. Al-Harrali said: because those named "people" are of the lesser age of hearts, as was mentioned, and most of what is specific to them, as was previously stated, are kings, tribal chiefs, and their followers, whom the love of desires has made attractive. — End of quote.

﴿in the Book﴾, that is, the one that gathers all good. (p. 275) Al-Harrali said: what Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has made clear in the Book may not be concealed, because of what was mentioned, that the Book is what contains the rulings and the limits, unlike what is specific to the *Furqan* or rises to the rank of the Qur'an. — End of quote.

Since the present tense indicates continuous renewal, and persistence that continues until death indicates a bad disposition, he dropped the *fa'* of causation, indicating that they deserve disgrace in reality, without regard to any cause. So he said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the distant and detested, ﴿Allah curses them﴾, that is, the Greatest King expels them with the expulsion of disgrace and humiliation, ﴿and the cursers curse them﴾, that is, everyone who is capable of cursing; that is, they are prepared for it, and then it actually befalls them when the veil is lifted. Cursing is the casting of a thing down to its lowest place, until it stands in rank like the action of the common folk. This was said by al-Harrali. More specific and easier to grasp is to say: since the hardest patience is that over the loss of what is beloved, such as familiarity, security, and ease, and since it was known that the enmity of the disbelievers toward them would lead to their being tested with that, he followed the verse of patience with His saying ﴿And do not say﴾ [2:154] the two verses, as if it were said: "And do not say such-and-such, for jihad will certainly be prescribed for you in general," ﴿and We will surely test you﴾ [2:155] in it ﴿with something of fear﴾ [2:155], the verse, because al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah, (p. 276) and your reaching them is prevented by the disbelievers, so in the conquest there must be fighting against them, and such affliction has been the custom in warfare.

When the matter of the qibla and what followed from it was complete, and the passage was concluded with the law of the obligatory pilgrimage (ḥajj) on people in general, whose command was given by the builder of the House, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, on the command of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, through his saying when the Station stood: "O people! Pilgrimage has been prescribed for you, so make pilgrimage." Those whom Allah, glorified and exalted be He, knew would make pilgrimage answered him. Then the prophets from the Children of Israel, the sons of Ibrahim, peace be upon them both, made pilgrimage. Then the People of the Book concealed it among what they concealed from their Scripture, out of envy of the Arabs. The verse on pilgrimage was concluded with "Knowing" (ʿalīm), which returns to the matter of those who conceal, "who conceal the truth while they know" (Qur'an 2:146). The greatest of what they concealed was the matter of this Book, which is the guidance with which the surah opens.

When He stated their recompense, He made an exception for those who repent, specifying the three conditions of repentance, saying: ﴿Except those who repent﴾, by regret for committing the sin; ﴿and make amends﴾, by resolving not to return to it; ﴿and make clear﴾ what they had concealed. Thus their repentance became manifest through giving it up.

Since a person loves what is caused by himself, He encouraged them, after their repentance, to turn back (to Him), making it a cause of His own repentance and mercy, even though all of that is, in reality, a favour from Him. So He said, expressing it with the particle fa' (therefore): ﴿Those – I shall turn to them﴾, meaning: I shall accept their repentance, and I shall preserve them, by what the pattern of the verb (mithāl al-fiʿl, the morphological form) indicates, namely continuity, in what I have enabled them to begin. In linking with fa' there is an indication of the swiftness with which Allah's repentance rescues them from the fire of fear and regret, as a mercy from Him toward them by raising them to the place of intimacy. For the fire of fear in this world, for one who has committed sin, is a mercy from the punishment of the Fire, redeeming him from the fire of severity in the Hereafter. Whoever is not burned by the fire of striving, the fire of fear burns him; and whoever is not burned by the fire of fear, the fire of severity burns him. This was conveyed by al-Ḥarrālī.

Since it is in human nature to repeat sins, owing to forgetfulness, He concluded the verse with what indicates that the implied sense is: "Indeed I love those who turn back in repentance." So He said: ﴿And I am the Ever-Returning﴾, meaning: time after time, toward whoever returns to sin and then comes back to repentance again and again, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ toward whoever does what pleases Me.

[p-277]

[p-278] When He had cursed those who conceal and made an exception for those who repent among them, He mentioned the persistent ones, expressing their concealment by disbelief so that the expression would cover every kind of disbelief. He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ (i.e., by this concealment and by other than it) ﴿and die while they are disbelievers﴾. Al-Harrali said: "In its implication there is ease in the repentance of disbelievers and difficulty in the repentance of hypocrites, in that He explicitly mentioned the repentance of the one who conceals and passed over mentioning the repentance of the disbeliever. So those who disbelieve repent except for a few, while those who conceal persist except for a few. Therefore the exception was made regarding the concealer and the specification was made regarding the disbeliever." End of quote.

Since death upon something indicates the basic natural disposition (al-jibilla, innate constitution), the one who dies a disbeliever is made of an evil disposition. Glorified and exalted is He, who made clear that he deserves in reality every disgrace, and this is due to that [disposition] and not to a cause that He renewed. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame none but himself, because He, glorified and exalted, is not questioned about what He does. He omitted the fa' of causality and referred to them with the demonstrative of distance, indicating their expulsion, and said: ﴿Those﴾, who are at the utmost lowliness, ﴿upon them is the curse of Allah﴾, i.e., the expulsion and removal by the King, besides whom there is no king. Then He identified the ones who curse in the preceding verse, and said: ﴿and of the angels and of mankind, all together﴾, i.e., they are deserving of that, and everyone curses the wrongdoer, and the most wrongdoing of wrongdoers is the disbeliever. ﴿Abiding therein﴾, i.e., the curse [abides].

[p-279] Since cursing indicates punishment, He stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿The punishment will not be lightened for them﴾, because the curse is overwhelming upon them and encompasses them. Al-Harrali said: "He mentioned the description of the punishment by mentioning the curse that befell them, so that both punishments would be combined for them: a punishment from the description and a punishment from the act, as there is for the one opposed to them a bliss and a pleasure." End of quote.

﴿Nor will they be reprieved﴾. Al-Harrali said: from al-nazra, which is the anticipated delay of its completion. The meaning is that they will not be granted any respite from any granter at all, as they are granted respite in this world. Rather, the punishment will fall upon them at the moment of their departure from life, and then it will not be lightened for them. Al-Harrali said: "In this there is an indication regarding a group, i.e., of the disobedient believers, whose punishment is postponed. And in contrast with the knowledge of recompense regarding the states of the people of this world, they are classified into categories in committing evil. Whoever persists in it, the punishment persists for him; whoever is delayed for a time in his worldly life, his punishment is delayed for him; and whoever increases in it, his punishment increases. This is because the world is the field of the Hereafter, and the recompense is according to the description." ﴿He will recompense them for their description. Indeed He is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 139]. End of quote.

And when He, glorified and exalted, bestowed upon them what He bestowed of the seas of proofs, varied with waves, and established what He willed of the laws of Islam with perfection and firmness, and this context, in which the reward of the obedient and the punishment of the disobedient are mentioned, indicated that the implicit meaning is: "Your God is one God, having no partner, whom none can repel from what He wills; there is no god but Him, the Avenger upon His enemies, the Mighty in His majesty," He followed it, repeating the admonition for every hypocrite and disbeliever and reminding, with the conjunction, every one who agrees and is friendly, with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your God﴾. Since the intent is that unity is affirmed in reality concerning the true God, it is not valid at all that the true God be divided by kind, nor by person, nor by attribute, nor by act, nor by anything else in any way. He repeated the word "God" and said: ﴿one God﴾, meaning that He is not divided in any way, neither by sameness of kind nor otherwise. And He, with that, ﴿there is no god but He﴾. This is an affirmation of oneness by negating what is other than Him and affirming Him. It is not valid in any way, and it is not possible in reason, that anything other than Him be fit for divinity at all. So He alone deserves worship, because He is ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, meaning generally merciful with bounties that pass away, to His friends and His enemies alike; ﴿the Especially Merciful﴾, meaning singled out with enduring bounties for His friends. Thus it is established, through His sole divinity, that He possesses all greatness, and in His hand are the reins of majesty and dominance; and through the two attributes of mercy, that He bestows sublime bounties and subtle ones. So everything other than Him is either a blessing or one who is blessed. He is the One whose wrath is feared and whose mercy is hoped for; He forgives whom He wills, curses whoever disbelieves, and makes him abide in punishment, without anyone else being able to object to Him in any of that.

I do not find it far, though the distance is great, that the waw in His saying "and your God" be conjunctive with His saying at the beginning of the surah ﴿And He is Knower of all things﴾ [2:29], before His saying ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority﴾ [2:30]. For tawhid is the thing intended in itself, and from it all acts of worship arise. So when He first said ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [2:21], He followed it with His saying ﴿who created you﴾ [2:21] to its end, with an attribute that is the evidence of His deserving worship. Then, when the proof was established, He said ﴿So do not set up rivals to God﴾ [2:22], informing that He has no partner in worship, just as it has become clear that He has no partner in creation. Then He followed it with what suits that station, of what was previously alerted to. Then He returned to it, saying a second time, ﴿How do you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life﴾ [2:28], to its end, and so He repeated the proof in a manner clearer and more expansive than the first. So when the matter of oneness and resurrection was established in a manner free of any flaw, what was most fitting was the verses preceding it, which mention other important matters, until He came to the mention of the concealers, the repentant, and the persistent, and the mention of what has been prepared for each of them as recompense. So He followed that with this verse, conjoining it to what I have mentioned, in a manner clearer than what preceded in establishing tawhid, as an explanation of what is the truth and an indication that He, exalted is He, is not like the kings of this world, who may be prevented by some of their followers from rewarding some of the obedient or punishing some of the disobedient. For He is one, with no equal, not even one near to Him, so there is no obstacle to the execution of His command. Nor is this conjunction to be deemed unlikely, for it is the custom of eloquent speakers that when one of them wishes to establish a matter by proof, for a ruling that he builds upon it, he begins with a sufficient proof, then follows it with bringing near the fruits gathered from it, then returns to confirming it in another way, so that souls may find comfort in it and hearts be gladdened. Perhaps the proof has long trailing parts and many branches, so he explains each of what is needed from its trailing parts and what follows from its branches. When he has completed that and sees that the opponent has not reached full submission, he repeats the proof in another way, conjoining it to the earlier forms, as a reminder of what is not strange in the course of their customs and the structures of their discourse. Whoever reflects on the debates of al-Baqillani and his like, from among those of broad memory and deep mastery of knowledge, will know this.

Al-Harali said: Since the content of the Book is calling creation to the truth, informing them of the right of the Truth over creation, and manifesting the excellences of those whom God chose from among those whom the origin of faith encompassed, from His angels, prophets, and messengers, and those who join them from among their people of guardianship, and manifesting the evidences of that from them, and establishing the proof thereby against those below them in obligating their followers; and since what harms creation is only dispersion, and what benefits them is only unity; so when God, exalted, showed them their return to the unity of the fatherhood of Adam, peace be upon him, in gathering the offspring, and to the unity of the fatherhood of Abraham, peace be upon him, in gathering Islam, and to the unity of the Ahmadiyya of Muhammad (ﷺ) in gathering religion, the defect of dispersion and division became clear to them, and the witness of benefit in gathering into unities was verified for them. That was a sign of the greatest benefit in returning to the unity of divinity in the matter of the truth and in conveying that by unities, which is what is supposed in the apparent unities: the unity of spirit, the unity of soul, and the unity of intellect. So He, exalted, said, conjoining to what the structure of the apparent unities manifested and what their conveying indicated of hidden unities: ﴿And your God is one God﴾. So if dispersion is ugly along with the unity of the begetting father, how much more so along with the unity of the father who is indebted! How much more so along with the unity of the perfecting Prophet! How much more so along with the unity of the God who is the Most Merciful, whose mercy encompassed His creation, the Especially Merciful who singled out His friends and chosen ones with care, gathering them by His unity, which is the sustainer of every unity other than Him! So all His names have a unity whose unity ends at the unity of the God in whom divinity culminates, which is the outward worship compelling the worshipper to Him in all his needs and his outward and inward states. And there is no more complete unity than the unity of what the intellect cannot conceive and the senses cannot perceive, in the loftiness of the unity of the unseen, in which no essence appears so that there would be quantities or qualities belonging to it or within it.

Then he said: It has been confirmed by experience that rest lies in the unity of the One, and that weariness lies in following the many, since each one is singled out by an aim in the follower, over which they contend; and the condition of their followers is thus. So the greatest call to gathering creation was calling them to gather in the unity of divinity, in harmony with what they were called to in the gathering under the name of Lordship, in His saying, exalted, earlier: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [2:21]. So the elevation of address from the rank of Lordship to the rank of this call by divinity is so that it rises from this limit to the call to God, the One, whose oneness is inscribed in the innate nature of all creation and their dispositions, since shirk did not occur in it in any way, but occurred only in the rank of divinity. So this was the middle of the call, by gathering in the unity of divinity, and in attributing the name God to them, the most complete descent according to the measure of their intellect from their worship, which is their deifying. And since in divinity there is a claim whose multiplicity suggests manifest error, He followed that with the word of tawhid, based on His hidden name within the outward aspect of divinity, saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no god but He﴾, as a refutation of what was implied in the first. He did not mention His manifest name, so that the call to Him would have a lofty rank, to which this one would be ascended. And since this divine tawhid is a matter of the unseen from God, which He, glorified and exalted, made manifest through the aspect of the all-encompassing, all-inclusive Mercy and the specific Mercy, for what creation has as witness of that in what they find of the effect of the all-encompassing mercy in their worldly life and its traces, and what they find of the traces of the specific mercy [in their being singled out with the distinction of multiplied mercy]; so in the totality of this verse there is a greatness from the unseen of divinity to the completeness of the specific Mercy. Therefore this verse, together with the verse of encompassing at [the beginning of] Al 'Imran, which gathers in contrast what is in this verse of the specific Mercy with its specific opposite, the outward attribute of vengeance, from the attribute of might, which His saying, glorified and exalted, manifested: ﴿And God is Mighty, Owner of Retribution﴾ [3:4]. So this verse, with ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ [3:1] and ﴿God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾ [3:2], is for that reason the greatest name of God, encompassing the unseen and the witnessed, gathering mercy and retribution outwardly and encompassing majesty inwardly. So this limit of the loftiness of address was the beginning of raising creation to attachment to the greatest name of God, which lifts them from the lowliness of their confinement to their debased selves, manifesting the principle of care for this final community. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 164 (part 1 of 2):

Since this station can only be sound with complete knowledge and perfect power, he set forth the proofs for that in this third verse in a more expansive way than in the second verse, just as the second was more expansive than the first, and clearer in making the ignorant see and in reminding the scholars. This verse therefore constitutes a detailed explanation of the two preceding verses. There was no need for such detail in the verse of Al 'Imran, because its main purpose is to show the comprehensiveness of power [and as for this verse, it is evidence of God's unique oneness, so it was necessary to mention what may have been attributed to its proximate causes], as an alert that He has no partner in any of this, and that all of it is by His creation, even if He established apparent causes for it. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, and in their alternation (ikhtilaf). The creation of what is mentioned in the verse is among His blessings upon His servants, as was mentioned at the beginning of the surah. Then He mentioned what arises from them, saying: ﴿and the alternation﴾, which is ifti'al from al-khulf, and it is the separation that occurs after union in some matter, ﴿of the night﴾. He placed it first because it is the origin and the older, ("And a sign for them is the night and the day"), and their creation. So the verse uses al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which a term is omitted from each of two parallel elements, the mention in one indicating the omission in the other). He mentioned the creation first as an indication of its omission in the second, and the alternation second as an indication of its omission in the first.

Al-Harrali said: Since it is among the custom of God that whoever He calls, along with His messengers, by a witness of breaking custom in creation or in affairs, He hastens to punish him in this world and raises after him another community, as He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the earlier ones denied them﴾ [al-Isra': 59]. This community was the seal, with no community after it other than itself, and its Lord spared it from needing the breaking of customary patterns. The Prayer and Peace of God be upon him said: "There was no prophet except that he was given signs such that people believed upon their like, but what I was given was a revelation which God, glorified and exalted, revealed to me, so I hope to be the one with the most followers." So reflection (i'tibar) became more general in responding and more lenient in opposing, and what He had already displayed [for them] in His creation through manifestation and subjection of witnesses was sufficient for it, so that they would be scholars submitting to the spirit of knowledge, not to the authority of compulsion, and that would be among their distinctions over others. He did not grant them what they asked for in that regard. When, exalted is He, He connected with the call to lordship, He mentioned creation and provision, and He mentioned the earth as a bed and the sky as a building, in accordance with the custom of the Arabs regarding the rank of apparent sense, the highest of whom in this address is by presenting His signs and witnesses for the elevated rank of an intelligible meaning above the rank of the sensed matter [preceding], so He said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, addressing one who has intellectual reflection that exceeds sensory perception, by considering the heavens as their spheres, and counting them by the witnesses of their stars, until one comes to know that they are counted heavens. That becomes evident to one who has consideration for the creation of the heavens. Since the earths have no sensible witnesses to their number as the heavens do, mention of them in the Qur'an came only in the singular, while the mention of the heavens came in the plural for people of intellectual reflection and in the singular for people of sensory reflection. The clearest consideration between the heavens and the earth lies in the contrast of their shares: the heavens are in a state of elevation, purity, luminosity and motion, while the earth in contrast has lowness, density, darkness and stillness. So reflection occurs through the cooperation of the visible with the visible opposite, and that is something creation is unable to do, so they know that it is from the command of the Real. For creation achieves cooperation only through what is similar, not through what is opposite. Whoever's instrument is water, for example, will find fire spoiled for him, and whoever's instrument is fire will find water spoiled for him. But the Real, glorified and exalted, established for creation and for existent things and for births units that are gathered together, in which He subdued the mutually repellent existents of the elements. The existence of the creation of the visible heavens and earth opposes them. So there occurs the union of fire with water despite the opposition between hot and cold, the union of air with earth despite the opposition between dense and subtle, and the union of all in one thing, one body, and one organ [p-291] in one part, even in the finest of its parts, except by a command which creation cannot accomplish and which none can determine except the Real, about which creation is bewildered. So He is then their God, who is one God. His traces are present in their selves, His witnesses are visible to their eyes, and the realities of those witnesses are manifest to their minds. It is as if He, glorified and exalted, made them read His wise remembrance, visible to their eyes, uncovering the veil over their eyes so that they would be distinguished from those whose eyes were under a covering from His remembrance.

When God, glorified and exalted, mentioned the creation of the opposites of height and lowness in the mention of the heavens and the earth, He strung together with them the alternation of the two horizons in which the appearance of the two alternating night and day occurs, so that their reflection would be spacious between the reflection of the high and the low, and the east and the west. Thus there occurs the witnesses of encompassment over them, in the oneness of their Lord and returning that to Him, without attributing it to anything other than Him, of what is included in the scope of the existence of this encompassment: from the highest encompassing, and the lowest encompassing, and the encompassing from all sides, from the covering horizons of night and day. It is an address of summary (ijmal), suitable for the place of the surah, whose subject is the summaries of what is explained in it and in the rest of the Qur'an, in that it is its tent-pole and its hump. End of quote.

When He, exalted is He, mentioned what the motion of the stars in the courtyard of the sphere produced, He followed it with the motion of the ship in the expanse of the sea, and said: ﴿and the ship﴾, which is what is large among ships [p-292] [as opposed to] the small boat, which is the lighter of them. Al-Harrali said: its singular and plural are equal, the movements of the singular being first in the mind and the movements of the plural being secondary in the mind, insofar as the singular is first and the plural is second and broken. End of quote. Since he here intended the plural because it is more indicative of power, he described it with the feminine particle, saying ﴿which run﴾ by God's decree, and he confirmed the matter by saying ﴿in the sea﴾. He attributed the running to them, and it is known that they have no running in reality, nor any action in the manner of an elevation to a belief like that about the stars, as an indication that they have no action and no governance, as some philosophers believe. Al-Harrali said: When He, glorified and exalted, mentioned the totality of creation and the totality of alternation in both aspects, He connected with that the encompassment of the sea over the earth and the sea's intersecting of the lands, so that the benefits carried in the ship would be conveyed from the benefits of the east to the west, and the benefits of the west to the east, and the benefits of the north to the south and vice versa. Thus no running vessel carries anything beneficial except that the indefinite word "what" in His saying ﴿with what benefits people﴾ has included its mention. He mentioned them by the name "people", which is the first place where gathering, cooperation and insight into the aspect of what is near occur, which is the witness of this statement, regarding the benefits of this world. End of quote.

When He mentioned the benefit of the sea through ships, He mentioned from its benefit what is more general than that, saying: ﴿And what God sent down﴾, He to whom belongs complete greatness, ﴿from the heaven﴾, that is, from its direction, by the drawing of the clouds to it. Since what descends from it is of various kinds, and the context was one of coaxing toward removing disagreement, He mentioned what is the cause of life, saying: ﴿of water, and He gave life thereby to the earth﴾ by what grows from it. Since giving life takes up the time that follows death, He negated the preposition, saying: ﴿after its death﴾, by its non-existence. [p-294] When He mentioned the life of the earth by water, He indicated that the life of every living being is by it, saying ﴿and He dispersed﴾, from dispersal, which is the scattering of numerous units in different directions, ﴿therein﴾ by multiplication, ﴿of every creature﴾, from crawling, which is movement by oneself. Al-Harrali said: He, exalted is He, left the matter of creation, alternation and running undetermined, not attributing it to any of His names that would make it manifest, but He attributed the sending down of water from the sky to His great name, which is Allah, because of the manifest position of His dominion over creation in the bounty of water's supply and its renewal from time to time, unlike the constant nature of the undetermined creation of the heavens and the earth, which remains in one state, and the alternation of night and day, which continues in one direction, and the conjectured running of the ship which proceeds according to the custom of its habit. So He manifested His name in what testifies against them through their need for it in every year, so that they would turn in worship to the high place from which water descends, and thus transfer them from worshipping what is on the earth to worshipping [p-295] Him who is in heaven: ﴿Are you secure from Him who is in heaven that He will cause the earth to swallow you?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16]. The Prayer and Peace of God be upon him said to the slave-girl: "Where is God?" She said: "In heaven." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer." So the lowest degree of faith is to turn in worship to Him who is in heaven, rising to the height of being established on the Throne, to the unseen existent in the secrets of hearts. In this preliminary there was a direction of creation toward the God who sends down water from the sky, and He is Allah, whom none has associated with Him, so that this would be a preparation for the oneness of God. For this reason He, exalted is He, mentioned the sign of divinity, which is giving life, and life is every departure from inanimacy, insofar as the true meaning of life is only completion in what is deficient. So what moves is alive in relation to the inanimate, rising to what is above that from ranks of life, such as the life of animals and the beasts of the earth. Therefore He, exalted is He, mentioned the two givings of life by meaning, and He manifested the name with the earth because it is manifest in animals, so He manifested where it was hidden from creation, and did not mention it where it is manifest to creation, thereby alerting them to the two considerations: the sending down of water, from which they have drink, from which there are trees, by which the life of animals exists, and from which is their pasture.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 164 (part 2 of 2):

When He, glorified and exalted is He, had mentioned the spreading forth of what is the cause of plants, which are the effect of water, He mentioned the spreading forth of what is a cause of the clouds, which are the cause of rain, which is the cause of life. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and the turning of the winds﴾, meaning: at times a ṣabā (east wind), at other times a dabūr (west wind), at one time a shamāl (north wind), and at another a janūb (south wind). Taṣrīf (turning, directing) is causing the thing that is directed to proceed according to the requirement of the ruling over it. The wind is the moving of air in the regions. ﴿And the clouds﴾, which are what accumulates in the direction of height, from a substance between water and air, drawn out in the atmosphere, ﴿subjected﴾, meaning: by them (the winds). Taskhīr (subjection) is causing a thing to proceed according to the purpose for which it was subjected, ﴿between the sky and the earth﴾. It does not fall downward despite its weight from carrying the vapour of water, unlike the rest of the high bodies, since it has no sensible holder. Nor does it disperse, although nature requires one of three things: the dense requires descent, the subtle requires ascent, and the intermediate requires dispersal. ﴿Are signs﴾.

(Al-Harrālī) said: When He, exalted is He, mentioned the high and the low, the rising of night and day from both sides, and the sending down of water as a provision, He mentioned what fills what lies between these: the winds and the clouds, which is what lies between an airy motion and a watery illumination, and what necessarily follows from that of its luminous beginnings, such as its thunderbolts and the totality of its occurrences. In this discourse there is sufficiency with principles from the beginnings of reflection. So He mentioned the sky, the earth, the horizons, and what lies between them of winds, clouds, and the sent-down water, the whole of which is the foundation of creation's livelihood in their present world, so that He might make for them that as a sign of a higher matter beyond it, and each aspect of it would be a sign of one of God's matters, and thus they would be signs. So the sky is a sign of the loftiness of God's command, so that it is higher than the highest; the earth is a sign of the inner reality of God's command, so that it is more hidden than the most hidden; the alternation of night and day is a sign of the light of its appearance and the darkness of its absence, from what lies behind the command of night and fire; the water He sent down to give life to the earth and to create living beings is a sign of what descends of the light of His knowledge upon the hearts, so that they live by it a life, and the life of the outward is a sign of it; and the turning of the winds and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth are signs of the turning of what lies between the earth of the servant, which is his outward, and his sky, which is his inward; and the subjection of some of it to others is so that this may be a sign of God's loftiness over His lofty heaven in the sensible, and over the heaven of the lofty hearts in the perceptual. ﴿Are signs for a people﴾, from all of that, the various kinds of these considerations, which He made for the totality of that. ﴿For a people﴾ are those who stand up to the matter with the right of standing up. In this there is an indication that this is not attained by one who is of the age of people until his nature matures and the excellence of his intellect grows, until he becomes of a people who stand up in consideration as those who rise up in worldly affairs. For the Arabs knew that the use of the word qawm (people) refers only to valour and strength, until they say: "qawm or nisā'" (men or women), as a contrast between the two meanings. He mentioned the intellect, which is a light of His light, as guidance for whoever establishes it, from the limit of the wavering of people's states toward being illuminated by its light in reading the letters of His Wise Book, which He wrote with His own hand, and which made the unlettered independent, by reading what was written for them, of reading the book of what creatures have written. End of quote. So He said: ﴿they reason﴾, meaning: they know that the Turner of these matters in these various modes and firm aspects is an agent who chooses, and that He is able, as is witnessed by the reviving of the earth and other things greater than it, to resurrect the dead and to do other things He wills. And that He, with all of this, is One, with no partner who could contest Him, as rational people know by this, so they do not take rivals besides Him, nor do they turn away from His exalted presence toward anything else.
