For this reason, the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, feared disagreement among the people of this religion concerning the Qur'an, as the Jews and Christians had disagreed, so they gathered them upon one single mushaf. Therefore, the disagreement in the variant readings and the modes of understanding is not of that kind. And as you see, the warning to the polytheist Arabs has occurred without what the warning to the Children of Israel contained of rebuke and reproach, distinguishing between them, because the disbelief of the polytheists is out of ignorance, while the disbelief of those is out of obstinacy after repeatedly witnessing the signs. Whoever reflects upon the Qur'an and studies the Torah will know the long duration of Musa, upon him be peace, among them, reciting the Torah to them according to its revelation little by little, and that they, despite this, whenever they witnessed a sign, they introduced disbelief, cast off gratitude, and asked for something else out of stubbornness and deceit. ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13]. Much of that has already passed from the beginning of the surah concerning the Torah, and the rest of it will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in its fitting places among the verses of the Qur'an.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: Whenever something is explained in the Noble Book concerning the condition of the Christians, it is not as what has come of its like concerning the Jews, for the reason mentioned, i.e., that their disbelief is obstinacy. The address to the polytheist Arabs in what was pointed to is apart from the address to the two groups, since there came to them what did not come to the Arabs, and they were given good tidings in their books, whereas the polytheist Arabs have nothing like that. Deviation from guidance is comprehensive for all, and they are not on any part of the Straight Path. Yet the worst condition is the condition of one whom Allah has misguided knowingly. Here ends the mention of what He warned against and forbade to one who wishes to follow the Straight Path, and the explanation of the condition of one who swerved from it and deviated from it, and thought he was upon something. He gathered the scattered categories of those who deviate into three categories, and they are the Jews, the Christians, and the people of polytheism. By them all the rest who deviate are joined: the hypocrites of our community who doubt after displaying their faith and do their deeds of deceit, trickery and mockery are joined to the Jews; whoever takes on their conditions is joined to the Christians; and whoever sets up a rival to Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and believes that an act belongs to other than Him, in a manner other than acquisition, is joined to the polytheists. The Magians are joined to the people of polytheism. Polytheism is the most ramified of these six paths, and for this reason he, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Shirk is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." Whoever does the deeds of those mentioned, and the matter does not reach the point of leaving his religion and departing in any part of his belief, it is feared that this may be a means to joining the one he resembles. To this he, upon him be blessings and peace, pointed with his saying: "Four traits, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he betrays, when he promises he breaks it, and when he disputes he transgresses." And other similar hadiths. End.

(p-1) When the Exalted and Glorified One had made clear the disbelief of the People of the Book, who censured the change of the qibla by denying the Messenger (ﷺ), concealing the truth and other things, until He concluded with their disbelief in their differing over the Book and their concealing what it contains of the supports of Islam, He followed this with an indication that the matter of the branches (al-furu') is more deserving of attention than the matter of the roots (al-usul), because the branches are not sought for their own sake. The qibla, which they made part of their enmity by concealing what they possessed of evidence for its truth, and by greatly reviling the righteous on account of it, is not sought for its own sake. What is sought in itself is faith. When faith is established, all acts of obedience follow it, including the prayer, for which facing the qibla is a condition, and others. So He said, Exalted is He: ﴿It is not righteousness﴾, that is, the act that is pleasing, which in purifying the soul is like righteousness in nourishing the body, ﴿that you turn your faces﴾, that is, (p-2) in prayer, ﴿toward the east﴾, which is the direction of the rising of the lights, ﴿or the west﴾, which is the direction of their setting, that is, or other spatial directions. For all of that belongs to God, Exalted and Glorified, as has passed at the first of their objection, when the ascription of all of it to Him was stated explicitly: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 115].

Since it had become clear to the righteous, as was mentioned earlier, what departs from the straight path, and they had been warned against it so that they would avoid it, He followed this with what is incumbent upon them so that they would act upon it. Thus He began here with the mention of the rulings, up to His saying ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285]. He began that with what He began the surah with, and He detailed for them much of what they were charged with, which He had summarized before that. He detailed faith with a detail not preceded [by anything similar]. So He said: ﴿But righteousness is [the faith] of one who﴾, that is, the faith of the one who, and perhaps (p-3) He expressed it this way to convey that the doer of this is himself righteous, that is, he has purified himself until he becomes the very essence of purification: ﴿believes in God﴾, whose oneness is called for by the verse of Oneness. So He established for Him the attributes of perfection and declared Him free of every trace of deficiency, from what is evidenced by His acts.

Since among the most important characteristics of faith is the readiness for resurrection and belief in it, because it necessitates adherence to good and distance from evil, He said: ﴿and the Last Day﴾, which many people have denied, so their order was disrupted by some of them transgressing against others. The first [belief] keeps one free of rivals, and this [belief] keeps one far from harming the servants.

Since this is the faith of the perfected, and since most people have sleeping minds, knowing nothing except through reminder, and misguided insights that need guidance, He, Exalted and Glorified, mentioned the guides whom He made intermediaries between Himself and His servants, beginning with the first and then the next. So He said: ﴿and the angels﴾, that is, those whom He placed between Himself (p-4) and people, and who are pure unseen. ﴿and the Book﴾, which they bring in a manner in which there is no doubt, more general than the Qur'an and other than it. ﴿and the prophets﴾, to whom the angels bring it down, because they are the essence of creation. For them is a angelic aspect by which they are able to receive from the angels, due to their kinship with them, and a human aspect by which people are able to receive from them. And they possess, from the sublime and beautiful meanings in which God has disposed them by perfecting their bodies and their spirits, what no one knows except Him. So upon them be prayers, peace, greetings and honor.

Al-Harali said: In it, that is, in believing in them and in what came before them, is the subduing of the self to submit to one who is of its own kind, and belief in the unseen of one who is not of its kind, so that in this there is that which restrains the self from its desires. End of quotation.

Likewise, the Exalted and Glorified One favored charity, and placing belief in connection with it indicates that it confirms that belief. Whoever is stingy with it is claiming faith without proof, and it is guidance that in giving it there is safety from the trial of wealth: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15], because whoever believes and gives charity has surrendered to God his soul and his wealth, which is the equal of his soul, and so he becomes truly the servant of God. In this is an indication of urging the abandonment of every beloved other than God, Exalted and Glorified, for God's sake.

Al-Harali said: So whoever thinks (p-5) that his need is met by wealth is not righteous. Rather, righteousness is that in which one is certain that his need is met only by his Lord through His hidden kindness. End of quotation.

Therefore He said: ﴿and gave wealth﴾, that is, which He permitted, after making it a sign of it, out of generosity of soul and confirmation of faith, by trusting in the One who guaranteed provision for the future, and He is over all things Capable. He indicated that the condition of believing in Him is preferring Him, Exalted and Glorified, over everything, by His saying: ﴿despite love for it﴾, that is, giving that is lofty, in which the love of God surpasses the love of wealth. It indicates giving charity while in health and while being stingy, hoping for riches and fearing poverty. He also indicated that it is for His sake, not for what they used to do in the age of ignorance of boasting, so He said: ﴿to relatives﴾, because they are the most deserving of kindness, since giving to them is charity and maintaining ties (p-6), ﴿and orphans﴾, from among relatives and others, because they are the most helpless of people, ﴿and the needy﴾, because they are next to them in helplessness, and the poor are included in them by agreement, ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, because of their helplessness through being far from home. If we make this more general, covering the present state and the future, the one fighting in the way of God is included in it. ﴿and those who ask﴾, because most often their asking is out of need, and the debtor is included. ﴿and for freeing captives﴾.

Al-Harali said: It is the plural of raqabah, which is what slavery has reached of the children of Adam. So what is meant is the enslaved captives who are sought to be freed through a contract of emancipation and the freeing of prisoners from it. He put those first because their need is for establishing proof.

Since He, Exalted and Glorified, mentioned the aiding of creation and put it first to encourage greater attention to it, so that the soul would be willing to give up what love for wealth has adorned for it, He followed it with the right of the Right (p-7). So He said: ﴿and established the prayer﴾, which is the best of bodily acts of worship, and which is not possible except after meeting the needs of the body, and its establishment is not possible except with all its limits and preserving them. Since He mentioned what purifies the spirit through standing before God, Exalted and Glorified, and drawing near through voluntary charities, He mentioned what purifies and increases wealth, which is the right of creation. So He said: ﴿and gave zakat﴾. In restricting it to giving, there is an indication that bringing out wealth in this manner is not possible except from sincerity.

Since He had completed faith and what confirms its claim in general, He began on the completion of that. He joined to the beginning of the speech what, by being conjoined in this way, indicates that it is sought for its own sake, for it comprises entry into all that preceded it. So He said: ﴿and those who fulfill their covenant﴾ (p-8).

Al-Harali said: From fulfilling (al-iyfa'), which is taking up fidelity, we requite what is promised in the matter that was agreed upon. End of quotation.

His saying ﴿when they make a covenant﴾ clarifies that what is required is what they bound themselves to, whether toward the Right or toward creation, explicitly stating what the preceding had implied. Since He separated fidelity to honor it, because it is included in what came before, He did the same with patience for that very reason, and said: ﴿and the patient﴾. In this is an allusion to treating it as its due right, had it been conjoined to "those who believe," had it been brought in its original order.

Al-Harali said: In it is an indication that whoever has truly realized patience in giving preference (to God), and was thankful, has truly realized patience in tribulation and in jihad, as confirmation from God, Exalted and Glorified, for one who thanked Him at the beginning, by aiding him in patience and perseverance at the end. It is as if, when he gave generously of the good of this world out of love for it, God afflicted him with its trials as an honor to him, so that He might give him his portion of what is decreed for him in his life, and so that he would be among those who find rest at their death. And if he strives, he remains steadfast through what arises in the soul of the thankful and patient one of longing for meeting God, Exalted and Glorified, disowning this world and realizing attainment of the good from God. End of quotation.

He specified the most severe situation in which patience is required, and said: ﴿in misfortune﴾, that is, at (p-9) the arrival of hardship upon them in their souls from God, Exalted and Glorified, without intermediary, or from Him through the intermediary of servants, ﴿and in adversity﴾, through the occurrence of harm to their wealth and the rest of their conditions, such as people's contempt for them and the like. The Qamus interprets it as hardship and deficiency in wealth and persons. So it is then more general, so that the more specific is mentioned twice. Al-Harali said: "Al-ba's" is a form (fa'la') from "al-bu's," which is bad condition, poverty, and lack of the favor that would set it right. "Al-darra'" is illness of the body and its afflictions. So "al-ba'sa'" is in state, and "al-darra'" is in the body. End of quotation.

﴿and at the time of battle﴾, that is, war, which combines both souls and wealth. Al-Harali said: "Al-ba's" is the severity in war.

(p-10) Since these qualities are the most noble of qualities, He indicated their nobility by the nobility of their possessors, and said, beginning a new statement to explain that one does not deserve the name of righteousness except one in whom these qualities are combined: ﴿those are﴾, that is, specifically, those whose aspirations are lofty and whose characters and dispositions are great. ﴿those who are true﴾, that is, in what they claimed of faith. In this is an indication that whoever does not do their deeds is not regarded as truthful in his claim. ﴿and those are﴾, specifically, ﴿the righteous (al-muttaqun)﴾ for the Day of Recompense. In making this a description of them is an indication that they undertook these deeds out of great fear.

Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Burhan: Then He mentioned zakat, fasting, hajj, jihad, and other rulings such as marriage, divorce, waiting periods, menstruation, nursing, the prescribed punishments, usury and sales, along with what intervenes in these verses of detailed and summarized rulings. He placed first among them fulfilling the covenant and patience, because these are needed in all deeds. What intervenes in these verses from His saying ﴿It is not righteousness﴾ up to His saying ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285] (p-11) is not of the category of obligation and imposition, but is for a causal connection that made its mention necessary, and a link that called for it. End of quotation.

The summary is that, when He, Exalted and Glorified, had purified them from the burdens of forbidden things with the thunderbolts of admonitions, He began to make them pure by plunging them into the depths of commands, so that He might complete their worship, by their adorning themselves with His command after their being emptied of His wrath through the piercing of His restraint. So in this surah He mentioned all the pillars of this letter and its enclosure.

Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harali said in al-'Urwa: The purpose of sending down this letter is to bring creation to sincere humility before God, Exalted and Glorified, after purification from their filth, so that by this the connection that had been severed returns and what had been veiled is unveiled. It is the letter of worship received through faith, persevering in it, with prior fear hastening toward it, and eagerness through sincere love. So the worshipper is one whom fear drives toward it, and the knower is one whom love leads to it. It is a building with a pillar and pillars, and it has an enclosure surrounding it. As for its pillar, it is the singling out of humility to God, Exalted and Glorified, in oneness, and its vanguard is the verse of the sort of His saying, Exalted and Glorified: ﴿Worship God and associate nothing with Him﴾ [al-Nisa': 36]. The letter of prohibition purified them from the filth of worshipping another god, then the letter of command established for them singling out, so that they would not associate with Him in humility anything whatsoever, other than Him. This is the first of what God established of the building of religion, and He did not prescribe anything else for about ten years in sending down what was sent down in Makkah. Along with its prescription, He established the first pillar, which is prayer, and it began with ablution as a practice imitating the purification of the heart and soul by the letter of prohibition. It was followed by prayer as a practice imitating the purity of the heart through monotheism before the Lord, Exalted and Glorified. So ablution is the aspect of the working of the letter of prohibition, and prayer is the aspect of the working of the letter of command. He established, on the foundation of the house of love, so that the strength of faith might appear in the witnessed continuity of serving the bodies.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 177 (part 2 of 2):**

So the strongest of them in faith were the most numerous and longest in prayer (*salah*) and in *qunut* (devout standing). He who loves a king serves him and remains constantly with him, and kings are not served with laziness and negligence, but with effort and humility. Thus prayer became the *'ilm* (sign) of faith: it increases with its strength and decreases with its weakness. For had it been made obligatory, the difference in the strength of faith and the sincerity of truthfulness would not have appeared in it, just as it does not appear after its obligation except in the voluntary prayers (*nawafil*). Because the Prophet ﷺ exerted himself and his body in this, there was revealed to him: ﴿We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to make you suffer﴾ [Ta-Ha: 2], ﴿but as a reminder for those who fear﴾ [Ta-Ha: 3], ﴿a revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾ [Ta-Ha: 4], ﴿the Most Merciful, established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], up to His words ﴿Allah, there is no god but He; to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [Ta-Ha: 8]. This *tawhid* and its manifestation was, on that day, the first aim. That was before the conversion of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and ʿUmar was the fortieth in the number of the believers. When there entered Islam those whom love and ease did not move to prayer after about ten [years] or so, prayer was made obligatory, and in its obligation the lover and the fearful became equal. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established voluntary prayer according to its original basis, and that was on the morning after the Night of the Isra' (Night Journey). The first revelation of this *harf* (section) — and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best — concerning the obligation of this pillar, or from the beginning of its revelation, is the words of Allah, exalted: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and [recite] the Qur'an of dawn﴾ [al-Isra': 78]. He singled them out with it at the times of mercy and protected them through it from the times of trial, and from it comes all the verses on establishing the prayer and perfecting it.

The other pillar is fasting (*sawm*), which is the humbling of the self before Allah, glorified and exalted, by restraining it from everything it longs for from its particular desires during the day, for the one who is moderate, and continuously for the one in seclusion (*i'tikaf*). It is a link between the servant and his own self, and a joining of his scattered parts within his essence. The first revelation of this pillar from this *harf* was in Medina, after a period from the Hijrah, and its first revelation was: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 183]. It was made obligatory — and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best — in Medina, because when they believed, from the enmity of the equals and the strangers and the year of trial in Medina, trial returned specifically within the selves through indulgence in desires, and that is not fitting for believers who prefer the religion over the world. Then Allah, glorified and exalted, completed it by His words: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], along with what of the verses specifically concerns the rulings of fasting.

The other pillar is zakat, which is the breaking of the self of the wealthy by taking from him the right of its categories (of recipients), as a manifestation that those occupied with religion are more preferred by Allah, glorified and exalted, than those who remain upon their wealth, and so that by it He may distinguish those who believed from the hypocrites, since the hypocrites were capable of showing off in the pillar and the two pillars. Allah, glorified and exalted, has not testified to hypocrisy openly more greatly than His testimony against the withholder of zakat. Whoever withholds the zakat of wealth from the creation is like one who refrains from the zakat of his strengths through prayer from the Truth. Therefore there is no prayer for one who has no zakat. Just as zakat was love before it was made obligatory, so too spending over and above the surplus was a well-known resolve among them, which they knew no other, and they did not perceive in Islam anything else. When mixtures entered Islam and souls became miserly, zakat was made obligatory and its categories were specified. That was in Medina, when their wealth increased and the bounty of Allah became abundant among them, and when a sense of pride spread among a people there, fearing the lowering of their leadership through Islam's humbling itself before Allah and fairness toward the creation of Allah. The address appeared in it once to the owners of wealth, in His words: "And give zakat" [al-Baqarah: 43], so that it would be for them a means of nearness if they give it willingly; and once to the one in charge of the matter, in His words: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103], when miserliness is perceived in their souls. Allah, glorified and exalted, intensified in it the warning in the Qur'an, to compel the weakness of its categories, and He arranged in relation to it all that was revealed concerning the explanation of expenditures and charities, as a hastening out of love or an obedience out of fear.

The other pillar is Hajj, which is the gathering of creation from the regions of the earth to stand before their Lord at the end of their appointed time and the approach of their death, so that it becomes for them a security from the gathering after their death. Thereby the structure of the religion was completed. This was in the final years of the Hijrah, and from the last of what was revealed in Medina, and at the beginning of its address: ﴿And for Allah, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], with its alerting to the call of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot﴾ [al-Hajj: 27], along with what was revealed concerning the matter of Hajj and its rulings. *Al-Hazirah* means the enclosing wall, and it is *jihad*. The companionship of all the pillars never ceased, either with weakness, as in Mecca, or with strength, as in Medina. From the beginning of the clear statement of its revelation:
﴿Permission is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged﴾ [al-Hajj: 39], up to His words ﴿and fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], ﴿fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 123], up to His words: ﴿strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73], up to the end of the fighting against the People of the Book in His words: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29], the verse, up to the completion of what was revealed concerning it in His words: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 39]. This is the completion of the *harf* of command. Each of these, in the outward aspect within Islam, has its place in the limits of faith, and a place in *ihsan* (excellence), in the three (levels) which is the perfection of the whole religion. That is from the descent of the Qur'an, between clarification and comprehension, in this *harf*, and it is the fulfillment of the religion and the worship of Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Then he said, concerning what by it the recitation of the *harf* of command is attained: Know that fulfilling the recitation of the *harf* of prohibition completely frees one for the recitation of the *harf* of command, because the one who is content in the livelihood of this world finds it easy to expand in the work of the Hereafter, while the one who expands in the enjoyments of this world cannot expand in the work of the Hereafter, because of the conflict and opposition between them. What by it the recitation of this *harf* is attained is, on the side of the heart, *tawhid* and sincerity (*ikhlas*). The most general of that is disassociation from the great *shirk*, lest one take with Allah another god, for the polytheist in divinity, his acts of worship are not valid. ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows hard upon on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾ [Ibrahim: 18]. More specific than that is sincerity along with disassociation from the manifest *shirk*, by not seeing a partner for Allah, glorified and exalted, in anything of His manifest names, for the polytheist in the rest of His manifest names, his acceptance is not valid. And what ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, swore by was: "If one of them had gold equal to Mount Uhud and spent it, Allah would not accept it from him until he believes in qadar (divine decree)."

For each of the commanded acts there is a specific name in sincerity, like the sincerity of the one who spends: that the bestowing is from Allah, glorified and exalted, not from the spending servant; and like the sincerity of the fighter: that victory is from Allah, glorified and exalted, not from the fighting servant. ﴿And victory is only from Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 126]. Likewise, all other acts are specified by sincerity in a name of the names which is most apt for that act. As for the side of the states of the self, its first and foundation is the self's tranquility with its Lord in its sustenance, without tranquility in anything other than Him. So whenever the self is at rest with what it can attain, or with what favor it has, or with what it owns of slaves, or with what it leans upon from other than Him, all its worship is returned to that in which it has found rest, its name is written upon it, and it becomes its slave, not the slave of its Lord; and the man becomes the servant of that rather than the servant of his Lord. "Wretched is the slave of the dinar, and the slave of the dirham, and the slave of the velvet cloak." This is what nullifies the deeds of the doers without their perceiving it. As for the side of what pertains to each of the commands in the states of the self, it is what suits it of its states and dispositions: such as its gathering in prayer, by not giving ear to the whisperings of Satan, and not speaking in its embellishment; and like its generosity and munificence in spending and giving zakat; and like its patience in fasting, for fasting is entirely patience. All of this is accompanied in Hajj with increased certainty; and in jihad all of it is accompanied by the instinct of courage. This is from the side of the state of the self. As for the side of action and the states of the limbs, the etiquette of one who utters the testimony of faith is that he gathers his senses to his heart, brings to his heart every limb within it, and speaks with his tongue on behalf of his whole essence: the states of the self and the limbs of the body, until each member of him, every limb within him, and every state of his self takes its portion of it, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ indicated. Know that with this: "Sins fall away from him as leaves fall from a tree." Whoever is not in this state does not recite the *tahlil* of the Qur'an, and likewise in the *tashahhud* of the adhan. By this, the *tahlil* demolishes his sins in Islam, just as he who is delivered by it demolishes the crimes of disbelief. "The Prophet ﷺ heard a man calling the adhan, and when he said: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar,' he said: 'Upon the fitrah.' When he said: 'La ilaha illa Allah,' he said: 'You have come out of the Fire.'"

As for the etiquette of prayer, it is the humility of the limbs, stillness in the postures, completing each posture with its specific remembrances, and gathering the senses to the heart as in the state in the testimony, so that no faculty perceives heedlessness. As for the etiquette of spending, it is good manner in giving: the Prophet ﷺ would hand the beggar [the gift] with his own hand and would not entrust it to another. Concealment is more complete: ﴿And if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 271]. And one spends from everything according to what He has provided, daily, monthly, or yearly: ﴿and from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3]. As for the etiquette of fasting: the suhur is delayed, the iftar is hastened, and the fasting of all the limbs from injustice, and all the more from wrongdoing; and leaving concern for what one breaks the fast with until after noon, and taking of it for the desire of one's dependents. As for the etiquette of Hajj: making the provision good (*tayyib*), relying upon what is in Allah's hand and not upon what is in the servant's own possession. It is taking provision of piety (*taqwa*), gentleness with companions, kindness to the mount, good character, spending on the sacrificial offering, which is the flowing of blood (*thajj*), and proclaiming the *talbiyah* aloud, which is *ajj* (raising the voice). It is following its pillars according to what its rulings require, and establishing its rites according to the known Sunnah, not according to the customary habit. As for the etiquette of jihad: making the provision good, preparing the equipment, being easy with comrades, good care of horses, making their fodder pure in purity and scrupulousness, and handling it with one's own hand. "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would take the fodder of his horse with his own hand and wipe it with his cloak." And adhering to what one finds with him of obligation, whether he is a horseman, a foot soldier, a spearman, or an archer; from burdening oneself with what is other than what one finds, ends in ruin, for he has lost the right and acted by burden. And silence at the encounter, and lowering the gaze from looking at the enemies. The Prophet ﷺ said: "When they draw near to you, shoot at them, and do not draw the swords until they overwhelm you." And restraining the hand from what has a right in it for another, which is *ghulul* (embezzlement); and that one does not call for single combat (*al-biraz*), and that one answers when called. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant, every servant of Mine is he who remembers Allah while he is meeting his opponent.'"

For every command and every engagement with a commanded act there is an etiquette specific to it, according to what is derived from the Prophetic Sunnahs and the traditions of the Caliphs and righteous leaders. By these matters, of sincerity of the heart, goodness of the self, and etiquette of the limbs, the recitation of the *harf* of command is valid. There is no power and no strength except by Allah, the Exalted, the Mighty. Ends.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 178:

When it had preceded that the condition for lifting sin from one who is compelled (al-mudtarr) is abstaining from transgression (al-'udwan), and such transgression, in this matter and in others, may often lead to killing, and [the surah] followed this with what it entails, as has preceded, until it concluded with this verse, and concluded it with praise of patience, truthfulness in the claim of faith, fulfilling the covenant, and everything else; and among the things the People of the Book feared regarding the covenant was the matter of shedding blood, so they changed all of it or part of it, as He, exalted is He, indicated by His saying ﴿And when We took your covenant: that you shall not shed your blood﴾ [al-Baqarah: 84] and so on; and patience in giving up the soul is the greatest patience, and doing it is the greatest confirmation of faith, and submission to retaliation (al-qisas) is more binding in fulfilling the covenant; He informed the believers of what was obligatory upon them of that and what follows from it. So He, exalted is He, said, delighting them by turning to them with address: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., who claimed faith with their tongues. And when this qualification was achieved by it, and the discipline that had occurred earlier was in place, the addressees knew that the ruling belongs only to Allah. His saying was constructed in the passive: ﴿prescribed for you﴾, i.e., it was enjoined (p-22) in the Book, and you have heard my warning to those who differed concerning the Book. What specified the intention of obligation is that the word "kataba" (prescribed) is widely used in the Sharia with this meaning, and the expression with ʿalā ("upon") indicates it. ﴿Retaliation (al-qisas)﴾, i.e., equality in killing and wounds, because it derives from qass, which is tracing a trace.

Al-Harali said: It is as if he follows the offender (al-jani) in the trace of what he committed, so he follows in the trace of his punishment the trace of his crime — end of quote.

﴿In the matter of the slain (al-qatla)﴾, i.e., in all matters of killing: whoever kills by something is killed by it, and whoever kills in a certain manner is killed in a similar manner. If he cut off a hand and it spread to the self, then he is to be cut off; if it does not spread, we cut off his neck, so that the verse is general, specified in some instances. And where generality is not affirmed, it would be unspecified, and specification is preferable to ambiguity. So affirm your claim of faith in what the leaders carry out as enforcement and others in submission to it, and do not be like the People of the Book who differed concerning their Book, so they believed in part of it and disbelieved in part of it. Also, when He mentioned giving wealth despite love for it, and He had mentioned that the righteous one is the one who believes in the Book, and among the Book is the giving of the soul whose love is known, He followed it with this to indicate that wealth is its equivalent, and it is not given for the sake of (p-24) Allah except with pure faith, just as the soul is not given except with that.

Since the People of the Book had altered the ruling of the Torah concerning retaliation, which the verse of al-Ma'idah indicated was prescribed for them as justice in it, whoever among them was stronger made a favor for his people in that; so the Banu al-Nadir, as Ibn Hisham transmitted in the Sirah, would take full blood-money for their slain, and the Banu Qurayza half the blood-money; and some of them, as al-Baghawi transmitted in surah al-Ma'idah from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, would kill a soul for a soul. He, glorified and exalted, indicated their opposition to this injustice, clarifying the equality: ﴿The free for the free﴾, and a free person is not killed for a slave, because that is not more binding than the stated ruling, nor equal to killing the slave for him, because that is more binding; nor is it by the ruling, so it is understood by implication of agreement.

Since He placed this first for its nobility, He followed it with His saying: ﴿and the slave for the slave﴾, magnifying the male status; likewise a slave is killed for a free person, because that is more binding, and a free person is not killed for a slave, because he is not equal in the ruling. ﴿And the female for the female﴾, and the female is killed for the male and the male for her, because each of them is equal to the other, in accordance with the original principle affirmed by his saying ﷺ, "Women are the twin halves of men," out of caution for blood, whose violation is the greatest of the major sins after shirk. The blood-money is halved if it is in place of the blood, in accordance with His saying: ﴿And for men over them is a degree﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228], and as an alert to the lowering of the sanctity of property below the sanctity of blood. Furthermore, the implication of the verse is that none is killed for the slain except his killer. When you reflect on His saying ﴿the slain (al-qatla)﴾ rather than saying "the killing (al-qatl)," you will know this.

Al-Harali said: Because taking from one other than the offender is not retaliation but a second aggression, and aggression is not lifted by aggression; aggression is lifted only by retaliation upon its like alone — end of quote.

Likewise, taking from one who is not equal is aggression, so a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, as indicated by retaliation itself, and the restriction of the ruling to the people of faith, along with His, glorified and exalted, saying ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of the Garden are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20], and in similar verses.

Since He, glorified and exalted, opened for us the door of mercy through retaliation, alerting to the rebuke of the People of the Book, and that was from the ruling of the Torah but as a binding obligation, and pardon was upon the Christians in the same way, He showed in the Furqan an additional expansion by removing this burden from us through the choice between them.

Al-Harali said: Transferring from the punishment of the Hereafter to the trial of this world, and transferring from the trial of this world in blood to expiation by taking a portion of wealth, as was in the first ransom for the slaughter of Ibrahim, upon him be peace, from his son. So He said: ﴿Whoever is pardoned﴾ for his offence, from pardon (al-'afw), which is what comes without strain or compulsion — end of quote.

He expressed it in the passive form to indicate that the ruling follows the pardon from whatever pardoner had the power of pardon in a matter (p-27) of the right, even if it is small. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿something from his brother﴾, i.e., whatever kind of pardon there was by descending from demanding blood to blood-money. In the expression of the word "brother," as al-Harali said, there is a bond between the offender and the one wronged and his guardians, from the standpoint of ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake﴾ [al-Nisa': 92]. Even if it was not a mistake of nature, it is a mistake of intention, since he did not intend to kill a believer; he intended to kill an enemy, a reviler, or one who attacks his family, property, or child. So when the veil of nature is lifted, he returns to the brotherhood of faith. ﴿Then compliance﴾, i.e., then the matter in that is compliance from the guardian of the blood ﴿with fairness (bil-ma'ruf)﴾, in which is the training of the self to break it from the heat of what the grudges of crimes drag it toward; and what is fair is what is witnessed plainly as agreeable, and accepted in its place among people, so no denial of it reaches them.

Since He commanded the one complying with the command of the one paying, He said: ﴿and payment to him with goodness﴾, lest (p-28) he combine his offence, or the offence of his guardian, with bad settlement. In informing him is an obligation upon the guardians of the offender to be humble, submissive, and equitable toward the guardians of the slain, given the authority they have: ﴿We have given his guardian authority﴾ [al-Isra': 33]; so they should be mindful before them of the mercy of Allah with which He showed them mercy, and so did not seize the offender for his offence — end of quote.

Since He, glorified and exalted, widened for us by this ruling, He alerted to its reason, magnifying the favor, and He said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the great matter of gentleness, which is the choice between retaliation and pardon freely or for blood-money, ﴿is a lightening﴾, i.e., relief from the killing and its guardians, ﴿from your Lord﴾, who is good to you with this upright and easy way and this beautiful ruling. He used the plural pronoun out of regard, as al-Harali said, for both sides, because each party is exposed to the other inflicting harm on it — end of quote.

﴿And a mercy﴾ for the guardians of the slain by blood-money, and for the others by pardon of blood. Al-Bukhari related in the Tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "Among the Children of Israel there was retaliation, and there was no blood-money among them. So whoever was pardoned something from his brother," i.e., accepts blood-money in deliberate killing, "that is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy, from what was prescribed upon those before you. Whoever (p-29) transgresses after that will be killed after accepting the blood-money" — end of quote.

The people of tafsir said: Retaliation was prescribed upon the Jews, and blood-money and pardon were forbidden to them; and pardon was upon the Christians, and blood-money was forbidden to them. Since this was a great favor, a threat against whoever rejected it followed from it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever transgresses﴾, i.e., by killing, ﴿after that﴾, i.e., after the choice and pardon, even if the pardoner was someone other than him, ﴿then for him is a painful punishment﴾ for his killing or for taking blood-money from him, as a recompense for his enmity in proportion to it and his excess, with what indicates refusal of this concession ruled by the Owner over His servants, the King whose opposition is not permissible. In naming his recompense "punishment" and not restricting it to one of the two abodes, there is a notice of its spreading to both, as a severity against him.

Al-Harali said: In the verse is evidence that one who kills deliberately does not thereby become a disbeliever. Al-Asbahani said: Ibn 'Abbas said: the killer was named at the beginning of the verse a believer, and in its middle a brother, and its end did not despair him of lightening and mercy.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 179:

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informed of the benefit of pardon (ʿafw), He then informed of the benefit of its counterpart, to complete the reproach of the People of the Book for their deviation from the text and their blindness to the wisdom (ḥikmah). So He said: ﴿And for you﴾, that is, O you who believe, ﴿in retaliation (qiṣāṣ)﴾, that is, this kind, which is the killing of a killer for the soul he has slain, without transgression or aggression, ﴿is life﴾, that is, a great and wondrous life, because whoever knows that he will be killed does not kill.

Al-Harali said: So life is for the relatives of the one who committed the crime, from among those who used to be wronged in this world by the crime of another, and life is for the offender through what is exacted from him in the Hereafter, because whoever has his sin expiated lives in the Hereafter, and whoever still bears a crime and is seized for it is, in that state, among those who neither die therein nor live, because the one being punished in the state of his punishment does not find the taste of life due to the overwhelming of his pain, nor is he in death due to his awareness of his punishment. End of quote.

As for the mere killing, as the people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, "Killing is the preventer of killing," this is not so, because whoever knows that if they kill two people, only one will be killed in return, that may encourage them to kill, and the killing becomes an initiation, and it is more inciting to killing, not more preventive of it. They were agreed upon admiring the meaning of their saying and the elegance of its wording. And it is known to every person of intellect that between it and what is in the Qur'an is as between Allah and His creation, for it exceeds the Qur'anic expression in letters and falls short in meaning. So when one wishes to correct it, "Retaliation (qiṣāṣ) is more preventive of killing (qatl) as oppression," the addition multiplies and does not reach the grace and sweetness of what is in the Qur'an. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the Granter of success.

Since this expression, as you see, is miraculous in the soundness of its meaning, the precision of its indication, and the abundance of its implications, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said, encouraging the elevation of aspirations: ﴿O people of understanding (ulī l-albāb)﴾, that is, the minds that benefit their owners by their purity from what is like the husk, since lubb is the pith (core).

Al-Harali said: It is the inner part of the intellect, whose nature is to observe the command of Allah in what is witnessed, just as the outer part of the intellect's nature is to observe the realities of created things. They are the ones who look to their Lord in His signs. End of quote.

Then He gave the reason for that in His saying: ﴿so that you may be God-fearing (tattaqūn)﴾, that is, of Allah, by submitting to what He has legislated, so that you avoid killing.

Al-Harali said: In the ambiguity of laʿalla (perhaps), which is from the speech of the Creator as has preceded, there is an indication of uncertainty that informs of their division into two categories: between one for whom that produces God-fearing (taqwā), and one for whom it bears that and increases him in transgression. End of quote.

When He, glory be to Him and exalted, urged the spending of wealth, both as recommendation and as obligation, in a state of health and stinginess, while hoping for riches and fearing poverty, as confirmation of faith, and followed it with urging the spending of the soul, its equivalent, by killing, which is one of the causes of death, He followed that with urging its spending in a state of approaching the transition, and in security from worldly poverty and with hope for the riches of the Hereafter, as a making-up for what was missed of spending it out of love for it. So He said. Al-Harali said: When He, glory be to Him and exalted, made clear the aspects of purification in these addresses, and what He obligated of the Book and taught of wisdom, and made clear that all of this rests upon taqwa (God-consciousness), which is either a fixed attribute or a renewed effort, according to how He concluded the verse ﴿It is not righteousness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177] with His words ﴿they are the God-conscious﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177], and how He concluded the verse of retribution with His words ﴿so that you may be God-conscious﴾ [al-Baqarah: 179], He raised the level of address to what is incumbent upon the God-conscious, since the first address had been prescribed for those who aspire to become God-conscious, for the sake of training and purification, through an address by which one reaches a higher address in purification, so that one advances in address from one rank to another until one attains the furthest ranks of the stages of the hearts and their states, as the indication to this has preceded. And since the preceding address mentioned killing and retribution, which are (p-34) the state of the presence of death, this brought in the mention of the bequest, because it is the state of one whom death is present. End of quotation. So He said: ﴿It has been prescribed for you﴾, meaning it has been made obligatory, as is widespread in the Law (shar'), and He emphasized it here with ʿalā (upon). Then the obligation of it was abrogated (naskh, abrogation) by the verse of inheritance, so its permissibility remained. The Sunnah clarified that inheritance and bequest do not combine, so the abrogation applies only to the close heir and not absolutely. So the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Indeed Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest to an heir." Related by Ahmad, the Four, and others, from ʿAmr ibn Kharija and Abu Umama, may Allah be pleased with them both.

﴿When death approaches one of you﴾, meaning when its causes and signs have come, ﴿if he leaves behind wealth﴾, meaning what is not appropriate to bequeath, whether little or much. As for its application to much, it is common, and it has been applied to little in ﴿Indeed, I am in need of whatever good You have sent down to me﴾ [al-Qasas: 24]. Then He mentioned the substitute for the subject of "it has been prescribed," after the longing for it had become intense (p-35), so He said: ﴿the bequest﴾, and He mentioned the verb that raises it, because of the intervening separation, to convey the strength of its demand. ﴿for the parents﴾: He began with them for their nobility and the greatness of their right. ﴿and the nearest relatives, according to what is reasonable﴾, meaning the justice that people recognize in equality and preference.

Al-Harali said: All of this concerns the one who is dying, and "what is reasonable" is that which souls accept and find no aversion to. End of quotation. He emphasized the obligation by His words ﴿as a duty﴾, and likewise His words ﴿upon the God-conscious﴾. So this is an urging, an arousing, and a reminder of what lies ahead of him, namely meeting the One who will hold him to account for the smallest and the least.

(p-36) When [the verse] made the obligation to act upon this (justice), which taqwa calls for, a consequence of its being an act, He said: ﴿So whoever alters it﴾, i.e., the bequest made in the lawful manner, or the thing bequeathed, by changing its substance if it is a specific item, or by reducing it if it is a fungible item (mithli).

Al-Harali said: When the God-fearing were entrusted with conveying what they left to their parents and relatives, and they carried it out in accordance with what is right, the threat was directed against whoever alters it among them. Its implication is that the obligatory shares (fara'id) were revealed because of a shortcoming that occurred regarding the bequest. It is as if, had matters remained as they were, the whole property would have been the portion of the deceased. When the shares were prescribed, two-thirds were taken away from his hands, and one-third remained under the first ruling. It also makes clear that the prescribed share is itself the bequest, so there is no bequest to an heir, because the prescribed share is its substitute. End of quotation.

﴿After he has heard it﴾, i.e., has known it with certainty. As for one who has not ascertained it and so exercises ijtihad, there is no sin. He reinforced the warning against changing the one who changes it, and against the silence of the rest about it, by His saying: ﴿Its sin is only upon those who alter it﴾, i.e., the alteration, ﴿upon those who alter it﴾, whether by act or by intention; nothing of it reaches the one who made the bequest. Since the testator and the one who alters it have sayings, deeds (p-37) and intentions, He warned with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿is Hearing﴾, i.e., of what each of them says, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their secret and open conduct in this matter. So let whoever does evil beware, even if he displays something other than it, and beware of the supplication of the wronged, for indeed Allah answers it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 182:

Since the warning against altering (the bequest) concerns only the carrying out of justice, and since the testator may at times deviate in his bequest out of ignorance or a motive, his words follow: ﴿And whoever fears﴾, that is, knows, anticipates and suspects, (the word for fear) being applied to it because it is one of its causes. Perhaps he expressed it this way to indicate that in this matter suspicion (ẓann) suffices. ﴿from a testator, deviation﴾, that is, inclination in the bequest, by mistake, ﴿or sin﴾, that is, inclination in it deliberately.

Al-Ḥarālī said: The true meaning of al-janaf is concealing an injustice in the form of righteousness, end of quote. (p-38) ﴿then makes peace between them﴾, that is, between the testator and the beneficiaries, if this happens during his lifetime, by advising him in a way that pleases hearts; or between the beneficiaries and the heirs after his death, if harm is feared, so that he brings them into agreement on a matter they accept.

Al-Ḥarālī said: In the mention of fear from the testator there is an indication that this occurs while the testator is still alive, not after the bequest has been fixed upon deviation following death, for that does not fall under the content of this address. And in placing the reconciliation upon the word "between" (bayn) there is an indication that the reconciliation reaches the separation which is the joining of what lies between them; so it is from the meaning of what the grammarians call an object of extension (maf'ūl ʿalā al-siʿah), since it is not "fa-aṣlaḥa baynahu wa-baynahum", end of quote.

﴿then there is no sin upon him﴾, that is, for this alteration. Since the one exercising independent judgment (mujtahid) may err, and if he were held accountable for his error he would refrain from ijtihad, God, glorified is He, rewarded him by giving the reason for lifting the sin in his words, to inform that the ruling is general for every mujtahid: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One specially encompassing knowledge (p-39) ﴿is Forgiving﴾, that is, toward one who intended good but erred, ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, He deals with him in honor the way a merciful one deals with one he shows mercy to.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 183:

When He, glory be to Him, permitted eating from what He had created, as a proof of His oneness and of His general and particular mercy, and since it is in human nature to monopolize (istithar), and monopolizing leads to strife (fitan), He followed this with the ruling on the one under compulsion (al-mudtarr). He indicated His restraining of people from transgression (al-'udwan) by forbidding it to them in a state of destruction (al-talaf). In this there is a restraint for others by way of a fortiori argument (bi-tariq al-uwla). Then He gave precedence to the recommendation (al-nadb) to relinquish what has come into one's hand of the goods of this world, for the six categories (al-asnaf al-sitta) and whoever accompanies them, and then to the obligation of zakat, as a way of making one renounce the splendor of the life of this world, so as to uproot transgression from its root. He followed this with the ruling concerning one who may transgress, then with what came after it of relinquishing wealth at the approach of death. Thus the soul was trained in renunciation through what is rationally understood in meaning, beginning from the relinquishing of it for one who benefits from it, and then followed by the command to relinquish it not for someone in need of it, but for God who brought it into being, purely for the purification and cleansing of the soul, so that it may be prepared for what the quality of being the Eternal Refuge (al-samadiyya) requires of it by way of wisdom. This is in addition to the suitability of retaliation (al-qisas) and bequest (al-wasiyya) to fasting, in that retaliation involves the killing of the soul in a sensory sense, and fasting involves the killing of desire, which is the cause of intercourse, which is the cause of the bringing into being of the soul in a sensory sense. In retaliation there is life for bodies in a spiritual sense, and in fasting there is life for spirits through the purity of hearts and their emptiness for reflection, and their preparation to receive wisdom and the fear that calls to piety, and the extinguishing of desire. Its month is the month of patience, which is sought as an aid to gratitude. In it there is a reminder of hardship, which urges beneficence toward the one who suffers hardship, and it is an incitement to renounce the world and to adorn oneself with the attributes of the angels. For this reason the Qur'an was revealed in it, received from the King. Thus it is the most fitting thing for the verse of bequest, in which the pious are commanded to renounce the world at the approach of gathering with the angels. Its conclusion with forgiveness and mercy is an indication regarding the fasting person, being among the people closest to these two.

So He said, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. He addressed them with what first turns to the lowest of the ranks who have committed themselves to the command of religion, because they had no driving love or longing that would move them to do it without obligation. This is unlike those above them in rank, the believers and the doers of good, for they used to perform the markers of Islam without compulsion, so they would fast according to the degree of spiritual vitality they found in it. This is what al-Harali said, and he said: Therefore they were not addressed in the Qur'an with a distant address, nor were they mentioned except in praise. Those who are addressed in the Qur'an as "O you who..." are the people who became aware of what some of them indicated to others, and those who have believed, being in the place of being commanded while falling short of hastening. Therefore every address in the Qur'an is directed to these two categories, except what is directed to the human being with a description of blame in a few verses. End of quotation.

﴿Fasting has been prescribed﴾, i.e., obligated, by what is widespread in the language of the Shari'a and confirmed by the particle of elevation ('ala), ﴿for you﴾. Fasting (al-siyam) is abstention from what breaks the fast, from the break of dawn until sunset, with intention. Al-Harali said: It was made obligatory because of what it contains of preparation for knowledge of wisdom and knowledge of what you did not know. It is steadfastness in restraint from what is proper for a thing to act upon, and the thing's condition being like the sun in the middle of the sky. It is said: "the sun fasted" (sammat) when no movement appears in it toward ascent or descent, which is among its nature; and "the horses fasted" (sammat al-khayl) when they are neither spurred nor ridden. Thus a person's restraint from what it is his nature to do, such as preserving his body by eating, preserving his offspring by marriage, and engaging in false speech and bad deeds, is his fasting. In fasting there is abstention from food, withdrawal from the condition of livestock, and cessation of the desires of the private parts. Its completion is turning away from the concerns of this world, turning toward God, and secluding oneself in His house, so that by this the springs of wisdom may flow from the heart. It was made obligatory (kataban) so that whoever is obligated to it does not fall short of it, for if he does, his religion is broken, just as the seam of a waterskin breaks when the waterskin on which it is written is torn. End of quotation.

﴿As it was prescribed﴾, i.e., obligated, so the comparison is in the general sense of obligation, ﴿upon those﴾ who came ﴿before you﴾. It seems that the People of the Two Books alone were intended. He also affirmed the situation by saying ﴿before you﴾. This indicates that it is among what they violated the covenant regarding and concealed, out of eagerness for the misguidance of the Arabs. Since emulation raises up the weak resolve and kindles and elevates the cold hearts, because a difficult thing becomes easier to bear when it is shared, He said: ﴿so that you may be pious﴾, i.e., that you may place between yourselves and incurring God's displeasure a shield, by hastening to it and persevering in it, hoping for the pleasure of your Lord and fearing those who came before you, so that piety may become a firmly established attribute for you, and you may be among those for whom I made the Book a guidance. For fasting breaks desire, subdues the passions, and so restrains one from agreeing with evil.

Al-Harali said: In its indication is a classification of those who are bound by this into two types: one for whom fasting, in its manner of intensity, bears the fruit of piety, and one for whom it does not bear that fruit.

(p-45) Since this Ummah has a compilation of what is in the earlier Scriptures and scrolls, the foundations of its rulings follow the rulings of the earlier ones. Just as they were directed to the direction of the People of the Book at the beginning, and then were given the direction of the Ka'bah at the end, so too they were made to fast the fast of the People of the Book: ﴿for a certain number of days﴾, meaning a few days, measured by a known number at the beginning. Then they were elevated to fasting the full month, the cycle of the moon, as a final measure. This is because those before them were people of reckoning for matters of worldly affairs, and their years were solar, so their fasting was a number of days and not a full month. In its announcement there is an obligation to renew the intention for each day, since they are ﴿counted days﴾. In its implication there is a prohibition against prolonging the fast into the night, which is the meaning of continuous fasting (wisal). Its validity indicates the elevation of the status of the fast to a fast of the month, which is the cycle of the moon, while it persuades (p-46) breaking the fast at night as a concession for the weak, not as a firm obligation on the one who fasts. The fast also had the same hardship as the fast of the People of the Book, in that there was no eating or intercourse after sleep. Thus it contained the hardship of what was in the Scriptures, so that the head and early members of this Ummah would obtain a share of the attainment of the early nations. Then God elevates it to the ruling specific to it, so it becomes trained, finding the taste of ease after hardship. End of quotation, with some alteration.

The position of al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, is the prohibition of wisal. They said: "O Messenger of God, you practise continuous fasting!" He said: "I am not like your condition." And he said: "Whoever is practising continuous fasting, let him continue until the pre-dawn meal (suhur)."

Al-Harali said: He informed of prolonging the fast until the pre-dawn meal, so that the meal of breaking the fast, which conforms to the condition of the People of the Book, is transferred to the meal of suhur, which is specific to the people of the Furqan. End of quotation. Regarding the Prophet's ﷺ practice of continuous fasting with them when they refused anything but continuous fasting for days, there is no evidence in it for one who permits this. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.

Al-Harali said: In founding it upon a number there is a refuge to which one returns when the month, which is the crescent, is obscured, as will be explicitly stated. So the number in fasting holds the place of tayammum in purification. They return to it when there is a necessity from the absence of the sighting of the crescent, just as they return to the earth (sa'id) when water is absent.

Since the sick person has a need for medicine and food according to the weakness of his body, the obligation was lifted from him. Therefore, from what preceded, the saying of God, glorified and exalted, follows: ﴿So whoever among you is sick﴾, meaning an illness that harms him immediately or increases his ailment later.

Al-Harali said: So he remains under the ruling of sustaining himself with certainty, with what nourishes and gives drink to the believer from the unseen blessing of God, glorified and exalted, as the blessed Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "I spend the night with my Lord; He feeds me and gives me drink." So the believer has nourishment in his fasting from the blessing of his Lord, by the ruling of his certainty, in what does not reach one who has not reached its station. According to the degree to which people's inner selves are supported by their outer selves, the outer self of the certain one is supported by his inner self, until it becomes strong in his limbs by the support of the light of his inner self, as this has appeared among the people of sainthood and piety. So the breaking of the fast by the sick person is a concession for the place of his treatment and nourishment.

Since illness is an attribute, it came with the wording of an attribute. And since travel, which is removing shelter from the head through movement away from it, completing a cycle of day and night in motion, such that one cannot return to one's dwelling within the orbit of one's day and night, is a relation between two physical bodies, it came with the separate preposition, so He said: ﴿or on a journey﴾. This is because the traveller needs nourishment for the full vigour of his exertion in his work during his journey, and because the time of his nourishment depends on the places, not on choice, since the traveller and his goods are in a state of anxiety, except whom God protects. "Travel is a piece of punishment." This is so that two hardships do not gather upon the servant, so that the difficulty is doubled upon him in religion and in worldly affairs. When the matter is lightened for him in one natural respect, he takes up the ruling from another religious respect. ﴿then a number﴾: its composition indicates that what is prescribed is a number ﴿of other days﴾, meaning consecutive or separate, ﴿other﴾, for the coherence of the parts of speech, some joined to others, in their beginnings and endings. So in its implication, the prescribed obligation for the sick and the traveller is other than the prescribed obligation for the healthy and the resident. Therefore, there is no need for an estimate: "then he breaks the fast," because the aim is the meaning of prescription, and what is below prescription remains (p-47) under the ruling of its bearing. It is as if it is said to the sick and the traveller: "Your prescribed days are other days, not these days." So these days remain free from the ruling of prescription, but not free from the legislation of fasting.

Since they were a people not accustomed to fasting, and God's care encompassed them out of honour for their Messenger ﷺ, He spoke, giving them a choice at the beginning of the matter: ﴿And for those who are able to do it﴾, meaning the fast, from the root ṭawq, which is what is placed around the neck as an ornament. So what he is able to do of actions becomes, in meaning, a collar for him. ﴿a ransom, the feeding of a poor person﴾, with the genitive construction or with separation. In the singular, it refers back to a single day, and in the plural, it refers back to the collective of days, so for each day there is one meal. It is a mudd and two handfuls with the two palms, which is the sustenance of one who scoops, for lunch and dinner, sufficient, neither stinting nor extravagant. Within it is the widening of the matter of fasting for one who is not able, from among those who, because the appetite of his nature is overpowering, are in the position of the sick and the traveller. He is ill with gluttony, as if it were a sickness the nature was created with. So in considering it there is the fulfilment of the mercy shown toward the sick and the traveller, except for the difference between the ranks of the two categories, in that this one is able and those two are not able or not capable. And in its announcement there is an explanation that whoever cannot restrain himself from eating must feed another, so that giving food stands in place of abstaining from food, because of the correspondence between the two meanings. Nothing is mentioned here together with the food, neither freeing a slave nor fasting. ﴿So whoever volunteers good﴾, meaning increases the ransom, ﴿it is better for him﴾, because he has done what shows his love for his Lord.

Since God, glorified and exalted, has driven the breaking of the fast when one is able and the ransom, obligatory and recommended, in the manner of the third person, and omitted mentioning breaking the fast even though context indicates it, as a pointer to its baseness, to repel one from it, He made the people of fasting the locus of direct address, as a notice of the nobility they have over all that, encouraging and urging them to it. So He said: ﴿And that you fast﴾, O you who are able, ﴿is better for you﴾ than the ransom, even if it is greater.

Al-Harali said: In this there is an indication that the one who fasts receives a considerable share of good in his body, his health and his provision, along with the great reward in the Hereafter, as the sacred hadith indicates: "Every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting, for it is for Me." This is because deeds are actions, expenditures, conduct and states, which are of the servant's concern to do for himself and his family in his worldly life, and since they are of his concern, they belong to him. Since fasting is not of his concern, it does not belong to him. Prayer, for example, consists of actions and speech, and that is of a person's concern. Zakat is expenditure, and that is of his concern. Hajj is travelling on the earth, and that is of his concern. But it is not of his concern that he does not eat, drink, marry, or take redress from one who wrongs him. So if someone reviles him or fights him, let him say: "I am fasting." So the totality of fasting's aims is not of his concern, and its reality is the dissolving of his body, the weakening of his self and its mortification. For this reason fasting is an expiation for killing by mistake, so that by fasting he may obtain, in some way, from the killing of his self what has happened at his hand by mistake of killing. So in fasting there is a diminishing of the fasting person's essence. Therefore He said: "it is for Me," since it is not of the kind of human action. God, glorified and exalted, said: "And I recompense it." So in its indication, its reward is from the unseen of God, of which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of any human. All of that is in the implication of His saying ﴿if you know﴾. End of quotation.

Its answer, and God, glorified and exalted, knows best: you fasted and volunteered. For if they did not know that it was better for them, they would not have done it, and then it would not have been better for them.

Al-Harali said: It was better, since between combining fasting and feeding there was no opposition, but rather mutual support, which the word "good" indicates. End of quotation.

Al-Bukhari, may God be pleased with him, in the Book of Tafsir, and Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', may God be pleased with him, who said: "When ﴿And for those who are able to do it﴾ was revealed, whoever wished to break the fast would pay a ransom, until the verse after it was revealed and abrogated it." In another narration: "until this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185]."

In al-Bukhari, from Ibn Umar: "From the companions of Muhammad, may God be pleased with them, they said: ﴿The month of Ramadan﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185] was revealed, and it was hard upon them. So whoever fed a poor person each day, left the fast, though he was able to fast, and they were given concession in that. Then it abrogated it: ﴿And that you fast is better for you﴾, so they were commanded to fast."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 185 (part 1 of 2):

When he had left the matter of the days vague at first, making it an obligation with a choice for the one able to fast, he specified it here and settled the matter concerning it by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The month of Ramadan﴾ (p-54), because that is more momentous and more emphatic than specifying it from the outset.

Al-Harali said: The "shahr" (month) is the crescent that by its nature completes one cycle from the time it appears (yuhilla) until it appears a second time, whether its days number twenty-nine or thirty; both numbers are one in the validity of the designation "month." It is applied commonly to two units that increase in number by the completion of the cycle, as one of the two units comes to its named (musammah) Ramadan. It is said: it is one of the names of God, glorified and exalted is He. Its derivation is from al-ramda' (the scorching), which is the intensifying of the heat of stones at midday. As if this month was named for falling in a time of intense heat, by an arrangement whereby Muharram is reckoned from the beginning (p-55) of the season of winter, so that the beginning of the year is the first beginning of creation through the reviving of the earth after its death. He said: By this the two springs coincide: the earthly spring preceding, when the sun enters Pisces, and the heavenly spring following, when the sun enters Aries. He said: When this community's predecessors had a fast like the fast of the People of the Book, just as they had been directed to the qibla first, facing the People of the Book, the elevation to the ruling of the Criterion (al-Furqan) specific to them overtook that, so their fixed fast was made for them by the month, because they are a people of months, looking to the crescents, not absorbed in the reckoning of the sun. So their fasting was made dependent on the sighting of the month, and the month was made for them a single day. It is as though they were moved from fasting a number of counted days to fasting one uncounted day, by its unity, because they are an unlettered community. ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights﴾ [al-A'raf: 142] is the appointed time of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ); ﴿and We completed them with ten﴾ [al-A'raf: 142] is the appointed time of Moses, peace be upon him, and his community, and those after him of the nations up to this community. End of quotation.

Since this was a discourse of elevation, He praised Himself, exalted is He, by the sending down of the Reminder in it (p-56) all at once to the House of Honour (bayt al-'izza), and its descent to the earth began from there.

Al-Harali said: He manifested in it the purpose of the fast and its unseen wisdom, which did not occur in the earlier scriptures, the Book, so He said: ﴿in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾. This indicates that in fasting there is a good receptivity to its meaning and ease in its recitation, and for this reason it combines in it the fasting of the day and the night prayer (tahajjud) at night. The word is an intensive form (sighah mubalaghah) from al-qur' (gathering), which is what gathers the books, the scrolls and the tablets. End of quotation.

In praising it by the sending down of the Qur'an in it there is praise of the Qur'an through it, insofar as it indicates that among the greatest aims of its legislation (p-57) is the purifying of thought in order to understand the Qur'an, so that one may be made to stand upon the reality of what He followed this with of its attributes, which confirmed what the surah opened with: that it is "no doubt in it" and that it is "guidance" in a broader sense than that first one. So He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿a guidance for mankind﴾.

Al-Harali said: In it is an indication that a group of people is elevated by the fast, namely through preparation for reflection and understanding and the humbling of the self to the rank of those who believe and the believers, and it raises them to the rank of the doers of good. So it is guidance in which the lack of nourishment nourishes the heart just as its presence nourishes the body. For this reason, all who have tested the practices of religion among those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His face, agree that the key to guidance is only hunger, and that when the stomach and the limbs are weakened for God, God, glorified and exalted is He, illumines the heart, clarifies the self and strengthens the body, so that there appears in the matter of faith, by the turning of custom, a new custom which is for His friends more magnificent in strength and grace than their custom in the world, for the common run of His creation. In His indication there is a glimpse of what the fasting person is aided by: the shutting of the gates of the Fire, (p-58) the opening of the gates of Paradise, and the chaining of the devils, all of which is by what narrows the channels of Satan through the blood, which fasting diminishes. So in it is the key to all good. When it guides mankind, it is more guiding to those who believe, and it is a light for them, and for the believers it is brighter. Likewise, up to the highest ranks of the fasting, devoted, remembering ones who remember God much, who hold fast by the fast from everything other than sitting in the company of the Truth through His remembrance.

In His saying: ﴿and clear proofs﴾ is an announcement of the mention of what the fasting person finds of the light of his heart, the humbling of his self, and the preparation of his thought for understanding, so that he witnesses those clear proofs within himself, and that they are ﴿of the guidance﴾, the more general, more complete, more perfect, encompassing all creation, ﴿and the Criterion﴾, the most perfect. In the attainment of the Criterion through the blessing of the fast, which is the explanation of the ranks that the Truth has manifested in their proper form, is an indication of what the fasting person is granted of gathering (jam'), which is from His name the All-Gatherer (al-Jami'), which is not attained except after the Criterion is realized. For the building upon piety, which is bestowed on the fasting person in His saying in the earlier books ﴿that you may be God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 183], is a fast upon which piety is built, upon which the Criterion is built, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you fear God, He will grant you a Criterion﴾ [al-Anfal: 29], which ends in a gathering indicated by the transfer of the fast from the number of days to the unity of the month. End of quotation.

So according to what I have said, the intended "guidance" is the literal meaning; according to what al-Harali said, it is a metaphor whose relation is causality, because the fast prepares for understanding and necessitates light.
