The meaning of the first is the prophethood of Moses, peace be upon him, which is clear; the meaning of the second is the prophethood of Jesus, peace be upon him, for the Mount Seir is the mount of Galilee, which lies between Tiberias and the Plain of the Children of 'Amir; and the meaning of the third is the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), for Paran is blessed Mecca.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 211:

Since the Children of Israel were the people most knowledgeable about the manifestation of Allah's glory in the cloud, because of what their forefathers saw from Him when they left Egypt, at Mount Sinai (Jabal al-Tur), and in the Tent of Meeting (Qubbat al-Zaman), and what was transmitted to them of the abundance of awe and the magnitude of majesty in that, (p-187) Allah the Exalted said, answering one who seemed to ask: "How can this be?" ﴿Ask﴾ by transferring the vowel of the ʿayn (ḥarakat al-ʿayn, the vowel of the middle letter) to the fāʾ (the first letter), so that the hamzat al-waṣl (the connecting hamza, a hamza dropped in connected speech) was dispensed with. ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, that is, those who are the most envious of the Arabs. Then He asked a question, or began a new statement: ﴿how many clear signs did We give them﴾ of that and of other things (p-188) ﴿through their prophets﴾. They cannot deny that, and their silence while hearing it from you is an acknowledgment from them.

Al-Harali said: "Since what they were warned of was a general matter, they were referred to the details of events, the specification of battles, and the occurrence of similar cases and parallels, as had happened before, and its example occurred among the Children of Israel, because what happened among them is repeated in this community, exactly like the sandal matching the sandal and the feather matching the feather. So He said: ﴿Ask﴾, seeking to make them speak about their condition, not to inform them or have them report. The Prophet's ﷺ attention to what Allah witnesses of the conditions of the Children of Israel, their kings, their rabbis, their days, their dispersion, their divisions and the various forms of their afflictions, is his questioning and seeking insight, not that he should ask one of them and be told." End of quotation. He said this, but the apparent meaning is that it is a permission to question them, for the Prophet ﷺ never asked them about anything and they lied in their answer without his clarifying their lie, except that they were exposed as liars, as in the case of the punishment for adultery, the matter of their question about their father, the matter of the poisoned sheep, and similar cases. In that there is an increase in the faith of whoever witnesses it, an establishment of proof against them (p-189), and other benefits.

Since the implied meaning is: "So whenever they changed any of Our signs and treated it lightly, We punished them and intensified their punishment, as is indicated by what I have quoted from the Torah in this register for whoever reflects," He linked to it His saying: ﴿And whoever substitutes﴾, from substitution (al-tabdīl), which is making a thing other than what it was, ﴿the blessing of Allah﴾, that is, the One from whom there is no blessing except from Him, which is the cause of guidance. So he makes it a cause of misguidance, or a cause of gratitude, and he makes it a cause of disbelief, whoever he may be.

Al-Harali said: "The origin of this substitution is rejecting the knowledge of the learned man, rejecting the righteousness of the righteous, not following the learned man's knowledge, and not being guided by the righteous man's piety. That is the partnership that takes place between the common people and the scholars and the pious, and it is the disbelief in Allah's blessing and its substitution." End of quotation.

Since the intelligent of people seeks out blessings before they come to him, while the dull and foolish (p-190) rejoices in them only after they have overflowed upon him, and since what is feared is substituting them at a certain time and not at every time, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿after what has come to them﴾, that is, and has become firmly established in their knowledge. This is to alert that whoever substitutes it in that state has sunk below the lowest of human beings and joined what has no intellect among the animals.

Since the implied meaning is: "Allah destroys him," He gave the reason with His saying: ﴿for indeed Allah﴾, that is, the Mighty in station, ﴿is severe in punishment﴾, and that is a punishment that follows the crime. He mentioned some of what indicates the truth of the claim concerning the knowledge of the Children of Israel, through what was in the manifestation of glory in the cloud of terror and the clear signs He gave them. He said at the beginning of the fifth book of the Torah: "Now hear, O Israel, the statutes and the judgments which I teach you, that you may observe them and live, and go in and possess the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, is giving you. You shall not add to the word which I command you (p-191), nor take from it. You have seen what the Lord did at Baal-peor; for the Lord your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal-peor. But you who held fast to the Lord your God are alive today. See, I have taught you statutes and judgments, just as the Lord my God commanded me, that you should act according to them in the land which you are going to possess. Keep them and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, who, when they hear all these statutes, will say, 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.' For what great nation is there that has God so near to it, as the Lord our God is to us, for whatever reason we may call upon Him? And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law which I set before you today? Only take heed to yourself, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. And teach them to your children and your grandchildren, especially the day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, when the Lord said to me, 'Gather the people to Me, and I will let them hear My words, that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live on the earth (p-192), and that they may teach their children.' So you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of heaven, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness. Then the Lord spoke to you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but saw no form; you only heard a voice. So He declared to you His covenant which He commanded you to perform, the Ten Commandments; and He wrote them on two tablets of stone. Take careful heed to yourselves, for you saw no form when the Lord spoke to you at Horeb out of the midst of the fire, lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the form of any figure: the likeness of male or female, the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged fowl that flies in the air, the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, or the likeness of any fish that is in the water beneath the earth. And lest you raise your eyes to heaven, and when you see the sun, the moon, and the stars, all the host of heaven, you are drawn away and worship them and serve them, which the Lord your God has divided to all the peoples under the whole heaven. But the Lord has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be His people, an inheritance, as you are this day." This is its text. It has been fully discussed before, from the second book of the Torah, at His saying: ﴿And when Moses asked for water for his people﴾ [al-Baqara: 60]. So the return to narrating what Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, wills (p-193) of the conditions of the Children of Israel for the purposes already stated, to the utmost degree of judgments and at the highest level of excellent order, and the manifestation of the angels in the shades of the cloud, is a familiar matter. In the Ṣaḥīḥ, from al-Barāʾ, may Allah be pleased with him, he said:

"A man was reciting Surat al-Kahf, and beside him was a horse tied with two ropes. A cloud covered him and began to draw near and draw near, and his horse began to shy. When morning came, he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said: 'That was tranquillity descending with the Qur'an.'"

And from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, may Allah be pleased with him, that "while he was reciting Surat al-Baqara with his horse tied beside him, the horse began to leap about. He fell silent and it calmed down; then he recited and it leapt again, so he left. When morning came, he related it to the Prophet ﷺ, and said: 'I raised my head to the sky and saw something like a shade in which were things like lamps. I raised my head until I could no longer see them.' He said: 'Do you know what that was?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Those were angels who drew near to your voice. Had you recited, the people would have seen them in the morning, looking at them, and they would not have hidden from them'" (p-194).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 212:

When there had preceded the command to peace (silm) and the warning against deviating from it, with what necessarily requires adherence to it definitively, it was as if it were said: What did those addressed by these commands do, and who were restrained by those deterrents? It was said: most of them refused. It was then said: Indeed, this is astonishing! What was it that barred them? It was said: the decree of the Mighty (al-'Aziz), whose purpose cannot be opposed, the Wise (al-Hakim) whose gradual leading (istidraj) is too subtle for thoughts. It was then said: How is ingratitude for blessing (kufr al-ni'mah) conceivable from a sane person? So He explained that the cause of this is generally haughtiness, pride, arrogance and insolence, exulting in what is in hand and inclining toward it, and turning away from what is hidden in the treasuries of God under the veil of power. So He said, resuming, with the passive verb to indicate the weakness of their minds, in that they are deceived by everything that is adorned: ﴿Adorned is﴾

Al-Harali said: it is from adornment (tazyin) by that which has adornment (zinah), and it is the brightness of the eye, which does not penetrate to the inner reality of what is adorned, end of quote.

﴿For those who disbelieved﴾, to the point that they replaced blessing, ﴿is the life of this world﴾, because of its presence, so it diverts them from the unseen Hereafter.

Al-Harali said: Within it is an indication that admiring the brightness of this world is itself disbelief, insofar as the sight of reason and faith perceives its folds and witnesses its carrion, so one is not deceived by its adornment. It is the affliction of creation in their cutting off from the Truth. God, exalted, left the adorner unspecified in this verse so that it would include the lowest adornment, which falls upon the tongue of Satan, and the most hidden adornment, which comes from God's gradual leading (istidraj), as in His saying, exalted: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every nation their deeds﴾ [al-An'am: 108].

When He mentioned that, He explained their state in His sight, saying: ﴿And they mock﴾, meaning, while the state is that they continually mock, that is, they cause mockery to occur, and it is (p-196) the belittling of reason to jest. Al-Harali said: it is the belittling of reason in meaning, in the position of ridiculing in action, in the senses. ﴿at those who believe﴾, because of their weakness and need, due to their turning away from this world out of desire for what is with God, because God, glorified and exalted, has granted them knowledge that pierces those veils and uncovers the curtains of the unseen; and because God withholds this world from them and protects them from it, out of His desire for them, away from it, for their honor with Him, just as a person protects his beloved from food and drink if he is ill, out of honor for him. Thus the disbelievers, with this adornment, together with what We have made them to inhabit of humiliation through various kinds of threats, of which there is no doubt about Our power, are occupied with a trifle of life. They are content with their conditions and delighted with them, to the extent that they do not look to the outcome, but rather remain with the present state, so they mock the people of truth, blind to the clear proofs, turning away from the warning, abandoning reflection on the conditions of the Children of Israel.

When the ridiculing of people of rank was bitter and harmful to souls, God, exalted, gave good news of the reversal of affairs in the abode of eternity, encouraging taqwa after faith, saying: ﴿But those who were mindful [of God]﴾, meaning they believed out of fear of God, exalted, thereby excluding the hypocrites and those who could be included in the preceding statement, ﴿will be above them﴾ in provision, rank and place, according to the evidence of ﴿Then depart [in multitudes]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 199] and the verse ﴿He said: Indeed I had a companion﴾ [al-Saffat: 51], and every delightful matter, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾; so they will laugh at them, as recompense for what they used to do.

When the change of conditions was near to them as something impossible, it was as if it were said, bringing that near: with a provision from God which He will give them, ﴿and God﴾, with the might of His dominion, the majesty of His greatness and the dazzling of His generosity, ﴿gives provision to whomever He wills﴾, meaning in this world and in the Hereafter, even if he is the poorest and most incapable of people.

When giving is without measure and occurs only out of abundance and in abundance, He said: ﴿without reckoning﴾, meaning provision that has no limit and cannot be counted, for everything that is subject to limit is confined, finite, and countable. In this nation there is one whom God does not hold to account for what He has given him, so it is (p-198) in his case literally in this respect.

It is as if it were asked: was this disbelief and adornment (of falsehood) from the beginning of the matter, or is it something that occurred, so that its occurrence would be more astonishing? It is said: for the Wise One there is no difference between this and that, for His power over the great and the small, the ignorant and the knowing, the frivolous and the forbearing, is on one level. Moreover, what has actually happened is that this was something that occurred after the clarification and the manifest proofs. ﴿The people were﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿a single community﴾, that is, gathered upon one thing, some of them leading others and some following others. Then He emphasised their unity by saying: ﴿one﴾, that is, upon the Straight Path. Then some of them slipped, so they differed, and the paths scattered them, as in the verse of Yunus: ﴿And the people were not but a single community, then they differed﴾ [Yunus: 19]. This is the view of most of the verifiers (muhaqqiqun), as stated by al-Isfahani. Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili has also narrated it in his Musnad with a continuous chain from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "upon Islam, all of them."

(p-199) ﴿Then Allah sent﴾, that is, the One for whom there is no judgement besides Him, ﴿the Prophets﴾, whom Allah Most High raised above the rest of His creation, so He informed them of what He willed of His command and sent them to His creatures, ﴿as bringers of good news﴾ to whoever obeys, and this is in the manner of preserving health; and because it is intended in itself, He placed it first, ﴿and warners﴾ to whoever disobeys, and this is in the manner of removing sickness by medicine.

Al-Harali said: In this is an announcement that the Prophets had no share in guidance; rather they are only those who bring out what is hidden in the innate natures and dispositions of creation, so they give good news to whoever has been created upon goodness and warn whoever has been formed upon evil. They do not introduce a matter that was not there; rather they make manifest a matter that was hidden. This is the state of every imam and scholar in his time, through whom Allah distinguishes the wicked from the good. End.

﴿And He sent down with them the Book﴾, that is, His speech comprehensive of guidance.

Al-Harali said: To make firm the doubled matter, so that the command is established by two witnesses, which is stronger than by one witness. For in the Messenger there was sufficiency, and in the Book alone there was sufficiency, but Allah Most High doubled the matter and joined the Book and the Messenger, so that the proof would be complete. End.

﴿with the truth﴾, that is, the established, firm in every way, ﴿that He might judge﴾, that is, Allah through the medium of the Book, ﴿between the people concerning that in which they differed﴾, from the true religion upon which they were before that, being ﴿one community﴾. Then, after the striving for the most upright way, they went astray knowingly after the death of the Messengers, and so they differed concerning the religion because of their differing about the Book. ﴿And none differed concerning it﴾, that is, concerning the Book that guides to the truth, in which there is no doubt, sent down to remove differing, ﴿except those﴾. Since it is abominable for one who has knowledge to oppose knowledge absolutely, not restricted to a particular teacher, the verb is put in the passive: ﴿to whom it was given﴾, that is, they exchanged the blessing of Allah by causing dispute over what was sent down to remove dispute. In this there is the utmost astonishment and a manifestation of the dazzling power that drove them to that.

(p-201) Since the disagreement may sometimes be about an obscure matter, He clarified that the matter is otherwise, and so, indicating by the affirmation of the preposition that it did not extend over the whole of time, He said: ﴿after the clear proofs had come to them﴾, that is, the rational and transmitted proofs by which prophethood was established, by which the Book was established.

Al-Harali said: They comprise the signs of what is in the sensible and the signs of what is in the heard, and therefore the clear proofs were completing by the joining of their two witnesses. End.

Since this is the place of the question about the cause, He clarified that it was envy and the desire for superiority, a turning away from the truth out of love for the worldly things that were adorned and rivalry over them, and so He said: ﴿out of insolence﴾.

Al-Harali said: Insolence (al-baghy) is the practice of envy by word and deed. He, upon whom be prayers and peace, said: "Three things none is free from, and among them is one who adorns himself with envy, bad omen and suspicion. So when you envy, do not commit insolence." Because envy is something that occurs in the soul, as if it were innately disposed to it, it is therefore excused in that; but when it acts according to it in its speech and deeds, it becomes insolent. End. He increased the wonder by His saying ﴿among themselves﴾, that is, not insolence against others, so they changed from every direction.

When He mentioned the sending down of the Book and its cause, He mentioned what resulted from it, and so, by coordinating with what is implied in His saying — they were blind to the clear proofs — He said: ﴿Then Allah guided﴾. Its attribution to the Greatest Name, as al-Harali said, is an announcement that it is not within the capacity of creation except by the help and enabling success from the Truth. End.

﴿those who believed﴾, that is, in the Prophets, by the blessing of their faith, ﴿to the truth about which they differed﴾, that is, the people of error. Then He clarified it by His saying: ﴿of the truth﴾. It is permissible that the preposition min here be partitive, for what they were blind to of the truth that the Book brought down and that the Prophets came with. ﴿By His leave﴾, that is, by what He approved for them of His knowledge, His will and His enabling.

Al-Harali said: In this is an indication of what He created them upon of enabling them to accept it, for permission at its least is enabling and the removal of prevention. End.

﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing in knowledge and power, ﴿guides whom He wills﴾, that is, by what He has of the attributes of perfection, ﴿to a straight path﴾.

Al-Harali said: This is a guidance higher than the first. As if the first were guidance to the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge and power, and this is guidance to Him. In the present tense there is good news to this community of the continuance of their guidance until the end of the Muhammadan day:

"A group of my community will not cease to be victorious upon the truth until the command of Allah comes." End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 214:

When the preceding discourse made clear, by explicit statement, the occurrence of disagreement, and that hostilities arose from it, and since hostilities risk wealth and lives, and this is the hardest of matters, and since custom dictates that those who are called to this, if they do not resolve firmly upon the signs, will be among those who find the commands of the Messengers burdensome, seeing that they divide what the word had united and what people had agreed upon for themselves, and scatter their affair, finding it burdensome because of the long wait for victory, their state became that of one who seeks the comforts of the highest Gardens without hardships, and that is impossible and pure error. For steadfastness upon the Straight Path is not achieved except by bearing the severities of the obligations. So it was as if it were said, in answer to this, deviating from addressing the Prophet ﷺ, to whom it was said ﴿Ask the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Baqarah: 211], to addressing the followers, honouring him by that, and raising (p-205) their resolve by addressing them directly, and consoling them with those among the people of understanding who passed before them, to energize them and strengthen their resolve: Did you suppose that We would not send the Messengers to distinguish the corrupt from the good? ﴿Or did you suppose﴾ after their sending that the matter is easy, that you would attain happiness without striving in worship.

Al-Harali said: It is of the kind from which comes ḥusbān (supposition), which is what prevails in matters of the kind that are innate and whose habit is established, whereas ẓann (assumption) is the prevalence in what is known and acquired through evidence and knowledge. So the weakness of the scholar's knowledge is ẓann, and the weakness of the intellect of the sensible person is ḥusbān, and so on, ended.

This that I have estimated is the meaning of ﴿that you would enter the Garden﴾, that is, which is eternal bliss, "and the case being that" (p-206) "there has not yet come to you the likeness of" — that is, the description of ﴿those who passed away﴾. Since nearness in time is more intense for consolation, he affirmed the preposition, saying ﴿before you﴾, that is, it relates to you so that you may know by it, or that there may befall you what befell them of strange circumstances and wondrous events, which in their strangeness are like parables.

Al-Harali said: "Am" (or) is a conjunction joining with matters that the beginning of the address makes understood, as if he were saying: Did you suppose that your states would be different from the states of the past nations in God's wisdom and His sunnah, and you will never find any alteration in God's sunnah, extending to what the meaning of the address draws in general and in detail, in the reality of the world, of its hardships, its heat and its cold, the narrowness of its livelihood and the kinds of its harms, the state of the barzakh (intermediate state), and the state of resurrection and gathering, and beyond that to the final end of entering the Garden. So at the conclusion of that, the beginning of the address ﴿Or did you suppose﴾ was a transition across what lies between the first of the raising and the final end of entering the Garden, ended.

I have noted that the particle "lamma", which carries the meaning of anticipation, is in negation the counterpart of "qad" in affirmation. Moreover, it was fitting for them that their entry into the religion be with insight into the occurrence of severities, because of the multitude of opposers and obstinate enemies, so that they would be anticipating at every time the affliction of calamities and the descent of blows and shocks, so that this would make their matter more earnest and more worthy for them in steadfastness and in ascending to the highest ranks.

Since it was as if it were said: What is that likeness? It was answered by way of explanation with His saying: ﴿Adversity afflicted them﴾, that is, calamities in their wealth, ﴿and hardship﴾, that is, in their persons. Abu 'Ubayd al-Harawi transmitted this from al-Azhari, but in my view the better is the reverse, because al-ba's (adversity) is used most often in war, and al-darr (hardship) is used most often for poverty. That is, as a requital for them, as al-Harali said, for what they changed of what brings about each of these, and for every deed there is a requital. ﴿And they were shaken﴾ by inward matters from the hidden recesses of the hearts (p-208), ended.

The meaning is that they were disturbed by kinds of afflictions, calamities, terrors and frights, with a severe disturbance resembling the earthquake that nearly levels the earth and crushes the mountains. ﴿Until the Messenger said﴾ — Nafi' read it in the nominative, as a narration of the state at its time, meaning that the limit and what is limited have both been realized and have passed, so both are past tense, and you are narrating that at the moment of its occurrence, like someone saying about a sick man he is observing: He fell ill until they despaired of him. For the accusative is with the supposition of "an" (that), which is the sign of the future, so it governs only a present-tense verb with that meaning. The group read it in the accusative as well, as a narration of the state, but with the supposition that the earthquake is witnessed and the saying is awaited, the clear one established it: (p-209) ﴿the Messenger﴾, who is the most steadfast of people, ﴿and those who believed with him﴾, and they are the most steadfast after him because of the long passage of time over what touched them. He expressed it in the present tense to depict their state and to indicate the repetition of that from their saying.

Al-Harali said: He mentioned the saying of the Messenger which occurs in the rank of those who believed with him, not his saying concerning what pertains to him alone in his essence, nor him who is of him or follows him, because the Prophet has a standing in what appears of saying and doing with respect to the ranks of his community. So the saying of the Messenger, announcing their state, was ﴿When will God's help come?﴾ — it is as if they were in the position of one who waits in perplexity and bewilderment, for even though he is promised what is true, the delay gives him the appearance of one whose affair has become obscure, because of what he sees of the uprooting of the causes of relief. So in its implication there is information that God, glorified and exalted be He, relieves (p-210) His prophets and those with them only after the severing of their causes from anyone other than Him, in order to test their hearts for piety, so that their inner selves are purified from leaning upon any of creation, and their hearts are attached to God, exalted be He, alone, until the Prophet ﷺ says: "There is no god but God alone, He fulfilled His promise, He helped His servant, and He alone routed the confederates," announcing that God, glorified and exalted be He, is His helper without any veil or means of any of His creation. Likewise is His sunnah with His Messengers: ﴿Indeed We help Our Messengers and those who believed in the life of this world﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. And upon this have the extraordinary customs of the friends of God and the people of wonders proceeded; it hardly occurs for them except out of the necessity of severing the causes. In the reading in the accusative there is an indication that the limit of the earthquake is the saying, and in the nominative there is an indication of the limit of the earthquake and that it is an obscure matter, which has befallen the inner and outer aspects, and one of those outer aspects is the occurrence of this saying. So in the nominative there is information about the intensification of the affair through its effect upon the outward expression of the saying and what lies beyond it, ended.

In the accusative it is clear, for "ḥattā" governs the verb. As for the nominative, it is then cut off from the verb, since it does not govern it because it is past, so that the soul goes every way toward the limit, then some explanation of it is resumed by the verb.

Since the meaning of the speech was a request for help and a slowness in the matter, He, exalted be He, answered them as one who answers a caller in a state of intensified distress, with His saying: ﴿Unquestionably﴾.

Al-Harali said: as an opening, an alert, and a gathering of hearts for listening. ﴿Indeed﴾, as emphasis and confirmation. ﴿The help of God﴾, which has no cause but the care of the King of kings after the severing of every cause other than Him, ﴿is near﴾, because He is independent of preparation and duration. So in this sentence there is good news of the removal of the burden of help through means, equipment and implements that are required, and of the sufficiency of attaching the hearts to God. For this reason God helps this community through its weak ones, because its help is through the piety of hearts, not through repelling bodies. For this reason the last of this community will conquer "Constantinople of the Romans" by glorifying and magnifying God. He ﷺ said: "Indeed when We descend in the courtyard of a people, the morning of those who were warned is evil." So that was in line with what God, blessed and exalted be He, intended for His prophets and His chosen ones of ease, whose perfection is for this community, so He intended ease for them in every state, ended.

In some reports: "You only fight people by your deeds." The summary is that the mere claim of entering into peace does not suffice; rather there must be the establishment of proof through patience (p-212) upon what He tests them with, as He tested the earlier nations and the past generations. So consider this training in the ascents of discipline, and reflect on how the Arabs were addressed, though the address was to the believers, with the mention of the Resurrection in His saying ﴿and those who feared God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Baqarah: 212], and of the Garden in His saying ﴿that you would enter the Garden﴾, while they deny both, casting what is as if it were established and beyond dispute, to make them at ease with the mention of both. Consider what subtle wisdoms lie in that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 215:

Since spending (al-nafaqah) is among the foundations on which the surah is built, as one of the attributes of the believers, ﴿and from what We have provided for them they spend﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3], and then He repeated the exhortation to it throughout the verses, until He commanded it at the beginning of the verses of the pilgrimage mentioned just before, although it is also among the pillars of the beginnings of jihad, until the preceding verse included it together with killing, which is the end of jihad, this became the point of the question about both. So God, exalted is He, informed about that by way of scattered (al-nashr al-mushawwash, a style in which items are not presented in their usual order) arrangement, and this supports what I understood regarding al-ba'sa' and al-darra' (hardship and adversity), for its use in the Qur'an is more frequent than the ordered (al-murattab) style. He then said, teaching the one who asked: Did those addressed ask about these two? ﴿They ask you what﴾, meaning what thing (p-٢١٣) ﴿they should spend﴾ of wealth.

Al-Harali said: Since the revelation of the Qur'an follows the manner of a person's disposal of his times, the arrangement of its address alternates between address of religion received from God, and establishing rule in which the servant is a deputy of God in the execution of His command, and spending in which he is a deputy in conveying His bounty, because courage and generosity are a caliphate (khilafah), while cowardice and miserliness are a dismissal from it. So within what preceded of address was kindness and spending, and it was right that one should not ask "what should he spend," because what is spent is all surplus. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O son of Adam! If you give away the surplus it is good for you, and if you withhold it, it is bad for you." So in this question, on the part of the one who asked, there is a kind of hesitation similar to what preceded regarding the Children of Israel in the matter of the cow, in the form of repeated questioning. Al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him) did not seek permission when he came with all his wealth, nor did Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) seek permission when he came with half of his wealth, nor did Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' seek permission when he offered Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with them both) half of his wealth and one of his two wives. So in this question there was a display of the example of those who passed before them, and had it not been that Allah is Merciful, their answer would have been: "Spend the surplus," which would have become obligatory. But Allah was gentle toward the weak because of their weakness, affirmed spending, and left its amount undefined, in the form of spending that gives to strangers while relatives are in need. So God, exalted is He, said, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ) and turning away from the questioners because of the Israelite-like dullness in the question: - end.

He said: ﴿Say: whatever good you spend﴾, meaning of wealth. He turned away from specifying the one who spends to specifying the recipient, because that is more beneficial, in a manner by which their question is known. It is every wealth they consider good. He said, expressing it in the past tense so that it is more inclusive: ﴿whatever good you have spent﴾, so He generalized the spent amount, which is all the wealth you regard as good, and specified the recipient, clarifying its most important aspect, because spending is not counted unless it falls in its proper place (p-٢١٥). He said: ﴿then for the parents﴾, because they brought him into existence in the world of causes, ﴿and the relatives﴾, because of their established right, as they are like a part of him by the closeness of kinship, ﴿and the orphans﴾, because they are exposed to loss due to their weakness.

Al-Harali said: Because they are relatives after relatives, by the orphanhood that made others responsible for them - end. ﴿And the needy﴾, because they share with orphans in weakness, while they are generally able to earn in some way.

(p-٢١٦) Al-Harali said: They are the ones who ask (al-muta'arridun) linguistically, and the hidden ones (al-mustatirun) who are not noticed and do not find what suffices them, in both religious law and the Prophetic linguistic usage - end. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾, because of his weakness in being away from home. The verse is muhkam (clear and unabrogated), so what is in it is taken in a way that does not conflict with other verses.

When He specified those mentioned, He generalized and gave good news with His saying: ﴿And whatever good you do﴾, meaning whatever is considered good, in substance or in meaning, of this or other kinds, with these or others, ﴿then indeed Allah﴾, who encompasses everything in knowledge and power.

Since this came as a new statement in the context of encouragement and warning, because He had entrusted the matter to the spenders, and since He, glorified is He, is of great gentleness toward this community, He emphasized His knowledge of it, and placed the adverbial phrase first, as an indication that He has ultimate regard for their good deeds. So He said: ﴿is Knowing of it﴾, meaning of utmost knowledge (p-٢١٧), and He is the most worthy to reward good.

Al-Harali said: He ended with knowledge because of the entry of defect into intentions in spending, for it is among the things the soul most vaunts itself with, so almost nothing of it remains safe for her except what her left hand does not know, which is her self-regard and vanity, while what is specific to her right hand, which is her sincerity and sincere purpose, is preserved - end.

When they were informed of what they had asked about, namely one of the two aspects implicit in the verse of the earthquake (al-Zilzal), this became the point of the question about the other. So they were answered by way of a resumptive sentence (istinaf, a new sentence that picks up the thread), with His saying: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾.

Al-Harali said: When the ruling on the pilgrimage (hajj) became intertwined with fighting, the verses concerning their shared character overlapped. As already mentioned, the establishment of the obligation of the pilgrimage in the verse ﴿Whoever undertakes the pilgrimage therein﴾ [al-Baqara: 197] brought together the prescriptions of fighting. Obligation (fard) of a thing is what comes to stand in the place of a part of it, and prescription (kutub) is that which is stitched onto a thing so that it becomes a joining within it, just as fasting was made [a form of struggle], since in fasting there is a struggle of the self, just as in fighting there is a struggle against the enemy. Thus what is by nature (p-218) defence took the meaning of prescription, and what is by nature action and turning toward (God) took the meaning of obligation. These are two intended meanings in the Book and the Sunnah, and it is essential to give care to understanding them, so that each settles in the heart in its proper place, and the intention is specified for each one in its proper manner. The first revelation concerning the verses of fighting was ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against﴾ [al-Hajj: 39]. The first was a permission for those whose nature is defence of the religion out of an inner impulse, in the way that prayer, before it was made obligatory, was performed by the earlier people out of an impulse of love for their Lord, and their eagerness for Him in solitude with Him and their intimacy in intimate conversation with Him. Thus, those whose prayer was love, the address to them concerning fighting was a permission, because they turned toward it in giving up their lives for God. For those for whom that was love, they sought to fulfil it out of love for meeting their Lord through death, just as they loved meeting their Lord through prayer "when they came to understand" and were certain that there is no rest for a believer except in meeting his Lord. So their works included meeting their Lord through prayer in peace, and seeking to meet Him through martyrdom "in war." When the affair of the religion expanded and the Bedouins and the followers entered, whose sincere love for meeting God does not carry them to rush to jihad, the prescription of fighting was revealed, just as the obligation of prayer was revealed, as a supplementary ruling. So He said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾, that is, O community! In meaning it returned to this category of people who ask about spending. By this meaning the verse is connected with what precedes it, for they were tightening up in spending in a Children-of-Israel fashion, and they were holding back from jihad like the people of the Wandering (al-Tih), among whom were those who said:

"Go you and your Lord and fight, the two of you" (al-Ma'ida: 24). End of quotation.

﴿And it is hateful to you﴾: that is, what opposes the aim and desire of the self. Perhaps, because it was good, He expressed it with the preposition "to" (la-) in ﴿to you﴾. This is taken in terms of the general case. As al-Harali said, among those who love meeting God, it is among the sweetest things their souls attain, to the point that a man among them would contend with the one who held him back, asking him to let him go, to face the fight and martyrdom. One of the Successors said: "We met people for whom death was more desirable than life is among you today. That was because they had ruined their worldly life and built up their next life, so they loved moving from the ruin to the building." End of quotation.

Since this was disliked because of the burden on wealth, the hardship on the self and the danger to the soul, by natural inclination, yet desirable because of the promise in it of one of the two good outcomes by the Law, He indicated this with a circumstantial clause, saying: ﴿And it may be that﴾. What will come, if God Most High wills, in the surah of Bara'a concerning the meanings of "it may be" ('asa) will clarify that the meaning is: your condition is worthy and fitting for covering from you the knowledge of consequences, so that ﴿you dislike something﴾, that is, like the raid, (p-221) and so you turn away from it, supposing it to be an evil for you, ﴿while it is good for you﴾, that is, while the state is that it is good for you because of what it contains of victory and booty, or martyrdom and Paradise. ﴿But you do not know.﴾ The One who imposed that upon you is All-Knowing of everything, needing nothing, and He imposed it upon you only for your benefit.

Al-Harali said: He bore witness for them, since they did not witness the station of those with certainty who see the unseen of faith as they see through the senses. As Tha'laba said: "It is as if I look at the people of Paradise in Paradise enjoying themselves, and I look at the people of the Fire in the Fire being punished." He did not make martyrdom certain for them, but tied it to the word "it may be", because He knew the weakness in the acceptance of the one addressed. In informing him there is an obligation through the descent of the higher to the lower in rank, because this address manifested the descent of the Truth in addressing creation to the point of exceeding the gentleness of discourse. End of quotation.

Since He, glorified and exalted, encouraged them to jihad by what the men had of good in it, He warned them against sitting back from it by what is feared of evil in it.

Al-Harali said: He made it known that the one who holds back from it in his holding back faces calamities and evil in this world and the next, not merely failing to attain the good of jihad, but also attaining the evil of sitting back and staying behind. End of quotation.

(p-222) So He, Most High, said: ﴿And it may be that you love something﴾, that is, like sitting back, so that you turn toward it, supposing it to be good for you, ﴿while it is evil for you﴾, that is, while the state is that it is evil for you because of what it contains of humiliation, poverty, deprivation of booty and reward. None of you has not experienced the like of this many times in the affairs of his worldly life. When this is established in one instance, every matter becomes possible of being good or evil in the same way, so it is necessary to abandon desire and return to the Knower who is free of purpose. For this reason He said, conjoining it to what is implied by its context: "So God has concealed from you the secret of decree." ﴿And God﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs complete encompassing, ﴿knows﴾, that is, to Him belongs the knowledge of everything. He has already informed you at the beginning of this matter that He is Compassionate to the servants, so He does not command you except with good.

Al-Harali said: It is a testimony to the reality of knowledge, to which the ignorant return concerning the descent of the address. End of quotation.

The verse belongs to ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which something is mentioned in one part and omitted in its counterpart): mention of the good first indicates its omission second, and mention of the evil second indicates its omission in the first.

(p-223) Since He, glorified and exalted, affirmed knowledge for Himself, He negated it for them, saying: ﴿But you do not know﴾, that is, you have no knowledge from yourselves, but it has come to you only before He taught you. So trust Him, and hasten to everything He commands you, even if it is hard.

Al-Harali said: He negated knowledge from them by the word "not" (la), which is for the future, so that it indicates the continuance of the state, ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [al-Isra': 85]. He said, in terms of the rank of this class of people, among the Bedouins and others. As for the believers, that is, those firmly grounded, God has taught them from His knowledge what they knew: that fighting is good for them, and that staying behind is evil for them. End of quotation.

To the extent that their knowledge of that poured out upon their tongues what makes tears flow and illumines hearts. When the Prophet (ﷺ) consulted them about setting out for the Battle of Badr, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) stood and spoke well, then 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) stood and spoke well, then al-Miqdad (may Allah be pleased with him) stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Proceed with what God has shown you, for we are with you. By God, we will not say to you what the Children of Israel said to Moses: ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting right here﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 24]. (p-224) Rather: go you and your Lord and fight, we are with you, fighting alongside you! By Him who sent you with the Truth, if you were to travel to Bark al-Ghimad, we would strive alongside you against whoever is before it until you reach it." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said good things to him and prayed for him. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Advise me, O people!" Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By God, do you mean us, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Indeed." He said: "We have believed in you, affirmed you, and testified that what you have brought is the Truth, and we have given you on that our pledges and covenants of hearing and obedience. So proceed, O Messenger of Allah, with what you intend, for we are with you. By Him who sent you with the Truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge into it with you! Not one man of us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us tomorrow! We are indeed patient in war and truthful in encounter. Perhaps God will show you from us what will delight your eye, so march with us in the blessing of God Most High." End of quotation.

(p-225) When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informed them of the obligation of fighting, sent down generally for all times, and He had previously commanded them to kill [the disbelievers] wherever they encountered them, and then restricted fighting within the Sacred Mosque for them, there arose a question: Does the command apply within the Sanctuary (al-haram) and the Sacred Precinct (al-haram) as it did before, or not? The polytheists had accused the believers, in the expedition (sariyya, a small raiding detachment) of 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, in which they killed 'Amr ibn al-Hadrami from among the polytheists, of transgressing by fighting in the Sacred Month, and their reproach to them over this had intensified. So the point of the question is: Did they ask about what the disbelievers reproached them with in this regard? He said, reporting their question and clarifying their state: ﴿They ask you﴾, that is, the people of Islam, especially the people of the expedition of 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, may Allah be well pleased with them, ﴿about the sacred month﴾. He did not specify the month, which is Rajab, so that the reference would be more general. The month was called "sacred" (al-hurum) for the magnification of its sanctity, to the extent that they forbade fighting in it. So the subject of the question was left vague, so that the soul would be drawn to it. Then He specified it by a substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal, a substitution in which the replacement comprises the original) in His words: ﴿concerning fighting in it﴾. Then He commanded the answer in His words: ﴿Say: fighting in it is⦅ ⦆﴾, whatever kind of fighting it is, so the justification is generality.

Since the absolute fighting in it, in their assumption, was not permissible even against one who deserves to be killed, and in reality fighting in it is greater aggression than in other places, He said: ﴿is a great [sin]﴾, that is, in general.

Since it is known that the believers strive utmost to facilitate the path of Allah, and so they are not of those who bar from it nor of disbelief in any way, there is no ambiguity that what follows is a new, independent statement, and it is for the disbelievers. It is His words: ﴿and barring﴾, of any kind whatsoever, ﴿from the path of Allah﴾, the King to whom all command belongs, that is, the religion which is His, which leads to Him, that is, to His good pleasure, or the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), for the Prophet (ﷺ) called the Hajj "the path of Allah."

Al-Harali said: "Barring (sadd) is turning someone toward a direction with aversion and disgust, and the path (sabil) is the main, well-trodden road, manifest to every traveler along its course," ﴿and disbelief in Him﴾, of any kind whatsoever, that is, in the religion, or in that barring, that is, because of it, for it is disbelief added to their disbelief. The predicate has been omitted because what follows it indicates it clearly to whoever reflects carefully, and it is: ﴿is greater﴾, that is, than fighting in the sacred month. The restriction expressed afterward in His words ﴿with Allah﴾ indicates what I have understood: that by His words ﴿is a great [sin]﴾ what is meant is in their assumption and in general, not that it is one of the major sins (al-kaba'ir).

Since the earlier permission for fighting in the sacred month and in the Sacred Mosque was given under a condition, as has passed, it was something that would prompt the question about fighting in it in general without that condition, or with another, anticipating an unrestricted ruling. Especially since the expedition which was the cause of the revelation of this verse, namely the expedition of 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, had discussion of both matters, as Ibn Ishaq narrated: he said, "They met the disbelievers who had killed some of them and taken captives and seized their caravan on the last day of Rajab. They feared them, so they were gentle with them until they were at ease. Then they consulted about their affair and said, 'If you leave them this night, they will enter the Sanctuary; and if you kill them, you will be killing them in the Sacred Month.' They hesitated, then encouraged themselves and did what they did. The polytheists reproached them for that, and their reproach intensified, and the anxiety of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, intensified, especially that of the people of the expedition over this." Without doubt they informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of all of that. Their informing him in this form is sufficient for their many questions, in addition to the indication of what has passed of their eagerness to ask about it. When that was so, Almighty Allah said: ﴿And about the Sacred Mosque﴾, that is, and they ask you about the Sacred Mosque, ﴿the sacred [mosque]﴾, that is, the Sanctuary which is for prayer and worship through submission and for nothing else, ﴿fighting in it. Say: fighting in it is a great [sin]﴾ in your view, in the manner that has passed. Then He began speaking: ﴿and expelling﴾, just as He began His words ﴿and barring from the path of Allah﴾, and He said: ﴿its people﴾, that is, the Mosque which Allah had decreed for them from of old, and they are the most worthy of people of it. ﴿is greater than it﴾, that is, than fighting in the sacred month, is an error and is based on assumption, and killing in it ﴿with Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge.

So He omitted from each clause what was indicated by what was established in the other. This is of the type of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which an element mentioned in one part is omitted from the other and vice versa). The secret of what He did at this point of ihtibak is that since fighting in the sacred month had occurred from the Muslims at the time of this question, in the expedition of 'Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, He brought forth the question about it and the answer. And since fighting in the Sacred Mosque had not yet occurred, but would occur from the Muslims also in the year of the Conquest, He concealed and hid it. And since barring from the path of Allah, which is the House, and the disbelief resulting from it, had not yet occurred, but would occur from the disbelievers in the year of al-Hudaybiyya, He concealed its report and left it implicit. And since expulsion had occurred from them, He mentioned its report and made it manifest. Thus Glorified and Exalted is He made manifest what He brought forth by the hand of events, and concealed what He concealed in the breast of time, and stated explicitly what the tongue of the actual situation stated, and alluded to what the decisive, cutting sword of the Conquest alluded to. And Allah is the Guide.

The intended meaning of "the Sacred Mosque" is the whole Sanctuary. Al-Mawardi, from our companions (the Shafi'is), said: "Every place where Allah mentions the Sacred Mosque, what is meant by it is the Sanctuary, except His words, ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾ [al-Baqarah: 144], for what is meant by it is the Ka'bah." He related this from Ibn al-Mulaqqin.

Others said: It is also applied to Mecca itself, like ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque﴾ [al-Isra': 1]. In some chains of al-Bukhari: "The roof of my house was opened while I was in Mecca, and Gabriel came down and opened my chest, then washed it with Zamzam water, then brought a basin..." until he said, "Then he took my hand and ascended with me to the heaven." It is also applied to the mosque itself, like His words, ﴿and they bar from the path of Allah and the Sacred Mosque which We have made for the people equally, the one who resides in it and the visitor﴾ [al-Hajj: 25].

Since all that has preceded of the disbelievers' conduct was a trial (fitnah), it was as if it were said: "Greater, because that is a trial." ﴿And trial﴾, that is, by disbelief and by covering the truth, by barring and expelling, and all kinds of harm which you commit against the people of Allah in the Sanctuary and in the sacred months, ﴿is greater than killing﴾, even if it were in the sacred month, because its distress passes away while its grief lasts long.

Since the implied meaning is: "They have tried you and fought you," and since Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knew that if they delayed in fighting them so that they would abandon disbelief, they would not delay in fighting them so that they would abandon Islam, and since the worst enemy is the one who, if you leave him, does not leave you, Almighty Allah said, joining to what you have supposed: ﴿And they will not cease﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿to fight you﴾, that is, they will renew their fighting against you whenever an opportunity appears to them.

Since their fighting is only to replace the true religion with falsehood, Almighty Allah gave its reason in His words: ﴿until﴾. But since they supposed that it would be easy for them because of the scarcity and weakness of the Muslims, they imagined it as a goal they must reach. He indicated this by the expression of the particle of goal (hatta), ﴿they turn you back﴾, that is, all of you, not one of you left, ﴿from your religion﴾, the true one. He drew attention that hatta here is causal by His words, warning against slackness toward them, lest their scheming become firmly established, arousing you to earnestness in fighting them, though it implies that they are not able: ﴿if they are able﴾, that is, to that, a way. Thus you are more deserving not to cease in that manner, because you are certain that you are upon the truth and that you will be victorious, and that they are upon falsehood and that they will be forsaken. There is no doubt, even if the time is long, because you rely upon Allah and they rely upon their own strength, and whoever is left to himself is lost. So the matter between you and them is more serious than speech, and it is fitting to prepare for it with its equipment and to make ready for it with its readiness, let alone to be swayed by their words, which the devils inspire to them, slandering the religion and barring from the path, and by their doubts with which they misled their own religion, which have no basis. In the verse there is an indication of the apostasy that occurred after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), for fighting over the religion did not end until after the completion of the matter of those people.

Al-Harali said: "Istita'ah (ability) is the soul's compliance in action and its giving itself submission to it." Then he said: "In it is an indication that a group will apostatize from their religion and a group will remain firm, because the speech of Allah does not come with its decisiveness and its condition except for a meaning that occurs in some way. It is clarified by the explicit address in His words: ﴿And whoever of you apostatizes﴾ to its end. It is from riddah (apostasy), and from it is ridda, which is a restraint by compulsion for what by nature inclines toward agreement." End of quote.

The form of the iftial pattern (ifti'al), which indicates artificiality and effort, [in the word] yartadid, is an indication that the religion is not turned away from except by compelling the self, because of the pain in departing from what is familiar. The consensus of the readers on the unassimilated (fakk) reading here indicates that the nullification (of deeds) is conditioned upon disbelief both outwardly by the tongue and inwardly by the heart. So it is lenient in pardoning utterance by the tongue along with the heart's tranquility. And the recitation with assimilation (idgham) in al-Ma'idah indicates that patience is a higher rank than responding by the tongue even if the heart is at peace.

Since Glorified and Exalted is He protected them by attributing the religion to them, indicating that they wish to strip them of what they chose for themselves because it is the truth, and to force them back to what they turned away from because it is false, He warned them against delaying from them until they reach that. So He said: ﴿And whoever of you apostatizes﴾, that is, does what they intend of apostasy, ﴿from his religion﴾. He joined to the condition His words: ﴿and dies﴾, that is, his apostasy is followed by his dying, ﴿while he is﴾, that is, and the state is that he is, ﴿a disbeliever﴾.

Since He made the pronoun singular according to the wording, to explicitly refer to each individual, He made it plural (in the following), because humiliating the group is humiliation of each individual among them, but not the reverse. He linked it with the fa' of causation, to inform that the evil of their deeds is the cause of their punishment. So He said: ﴿Those﴾, the distant ones, the hateful, ﴿their deeds have become void﴾, that is, their meanings have been nullified while their forms remain, from habita al-jurh (the wound has healed and its trace has been removed).

Al-Harali said: "From habat, which is corruption in a good thing in a way that makes it seem good. In deeds it is like a blow to a standing thing that keeps it from standing; likewise habat corrupts a good thing, making one think it is good." ﴿in the world﴾, by the removal of the spirit of intimacy with Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and the subtle connection with Him, and the falling away of their attribution to Him, except as linked with the explanation of their nullification only. Thus has been nullified what they had of the attention of the Truth (al-Haqq) ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, by the nullification of what they deserved of reward through the true promise.

Since apostasy is the worst type of disbelief, He repeated the call to distance upon its people, and said: ﴿And those are the companions of the Fire﴾. By the word "companionship" He indicated that they are most deserving of it, so they are not separated from it.

Since they were thus, they were as if they were the exclusive ones of it, to the exclusion of others, because of the lowness they reached in it, to a degree no other matches. So the people of the Fire will have a precedence over others in that respect. So He said, confirming the sentence preceding it: ﴿They therein abide forever﴾, that is, they remain in a dwelling that has no end. This condition alludes to what occurred after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ) of apostasy, because when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, places something in the form of a condition, it implies that something of it will occur. So the meaning is: "Whoever apostatizes and then repents of his apostasy, Allah will accept his repentance," as occurred with most of them. The expression by "mā" (which indicates exclusivity) may be used to indicate exclusivity, an indication that the punishment of others is nothing (p-236) in comparison to their punishment, because their disbelief is the most heinous kind of disbelief.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 218:

When Glorified and Exalted is He had explained those destined for the Fire, He explained those who are the people of hope for Paradise, so that the servant would not cease fleeing from the causes of the Fire and turning toward the things that bring hope of Paradise, out of fear of falling into what would cut off his hope.

Al-Harali (al-Ḥarālī) said: When he mentioned the matter of those who waver, he mentioned the matter of those who are steadfast; end of quote. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed﴾, meaning they affirmed faith with their tongues.

Since emigration (hijrah), which is parting from what is familiar, and striving (jihad), which is the risking of the self in leaving the homeland of the body and wealth in leaving the homeland of blessing, are the greatest things for the soul after leaving the homeland of religion, He repeated the relative pronoun for them, indicating (p-237) that each of them deserves to be a companion in itself. So, emphasizing the meaning through the expulsion in the form of mufā'alah, He said: ﴿And those who emigrated﴾, meaning they carried out the emigration by leaving, with hatred and aversion, their dwellings and whoever among their people and loved ones opposed them in it, confirming their affirmation of that.

Al-Harali said: From al-muhājarah, which is a mufā'alah from al-hijrah, meaning withdrawing from what one would naturally be pleased with because of some harm in it. ﴿And strove﴾, meaning they carried out the striving, a mufā'alah from al-jahd, with either a fatha or a ḍamma on the jīm, meaning exerting oneself to the utmost of one's capacity and hardship in the work, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, meaning the religion of the Supreme King, against everyone who opposed them. ﴿Those﴾ are the high-ranked, the greatly honored in nearness and proximity. Since their reward is only from the grace of Allah, He said: ﴿hope﴾, from al-rajā', which is awaiting benefit from something whose cause has preceded it, as al-Harali said, ﴿for the mercy of Allah﴾ (p-238), meaning His honoring them, not being certain of it, knowing that He may do whatever He wills, for He is the Supreme King, and none is His equal, while they are not certain of their own death being in a state of goodness, though they are certain that Glorified and Exalted is He, if He were to seize them for what He knows of their sins, would punish them.

Since man is a place of deficiency, he is always doing what, if he were seized for it, he would perish. Pointing to this, while announcing the vastness of forbearance, He said it in a circumstantial clause from the waw of ﴿hope﴾; it may also be taken as a coordination with what is implied: "and they fear His punishment," for Allah is the Mighty Avenger. ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Oft-Forgiving﴾, meaning He covers over what has passed from them of minor sins, or who repented from major sins, ﴿Most Merciful﴾, dealing with them as the merciful deals, with kindness, honor, and receiving them with approval.

Al-Harali said: In ending verses always with mercy there is an indication (p-239) that the grace of Allah in this world and the Hereafter is an initiating grace, which in reality is not a recompense for deeds; just as a servant shows mercy to a child at the outset, he shows mercy to him as an old man at the end, and He begins him with His mercy in his return just as He began him with His mercy at his beginning. End of quote, in meaning.

[p. 240] Since drinking was among the things permitted during the nights of fasting, and most of their drink was nabidh (a beverage made from dates and raisins), and since their land was hot, it would sometimes grow strong and become an obstacle to worship, especially jihad, because an intoxicated person cannot be relied upon for judgment or for striking. Drink was also not essential for sustaining the body as food is. He therefore delayed its explanation until he had finished with what was more important to make known. He concluded the verses that intervened between it and the verses of permission with what he had opened them with concerning jihad, and he stated explicitly that the doer of the greatest striving and the mothers of goodly things are from jihad and what is mentioned with it, in the place of hope for mercy. The situation therefore required the question: did they ask about the most worthless of frivolities and the mothers of wickedness? He said, teaching them by their question about it, clarifying what the situation required of His forbearance, so that what is other than it remains upon pure permissibility: ﴿They ask you about wine﴾, which is one of the things that Abd Allah ibn Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with him) gained in his sariyya (a small military expedition), for which the preceding verses were revealed. [p. 240]

Al-Harali said: It is from that which is khamr (with a fatha on the mim), which is what covers trees and the like. Khamr (with a sukun) concerning what is hidden internally has the status of khamar (with a fatha) concerning what is apparent, as if wine covers what lies between the discerning intellect of a human being and his unreasoning animality. It is whatever intoxicates from any drink whatsoever, whether little or much. ﴿And gambling (maysir)﴾.

Al-Harali said: It is the name of a gambling practice which the Jahiliyyah engaged in, aiming to benefit the weak and to obtain the win of contest. End of quotation.

He (glorified and exalted is He) coupled them because of their kinship in harm through the squandering of wealth without good will, as with jihad and other things. What He (glorified and exalted is He) made clear of the kinship between them here and in al-Ma'idah is noted. Although He (glorified and exalted is He) confined Himself here to harm to religion, which is sin, because it is a foundation that every harm follows, He said in the answer: ﴿Say: In both there is great sin﴾, that is, in using them, ﴿great sin﴾, because of the corrupt things in them that oppose the excellences of the Law, such as lying, abuse, loss of reason, and appropriating the property of others. This establishes prohibition by affirming sin. Also, they are among the major sins.

Al-Harali said: The two readings, with the single-dotted ba' and the three-dotted tha', indicate the combination of both matters: largeness of quantity and abundance of number. Either of these two would restrain a person of noble disposition and sound intellect from undertaking it, rather he would refrain from even a small and minor sin, so how much more from a great and abundant one. End of quotation.

﴿And benefits for people﴾, for which they commit them: from trading in wine, and the pleasure of drinking it; and from taking much wealth in gambling, benefiting the poor, plundering property, boasting over the abram (those who withhold), and using them to reach friendships and companionships with young men, and to obtain their food, drink and gifts. Averting harms takes precedence. So how can it be ﴿and their sin is greater than their benefit﴾? In this, as al-Harali said, there is an alert to consider the difference between the two goods and the difference between the two evils. End of quotation.

Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Ahmad al-Razi said in the Kitab al-Zina: One of the people of knowledge said: The benefit that Allah mentioned in gambling is that the Arabs in winter and in barren times used to gamble with arrows over camels, then they would give their meat to those in poverty and need. They benefited and their conditions were balanced. Al-A'sha said concerning that:

Those who feed the guest when they are in need of winter,
And those who make their sustenance available for the gambler.

End of quotation.

Another said: They used to give it to the poor and would not eat from it, and they would boast of that and disparage whoever did not enter into it, calling him al-barim (the one who refuses). The explanation of what is meant by maysir is rare to find collected together, and I have searched as far as I was able into it, for completing the benefit.

Al-Majd al-Fayruzabadi said in his Qamus: Al-maysir is playing with arrows (qidah), from yasara, yaysaru; or the slaughtered camel over which they gambled; or dice; or every kind of gambling. End of quotation.

The author of the Kitab al-Zina said: The plural of al-yasir is yusur, and the plural of al-yusr is ayesar, so it is a plural of a plural, like hares and haras and ahras. End of quotation. Qimar (gambling) is every wager upon pure hazard, and it seems to be taken from al-qamar (the moon), the sign of the night, because it increases the gambler's wealth at one time and decreases it at another, as the moon increases and decreases.

Abu Ubayd al-Harawi in al-Gharibayn and Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili in his book al-Wa'i said: Mujahid said: Everything in which there is qimar is maysir, even children's play with walnuts. In the tafsir of al-Asbahani from al-Shafi'i: Maysir is anything that requires giving or taking property. So when chess is free of wagering, the tongue free of transgression, and prayer free of forgetfulness, it is not maysir.

Al-Azhari said: Maysir is the slaughtered camel over which they gambled. It was named maysir because it is divided into parts, so it is as if it is the place of division, and everything you divide, you have "yasarta" it. Al-yasir is the butcher, because he divides the camel's meat. He said: This is the origin of al-yasir. Then it is said of those who strike with arrows and those who gamble over the camel: yasirun (gamblers), because they are butchers, since they were the cause of that. It is said: "yasara al-qawm" when they gambled. A man is yasir and yasir, and the plural is ayasir. Al-Qazzaz: "So you are yasir, and it is maysur by rajʿ" and the object is maysur, meaning the camel. Ayasir is the plural of yusr, and yusr is the plural of yasir. Al-Qazzaz said: Al-yusr are the people who gamble over the camel, whose singular is yasir, as you say: ghaʾib and ghuyyab. Then ayisr is pluralized, so it is said ayasir, and the ayasir is a plural of a plural. It is said of the one who strikes with arrows: yusr, and the plural is ayasir. It is said of dice: maysir, because it is struck upon as the camel is struck upon. This is not said of chess, because it departs from that meaning. [p. 245]

Abd al-Haqq in al-Wa'i said: Maysir is the place of division.

Abu Abd Allah said: The matter of maysir was that they would buy a camel, slaughter it, then divide it into parts. Abu Amr said: into ten parts. Al-Asma'i said: into twenty-eight parts. Then they would cast lots over them with ten arrows: seven of them had shares, and they are al-fadhdh, al-tawam, al-raqib, al-hils, al-nafis, al-musbil and al-mu'alla. Three of them had no shares, and they are al-manih, al-safih and al-wagh. Then they would place them in the hand of a man among them who was just, who would shake them for them, calling the name of each man. Then they would distribute the parts according to what the arrows yielded for them. Whoever's arrow came out from these seven took a portion of the parts according to that share. Whoever had one of the three come out for him, people differed on this point. Some said: whoever's name came out gets nothing and is not charged, but the second draw is repeated and he has no share, and it is void. Others said: rather the whole price of the camel becomes due upon the owners of these three, so they are the losers, and the owners of the seven take shares according to what came out for them. These are the yasirun (gamblers).

Abu Ubayd said: I have not found our scholars investigating the knowledge of this or claiming it. I saw Abu Ubayda as the least of them in claiming it. Abu Ubayda said: I asked the Bedouins about it and they said: We have no knowledge of this; this is something Islam has cut off since it came, so we do not know how they used to cast lots. Abu Ubayd said: This was among them only among the people of nobility, wealth and generosity. End of quotation. Perhaps this is the reason it was named maysir.

The author of the Kitab al-Zina said: Those for whom there is gain and upon whom there is loss, that is from the arrows, are called mawsumah (marked), because of the shares, for they are like a mark. The number of the yasir is seven persons, each man taking one arrow. Sometimes the number of men falls short of seven, so the man takes two arrows. When he does that, he is praised for it and is called mathna al-ayadi (the doubler of favors). Al-Nabigha said:

I complete my generosity, and I bestow on them
Doubled favors, and I clothe the handful with ample garments.

He said: The one who strikes the arrows is called hurdah. He was named so because he is a man who shakes but does not enter among the yasir and does not take a share, and therefore they choose him, because he has no gain and no loss upon him. The one who does not strike the arrows and does not enter among the yasir in any of their affairs is called al-barim. The arrows are gathered in a skin, and some said in a cloth, and that skin is called al-rababah (with a kasra on the ra' and the two b's). Then its edges are gathered, it is evened out, and his hand is covered with leather so that he does not feel the touch of an arrow that he has an opinion about, and his eyes are bound. He gathers his fingers over it and presses them together like a bundle of grass, then strikes its heads with the flat of his palm. Whichever arrow emerges from the rababah is the winner. He said: Another said: The rababah is like a sack in which the arrows are gathered, then the hurdah is commanded to shake it. Some of them stick in the rababah and do not come out, and some do not stick and come out. That one is the winner. A trustworthy man sits over the hurdah called al-raqib. The one who strikes with the arrows is called mufid, and al-ifadah is the push, which is to push them all at once forward and shake them so that one arrow comes out. Likewise, al-ifadah from Arafat is the departure from it toward Jam'. End of quotation.

In al-Qamus he said: When they wanted to gamble, they bought a camel on credit and slaughtered it before they gambled, and divided it into twenty-eight shares or ten parts. When one arrow after another came out in the name of each man, the winning of those who drew the shares was made apparent, and whoever drew the al-ghafl (blank) was charged. End of quotation.

Abd al-Ghafir al-Farisi said in Majma' al-Gharib: The yasir is the one who strikes with arrows. It is from maysir, which is the gambling that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do. They gambled over a camel or other things, divided them into parts, and cast lots over them, for example with ten arrows, seven of which have shares, namely al-fadhdh, and so on to the end. Then they bring that out. Whoever's arrow comes out from the seven takes his portion, and whoever has one of the three comes out gets nothing. They have doctrines about this which the people of Islam did not know, and none of the people of language was certain of the manner of it. End of quotation.

This is what they said in the root yasara. I have arranged the names of the arrows to facilitate memorizing them in my saying:

Al-fadhdh, al-tawam, al-raqib, and al-hils,
Al-nafis, O you who strikes!
And al-musbil with al-mu'alla in running,
Then al-manih, al-safih and al-wagh.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 219 (part 2 of 3):

As for what they said about the root of each of its names, al-Qamus (the Lexicon) says: *al-Fadhdh* (with a fatha on the fa and a shadda on the dhal) is the first of the arrows of the *maysir* (the game of chance with arrows, a form of gambling). *Al-Tawam* [p. 250] (with a fatha on the initial letter, which is substituted for a waw, a sukun on the waw, and a fatha on the hamza, in the form of *kawkab*) is an arrow of the arrows of the *maysir*, or its second. *Al-Raqib* is the trustee of the companions of the *maysir*, or the trustee over the striking of the arrows, and it is the third of the *qidah* (the arrows used in the *maysir*). In the entry on the root *DRB* he says: *al-Darib* is the one entrusted with the arrows, or the one who strikes with them, like *al-darib* (the striker), and *al-qadah al-thalith* (the third arrow). In combining al-Ubab and al-Muhkam he says: *al-Raqib* is the guardian, and *raqib al-qidah* is the trustee over the striking. It was said that he is the trustee of the companions of the *maysir*, and it was said that he is the man who stands behind the *hurdah* (the one who shakes the arrows) in the *maysir*. All of these meanings are the same. The Pleiades' watcher (al-'Ayyuq) was called *raqib al-Thurayya* only by analogy with the *raqib* of the *maysir*, which is the third of its arrows. It has three shares: if he wins he gains the portions of three shares, and if he does not win he owes three. In the entry on *DRB* he says: "He struck with the arrows; *al-darib* is the one entrusted with the arrows, and it was said: the one who strikes with them." Sibawayh said: *fa'il* in the sense of *fa'il* (active). *Al-Darib* is the third arrow of the *maysir*. Al-Lihyani said: it is the one called *al-raqib*. He said: it has three shares, and so on to the end of what is in *al-Raqib*. Al-Qamus says: *al-Hurdah* (with a damma on the unpointed letter, a sukun on the unpointed letter, then a dotted letter) is the trustee of the gamblers.
