This is after He, glorified and exalted be He, had established for him, out of the perfection of His compassion for His servants, the return in revocable divorce twice (p-316), because a person in the state of union does not know what his state will be afterward, and the first [pronouncement] does not give him full experience, since some doubt may arise after it; but after the second it greatly diminishes, and the situation comes close to certainty, so separation after it is attributable only to lack of reflection and mere recklessness through haste, which is forbidden. ﴿So if he divorces her﴾, meaning the second husband. The use of ﴿if﴾ (in), which indicates doubt, is to alert that whenever divorce is made a condition on the one who makes her lawful, the contract becomes void, because it has left the boundaries of the stated limits. For marriage, as al-Harali said, is a contract of perpetual prohibition, not a limited enjoyment for a fixed term. Therefore enjoyment for a set period was not permitted in the Sunnah or by the scholars, because of the distinction between marriage and temporary marriage (mut'ah) in permanence and fixed duration. End of quotation.

﴿Then there is no blame upon them both﴾, meaning upon the woman and her first divorcer, ﴿for them to return﴾ by a new contract after the waiting period of the second divorce, which is known from His earlier words, ﴿And divorced women shall wait﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:228]. This [return] is absolute as to the state they had been in, of marriage. ﴿If they think﴾, meaning if it occurs to the mind of each of them, ﴿that they will keep the limits of God﴾, meaning the limits, which belong to Him in total perfection, which He set for them both regarding companionship (p-317).

Al-Harali said: When He made divorce a release, He made the renewal of marriage a return of all of that, as a notice that the return to the husband takes precedence over the renewal with another. End of quotation.

Since religion, despite its ease and facility, is severe, and no one who opposes it will fail to be overcome by it, and since rulings, though clear, may remain hidden because applying universals to particulars involves subtlety, as a single particular may be pulled by two or more universals, so one does not strip them of points of doubt except one whom God has illuminated in insight, He added, exalting the limits, to those preceding verses His words: ﴿These﴾, meaning these rulings, which reach the highest levels of greatness and the ranks of wisdom, ﴿are the limits of God﴾, meaning the great ones, by attributing them to Him, glorified and exalted be He, and by linking them to the Greatest Name. ﴿He makes them clear﴾, meaning He removes ambiguity from them by illuminating the heart, ﴿for a people﴾ who possess vigor, earnestness in striving, readiness and capacity, ﴿who know﴾, meaning who renew their examination and reflection with utmost striving at every time. Through this God grants them a faculty by which they distinguish what is obscured to others: ﴿If you fear God, He will grant you a criterion﴾ [al-Anfal 8:29], ﴿And fear God, and God teaches you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:282].

ولَمّا ذَكَرَ الطَّلاقَ رَجْعِيَّةً وبائِنَةً عَقَّبَهُ بِبَيانِ وصْفِ الرَّجْعَةِ مِنَ الحَلِّ والحُرْمَةِ وبَيانِ وقْتِها وتَحْدِيدِهِ والإشارَةِ إلى تَصْوِيرِ بَعْضِ (p-٣١٨)صُوَرِ المُضارَّةِ تَرْهِيبًا مِنها فَلَيْسَتِ الآيَةُ مُكَرَّرَةً فَقالَ: ﴿وإذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ أيْ طَلاقًا رَجْعِيًّا والمُرادُ مَن يَمْلِكُ نِكاحَها مِن هَذا النَّوْعِ الشّامِلِ لِلْقَلِيلِ والكَثِيرِ ولَمْ يَقِلْ: نِساءَكُمْ، لِئَلّا تُفْهِمَ الإضافَةُ أنَّ لِطَلاقِهِمْ غَيْرَ نِسائِهِمْ حُكْمًا مَغايِرًا لِهَذا في بُلُوغِ الأجَلِ مَثَلًا ونَحْوَهُ.

ولَمّا كانَتْ إباحَةُ الرَّجْعَةِ في آخِرِ العِدَّةِ دالَّةً عَلى إباحَتِها فِيما قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ بِطَرِيقِ الأوْلى وكانَ مِنَ المَقْطُوعِ بِهِ عَقْلًا أنَّ لِما بَعْدَ الأجَلِ حُكْمًا غَيْرَ الحُكْمِ الَّذِي كانَ لَهُ قَبْلَهُ لَمْ يَكُنِ التَّعْبِيرُ بِالبُلُوغِ مُلْبِسًا وكانَ التَّعْبِيرُ بِهِ مُفِيدًا أقْصى ما يُمْكِنُ بِهِ المُضارَّةُ فَقالَ: ﴿فَبَلَغْنَ أجَلَهُنَّ﴾ أيْ شارَفْنَ انْقِضاءَ العِدَّةِ، بِدَلِيلِ الأمْرِ بِالإمْساكِ لِأنَّهُ لا يَتَأتّى بَعْدَ (p-٣١٩)الأجَلِ.

وقالَ الحَرالِيُّ: ولَمّا كانَ لِلْحَدِّ المَحْدُودِ الفاصِلِ بَيْنَ أمْرَيْنِ مُتَقابِلَيْنِ بُلُوغٌ وهو الِانْتِهاءُ إلى أوَّلِ حَدِّهِ وقَرارٌ وهو الثَّباتُ عَلَيْهِ ومُجاوَزَةٌ لَحَدِّهِ ذَكَرَ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى البُلُوغَ الَّذِي هو الِانْتِهاءُ إلى أوَّلِ الحَدِّ دُونَ المُجاوَزَةِ والمَحَلِّ، والأجَلُ مُشارَفَةُ انْقِضاءِ أمَدِ الأمْرِ حَيْثُ يَكُونُ مِنهُ مَلْجَأُ الَّذِي هو مَقْلُوبُهُ كَأنَّهُ مُشارَفَةُ فَراغِ المُدَّةِ - انْتَهى ﴿فَأمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ أيْ بِالمُراجَعَةِ إنْ أرَدْتُمْ ولَوْ في آخِرِ لَحْظَةٍ مِنَ العِدَّةِ ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ أيْ بِحالٍ حَسَنَةٍ تُحْمَدُ عاقِبَتُها، ونَكَّرَهُ إشْعارًا بِأنَّهُ لا يُشْتَرَطُ فِيهِ رِضى المَرْأةِ ﴿أوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ بِأنْ تَتْرُكُوهُنَّ حَتّى تَنْقَضِيَ العِدَّةُ فَيَمْلِكْنَ أنْفُسَهُنَّ مِن غَيْرِ تَلْبِيسٍ بِدَعْوًى ولا تَضْيِيقٍ في شَيْءٍ مِنَ الأشْياءِ. (p-٣٢٠)

وقالَ الحَرالِيُّ: هَذا مَعْرُوفُ الإمْتاعِ والإحْسانِ وهو غَيْرُ مَعْرُوفِ الإمْساكِ، ولِذَلِكَ فَرَّقَهُ الخِطابُ ولَمْ يَكُنْ: فَأمْسِكُوهُنَّ أوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ - انْتَهى.

ولَمّا كانَ المَعْرُوفُ يَعُمُّ كُلَّ خَيْرٍ وكانَ الأمْرُ بِهِ لا يُفِيدُ التَّكْرارَ خُصَّ تَرْكُ الشَّرِّ اهْتِمامًا بِهِ مُعَبِّرًا بِما يَتَناوَلُ جَمِيعَ الأوْقاتِ فَقالَ: ﴿ولا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ أيْ بِالمُراجَعَةِ في آخِرِ العِدَّةِ ﴿ضِرارًا﴾ كَمّا كانَ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ ﴿لِتَعْتَدُوا﴾ أيْ قاصِدِينَ بِذَلِكَ التَّوَصُّلَ إلى شَيْءٍ مِن مُجاوَزَةِ الحُدُودِ الَّتِي بُيِّنَتْ لَكم مِثْلَ أنْ يُرِيدَ تَطْوِيلَ العِدَّةِ عَلَيْها فَإنَّهُ قَدْ يُفْضِي إلى اعْتِدادِها تِسْعَةَ أشْهُرٍ.

ولَمّا كانَ التَّقْدِيرُ: فَمَن يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ زَوْجَهُ عُطِفَ عَلَيْهِ زِيادَةً في التَّنْفِيرِ عَنْهُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ أيِ الفِعْلَ البَعِيدَ عَنِ الخَيْرِ، وفي التَّعْبِيرِ بِالمُضارِعِ إشْعارٌ بِأنَّ في الأُمَّةِ مَن يَتَمادى عَلى فِعْلِهِ ﴿فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ﴾ أيْ بِتَعْرِيضِها لِسُخْطِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ونَفْرَةِ النّاسِ مِنهُ.

ولَمّا كانَ قَدْ لا يَقْصِدُ شَيْئًا مِنِ انْتِهاكِ الحُرُماتِ ولا مِنَ المَصالِحِ فَكانَ مُقَدَّمًا عَلى ما لا يُعْلَمُ أوْ يُظَنُّ لَهُ عاقِبَةٌ حَمِيدَةٌ تَهاوُنًا بِالنَّظَرِ وكانَ فاعِلُ ذَلِكَ شَبِيهًا بِالهازِئِ كَما يُقالُ لِمَن لا يَجِدُ في أمْرٍ: هو لاعِبٌ، قالَ: ﴿ولا تَتَّخِذُوا آياتِ اللَّهِ﴾ أيْ مَعَ ما تَعْلَمُونَ مِن عَظَمَتِها بِعَظَمَةِ (p-٣٢١)ناصِبِها ﴿هُزُوًا﴾ بِإهْمالِها عَنْ قَصْدِ المَصالِحِ الَّذِي هو زَوْجُها.

ولَمّا كانَ عَلى العَبْدِ أنْ يَقْتَفِيَ أثَرَ السَّيِّدِ في جَمِيعِ أفْعالِهِ قالَ: ﴿واذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ [المائدة: ٧] أيِ الَّذِي لَهُ الكَمالُ كُلُّهُ ثُمَّ عَبَّرَ بِأداةِ الِاسْتِعْلاءِ إشارَةً إلى عُمُومِ النِّعَمِ وغَلَبَتِها فَقالَ: ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ هَلْ تَرَوْنَ فِيها شَيْئًا مِن وادِي العَبَثِ بِخُلُوِّهِ عَنْ حِكْمَةٍ ظاهِرَةٍ ﴿وما﴾ أيْ وخُصُّوا بِالذِّكْرِ الَّذِي ﴿أنْـزَلَ عَلَيْكم مِنَ الكِتابِ﴾ الَّذِي فاقَ جَمِيعَ الكُتُبِ وعَلا عَنِ المُعارَضَةِ فَغَلَبَ جَمِيعَ الخَلْقِ بِما أفادَتْهُ أداةُ الِاسْتِعْلاءِ ﴿والحِكْمَةِ﴾ الَّتِي بَثَّها فِيهِ وفي سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ (ﷺ) حالَ كَوْنِهِ ﴿يَعِظُكُمْ﴾ أيْ يُذَكِّرُ بِما يُرَقِّقُ قُلُوبَكم ﴿بِهِ﴾ أيْ بِذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أيْ بالِغُوا في الخَوْفِ مِمَّنْ لَهُ الإحاطَةُ بِجَمِيعِ صِفاتِ الكَمالِ بِاسْتِحْضارِ (p-٣٢٢)ما لَهُ مِنَ العَظَمَةِ الَّتِي لا تَتَناهى ونَبَّهَ عَلى عَظِيمِ أمْرِهِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿واعْلَمُوا﴾ وبِتَكْرِيرِ الِاسْمِ الأعْظَمِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ فَلَمْ يَبْقَ وراءَ ذَلِكَ مَرْمًى ﴿بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ أيْ مِن أُمُورِ النِّكاحِ وغَيْرِها ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ أيْ بالِغُ العِلْمِ فاحْذَرُوهُ حَذَرَ مَن يَعْلَمُ أنَّهُ بِحَضْرَتِهِ وكُلُّ ما يَعْمَلُهُ مِن سِرٍّ وعَلَنٍ فَبِعَيْنِهِ.

قالَ الحَرالِيُّ: والتَّهْدِيدُ بِالعِلْمِ مُنْتَهى التَّحْدِيدِ - انْتَهى.

When he forbade harming (the wife) through the marriage bond and through its consequence, which is the waiting period (ʿiddah), he followed it with a prohibition of what used to happen after that period ended, namely preventing (the woman from remarrying) (ʿadl), by any person from whom such preventing could be imagined. However, since forbidding the guardians (awliyāʾ) when they are husbands is a prohibition aimed at others by way of priority (bi-ṭarīq al-awlā), he attributed it to the husbands, who are among the general population. So he said: ﴿And when you divorce﴾, that is, O husbands. He stated the noun explicitly and did not use a pronoun, because what is mentioned here is more general than the first. He said: ﴿women﴾, of any kind of divorce, ﴿and they reach their term﴾, that is, (p-323) their waiting period has ended. The context of the two statements indicates a difference between the two "reachings." This was transmitted by al-Iṣbahānī from al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him and have mercy on him). This means that the first (reaching) indicates approaching the end (of the term), because of the command to retain them, while this one (reaching) is literal, because of the prohibition of ʿadl: ﴿do not prevent them﴾, that is, do not hinder them, O guardians, whether you are husbands or not. ʿAḍl, al-Ḥarālī said, is the worst kind of prevention, from ʿaḍalat al-dajājah, when you lodge its egg inside it until it dies. End quote.

(p-324) ﴿from marrying their husbands﴾, that is, those who divorced them and others. They were called husbands because of what their affair would eventually come to, just as those who divorced were called husbands because of what had been. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him and have mercy on him, used this verse as evidence that there is no marriage except with a guardian, because the expression ʿaḍl indicates strong prevention, the kind called the incurable disease (al-dāʾ al-ʿuḍāl). If (the guardian) prevents (the marriage) with an unsuitable (non-equal, ghayr kufʾ) man, it is permissible, and she is not to be married to him. If the woman could marry herself, there would be no hardship, and his prevention, which is forbidden, would not be established so that he could be removed, unless he prevents (the marriage) before the judge (ḥākim). The Sunnah has explained this.

This verse is one of the wonders of the rhetorical device of ihtibāk (the device in which two matching elements are mentioned and each implies the other). ﴿divorced﴾ implies the husbands from ﴿do not prevent them﴾, and ﴿do not prevent them﴾ implies the guardians from ﴿divorced﴾. I have explained this in my book al-Idrāk. ﴿when they agree among themselves﴾, that is, the women and the husbands who are suitable (akfāʾ), by what the possessive construction indicates, rather than saying "husbands for them," for example.

Since agreement should be according to what is just, he indicated it by his saying ﴿among themselves﴾. Since the two might agree on what is not proper, he restricted it by his saying ﴿in a reasonable manner﴾. If they agree on something other than that, such as when the husband is unsuitable, then ﴿do not prevent them﴾. Al-Ḥarālī said that it (the reasonable manner) is ʿurf because it gathers two recognized (matters) from both of them, so their combined whole becomes the complete reasonable manner. As for the disapproved, he described one of them. End quote.

Since he mentioned the rulings while explaining their wisdom, ﴿that﴾ became an admonition (waʿẓ). Most people think that admonition is different from rulings, so he turned to the chosen one for perfection and said: That great matter, O Messenger, ﴿is admonished﴾, that is, the hearts of ﴿whoever﴾ are softened ﴿by it﴾. Al-Ḥarālī said that admonition (waʿẓ) is the stirring of the soul by the promise of reward and its threat. End quote. So it is a warning for those for whom the rulings are hard, and they are the majority.

Since among the followers of (ﷺ) there are those who struggled against their own souls until they became fit to understand subtleties and grasp allusions and fine points, and who gave their full attention to listening (p-326) for their benefit, he said: ﴿among you﴾, informing that the address is in reality to every understanding person. It was restricted to them because they are the ones who benefit from it and understand it, due to the tenderness of their hearts arising from submission. Although the address concerns rulings, it is an admonition that includes both warning and encouragement. Since it is part of wisdom that whatever does not benefit from something is not addressed by it, he indicated this by his saying: ﴿who believes in Allah﴾, that is, because of His greatness, ﴿and the Last Day﴾, out of fear of disgrace on it. In calling it an admonition there is an indication that whoever oversteps a limit regarding another will have someone oversteps a limit regarding him.

Al-Ḥarālī said: Because whoever does something has its like done to him. It is as if whoever prevents a husband from (remarrying) is prevented by another guardian when he himself is a husband, and whoever commits adultery is committed against. ﴿He will repay them for their description﴾ [al-An'am: 139].

When what they were stirred toward of complete attentive listening occurred, he turned toward them and said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the matter of great importance, ﴿is purer for you﴾, that is, more conducive to growth, increase, purification and cleansing, through what arises from it among you of affection and blessing from Allah, glory be to Him, ﴿and more purifying﴾ for the hearts.

Since attributing knowledge to the speaker makes others more ready to accept from him, he said, showing and repeating the Greatest Name to magnify the matter: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, I point this out to you while the Greatest King ﴿knows﴾, that is, has this attribute, ﴿and you do not know﴾, that is, you do not have this attribute in essence, neither now nor in the future, as indicated by the negation with the word "not" (lā) and the form expressing permanence.

[p. 328] Since marriage may result in childbirth, and childbirth may result in nursing, and the nursing mother may be a wife or a stranger, and the wife may be still in the marriage or separated from it, and since separation by divorce is more common than separation by death, He placed (the ruling on nursing) between the two waiting periods (ʿiddah): the waiting period of divorce and the waiting period of death. This is because each of the two (kinds of separation) has its own cause, and because of His concern for the matter and His urging of compassion toward the infant and of great care for his affairs. A mother who has been divorced may neglect the child out of spite toward the husband, if the divorce was due to discord, or out of desire for another husband. The same applies to the father. So God, the Exalted, said, joining (this ruling) to what is implied as an assumed preface: "So for women there are many rulings, and you have learned from them here principles from which, for whoever God has given insight, many branches can be understood. As for divorced women, if there is no bond between you and them through childbirth or the like, then there is no way for you to act against them."

Al-Ḥarālī said: When He, glorified and exalted, mentioned the rulings on the bonds between spouses, on which the revelation of the Book was greatly emphasized, and since among the rule of the interlacing of spouses is the occurrence of a child and the rulings of nursing, [p. 329] He arranged it, also by way of joining, upon the meanings that exceed explicit expression and are contained in implicit understanding. This is because it is known that the understanding of the Qur'an is many times its explicit expression, in an amount that its counting does not nearly end. Therefore, address in it often comes by way of joining, that is, upon something not mentioned, so that explicit expression will always indicate an understanding that is attained by whoever has been granted the spirit of intellect (rawḥ al-ʿaql) in understanding, just as the deep comprehension of explicit expression is attained by whoever has been granted the very essence of intellect, which is knowledge. End quote. Then God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And mothers﴾, that is, from among divorced women and others. Their being commanded to nurse is expressed in the form of a report, which by its nature should be something already done and completed, as a way of alerting to its emphasis. Although the command is recommendatory, what it implies is that they are owed a wage here, in Sūrat al-Ṭalāq, and in what comes later about hiring wet-nurses. So He said: ﴿nurse their children﴾.

Al-Ḥarālī said: God, the Exalted, made the mother [p. 330] the earth of the offspring, which feeds on her nourishment in the womb as blood, just as her limbs feed on her blood. Therefore her milk is more fitting for her child than that of others, so that it becomes its nourishment, and the child, being nourished by it, becomes an infant (wulayd) and a fetus (janīn). Thus she is most entitled to nurse her children. He mentioned them as "children" so that it includes males and females. He also said: Nursing (riḍāʿah) is nourishment that removes weakness (ḍarāʿah), which is feebleness and emaciation, through sustenance that combines food and drink, namely milk, whose place is the breast of the woman, and the udder belongs to animals with cloven hooves. End quote.

When He mentioned nursing, He mentioned its period. Since the intended purpose is merely the passage of time through its four seasons and the return of the sun, after passing through the twelve zodiacal signs, to the sign it was in at the time of birth, and since the aim is not to indicate praise or dispraise of time, nor to describe it as narrow or wide, He expressed it with what indicates simply the passage of a cycle, saying: ﴿two years﴾. Ḥawl (year) is the completion of strength in a thing that ends with a cycle of [p. 331] the sun, and it is the year that gathers the full perfection of plant life, in which it completes its powers. Thus said al-Ḥarālī, and it seems to be derived from that which has the power of turning. Since a thing may be applied to its greater part figuratively, it would be possible to mean a year and a part of the second (year). So He clarified that the intended meaning is the literal one, definitively, to end any dispute between the spouses over the period of nursing, and to inform (us) of the time that determines the establishment of prohibition (of marriage through nursing), as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Nursing counts only when it is the one that relieves hunger." (He expressed this) by His saying: ﴿complete﴾. Since that might imply that completeness is obligatory, He negated this by His saying: ﴿for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾. That is, this ruling applies to whoever wishes to complete the nursing. Thus it is understood that weaning before that is permitted for a benefit, and that there is no nursing after completion.

Al-Ḥarālī said: That which is sufficient short of completion is what His saying combines: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning are thirty months﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 15]. So if the pregnancy is nine months, the nursing is twenty-one months, and if it is two years (i.e., twenty-four months), the total is thirty-three months. Thus there are three units and three tens, and this constitutes the completion of pregnancy and nursing, so that the completion of nursing and the sufficiency of pregnancy are gathered in the thirty. End quote.

Since it might be thought that this would be without payment, He negated that by His saying: ﴿And upon﴾. Since fatherhood is not realized in a man as it is in a woman, and since lineage is established by the marriage bed alone, and it belongs to the man and not to the woman, He said: ﴿the one to whom the child is born﴾, that is, on whose bed (the child was born), ﴿is their provision﴾, that is, the nursing women's provision for the sake of nursing, whether they are [p. 333] still married or divorced. So if the married woman defies her husband, her right to provision does not lapse, though what pertains to marriage (such as her husband's enjoyment of her) may lapse. Since her occupation with nursing may keep her from what the husband desires of enjoyment, this might imply that clothing lapses too, so He mentioned it, saying: ﴿and their clothing﴾, as a wage owed to them.

Al-Ḥarālī said: Clothing is the garment of the human being that covers what ought to be covered, for male and female. He also said: The attributing of provision and clothing to them indicates regard for the woman's condition in this matter and her custom according to the Sunnah, not according to innovation. End quote.

Since the situation varies in matters of maintenance and clothing according to the differing circumstances of men and women, He said: ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, that is, according to the condition of each of them.

Al-Ḥarālī said: He confirmed what the attribution implied, and the address made its general meaning explicit. End quote.

Then He gave the reason for it, or explained it, with the true religion (ḥanīfiyyah) by which God, glorified and exalted, has favored us. So He said: ﴿No soul is burdened﴾.

Al-Ḥarālī said: From taklīf (imposing a burden), which is to make a person bear a task with hardship, in matters to which his nature inclines him. ﴿a soul﴾, that is, the imposing of it does not occur, though it is within His power, glorified and exalted, to do whatever He wills, ﴿except what it can bear﴾, that is, what it can endure and withstand, not as He did with those before (you), [p. 334] one of whom would cut off what urine had touched of his skin with scissors. And the "capacity" (wusʿ) is what can be achieved with ease and complete strength.

Since the result of this is the attainment of benefit and the averting of harm, He said: ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾, that is, let not the one who provides (the nursing) be harmed by it, nor let her be harmed. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the rā' with a ḍammah (vowel mark), as a report of the good, which is more emphatic; the rest read it with a fatḥah, as a prohibition. It may also be read in the form of the active or the passive. ﴿nor a father through his child﴾ [p. 332], that is, the one to whose bed the child was born, it is not permissible for him to harm the mother through the child, nor for her to harm him through it, nor to harm the child by neglect or the like, taking the form of mutual action (mufāʿalah) as a simple verb. Whenever God, glorified and exalted, attributed harm to someone, He attributed the child to him, to move his compassion and stir his nature toward greater kindness to it.

Al-Ḥarālī said: In this is an announcement that the father should not prevent the mother from nursing her child, causing her harm by depriving her of it, nor treat her badly in her provision and clothing because of her child. Just as he may not keep her as a wife except with reasonable kindness, he may not hire her to nurse except with reasonable kindness, and reasonable kindness is not complete except with freedom from harm. In its implication is a warning to mothers against abandoning their children with the intent of causing harm, while their nature inclines them to care for them. Likewise, in its implication, (the mother) should not harm him by extravagance in provision or clothing. End quote.

Since the command to act reasonably and what follows it of explanation are complete, and since this applies on the assumption that the father is alive at that time, He clarified the situation after it, saying: ﴿And upon the heir﴾, that is, [p. 336] the heir of the father, who is the nursing infant, ﴿is the like of that﴾, that is, what is commanded of reasonable kindness, as explained above, concerning his property, if his father dies and he is the heir.

Al-Ḥarālī said: What the living receive from the dead is whatever right or property they had. End quote.

It has been said about the heir other than this, because the mothers, the child, and the one to whom the child is born have all been mentioned earlier, so it is possible that the heir is attributed to each of them.

Since He clarified the period of nursing and the matter of maintenance, He stated explicitly what the speech had implied, namely the permissibility of weaning before completion. So He said, causing it by what the expression implied: ﴿But if they both desire weaning﴾, that is, the two parents, ﴿weaning﴾, that is, the cessation of nursing for the child before the completion of the two years.

Al-Ḥarālī said: It derives from fiṣāl, which is the return of those who were joined to a previous separation. End quote. It is more general than fiṭm (weaning), which is why this word was used. Since He clarified that, He alerted that it is not permitted except with a benefit, so He said: ﴿by mutual consent from both of them﴾ [p. 337], then He clarified that the matter is serious and needs full consideration, by His saying: ﴿and consultation﴾, that is, discussion of the matter, so that the opinion that should be acted upon is brought out.

Al-Ḥarālī said: He made clear, by the indication of what is in His saying "that they complete", that sufficiency may occur with less than two years. So making this not be free from harm except with the combination of their desire, mutual consent, and consultation, for one who has insight, lest they both agree upon a deficient opinion. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, peace be upon him: "He who seeks guidance (istikhārah) is never disappointed, and he who consults is never regretful." Consultation (mashūrah) means extracting the sweetness of an opinion and its pure essence from the hidden places of the chests, just as honey is drawn from the comb. End quote.

﴿Then there is no blame upon them both﴾ regarding what they have reduced from [p. 338] the two years, because they are not suspected in this matter, and the agreement of their opinion on it, together with the opinion of those they consult, rarely errs.

Al-Ḥarālī said: This indicates that there are three ranks: a rank of completion, in which there is goodness and blessing; a rank of sufficiency, in which the blame is lifted; and a state of harm, in which there is blame. End quote.

The completeness of this care indicates that the weaker a person is, the greater God's mercy toward him and the more intense His care for him.

Since He explained the nursing by mothers and placed it first as evidence of its priority, He followed it with what indicates the permissibility of other than them, saying: ﴿And if you wish﴾, that is, O men, ﴿to seek wet-nurses﴾, that is, to seek someone to nurse ﴿your children﴾ from other than the mothers, ﴿then there is no blame﴾, that is, no sin inclining (toward wrongdoing), ﴿upon you if you hand over﴾, that is, to the wet-nurses, ﴿what you have agreed to give them﴾, that is, the payment you have set for them, ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, fully and with your hearts pleased, without haggling or harshness, because that cuts off the excuses of wet-nurses [p. 339], and it is more fitting for diligence in giving sincere care and not neglecting the rights of the infant.

Since the meaning is: Do all that I have commanded you, and refrain from all that I have forbidden you, for I have gathered for you the benefits of both abodes in this Book, which is guidance for the God-fearing, the verse continues with His saying: ﴿And fear God﴾, that is, the One who possesses complete power and perfect knowledge. Then He warned them of His punishments by saying, alerting to the greatness of these rulings: ﴿And know﴾, and He attached the command to the greatest Name, which gathers all the most beautiful names, saying: ﴿that God﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, to magnify the station. For this reason, His knowledge, glorified and exalted, is emphasized here in the manner of what passed in ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed God is Knowing of it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 215], by placing His statement first to indicate greater concern, ﴿of what you do﴾, that is, whether secret or public.

Since these rulings are more subtle than those in the verse that follows, and many of them depend on acts of the heart, He concluded them with what indicates sight and knowledge, saying: ﴿All-Seeing﴾, that is, one whose knowledge of it reaches its utmost extent, so act accordingly.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 234:

When He mentioned suckling, and among its determinations is that if the father dies, He mentioned the waiting period of death (ʿiddat al-wafah) for that, and as a completion of the types of waiting periods, He said:

Al-Ḥarrālī said: When He mentioned the waiting period of divorce, which is the separation of life, the mention of the waiting period of death, which is the separation of death, was joined at the head of its verse, and it connected with the preceding verse because of what was drawn into the mention of suckling concerning the death of the father and the matter of the heir. Likewise every verse that is a head for another has two connections: one connected to the head that is its counterpart, to which it is strung, and one connected to the verse preceding it in some respect. End of quote.

He said: ﴿Those of you who die﴾, meaning, and the wives of those ﴿who die among you﴾, meaning their death occurs, by which their souls, which were lent to their bodies, are fully taken back by the One who lent them.

Al-Ḥarrālī said: From tawaffi, which is the extraction of the right from where it was placed. God, mighty and majestic, breathed the spirit and deposited the soul so that He would take it back after a term from where He deposited it, and that is a tawaffi of the form tafaʿʿul, from wafaʾ, which is the discharge of a right. ﴿And leave behind﴾, from wadhr, which is for a person to be taken from what it is his nature to hold, ﴿wives﴾ after them.

Since the emphasis on the waiting period is intended, out of regard for the rights of the wives, for the protection of the hearts of relatives, and as a precaution for marriage, it was stated in the form of a report, which by its nature is something that has already occurred and been completed, and He said: ﴿they shall wait﴾, meaning they shall await their husbands' completion of the waiting period. Since what is forbidden is the contract itself and approaching it through actions, rather than seeking it through allusion, He expressed it with the self for this purpose, and to alert that haste in this matter is only a carnal, animal desire, so that this would contain distance from it: ﴿by themselves﴾, so they do not give themselves to a husband, do not leave the house of mourning, and abandon adornment and everything in which the self has desire that calls to marriage, as the Sunnah has explained. ﴿Four months and ten days﴾ if they are free women and there is no pregnancy, whether she is young or old, menstruating or not. Its beginning is from the moment of death, because that is the cause, and He gave precedence to the nights, so He dropped the feminine marker, because the beginning of the month is the night.

﴿So when they have reached their term﴾. Since God, glorified and exalted, has made the Muslims like one body, and since the discussion concerned the wives of the dead, He informed, glorified and exalted, that it is obligatory upon their Muslim brethren to guard their rights as they would have guarded them had they been alive, by His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning, O people of the religion, ﴿for what﴾. Since there must be the woman's permission, and she has been given authority over the judge despite the guardian when he prevents her, for example, He attributed the act to them, saying: ﴿they do with themselves﴾, meaning of marriage and its preliminaries, from which they had been prohibited by mourning. This is not to be taken as direct action, so that it is not evidence for a woman marrying herself, in opposition to the verse ﴿and do not prevent them﴾ [al-Nisa': 19], which is reinforced by the Sunnah. Since that may not be in a lawful manner, He said: ﴿in a reputable way﴾, so that it refers to the complete form, and there is no blemish of reprehensibility in it. If they do what is disapproved, there is blame upon the people for abandoning the enjoining of good, just as there is upon them for the act. The jurists, except Abu Muslim al-Isfahani, agreed that this verse abrogates the verse of the waiting period of one year, and precedence in recitation does not prevent lateness in revelation, since the arrangement is not according to the order of revelation. This is transmitted by al-Shams al-Isfahani, and what will be quoted from him from Mujahid refutes it.

Since the sense is: God has set these limits for you, so guard them, He connected (p-344) to it His saying, warning against negligence regarding any of them concerning themselves, or regarding enjoining good and forbidding evil with respect to the rights of others: ﴿And God﴾, meaning the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿is aware of what you do﴾, whether secret or open.

Since in this matter of the waiting period there is something the Arabs did not know before, hearts may deny it because they did not understand its secret, and since the matter of marriage, if it is restricted by what is reputable inwardly, He concluded with His saying ﴿Acquainted﴾, meaning He knows the hidden depths of the inner states as He knows their outward forms, so beware of opposing Him and obey His command.

(p-345) When Glorified and Exalted God set this term (*muddah*) for restraining them from men, He explained that allusion (*ta'ridh*) to a proposal of marriage is not included in that restraint. So He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning no sin that inclines (toward you), ﴿for what you allude to of [marriage] proposal﴾, meaning what you say while intending something distant from it, as if it lies on one side while the matter is on another side, and one reaches it only by a roundabout route, such as saying, "You are beautiful" or "You are beneficial," or "I am resolved to marry, and perhaps God will facilitate for me a righteous companion."

Al-Harali said: "Ta'ridh is from the form *tif'il* of *al-'ard*, and *al-'ard* is casting speech sideways (*'ardan*), that is, toward one direction, not intended directly and not aimed straight at it." End of quotation. The difference between it and *kinaya* (metonymy/implicature) is that allusion is speech that is apparent in one meaning while another meaning is intended by it, so the intended sense is not understood except through contextual indicators, like the words of a needy person: "I came to greet you and to look upon your noble face." It is also called *talwih* (hinting). *Kinaya* is mentioning the necessary concomitant while intending the thing it necessitates. Since permission was tied to allusion, it may be understood that clear explicit speech (*tasrih*), which is the opposite of allusion and of *kinaya*, is forbidden. *Sarih* is the name for that whose meaning is evident to the hearer, such that the intended sense comes to mind immediately when spoken without qualification, and nothing else comes to mind first. ﴿of [marriage] proposal﴾: *khitbah* is address made with the intention of marriage.

Al-Harali said: "It is the state of affairs between the suitor and the woman proposed to, of which the speaking is the *khutbah* (with a *dammah*)." ﴿women﴾ whose husbands have died, and those like them in irrevocable divorce (*talaq ba'in*) by three pronouncements or otherwise.

(p-346) Since allusion was made permissible for him, and he might resolve upon explicit speech once that became lawful, He removed blame for it by saying: ﴿or you conceal﴾, meaning you harbour ﴿in your selves﴾, whether explicit or otherwise, whether it stems from the desires of the soul or not.

Al-Harali said: "It is from *kann* (with a *fathah*), and its meaning includes *kinn* (with a *kasrah*), which is that which shields so that nothing can be reached through it."

Since God, Glorified and Exalted, has great care for this community in lightening its burden, He informed them of that by saying, as an explanation: ﴿God knows﴾, meaning with His attributes of perfection, ﴿that you will remember them﴾, meaning during the waiting period (*'iddah*), so He permitted you that according to the limit He set for you.

Al-Harali said: "In this is the application of the sacred law to the particular circumstances (*hilah*) of this community." End of quotation.

(p-347) Since the implied sense was: "then remember them," He made an exception from it by His saying: ﴿but do not make promises to them﴾, meaning in your mentioning of them, ﴿secretly﴾. Since *sirr* (secret) is applied both to what is actually kept secret and to what is fit to be kept secret even if openly stated, He clarified that the intended meaning is the second, namely secrecy in potential, so He said: ﴿except that you speak﴾, meaning in mentioning them, ﴿a known word﴾, that is one of which no one among people would feel shame, so the matter comes to this: the meaning is, do not make promises to them except what one would not be ashamed to mention, and it becomes secret, which is allusion. Thus this verse explicitly prohibits explicit speech, after the first verse had implied this, out of concern for it because of the soul's inclination toward it.

Since the waiting period of widowhood is long, and restraining oneself from marriage during it is severe, and since permission of allusion is close to grazing around the sanctuary (*hima*), and whoever grazes around the sanctuary is likely to fall into it, He singled them out by following the prohibition of concluding the contract before the period ends, as a measure of caution and a prevention of transgression. So He said: ﴿And do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾, meaning do not decide, that is, do not carry out an action decisively, definitively, without wavering in it (p-348), ﴿the tie of marriage﴾, meaning the marriage that becomes a contract for a woman in a waiting period during which she is irrevocably divorced. He thus included in the resolve the sense of finality, and for this reason He dropped *'ala* ("upon") and attached it to the tie, which is among its effects and cannot be realized without it, as if He had said: "Do not resolve upon marriage while the tie remains in place." This is more emphatic than saying "Do not contract the marriage," because the prohibition of resolving, which is the cause of the contract, is a prohibition of the contract a fortiori.

Al-Harali said: "The *'uqdah* (tie) is the binding of two separated ends together such that it is difficult to undo, (p-349) and it is a meaning below writing, which is a connection and stitching." ﴿until the decree reaches its term﴾, meaning the decree (*kitab*) that was prescribed previously in what He revealed to you, namely the explanation of the waiting period of women whose marital bond has been dissolved by a husband's death or divorce, or what was written and imposed of the waiting period. ﴿its term (ajal)﴾, meaning that He extended its period which He established for the waiting period.

Since Glorified and Exalted permitted allusion, prohibited resolving upon the tie, and made the matter more severe by linking it to the decree, and some matters remained between the two parties in which desire is usually dominant and inclination strong, He, Glorified and Exalted, reinforced the warnings to counter those drives. So He concluded these matters with the threat in His words: ﴿And know﴾, meaning, you who are eager for any of that, ﴿that God﴾, who possesses all perfection, ﴿knows what is in your souls﴾, all of it, ﴿so beware of Him﴾, and do not resolve upon evil, for knowledge encompassing all implies power encompassing all.

Since He threatened them with His knowledge, and that is the utmost in threat, and since each person knows within himself of deficiencies what is beyond description, He informed them of what necessitates postponing punishment, namely His bounty in forgiveness and forbearance, urging repentance and establishing a balance between hope and awe. So He said: ﴿And know that God﴾, meaning just as His majesty requires punishment (p-350), His beauty requires pardon, so He is, for that reason, ﴿Forgiving﴾, meaning One who conceals the sins of the sinners if they repent, ﴿Forbearing﴾, meaning none is hastened in punishment. So hasten to repentance, hoping for His forgiveness, and do not be deceived by His postponing, for the anger of the forbearing, coming after long patience, cannot be endured. It is also possible that the intended meaning is: "Do not speak openly to the women in their waiting period about the tie of marriage during any of the periods." The secret in their difference is that the waiting period of widowhood was lengthened out of consideration for the heirs, to a limit that is the furthest sign of the womb's being clear, because the water remains forty days as a drop, and likewise as a clot, and likewise as a lump, and then the soul is breathed into it, so these are four months. Months may be short by four days, so these were added and compensated by completing with the nearest of the units. In the authentic collection of Muslim, may Allah be pleased with him, the first period is given as "forty-two days," and in another narration "forty-five," and in another "some forty." If "some" is taken to mean six, and the days by which months may fall short are added (p-351), it becomes four months and ten [days]. It was not extended beyond that out of consideration for the woman, since it is said that women's patience diminishes after that. For the istibra' (ascertaining that the womb is clear) it was limited to one menstrual cycle (*qur'*), which is the least sign of the womb's being clear, because the master usually has intercourse with his female slave, so patience is difficult. The waiting period of a free woman was tripled, following the practice of the Lawgiver in taking extra caution by threefold measure, even though the cause of haste from intercourse has ceased. Also, because most divorces are revocable, they may arise from anger, so the period was extended so that anger subsides and one reflects. The waiting period of a slave-woman after divorce was between istibra' and the waiting period of a free woman, because the rights of the master, which require brevity, and the rights of the husband, which require length, both pull at her, while classification is not possible. And God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

When the rulings on the waiting periods (*'iddah*) and what follows them, in which the rights of men predominate, were complete, He followed them with the rulings on dowers (*sadaq*). Since the discussion had been lengthy on the rulings of divorce (*talaq*) and death (*mawt*) without mentioning the dower, and since He had concluded those rulings with the attributes of forgiveness (*ghafr*) and forbearance (*hilm*), and since the dower was known to them before Islam, this raised the question: is a dower obligatory upon separation, or is it among the matters covered by forgiveness and forbearance, so that it is not obligatory? Thus it was said: ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾, meaning there is no liability for a dower or anything else, except what comes next regarding the provision (*mut'ah*). The root of *junah* (blame) is inclination arising from weight. ﴿If you divorce women﴾, meaning if any one of you divorces those women over whom he holds the bond of marriage. ﴿As long as you have not touched them﴾, meaning as long as you have not had intercourse with them.

From *mass* (touching), and from *mumassah* in the other reading, which is the meeting of two bodies without a barrier between them. This was said by al-Harali. ﴿Or you have specified for them an obligation﴾, meaning you have named for them a known dower. That is: there is no blame upon you for as long as neither of the two matters has occurred, meaning during the period of its absence. An indefinite "one" is not negated except by the negation of both matters together. So when both are absent, the blame is removed. If both exist, or one of them exists, then it is established: if touching occurs, the named dower becomes obligatory, or the customary dower (*mahr al-mithl*). If an obligation has been specified, half of it becomes obligatory if there was no touching.

Al-Harali said: In this statement is the validity of the marriage contract even when mention of the dower is omitted, not its invalidity. Thus there is the validity of *nikah al-tafwid* (marriage without a specified dower) and of marriage where the mention of the dower is postponed. It becomes clear from this that the dower is not a pillar of the marriage, and that its nullification prevents its consummation. Therefore there are three states concerning the removal of blame in respect of the one who omitted it and did not touch: it is as if he were obliged to a specified obligation, and so blame is lifted from him, in that the one who touches bears the full gift, while the one who specifies bears half the gift. Blame of the obligation is lifted from him, and the place of the obligation is compensated by the provision (*imta'*). For this reason a group of scholars required the provision. End of quotation.

Since the implied sense is: "Divorce them if you wish, and observe in regard to them the rights I have made obligatory for you and against you," He followed it with His words: ﴿And provide for them﴾, meaning as compensation for the breach caused by divorce, according to the condition of the two divorcing parties. A woman divorced without touching and without a specified dower is entitled to the provision by consensus (*ijma'*). This was transmitted by al-Asbahani. ﴿Upon the affluent﴾ among them, that is, the one who has ample means in his circumstances.

Al-Harali said: It is from *iysa'* (abundance), which is the capacity for ampleness that exceeds sufficiency. ﴿According to his means﴾: from *qadr*, which is the limit delimited in a thing, sensible or abstract. ﴿And upon the straitened﴾, that is, the one whose circumstances are constricted.

Al-Harali said: It is from *iqtar* (restriction), which is the deficiency from the sufficient measure. End of quotation. ﴿According to his means﴾, meaning what he is able to afford and can bear. The reading with a fatha on the *dal* is like the reading with a sukun, for both are dialects; or the fatha indicates grace in undertaking something beyond capacity. ﴿A provision﴾, meaning a giving of provision. ﴿According to what is reasonable (*ma'ruf*)﴾, which is what contains no disapproval in the Law. ﴿A duty upon the good-doers (*muhsinin*)﴾, meaning those for whom excellence (*ihsan*) has become a settled attribute. Excellence is the ultimate rank of religion. As al-Harali said, it is as if: submission that is outward, sustained by faith that is inward, and perfected by excellence that is witnessing (*shuhudi*). End of quotation.

Thus the discourse in this arrangement is an incitement and an arousing, not a restriction. It is called excellence because its essence, as al-Harali said, is what gives the woman's soul contentment, while her inner state and the inner state of her family remain at peace or in affection. ﴿Perhaps God will bring about after that some matter﴾ (Qur'an 65:1). End of quotation. There is no doubt that this is excellence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 237:

When the absence of blame (junah) was negated by the absence of both touching (masis) and specification (fard), it conveyed that if both existed, blame would arise through the obligation of the entire stipulated dower. He then followed it with what applies when only one of them is absent, so he mentioned the ruling explicitly when touching alone is absent, in contrast to the previously mentioned woman whose dower was not specified (mufawwadah), and by that he implicitly conveyed what applies when specification alone is absent. He said: ﴿And if you divorce them﴾, i.e., the wives, ﴿before you have touched them﴾, i.e., have had intercourse with them, whether or not there was seclusion (khalwah) ﴿and you have already appointed for them a portion﴾, i.e., you have named for them a fixed dower (mahr), ﴿then half of what you have appointed﴾, i.e., what is taken is half of what you have named for them of the dowry, and nothing more.

When he made this obligatory for her, he encouraged her to forgo it, because the husband had gained nothing from her in return, by using the expression of pardon (al-afw). So he said: ﴿unless they pardon﴾, i.e., the women, for the nun is the pronoun referring to them and the waw is the plural marker of the verb, so nothing is taken from you, ﴿or he in whose hand is the marriage tie (ʿuqdat al-nikah)﴾ pardons, i.e., to him. But since most actions are carried out by the hand, the whole of them was attributed to it, and it became a metaphor for power. ﴿The marriage tie﴾ refers to the husband, who, if he wills, keeps it, and if he wills, dissolves it; so she is permitted to take all of it. The expression of this was a stirring of the husband towards pardon, in return for what was placed in his hand from this, and not hers.

Al-Harali said: When this statement is linked with His saying: ﴿And do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾ [al-Baqarah: 235], addressed to husbands, it strengthens the view of whoever makes the one in whose hand is the marriage tie the husband, as a counterpart to the wives; and whoever restricts their pardon to those who own their affairs, i.e., the mature women, restricts this to the guardians (awliya'). This pattern of indirect allusion to difference is not from broadness of ambiguity, and it is as though it is from a certain restraint from the end of full clarity. So the source of disagreement in it is other than the source of disagreement arising from broad expressions through ambiguity. End of quote.

The Imam (al-Biqa'i) took this to be understood from the expression ʿuqdah, because it denotes the thing acted upon, like akla (a single act of eating, i.e., morsel) and luqmah (a morsel), and the one in whose hand this is, is the husband, while in the hand of the guardian is the contract ('aqd), which is the verbal noun, like akl (eating) and laqm (feeding), not the tie resulting after the contract. ﴿And that you pardon﴾, O men and women, ﴿is nearer﴾, i.e., to piety than the judgment by justice, which is equality.

Since the context is one of encouragement, he used the lam, which denotes greater nearness, rather than ila, and said: ﴿to piety﴾. As for the woman, it is because the husband has received nothing from her and has not benefited from anything of hers, so pardon is closer to his contentment. As for the man, when He indicated him by placing the tie in his hand, just as he tied it by his choice, he dissolves it by his choice; so giving the whole is nearer to comforting the woman and securing her contentment, and whoever does the excess, by his act, is closer to doing the obligatory with one who did not exceed.

Since pardon is a favour from the one who pardons and a kindness to her from him, and since they used to boast only of virtues, he emphasised it with His saying: ﴿And do not forget the bounty﴾, i.e., do not leave what one who forgets leaves; the expression of forgetting is more emphatic in the prohibition, ﴿the bounty﴾, i.e., that you be those who are favoured in all that has passed, not those favoured over you, for the upper hand is better than the lower hand. He added emphasis with His saying: ﴿among you﴾, i.e., while it occurs among you, from some of you to others, nothing of it being outside you, and nothing of it will reach God, because He is free of all need; so He commanded you only for your own benefit, lest the husband be harmed by giving what he gains nothing for in return from the woman, nor the woman by a divorce from which nothing accrues to her in return for the breaking that befalls her because of it. It is also valid that this is addressed to both groups by way of predominance.

Al-Harali specified it to men, saying: It is the right of the husband, who has the excellence of manhood, to be the one who pardons, and not to hold the women to account for pardon; for this reason no command or incitement is addressed to them. Among the most abhorrent things is a man pressing a woman to recover what he gave her, which is clearly stated by His saying: ﴿And if you had given one of them a heap of gold, take not from it anything﴾ [al-Nisa': 20]. So you should not forget that excellence, and so act upon it where you were not obliged to it. End of quote.

Then He gave the reason for that, encouraging and warning, with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., He to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿of what you do﴾, i.e., however small, ﴿is All-Seeing﴾. And this implies: if you divorce them after touching and before specification, then the whole is the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 1 of 2):

When the rulings concerning women were mentioned and branched out, to the point that the broad intellect was constrained by their spread and nearly lost itself in the vast arena of their details, together with the likelihood there of inclination through love and aversion through hatred, which leads to rancour, and preoccupation with children and other trials, tribulations and afflictions, which the bounds of enumeration cannot contain, and some of which are a likely cause of negligence in prayer and indeed in every act of worship, the situation called for the prayer: "O Lord! Man is weak, and in some of this he is preoccupied from every important matter. Is there still room left for him to worship You?" So it was said: ﴿Guard﴾, in the form of *mufa'alah* (the form denoting reciprocal effort), which indicates the utmost resolve, that is, so that some of you may outdo others in this. It is also possible that this refers to the relation between the servant and his Lord, so that the meaning is: "Guard your prayer for Him, so that He guards His prayer over you, and does not act in it as one who forgets, thereby abandoning your honouring through it." And more concise than this: When Glorified and Exalted He mentioned what is between the servants specifically, He mentioned what is between Him and them, and so He said:

Al-Harali said: Since the purpose for which the Book was sent down is the establishment of three matters: establishing the affair of religion, which is what lies between the servant and his Lord; managing the affairs of this world, which is the house of the servant's trial; and setting right the state of the Hereafter and the return, which is the servant's place of abode, the rulings concerning the management of worldly affairs that are being mentioned became, as it were, the dawn, whose stars of illumination are the rulings of the affair of religion. Therefore, the risings of the stars of religious address occur amid the addresses concerning worldly affairs, so the address of the command becomes a star among the discourses on the lawful and the unlawful in worldly affairs. The star of this address concerning the guarding of prayer occurs for this reason: this discord mentioned between spouses, with the aversion that arises in souls and the rivalry over wealth, arose only from neglecting the guarding of the prayers, for prayer is a blessing in provision, a weapon against enemies, and a means of repelling Satan. It thus repels the matters through which souls become constricted, accept whisperings, and are visited by avarice. So in conveying the star of this address amid these rulings is the command to guard the prayers, so that their affairs proceed on a right footing that spares them confusion in this whole body of rulings. End of quotation.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Guard﴾.

Al-Harali said: From *al-muhafaza* (guarding) is a *mufa'alah* derived from *al-hifz*, which is the observance of the act in knowledge, manner, time and establishment, with all that by which its root is secured, its performance completed, and its perfection reached. He indicated the perfection of readiness for this by the particle of elevation, and so said: ﴿over the prayers﴾, and He gathered them and made them definite so as to encompass all their kinds. That is: act in guarding them as one who contends with another in it, for there is no escape from them in any state whatsoever, not even in a state of fear of destruction, since in guarding them lies the complete rightness of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, especially the flowing of provision and the humbling of enemies. ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer, and be steadfast in it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132], and ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153]. "When a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would turn to prayer." There is no doubt that the wording is suitable for including the funeral prayer within it, and what makes this clearer is that the two verses about death surround this verse, before and after.

Al-Harali said: Indeed Allah, Glorified and Exalted, gives the world in return for the intention of the Hereafter, and He refuses to give the Hereafter in return for the intention of the world. The disorder of a person's state in his worldly life and his return arises only from disorder in the state of his religion, and the pivot of his religion and its foundation are his faith and his prayer. So whoever guards the prayers, Allah sets right the state of his world and his next life. In guarding them, the requirements of their performance proceed as an act of submission, and as humble devotion and faithful surrender, and as the vision and witnessing of excellence (*ihsan*). Through this the guarding of them is completed. The first of this is purity for it, by using water in accordance with the sunnah and following the meanings of wisdom, as in wiping the ears together with the head, for whoever separates the two will hardly have his purification completed in the way that wisdom has shown and the sunnah and the practice of the scholars have established, and so he is turned away from it by the heedlessness of most people. Then, binding oneself to repentance at that point, for the purity of the heart is repentance, just as the purity of the body and the soul is water and earth. Whoever prays without renewing repentance prays in a state of impurity without true purity. Then, the presence of the heart in unity (*tawhid*) at the adhan and the iqamah, for whoever's heart is heedless at the adhan and the iqamah from unity, the spirit of his prayer is diminished, and it has no pillar of standing. Whoever's heart is present at the adhan and iqamah, his heart is present in his prayer, and whoever's heart is heedless at them, his heart is heedless in his prayer. Then, the form of the prayer in the completeness of its bowing and prostration, and the giving of speech to every physical pillar through the remembrance of Allah proper to it, at least three times, for there is no act in prayer without speech attached to it. Allah does not accept the prayer of one who does not straighten his back in bowing, prostration, standing and sitting. So by diminishing its completeness, the guarding of it is diminished, and by neglecting the guarding of it, enemies take possession of the soul, avarice overtakes it, the rulings pass over it, and the burdens of this world multiply upon it. No worker does any work at the time of prayer or during the adhan except that it becomes a burden upon him and upon those who benefit from his work, and what he takes as wages for it is a bitter, wicked toil that yields for him neither a work of righteousness nor peace of soul in this life or the next. This is especially so after Allah granted people six hours from the rising of the sun of their day until its decline, so that the world had no claim in the remaining six hours. How much more so if they are held accountable from those hours for the times of the adhan and the prayer, and no work diminishes from the prayer. Thus the guarding of the prayers became the foundation for the rightness of the states of creation with their spouses in all their conditions. End of quotation.

﴿And the middle prayer﴾, that is, especially, for it is the best of the prayers, because the Final Prophet was specially distinguished by it, as its explanation has passed at the beginning of the surah in His saying: ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153]. So Glorified and Exalted singled it out for added emphasis and concealed it, so that its performance would lead to guarding all of them. For this same reason He concealed the Night of Decree in Ramadan, the hour of response on Friday, the Greatest Name among all the names, and the time of death, so that one would be moved to repentance at every moment.

Al-Harali said: Every group has a flower, and so among the prayers there is what stands as the choice of the group, and the best of it is its middle. For this reason Exalted God specified the choicest of the prayers by mention, and described it by attribute, in general terms, so that the middle would include the particular middle belonging to this Ummah, which is the 'Asr, which is not valid for any other nation, and so that it would include the general middle for all nations, and for this Ummah, which is the Subh. Therefore, the field of scholarly opinion widened concerning taking it by attribute, and then their views extended to all of them, because of the vagueness in its mention, so that the guarding of them all would be emphasized in some respect. In the reading of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "and the prayer of 'Asr" (*wa salati al-'asr*), in apposition, which gives the outward sense that the middle is specific to the Subh according to what some scholars held, and there is room for its referring to "the middle prayer" itself, so that it becomes an apposition of attributes, and naming it "'Asr" becomes praise and description, insofar as 'Asr is the essence of time, just as the essences of things are their extracts. ﴿Then after that will come a year in which people will be given rain, and in which they will press﴾ [Yusuf: 49]. So the 'Asr of the day is its essence, being free from the heat of midday and the darkness of night, and for the balance of bodies, souls and states between the needs of lunch and dinner, which are the preoccupations of people with the need for food. And among the eloquence of the Arabs is the apposition of complete attributes: one says "So-and-so is generous and brave" when both attributes are complete in him, but if they fall short of completeness, one says "generous, brave" with the following form. Thus the meaning of this reading is accepted, that the middle is the 'Asr, in apposition to two attributes firmly established in one thing. End of quotation.

What he, may Allah have mercy on him, said is clarified by the saying of people about the sweet-sour pomegranate: "sweet, sour," without a conjunction. Its proof is that they said: when sentences follow one another without a conjunction, this indicates complete connection between them, so the second is either a cause of the first, or a resumptive statement on the supposition of a questioner's question, and similar to what the rhetoricians have said in the chapter on separation and connection. Had the first sentence not implied the second, requiring it, no motive for the question would have arisen. By contrast, when they are conjoined, this indicates that each of them is self-sufficient without what follows, and this indicates completeness. As for the names of Allah, Exalted, their succession occurs without conjunction, because none of them fully expresses the whole meaning of the proper name, the Essence. For this reason Glorified and Exalted concluded the verses of Surah al-Hashr with His saying: ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [al-Hashr: 24], meaning that these names mentioned are among what is understood from the meaning of the proper name that opens them, whether we say it is derived or not. Whenever you perceive a good attribute fitting for Him, Glorified and Exalted, it is among what is indicated by the Greatest Name, for whoever deserves worship can only be so, combining the attributes of perfection. Or, since souls are created and hearts are disposed to know that He, Glorified and Exalted, is exempt from every trace of deficiency and characterized by attributes of perfection, the absence of conjunction among them signals this. Whatever is conjoined among them is for a meaning that called for it, as its explanation will come, God willing, in its places. I have no doubt that the one who denies the divine attributes (*mu'attil*), when he falls into distress, when trouble seizes him and the affliction that overwhelms him makes him helpless, burns his heart and makes his tears flow, his heart necessarily turns to Allah, Glorified and Exalted, for relief, and humbles itself before Him for its removal, because of the perfection, greatness and majesty that have been fixed in its nature, forgetting what the evil companions have taught him of bad belief and what his soul has driven him to of obstinacy. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best. So here is a precious principle that I long sought and asked the learned about, but did not find. I applied my thought across the gardens of the sciences and the wastelands of knowledge until I conceived it. Then, after finishing my tafsir, I saw that al-Kashshaf (*al-Kashshaf*) pointed to it in the verse ﴿and those who seek forgiveness at dawn﴾ [Al 'Imran: 17] in Al 'Imran. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is the Granter of success.

When He had commanded guarding them, He followed it with what gathers all of that, and said: ﴿And stand before Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong majesty and honour, ﴿devoutly obedient﴾ (*qanitin*), that is, obedient. This was said by al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata', Qatadah and Tawus.

Al-Tabarani in *al-Awsat*, the Imam Ahmad, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili in their *Musnads*, and Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih* transmitted from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every mention of *qunut* in the Qur'an means obedience." It was also said that *qunut* means silence. In the two *Sahihs* from Zayd ibn Arqam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We used to talk during prayer: a man would speak to his companion who was beside him about his need, until there was revealed ﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾, and we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak."

Mujahid said: "khashi'in" (humbly submissive). It was also said to be other than this. When the basic meaning of this word is known linguistically, it becomes clear that the intended sense is "sincere" (mukhlisin), and all that they said returns to it. The root qanata, in whatever order its letters appear, revolves around emaciation (dumur) from al-qatin, meaning one with little flesh and fat, and qatana the musk when it dries out. This entails drawing together and purity, for were it not for the attraction of its particles to one another, the removal of what separates them, the musk would not become emaciated. From this comes "imra'ah na'tiq," a woman who bears many children, as if she draws in all the semen so that she obtains what results in a child. Or, since the greatest purpose of intercourse is the child, she is as though exclusively drawing in the semen, and the attraction of others is as though nonexistent. Or, she is as though drawing the child from her womb and bringing it out, and this derives from naqa al-siqa', meaning shaking it out, until it dislodges what is in it and becomes pure. From this also comes al-bayt al-ma'mur, the "nitaq" of the Ka'bah, meaning it overlooks it from above; if it were to draw something from the earth, it would draw the Ka'bah, because it is opposite it.

From emaciation also comes al-taqn, the sediment of water, which is the turbidity that remains in a basin, for it is prepared to attract the sludge. Emaciation also entails firmness, due to the close packing of the particles and their purity from any obstacle. From this comes "amrun mutqan," meaning a firm matter, and "rajulun taqn," meaning a man who is skilled in things, and so he is of pure opinion. It also entails sincerity, humility and submissiveness, and so obedience comes through supplication and other acts, for it gathers the aim upon the one obeyed: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient (qanit) during the hours of the night﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], and the like. Al-taqn also means natural disposition, for it is the secret and essence of a thing, and from it comes eloquence, from "taqana fulan," meaning his nature. Emaciation also entails standing, for it is emaciation in comparison with the rest of the postures. From this comes: the best prayer is the long qunut.

Silence is emaciation in comparison with speech. Emaciation also entails dryness and withering, and from it comes al-taqn for clay from which water departs so that it dries and cracks. And it entails scarcity, from which comes "qurad qatin," meaning a tick with little blood. Thus silence and firmness also come. When you review the meanings of this root, which are qanata, qatana, taqana and naqata, in the lexicons, you will gain greater insight into this. When this is known, it becomes clear that the verse conforms to the hadith and is open to all the statements of the scholars, may God be pleased with them. For when the prayer is made sincere, there is no statement or action in it that is not part of it, and this is pure obedience and humility.

Al-Harali said: qunut is steadfastness upon the matter of goodness and its performance. This is because doing good and righteousness is easy for most, but steadfastness and persistence are difficult for them. Among qunut is the perseverance in the truth regarding what was brought in prayer, until no turning toward creation occurs. Therefore, silence toward creation is required by its meaning, for the speech of people cuts off the continuation of intimate communion. So in its implication is that whoever stands before God, the Exalted, devoutly in his prayer, God, the Exalted, will establish his condition in his worldly life, in his standing and with his family, as the meaning of the verse indicates: ﴿Enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. In it is a notice that prayer rectifies the state with the family and draws down blessing in provision. End quote.

The hadith of Zayd is explicit that prayer at the beginning was not upon the limits it reached at the end. It is therefore possible that action was permissible in it, just as speech was. This is supported by the principle that the default regarding things is permissibility until a text prohibits it. By this, the difficulty in the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn is removed, which implies the permissibility of speech and action for the worshipper when he thinks he has completed the prayer or forgets that he is in it, "because the Prophet ﷺ prayed one of the two evening prayers and gave the salam after two rak'ahs, then stood up to a wooden post in the side of the mosque, leaned on it, and went out, and the hastening people left. When Dhu al-Yadayn informed him of the situation, he asked the people and they confirmed it, so he returned and completed the prayer." The hadith is not dated, so it is possible that it occurred before the prohibition of actions and speech by this verse. What supports the possibility of the permissibility of actions at first is that the verse is followed by the words of the Exalted: ﴿But if you fear﴾, meaning in some condition of jihad, which was previously stated as "prescribed for you," or the like, from an enemy, a beast, or a creditor from whom flight is permissible, or otherwise, ﴿then on foot﴾, meaning standing on the feet; it is the plural of rajil, in that it is closer to the form of prayer.

Al-Baghawi said: meaning, if you are unable to pray devoutly, fulfilling the prayer its due, because of fear, then pray on foot, ﴿or riding﴾, meaning being upon the backs of animals in a posture of steadiness.

Al-Harali said: No ruling that God legislated in ease is without His establishing it in hardship and necessity, in such a way that no blessing from the condition of ease is lost in hardship, so that one knows that the grace of God is not diminished by any time nor deprived by any condition. In it is also a notice that preserving prayer in reality is nothing but the heart's full turning toward the Lord. Whatever the condition allows beyond that, one does; otherwise one suffices with its reality. For this reason, according to the scholars, in intense fear the prayer is reduced to a single takbir, in which alone is gathered the blessing of the four rak'ahs that occur in ease, and in it, in its state, is the blessing in the expansion of provision and the rectification of family as in what occurs in ease, together with the seeking of help for the resolve to perform it under the possibility of fear. It has become clear, through the differing states of the prayer of fear, that its reality is that it has no fixed form. For it is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ fourteen forms, and more forms in the good hadiths. End quote.

Al-Bukhari narrated in the Tafsir, "from Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both," a description of the prayer of fear, then said: "If the fear is more severe than that, they pray standing on their feet or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it." Malik said: Nafi' said: I do not think Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, mentioned that except from the Messenger of God ﷺ, meaning because such a thing is not said from personal opinion. ﴿Then when you are secure﴾, meaning when safety has come to you from what you feared.

Since the greatest purpose of prayer is remembrance, which is the continuous presence of the heart, He said, indicating that in the prayer of fear this is difficult, alerting by the Greatest Name to what affirms presence in prayer and in other than it, of everything that is called remembrance: ﴿then remember God﴾, meaning the One to whom belongs all command. Al-Baghawi said: meaning, pray the five prayers completely with their due rights.

Al-Harali said: He manifested the purpose in the performance of prayer, and that it is only the remembrance, which is the standing of security and fear. End quote. So, as God, the Exalted, prohibited what is not of prayer among statements and actions, He exempted actions in a state of fear, so they remained upon the original ruling. However, al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, narrated, and stated it in Kitab Ikhtilaf al-Hadith from al-Umm, and Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated through the chain of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud from Abu Wa'il, "from Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: We used to greet the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was in prayer," and the hadith continues that when he returned from Abyssinia, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "God brings about from His command what He wills, and among what He has brought about is that you should not speak in prayer." He judged that the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn was prior to it, because in some of its routes there is what implies that his return was before the Prophet's ﷺ hijrah to Madinah, and that is so. However, Asim has errors in the hadith, and although he is a proof in recitation, his hadith is not strong in the face of the opposition of what is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Zayd mentioned above, qualified by the revelation of the verse.

Al-Baqarah is Madani, as in the Sahih in the Virtues of the Qur'an, "from A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: Surat al-Baqarah and al-Nisa' were not revealed except while I was with the Prophet ﷺ." In it, in marriage and elsewhere, is that he ﷺ consummated the marriage with her when she was nine years old, and she remained with him nine years, so that is in the second year of the Hijrah.

Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said in al-Risalah, in a chapter on another aspect of abrogating and abrogated: Muhammad ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Maqburi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We were detained from prayer with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day of the Trench until after Maghrib, when part of the night had passed, until we were relieved. That is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And God sufficed the believers in battle, and God is ever Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25]. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ called Bilal and commanded him, so he gave the iqamah for Zuhr, and he prayed it, performing it well as he used to pray it at its time. Then he gave the iqamah for Asr, and he prayed it likewise; then the iqamah for Maghrib, and he prayed it likewise; then the iqamah for Isha', and he prayed it likewise as well. That was before God, the Exalted, revealed the prayer of fear: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾."

The two Shaykhs also narrated the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "We used to greet the Prophet ﷺ while he was in prayer, and he would return our greeting. But when we returned from the presence of the Negus, we greeted him and he did not return it, and said: 'In prayer there is preoccupation.'" However, it is not explicit in forbidding speech, so the earlier possibility returns. If it is indeed the case that the hadith of Zayd is later, then what I have said is correct; otherwise, what should be held is that there is no difference between speech and action, because the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn includes both on an equal footing. This was authenticated by the author of al-Tatimmah among the companions of al-Shafi'i, and it is reported as the preferred view of Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi in his book al-Tahqiq, and al-Subki and others among the later scholars followed him. The words of al-Shafi'i are clear in this, for he said, in refuting one who attributed to him that he disagreed in deriving rulings from the aforementioned hadith: "You have opposed his principle and his branch, while we have not opposed his principle or his branch by a single letter." This is his text in the book al-Risalah.

When the Exalted ordered remembrance during safety, He gave the reason with His words: ﴿as He taught you﴾, meaning for the sake of His favor upon you in creating in you the knowledge that rescues from ignorance, so the kaf is for causation. Abu Hayyan permitted this in al-Nahr and transmitted it in another place from the grammarians, and God knows best. ﴿what you did not know﴾ through what He gave you by the tongue of this noble Prophet of the rulings that were mentioned in this detailed surah, with the wondrous secrets of principles and the subtle sciences, all of them.

Al-Harali said: Among the rulings of the form of prayer in the limbs and body, and its state in the soul of humility, submission, and freedom from whispering, and its state in the heart of veneration and reverence; and in his indication is what lies beyond the outward knowledge of the secrets of hearts, which were specific to the imams of this Ummah. End quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 1 of 2):
