When the rulings concerning women were mentioned and branched out, to the point that the broad intellect was constrained by their spread and nearly lost itself in the vast arena of their details, together with the likelihood there of inclination through love and aversion through hatred, which leads to rancour, and preoccupation with children and other trials, tribulations and afflictions, which the bounds of enumeration cannot contain, and some of which are a likely cause of negligence in prayer and indeed in every act of worship, the situation called for the prayer: "O Lord! Man is weak, and in some of this he is preoccupied from every important matter. Is there still room left for him to worship You?" So it was said: ﴿Guard﴾, in the form of *mufa'alah* (the form denoting reciprocal effort), which indicates the utmost resolve, that is, so that some of you may outdo others in this. It is also possible that this refers to the relation between the servant and his Lord, so that the meaning is: "Guard your prayer for Him, so that He guards His prayer over you, and does not act in it as one who forgets, thereby abandoning your honouring through it." And more concise than this: When Glorified and Exalted He mentioned what is between the servants specifically, He mentioned what is between Him and them, and so He said:

Al-Harali said: Since the purpose for which the Book was sent down is the establishment of three matters: establishing the affair of religion, which is what lies between the servant and his Lord; managing the affairs of this world, which is the house of the servant's trial; and setting right the state of the Hereafter and the return, which is the servant's place of abode, the rulings concerning the management of worldly affairs that are being mentioned became, as it were, the dawn, whose stars of illumination are the rulings of the affair of religion. Therefore, the risings of the stars of religious address occur amid the addresses concerning worldly affairs, so the address of the command becomes a star among the discourses on the lawful and the unlawful in worldly affairs. The star of this address concerning the guarding of prayer occurs for this reason: this discord mentioned between spouses, with the aversion that arises in souls and the rivalry over wealth, arose only from neglecting the guarding of the prayers, for prayer is a blessing in provision, a weapon against enemies, and a means of repelling Satan. It thus repels the matters through which souls become constricted, accept whisperings, and are visited by avarice. So in conveying the star of this address amid these rulings is the command to guard the prayers, so that their affairs proceed on a right footing that spares them confusion in this whole body of rulings. End of quotation.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Guard﴾.

Al-Harali said: From *al-muhafaza* (guarding) is a *mufa'alah* derived from *al-hifz*, which is the observance of the act in knowledge, manner, time and establishment, with all that by which its root is secured, its performance completed, and its perfection reached. He indicated the perfection of readiness for this by the particle of elevation, and so said: ﴿over the prayers﴾, and He gathered them and made them definite so as to encompass all their kinds. That is: act in guarding them as one who contends with another in it, for there is no escape from them in any state whatsoever, not even in a state of fear of destruction, since in guarding them lies the complete rightness of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, especially the flowing of provision and the humbling of enemies. ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer, and be steadfast in it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132], and ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153]. "When a matter distressed the Prophet ﷺ, he would turn to prayer." There is no doubt that the wording is suitable for including the funeral prayer within it, and what makes this clearer is that the two verses about death surround this verse, before and after.

Al-Harali said: Indeed Allah, Glorified and Exalted, gives the world in return for the intention of the Hereafter, and He refuses to give the Hereafter in return for the intention of the world. The disorder of a person's state in his worldly life and his return arises only from disorder in the state of his religion, and the pivot of his religion and its foundation are his faith and his prayer. So whoever guards the prayers, Allah sets right the state of his world and his next life. In guarding them, the requirements of their performance proceed as an act of submission, and as humble devotion and faithful surrender, and as the vision and witnessing of excellence (*ihsan*). Through this the guarding of them is completed. The first of this is purity for it, by using water in accordance with the sunnah and following the meanings of wisdom, as in wiping the ears together with the head, for whoever separates the two will hardly have his purification completed in the way that wisdom has shown and the sunnah and the practice of the scholars have established, and so he is turned away from it by the heedlessness of most people. Then, binding oneself to repentance at that point, for the purity of the heart is repentance, just as the purity of the body and the soul is water and earth. Whoever prays without renewing repentance prays in a state of impurity without true purity. Then, the presence of the heart in unity (*tawhid*) at the adhan and the iqamah, for whoever's heart is heedless at the adhan and the iqamah from unity, the spirit of his prayer is diminished, and it has no pillar of standing. Whoever's heart is present at the adhan and iqamah, his heart is present in his prayer, and whoever's heart is heedless at them, his heart is heedless in his prayer. Then, the form of the prayer in the completeness of its bowing and prostration, and the giving of speech to every physical pillar through the remembrance of Allah proper to it, at least three times, for there is no act in prayer without speech attached to it. Allah does not accept the prayer of one who does not straighten his back in bowing, prostration, standing and sitting. So by diminishing its completeness, the guarding of it is diminished, and by neglecting the guarding of it, enemies take possession of the soul, avarice overtakes it, the rulings pass over it, and the burdens of this world multiply upon it. No worker does any work at the time of prayer or during the adhan except that it becomes a burden upon him and upon those who benefit from his work, and what he takes as wages for it is a bitter, wicked toil that yields for him neither a work of righteousness nor peace of soul in this life or the next. This is especially so after Allah granted people six hours from the rising of the sun of their day until its decline, so that the world had no claim in the remaining six hours. How much more so if they are held accountable from those hours for the times of the adhan and the prayer, and no work diminishes from the prayer. Thus the guarding of the prayers became the foundation for the rightness of the states of creation with their spouses in all their conditions. End of quotation.

﴿And the middle prayer﴾, that is, especially, for it is the best of the prayers, because the Final Prophet was specially distinguished by it, as its explanation has passed at the beginning of the surah in His saying: ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153]. So Glorified and Exalted singled it out for added emphasis and concealed it, so that its performance would lead to guarding all of them. For this same reason He concealed the Night of Decree in Ramadan, the hour of response on Friday, the Greatest Name among all the names, and the time of death, so that one would be moved to repentance at every moment.

Al-Harali said: Every group has a flower, and so among the prayers there is what stands as the choice of the group, and the best of it is its middle. For this reason Exalted God specified the choicest of the prayers by mention, and described it by attribute, in general terms, so that the middle would include the particular middle belonging to this Ummah, which is the 'Asr, which is not valid for any other nation, and so that it would include the general middle for all nations, and for this Ummah, which is the Subh. Therefore, the field of scholarly opinion widened concerning taking it by attribute, and then their views extended to all of them, because of the vagueness in its mention, so that the guarding of them all would be emphasized in some respect. In the reading of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "and the prayer of 'Asr" (*wa salati al-'asr*), in apposition, which gives the outward sense that the middle is specific to the Subh according to what some scholars held, and there is room for its referring to "the middle prayer" itself, so that it becomes an apposition of attributes, and naming it "'Asr" becomes praise and description, insofar as 'Asr is the essence of time, just as the essences of things are their extracts. ﴿Then after that will come a year in which people will be given rain, and in which they will press﴾ [Yusuf: 49]. So the 'Asr of the day is its essence, being free from the heat of midday and the darkness of night, and for the balance of bodies, souls and states between the needs of lunch and dinner, which are the preoccupations of people with the need for food. And among the eloquence of the Arabs is the apposition of complete attributes: one says "So-and-so is generous and brave" when both attributes are complete in him, but if they fall short of completeness, one says "generous, brave" with the following form. Thus the meaning of this reading is accepted, that the middle is the 'Asr, in apposition to two attributes firmly established in one thing. End of quotation.

What he, may Allah have mercy on him, said is clarified by the saying of people about the sweet-sour pomegranate: "sweet, sour," without a conjunction. Its proof is that they said: when sentences follow one another without a conjunction, this indicates complete connection between them, so the second is either a cause of the first, or a resumptive statement on the supposition of a questioner's question, and similar to what the rhetoricians have said in the chapter on separation and connection. Had the first sentence not implied the second, requiring it, no motive for the question would have arisen. By contrast, when they are conjoined, this indicates that each of them is self-sufficient without what follows, and this indicates completeness. As for the names of Allah, Exalted, their succession occurs without conjunction, because none of them fully expresses the whole meaning of the proper name, the Essence. For this reason Glorified and Exalted concluded the verses of Surah al-Hashr with His saying: ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [al-Hashr: 24], meaning that these names mentioned are among what is understood from the meaning of the proper name that opens them, whether we say it is derived or not. Whenever you perceive a good attribute fitting for Him, Glorified and Exalted, it is among what is indicated by the Greatest Name, for whoever deserves worship can only be so, combining the attributes of perfection. Or, since souls are created and hearts are disposed to know that He, Glorified and Exalted, is exempt from every trace of deficiency and characterized by attributes of perfection, the absence of conjunction among them signals this. Whatever is conjoined among them is for a meaning that called for it, as its explanation will come, God willing, in its places. I have no doubt that the one who denies the divine attributes (*mu'attil*), when he falls into distress, when trouble seizes him and the affliction that overwhelms him makes him helpless, burns his heart and makes his tears flow, his heart necessarily turns to Allah, Glorified and Exalted, for relief, and humbles itself before Him for its removal, because of the perfection, greatness and majesty that have been fixed in its nature, forgetting what the evil companions have taught him of bad belief and what his soul has driven him to of obstinacy. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best. So here is a precious principle that I long sought and asked the learned about, but did not find. I applied my thought across the gardens of the sciences and the wastelands of knowledge until I conceived it. Then, after finishing my tafsir, I saw that al-Kashshaf (*al-Kashshaf*) pointed to it in the verse ﴿and those who seek forgiveness at dawn﴾ [Al 'Imran: 17] in Al 'Imran. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is the Granter of success.

When He had commanded guarding them, He followed it with what gathers all of that, and said: ﴿And stand before Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong majesty and honour, ﴿devoutly obedient﴾ (*qanitin*), that is, obedient. This was said by al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata', Qatadah and Tawus.

Al-Tabarani in *al-Awsat*, the Imam Ahmad, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili in their *Musnads*, and Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih* transmitted from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every mention of *qunut* in the Qur'an means obedience." It was also said that *qunut* means silence. In the two *Sahihs* from Zayd ibn Arqam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We used to talk during prayer: a man would speak to his companion who was beside him about his need, until there was revealed ﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾, and we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak."

Mujahid said: "khashi'in" (humbly submissive). It was also said to be other than this. When the basic meaning of this word is known linguistically, it becomes clear that the intended sense is "sincere" (mukhlisin), and all that they said returns to it. The root qanata, in whatever order its letters appear, revolves around emaciation (dumur) from al-qatin, meaning one with little flesh and fat, and qatana the musk when it dries out. This entails drawing together and purity, for were it not for the attraction of its particles to one another, the removal of what separates them, the musk would not become emaciated. From this comes "imra'ah na'tiq," a woman who bears many children, as if she draws in all the semen so that she obtains what results in a child. Or, since the greatest purpose of intercourse is the child, she is as though exclusively drawing in the semen, and the attraction of others is as though nonexistent. Or, she is as though drawing the child from her womb and bringing it out, and this derives from naqa al-siqa', meaning shaking it out, until it dislodges what is in it and becomes pure. From this also comes al-bayt al-ma'mur, the "nitaq" of the Ka'bah, meaning it overlooks it from above; if it were to draw something from the earth, it would draw the Ka'bah, because it is opposite it.

From emaciation also comes al-taqn, the sediment of water, which is the turbidity that remains in a basin, for it is prepared to attract the sludge. Emaciation also entails firmness, due to the close packing of the particles and their purity from any obstacle. From this comes "amrun mutqan," meaning a firm matter, and "rajulun taqn," meaning a man who is skilled in things, and so he is of pure opinion. It also entails sincerity, humility and submissiveness, and so obedience comes through supplication and other acts, for it gathers the aim upon the one obeyed: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient (qanit) during the hours of the night﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], and the like. Al-taqn also means natural disposition, for it is the secret and essence of a thing, and from it comes eloquence, from "taqana fulan," meaning his nature. Emaciation also entails standing, for it is emaciation in comparison with the rest of the postures. From this comes: the best prayer is the long qunut.

Silence is emaciation in comparison with speech. Emaciation also entails dryness and withering, and from it comes al-taqn for clay from which water departs so that it dries and cracks. And it entails scarcity, from which comes "qurad qatin," meaning a tick with little blood. Thus silence and firmness also come. When you review the meanings of this root, which are qanata, qatana, taqana and naqata, in the lexicons, you will gain greater insight into this. When this is known, it becomes clear that the verse conforms to the hadith and is open to all the statements of the scholars, may God be pleased with them. For when the prayer is made sincere, there is no statement or action in it that is not part of it, and this is pure obedience and humility.

Al-Harali said: qunut is steadfastness upon the matter of goodness and its performance. This is because doing good and righteousness is easy for most, but steadfastness and persistence are difficult for them. Among qunut is the perseverance in the truth regarding what was brought in prayer, until no turning toward creation occurs. Therefore, silence toward creation is required by its meaning, for the speech of people cuts off the continuation of intimate communion. So in its implication is that whoever stands before God, the Exalted, devoutly in his prayer, God, the Exalted, will establish his condition in his worldly life, in his standing and with his family, as the meaning of the verse indicates: ﴿Enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. In it is a notice that prayer rectifies the state with the family and draws down blessing in provision. End quote.

The hadith of Zayd is explicit that prayer at the beginning was not upon the limits it reached at the end. It is therefore possible that action was permissible in it, just as speech was. This is supported by the principle that the default regarding things is permissibility until a text prohibits it. By this, the difficulty in the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn is removed, which implies the permissibility of speech and action for the worshipper when he thinks he has completed the prayer or forgets that he is in it, "because the Prophet ﷺ prayed one of the two evening prayers and gave the salam after two rak'ahs, then stood up to a wooden post in the side of the mosque, leaned on it, and went out, and the hastening people left. When Dhu al-Yadayn informed him of the situation, he asked the people and they confirmed it, so he returned and completed the prayer." The hadith is not dated, so it is possible that it occurred before the prohibition of actions and speech by this verse. What supports the possibility of the permissibility of actions at first is that the verse is followed by the words of the Exalted: ﴿But if you fear﴾, meaning in some condition of jihad, which was previously stated as "prescribed for you," or the like, from an enemy, a beast, or a creditor from whom flight is permissible, or otherwise, ﴿then on foot﴾, meaning standing on the feet; it is the plural of rajil, in that it is closer to the form of prayer.

Al-Baghawi said: meaning, if you are unable to pray devoutly, fulfilling the prayer its due, because of fear, then pray on foot, ﴿or riding﴾, meaning being upon the backs of animals in a posture of steadiness.

Al-Harali said: No ruling that God legislated in ease is without His establishing it in hardship and necessity, in such a way that no blessing from the condition of ease is lost in hardship, so that one knows that the grace of God is not diminished by any time nor deprived by any condition. In it is also a notice that preserving prayer in reality is nothing but the heart's full turning toward the Lord. Whatever the condition allows beyond that, one does; otherwise one suffices with its reality. For this reason, according to the scholars, in intense fear the prayer is reduced to a single takbir, in which alone is gathered the blessing of the four rak'ahs that occur in ease, and in it, in its state, is the blessing in the expansion of provision and the rectification of family as in what occurs in ease, together with the seeking of help for the resolve to perform it under the possibility of fear. It has become clear, through the differing states of the prayer of fear, that its reality is that it has no fixed form. For it is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ fourteen forms, and more forms in the good hadiths. End quote.

Al-Bukhari narrated in the Tafsir, "from Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both," a description of the prayer of fear, then said: "If the fear is more severe than that, they pray standing on their feet or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it." Malik said: Nafi' said: I do not think Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, mentioned that except from the Messenger of God ﷺ, meaning because such a thing is not said from personal opinion. ﴿Then when you are secure﴾, meaning when safety has come to you from what you feared.

Since the greatest purpose of prayer is remembrance, which is the continuous presence of the heart, He said, indicating that in the prayer of fear this is difficult, alerting by the Greatest Name to what affirms presence in prayer and in other than it, of everything that is called remembrance: ﴿then remember God﴾, meaning the One to whom belongs all command. Al-Baghawi said: meaning, pray the five prayers completely with their due rights.

Al-Harali said: He manifested the purpose in the performance of prayer, and that it is only the remembrance, which is the standing of security and fear. End quote. So, as God, the Exalted, prohibited what is not of prayer among statements and actions, He exempted actions in a state of fear, so they remained upon the original ruling. However, al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, narrated, and stated it in Kitab Ikhtilaf al-Hadith from al-Umm, and Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated through the chain of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud from Abu Wa'il, "from Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: We used to greet the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was in prayer," and the hadith continues that when he returned from Abyssinia, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "God brings about from His command what He wills, and among what He has brought about is that you should not speak in prayer." He judged that the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn was prior to it, because in some of its routes there is what implies that his return was before the Prophet's ﷺ hijrah to Madinah, and that is so. However, Asim has errors in the hadith, and although he is a proof in recitation, his hadith is not strong in the face of the opposition of what is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Zayd mentioned above, qualified by the revelation of the verse.

Al-Baqarah is Madani, as in the Sahih in the Virtues of the Qur'an, "from A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: Surat al-Baqarah and al-Nisa' were not revealed except while I was with the Prophet ﷺ." In it, in marriage and elsewhere, is that he ﷺ consummated the marriage with her when she was nine years old, and she remained with him nine years, so that is in the second year of the Hijrah.

Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said in al-Risalah, in a chapter on another aspect of abrogating and abrogated: Muhammad ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Maqburi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We were detained from prayer with the Messenger of God ﷺ on the day of the Trench until after Maghrib, when part of the night had passed, until we were relieved. That is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And God sufficed the believers in battle, and God is ever Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25]. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ called Bilal and commanded him, so he gave the iqamah for Zuhr, and he prayed it, performing it well as he used to pray it at its time. Then he gave the iqamah for Asr, and he prayed it likewise; then the iqamah for Maghrib, and he prayed it likewise; then the iqamah for Isha', and he prayed it likewise as well. That was before God, the Exalted, revealed the prayer of fear: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾."

The two Shaykhs also narrated the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "We used to greet the Prophet ﷺ while he was in prayer, and he would return our greeting. But when we returned from the presence of the Negus, we greeted him and he did not return it, and said: 'In prayer there is preoccupation.'" However, it is not explicit in forbidding speech, so the earlier possibility returns. If it is indeed the case that the hadith of Zayd is later, then what I have said is correct; otherwise, what should be held is that there is no difference between speech and action, because the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn includes both on an equal footing. This was authenticated by the author of al-Tatimmah among the companions of al-Shafi'i, and it is reported as the preferred view of Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi in his book al-Tahqiq, and al-Subki and others among the later scholars followed him. The words of al-Shafi'i are clear in this, for he said, in refuting one who attributed to him that he disagreed in deriving rulings from the aforementioned hadith: "You have opposed his principle and his branch, while we have not opposed his principle or his branch by a single letter." This is his text in the book al-Risalah.

When the Exalted ordered remembrance during safety, He gave the reason with His words: ﴿as He taught you﴾, meaning for the sake of His favor upon you in creating in you the knowledge that rescues from ignorance, so the kaf is for causation. Abu Hayyan permitted this in al-Nahr and transmitted it in another place from the grammarians, and God knows best. ﴿what you did not know﴾ through what He gave you by the tongue of this noble Prophet of the rulings that were mentioned in this detailed surah, with the wondrous secrets of principles and the subtle sciences, all of them.

Al-Harali said: Among the rulings of the form of prayer in the limbs and body, and its state in the soul of humility, submission, and freedom from whispering, and its state in the heart of veneration and reverence; and in his indication is what lies beyond the outward knowledge of the secrets of hearts, which were specific to the imams of this Ummah. End quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 2, verse 240:

When the mention of the rulings on living with women in this manner was liable to prompt a questioner, as has preceded, to say: "Dealing with them has consumed time and harmed one's freedom for worship," and this question was a hint at seeking permission for monasticism (*tarahhub*) and castration, which some people asked about, as will be explained, God willing, in al-Ma'idah in His words: ﴿Do not make unlawful the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 87]; and since turning away from answering the questioner by commanding the preservation of the prayer may have suggested acceptance of the content of the question and permission for asceticism, by the indication of turning away from the question; and perhaps it was pointing to the prohibition of asceticism, by the indication of silence regarding what preceded of the command to live with them without any prohibition of it. He followed the command with some verses about women, as an emphasis on what that allusion had conveyed, meaning: abandon asceticism and be men in following your Prophet ﷺ (p-378) in upholding the rights of God and the rights of himself and others among the servants. He made what follows the verse about prayer, concerning the bond of marriage, only two verses: the first about a ruling of death, which is abrogated (*mansukhah*), as most scholars say, and is not among the pillars of the rulings of this topic. This indicates that devotion to worship should be greater, and that preoccupation with women and children should be only for the sake of provision for death and what follows it. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who﴾

Al-Harali said: When He, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the rulings on spouses in divorce and death, and the ruling on the obligatory gift and the provision for divorced women before consummation, He concluded these emphasized rulings with the obligation and the command to what is of their kind. So He arranged, with the provision, the maintenance, clothing, servants and what is of its meaning, the provision of residence for a woman whose husband has died, up to the limit of the waiting period (*'iddah*) that existed in the pre-Islamic era, so that goodness and what is right would have a continuation in Islam in some form. Whatever contract or covenant existed in the pre-Islamic era, Islam will only make it stronger. End quote.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those of you who die﴾, meaning: they are about to have their souls taken by the One who lent them their bodies, so He takes them back completely, leaving nothing of them and taking nothing of the body along with them, despite the perfect mixing between them, such that no one can distinguish one from the other except Him, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿And leave wives behind﴾ after their death, so let them make a bequest (*wasiyyah*) ﴿a bequest﴾. Whoever reads it in the nominative case (*raf'*), the implied meaning for them is: upon them (p-379) is a bequest. It is also permissible to take death in its literal sense, and the implied meaning is: a bequest from God for their wives, or God enjoins upon you a bequest ﴿for their wives﴾ to remain in their houses, ﴿a provision﴾ for them ﴿until﴾ the end of ﴿the year﴾ from the time of death.

Al-Harali said: That is the furthest limit of life, and it encompasses the whole of the divisions by whose fulfilment the states of patience with, and greed for, a thing become apparent. The second year is only an addition (*istidrak*).

﴿Not requiring them to leave﴾, meaning: without accompanying that provision with any kind of expulsion, or without them being people who leave.

Al-Harali said: So that the four months and ten days are an obligation, and the remainder of the year is a provision, so that the types of provision join the types of what is necessary in marriage: maintenance, clothing, servants and residence. Since this additional provision is only a confirmation of the wife's situation while she was with her husband, indicating that the bond remains, and a sign from God, exalted is He, of the good patience of the woman whose husband has died toward her husband, by not marrying anyone else besides him until she meets him, so that she is with him in the earlier marriage. This gives the community, regarding their wives, a share of the prohibition of the wives of their Prophet after him, who remain after him until they meet him as wives in their own condition. This is for those of his elite community who aspire to follow him in his rulings and the rulings concerning his wives, because men greatly approve of this for their wives. Among the hardest things that befall a man after his death is that his wife marries after him, for by that she becomes, as it were, the one who divorced him. For this reason it has been related that a woman belongs only to her last husband, because she left the husband and he did not leave her. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I and the woman with the two dark cheeks who kept herself for her orphans until they died, or until they separated, are like these two in Paradise," as if he ﷺ emphasized this meaning upon whoever left her, after the deceased, offspring, because that is the most firmly established covenant with him. End quote.

Al-Bukhari related in the *Tafsir* section, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾, that he said: This waiting period was observed at the household of her husband as an obligation. Then God, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, a bequest for their wives: a provision until the year, not requiring them to leave﴾. He said: God, glorified and exalted is He, made for her, for the full year, seven months and twenty nights, as a bequest. If she wished, she could stay in her bequest, and if she wished, she could leave. This is the saying of God, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿not requiring them to leave﴾. So the waiting period remains an obligation upon her as it is.

Since this obligatory provision on the husband's part is permissible on the wife's part, He drew attention to it by His saying: ﴿But if they leave﴾, meaning: of their own accord, without anyone disturbing or expelling them (p-381), ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, O people of religion, upon whom it is obligatory to command what is right and forbid what is wrong, ﴿for what they do with themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 234] of marriage and its preliminaries.

Since in the pre-Islamic era they had conditions that were reprehensible in the Sharia, He restricted it by His saying: ﴿in what is right﴾, meaning: according to you, O people of Islam.

Since in this there are two rulings, one from the side of the men, which is a favour, and another from the side of the women, which is pardon, the implied meaning being: then God is Forgiving and Forbearing, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And God﴾, meaning the One to whom none is equal, ﴿is Mighty and Wise﴾. Within this, as al-Harali said, there is a severe threat to the guardians if they do not carry out and enforce this bequest in what God has obligated. So in its indication is that whoever neglects that will suffer, from the might of God, punishments in his own person, in his wife, and in those who succeed him, and it proceeds on the course of what might requires, according to the measure of wisdom, as a fitting recompense and a just retribution. This verse is one in which some people have mentioned abrogation (*naskh*, the cancellation of one ruling by a later one), but it is only one of those that were subjected to forgetting, which God imposed upon creation, so that hardly anyone acted upon it except a person who was not mentioned for it and did not become known for it. It is among what was made to be forgotten, so forgetfulness fell upon it for a matter God, glorified and exalted is He, willed. God says the truth, and He guides to the way. It has been related that the Prophet ﷺ enforced for a woman from her deceased husband's estate a provision for one year. God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best, that this was before the revelation of the verses of inheritance, when the bequest was for parents and the nearest relatives according to what is right. End quote.

By what al-Harali said, that it is not abrogated, Mujahid also said, as has preceded in the narration of al-Bukhari from him, that if the wife chose this, her waiting period is the year, and otherwise her waiting period is the first verse. Al-Shams al-Isfahani transmitted it from him in his *Tafsir*. It is also transmitted from his fellow countryman Abu Muslim something close to it, for he said, after it had been transmitted from him that it is not abrogated: the implied meaning does not convey obligation upon the husband, like "so let them make a bequest," but rather the implied meaning is: "and they have already made a bequest," or: "and for them is a bequest" (p-383).

The sequence of the verse on guarding the prayer with the waiting period of death is made good by the fact that the fear mentioned in it is among the causes of killing. Perhaps its inclusion in the recitation, although its ruling is abrogated according to the majority, is a reminder to women of what was their waiting period at the beginning, lest they consider the fixed waiting period of four months and ten days lightly and thereby violate something of its sanctities. This is what the reports in the two *Sahihs* and others indicate, "from Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, that a woman asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to apply kohl to her daughter because of a pain that had afflicted her, and he refused and said: 'Some of you in the pre-Islamic era would throw a dung-ball at the end of the year.'"

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 241:

When He, glory be to Him and exalted, mentioned the provision (matā') for the women whose husbands had died, He followed it with the provision for divorced women, as an emphasis of the ruling through repetition and as a generalization after the specification of one of its particular instances. So He, exalted, said: ﴿And for divorced women﴾, that is, those who have been consummated with, whatever kind of divorce it was, ﴿there is a provision﴾, that is, from the husband, to mend what breakage has befallen them ﴿in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, that is, in accordance with their circumstances of both of them, ﴿a duty upon the righteous﴾.

Al-Harali (al-Ḥarālī) said: (p-384) Since what is due before consummation is a duty upon the good-doers, the good-doer gives a provision with the lightest form of gift in speech, short of intimacy; and the righteous one is obliged to give a provision in proportion to what has befallen her of the violation of intimacy, and to the distress and weariness that has occurred between them. Thus in the provision there is a removal of some of that, and a keeping of the relationship with peace or affection. End of quotation.

Within this there is an indication that divorce is like death, in that it cuts the rope of the union, which is like life, and that the provision is like the inheritance.

When He, glory be to Him and exalted, had made these rulings clear with such a healing explanation, it was as if a questioner had asked: Will He make clear other things like them? So He said: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like this explanation, ﴿Allah makes clear﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs perfect wisdom, for He encompasses everything, ﴿His signs for you﴾, i.e., the visible ones, by what He makes clear to you in His audible signs, ﴿so that you may understand﴾, i.e., so that you may be in a state in which there is hope for you (p-385) of reflection upon the audible signs and the visible signs, as the wise do, so that this guides you to the right path. He has repeated this kind of statement many times, and the verses have been explained in detail by it. By my life, it would suffice the discerning person who is free from the sickness of the heart and the blight of desire to hear it once, in trusting its content and relying on its meaning. He repeated it only to draw attention to the eloquence of the verses that end with it and to their being beyond human capacity and the power of created beings. For whenever they heard something of this kind, and they were the foremost in eloquence and the ones who prevailed over all masters of rhetoric and skill, they found it beyond their strength and far from their abilities, and the question about the like of that explanation occurred to them, forgetting what had already been said of the true promise and the firm word, that everything is on this wondrous pattern whose example is hard to attain, because of the bewilderment of minds and the dazzlement of intellects and understandings that overtook them.

(p-386) When the necessary matters had been concluded, those that were driven forth after the announcement of the obligation of fighting (*qitāl*), which is disliked by souls, following the detailing of what was made lawful during the nights of fasting, namely drinks, marriages, and what follows them, and since divorce, as has preceded, is like death, and reconciliation (*al-murājaʿah*, taking back a divorced wife) is like giving life, and since He concluded that with prayer in a state of fear, which is the most common form of *jihād* (struggle, here meaning fighting), then with the clarification of the signs, more general whether they concern *jihād* or other matters, He followed that with His words, as a proof of the verse on the prescription of fighting, in which He urges the believers to face hardships, because created beings are ignorant of the ends: ﴿Have you not seen﴾.

Al-Ḥarālī said: Since the affair of the religion is established by its five pillars, the outward observance of which is complete within the community, and since its completion depends on the piety of hearts and the sincerity of intentions, a few admonitions and stories concerning it were sufficient. But since the core of the religion is *jihād*, in which souls are spent and wealth is expended, the admonitions of the Qur'an concerning it are many and recur. This community was presented with information about what would befall it, so He mentioned the stories that occurred among the earlier nations, especially the People of the Two Books, the Children of Israel, and those who joined them from the sons of Esau (al-ʿAys). Their events were thus an example of the events of this community. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) was directed to interrogate their conditions, through what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, would reveal to him of their affairs visibly, and through what He would send down of their news as clarification. Among the comprehensive meanings of this is what preceded in His words, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them﴾ (2:211). Among the verses that merit being addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ) for the elevation of their meaning, the most noble meaning is that which is said with ﴿Have you not seen﴾, an address to the Prophet (ﷺ). The more general meanings are those said with ﴿Have you not seen﴾ in the plural, an address to the community, so that each is addressed according to the measure of what was offered to them of the preparation of the faculty of reason, so that the acquisition of knowledge is arranged according to the measure of the faculty of reason. Thus, among the lofty stories, the knowledge of subtle lessons is what these verses contain in His words: ﴿Have you not seen﴾ (p-388), so that this may be a lesson for this community, lest they flee from death as those before them fled. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «If the plague breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it.» This is so that their distinction over those before them may appear through their resolve, just as Allah, exalted is He, manifested their distinction over those before them through what He gave them of His bounty and mercy, which He did not bestow upon those before them. End of quotation.

Since leaving one's homeland is something that is not readily tolerated, He drew attention by mentioning it to the great calamity that overtook them, and so He said: ﴿to those who went out﴾, that is, from among those who came before you of the nations, ﴿from their homes﴾, which they were accustomed to and had long toiled to settle in, because of what befell them there that they had no power to bear, namely death, ﴿while they were thousands﴾, that is, very numerous, exceeding ten thousand, as the plural of multiplicity implies.

Al-Ḥarālī said: This indicates that their fear was not due to a shortage of numbers, but was from the anxiety of souls. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, (p-389) informed that caution does not save one from the decree, but only supplication saves from it, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Indeed supplication meets the decree, and they wrestle with each other until the Day of Resurrection.» End of quotation.

﴿fearing death﴾, by fleeing from a plague that had broken out in their city, or fleeing from an enemy whom their prophet had called them to fight, according to the differing reports, supposing that flight would save them.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, indicated that their death was as that of a single soul, by making them like one commanded who could not refrain from obeying, through His words, as a consequence of their departure in this manner: ﴿Then Allah said to them﴾, that is, He who does not let a fugitive escape and cannot be overcome by a seeker, because to Him belongs all perfection, ﴿Die﴾, that is, so they died together with the death of a single soul, and their caution did not avail them, nor did their averting of the decree. He taught them and made them see the matter, informing that whoever dreads fighting out of fear of death, his caution will not spare him, along with what he earned of angering his Lord; and whoever advances towards it, his advance will not harm him, along with what he gained of the pleasure of his Master.

Al-Ḥarālī said: In its indication (p-390) there is information that this death is a death brought about by speech, since He did not say "Then Allah caused them to die," so it is a death that is absolute, with no return from it. In it there is a manifestation of the meaning of the gradual progression of death itself through successive stages, from the limit of weakness of the limbs and faculties through lethargy, to the limit of drowsiness, to the limit of sleep, to the limit of unconsciousness, to the limit of swooning, to the limit of this death by speech, to the limit of the death that follows, over the whole of life, which does not return except after resurrection. Likewise is the death by which the body disintegrates while remaining in the form of its remains, which is more severe upon the dead than that which does not affect its limbs: «Indeed Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets, martyrs, scholars, and muezzins.» Just as life has stages, from the breath of the earth to the life of the believer and what is above that of life, so too death has stages equal to the stages of life, and with every stage of life there is a death, until the matter ends with the Living who does not die: ﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾ (53:42). Thus the person of understanding knows that (p-391) this is a preparation for His words: ﴿Then He gave them life﴾. In the word "then" (*thumma*) there is a delay, for as long as Allah wills. End of quotation.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made this an affirmation to the Prophet (ﷺ) of the seeing (*ruʾyah*), either because He unveiled these people to him in both states, or as an alert that he is, in the certainty of Allah's informing him, in a state that is like seeing for others, so as to train his community. Perhaps in the verse there is an exhortation to be generous in reconciling after divorce, as Allah showed generosity to these people by giving them life after disciplining them with death. He concluded what came before it with the expression of hope for reason (*tarajjī al-ʿaql*), and in this there is an indication that those who left their homes for this purpose were foolish. It is as if it were said: "So that you may reason, and not be like these who thought that their flight would save them from Allah. Rather, you should be those who know that wherever you are, you are in His grasp and subject to His will and power (p-392). This will lead you to advance upon what He has prescribed for you of what you dislike, namely fighting." Or it may be said: Since the one who is dying may divorce his wife during his final illness in order to flee from her inheritance, and may favor some of his heirs in a way that harms others, and may scheme against a divorced woman by withholding her right through some device, He concluded the verse about the death of husbands concerning wives and divorcées with the hope for reason, meaning: if you reason, you will not withhold from anyone the bounty of Allah that He has given you, knowing that He, exalted is He, is able to prevent what one intends to give and to grant what one intends to withhold, by means of causes He establishes and motives He creates; or He may heal the one who does such a thing from his illness and then strip him of His bounty, making him poor after his wealth and weakening him after his strength. Caution does not avail against His decree, and no scheme or stratagem turns aside His will, even if the numbers are many and the support is great.

﴿Have you not seen﴾, up to His words: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is, He who encompasses majesty and honor, ﴿is full of bounty﴾ ﴿toward mankind﴾, that is, in general. Let each one mention what bounty he has received from Him (p-393), and let them desire to pardon those whose withholding they see as just, because that is nearer to gratitude and further from disbelief. Thus, the divorce of one who flees is the removal of a wife from the sphere of his marital bond out of fear that his wealth will be diminished by taking from it what belongs to her, and the husband's departure from the sphere of marriage out of fear of a death that is restricted by her being under his marital bond, and the departure of thousands from the abode of residence out of fear of the death of one who divorces. Among the wonderful correspondences is that, since the true condition of the Arabs was that after their forefather Isma'il (peace be upon him) and those who followed him in goodness, they had moved from the narrowness of the abode of knowledge and faith, out of fear of the destruction of bodies through the obligations of religion, to (p-394) the pursuit of desires and disobedience, and so they fell into the death of ignorance and disbelief. When the Qur'an was sent down to them, and most of this sura was a refutation of the People of the Book, He repeated the guidance of the Arabs from disbelief and ignorance with the word of hope in more than one place, such as: ﴿And so that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided﴾ (2:150); ﴿so that you may be conscious of God﴾ (2:183); ﴿that they may be guided﴾ (2:186); ﴿that you may reflect﴾ (2:219); ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾ (2:220); and other such passages, until the closing of these verses with the hope for reason. The People of the Book had become intensely envious of them, because the Prophet they had been awaiting was from among them. An envious person clings, in denying good to the one he envies, to the slightest thing. It was as if they said: "Will these Arabs be given life, despite their great numbers and their spread across the regions of this peninsula, from the death of disbelief and ignorance into faith and knowledge, after disbelief and ignorance have persisted in them for so long, and the nights and days have passed over them, until they have grown arrogant and rebellious in them, hardened, and stubborn in them?" They were answered: "Yes, and what you deem unlikely is not far." They said: "If Allah has a care for them, why does He leave them in ignorance and disbelief after their forefather Isma'il (peace be upon him) prescribed for them the religion of his father Ibrahim (peace be upon him)?" They were answered that He did this to them because of a sin they deserved (p-395), for a wisdom that His preceding knowledge required. Then He reminded them of His power in similar punishment and kindness, through what they themselves know. So He, exalted is He, said, addressing His Prophet (ﷺ), while meaning them, as one says: "Speak to yourself, and listen, O neighbor": ﴿Have you not seen﴾. It is also possible that the address is to every person who understands, meaning: you know with your heart, O listener, a knowledge that is like seeing with your eyes, through the proofs that preceded, which are brighter than the sun, concerning the power of Allah to resurrect. What supports that the sense of seeing is intended is the use of "to" (*ilā*) after it in His words: ﴿to those who went out﴾. He said: ﴿Then Allah said to them﴾, that is, He to whom all greatness belongs, as a punishment for them for fleeing from His command: ﴿Die, then He gave them life﴾ after a long time had passed over them and their age had grown old, as the conjunction with the particle of delay implies, as a bounty from Him. Just as He bestowed favor upon those people by giving life to their likes after punishing them with death, so He bestows favor upon these people by giving life to their spirits from the death of disbelief and ignorance, to manifest the nobility of their Prophet (ﷺ). Then He justified that with His words: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is, He to whom all greatness belongs, with all His majesty, greatness, and perfection, ﴿is full of bounty﴾, that is, great, ﴿toward mankind﴾, that is, (p-396) all of them, the obedient among them and the disobedient.

Al-Ḥarālī said: By attributing them at one time to states of ruin and then delivering them from these to states of salvation, such that if He had left these people in this death, and whoever followed their way after them, their hereafter would have perished just as their worldly life perished. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, gave them life to renew His bounty upon them. End of quotation.

Just as He bestowed favor upon you, O Children of Israel, by giving you life from the death of servitude and that humiliation, after He had imposed it upon you for your sins for long ages; and just as He bestowed favor upon you, O Arabs, by relating to you the likes of these reports so that you may take heed. ﴿But most people do not give thanks﴾. He repeated the explicit noun and did not use a pronoun, so as to make it more explicit as a general statement, lest someone claim that the first "people" refers to the people of a particular time, thereby restricting the second to most of them. ﴿do not give thanks﴾. This is an allusion to the Children of Israel, in that they did not give thanks to Him, glorified and exalted is He, by fulfilling His covenant with them to follow this noble Prophet, upon whom be the best of blessings and peace. And in this manner, after these correspondences, there is an affirmation of His power, glorified and exalted is He, to bring back, and a turning of the one who denies this towards the truth from a direction he does not perceive (p-397).

Al-Harali said: Gratitude (shukr) is the manifestation of the inner reality of a matter upon the outward character, through that which is inward. Since the whole matter belongs entirely to Allah by compulsion, gratitude is that the whole character should appear as gratitude to Allah, for the origin of "shakur" (grateful) is the beast upon which what it eats shows itself as fatness and goodness. So whoever has been entrusted with the character of a matter but it does not appear upon his character is ungrateful (kafur).

When Allah, glorified and exalted be He, deposited within the essences of things knowledge of Him, awareness of Him, and magnifying of Him, whoever does not let that appear upon the outward character is ungrateful (kafur), and whoever lets appear what is hidden within him of that is grateful (shakur). This description does not belong to people in general, because they waver between the manifest matter upon them being, in their view, at times from Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and at other times from themselves and from others besides Allah, from those whom they have taken as protectors, according to the measure of disbelief, desire, innovation, or sin, and according to the measure of the "rust" (rayn) of their acquisition upon their hearts. Thus in reflecting upon this verse there is a warning to this community that they should beware of death.

Some of the Successors (tabi'in), may Allah be pleased with them, said: "We have seen peoples—meaning from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)—for whom death was more desirable to one of them than life is to you today. This was only because they had verified the promise of the Hereafter, to the point that it was as though they were witnessing it, so leaving the ruin of this world for the building of their Hereafter became easy for them." End of quotation.

How excellent is the return to the narratives of the earlier generations and the attention to His saying: ﴿Fighting is prescribed for you, and it is hateful to you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216], in this light, and to those whom Allah caused to die and then brought back to life. The people of tafsir said: their revival was at the hand of Ezekiel (Hizqil, Hizqiyal), one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, peace be upon them. Al-Baghawi said: he was the third of their caliphs (khulafa'). What I have seen in the Book of the Prophets who were sent among them after Moses, peace be upon him, for renewing the matter of the Torah and re-establishing what had been effaced of its rulings—they were sixteen prophets, the first of whom was Joshua son of Nun and the last of whom was Daniel, peace and blessings and honour be upon all of them—is that Ezekiel was the fifteenth of them, peace be upon him.

In Chapter 21 of his prophecy it says: "The hand of the LORD was upon me, and the Spirit of the LORD carried me out into a valley full of bones, and He caused me to pass round among them, and behold, there were very many in the open valley, and they were very dry. And He said to me: 'Son of man, can these bones live?' I said: 'O Lord GOD, You know.' Then He said to me: 'Prophesy over these bones, and say to them: O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live. I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the LORD.' So I prophesied as I was commanded; and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone. And I looked, and behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh came upon them, and skin covered them, but there was no breath in them. Then He said to me: 'Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel, and the prophets who were slain...and their bones are dried, and every man is a hero.' Prophesy, O son of man, and say to the breath: thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as He commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army. Then He said to me: 'Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel...Therefore prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will open your graves and bring you up from your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I have opened your graves and brought you up from your graves, and put My Spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land.'" End of quotation.

When Glorious and Exalted God explained that fleeing does not spare one from death, He commanded fighting in the path of God, which is the greatest aim of these passages. He turned the speech toward those who need to be commanded to it, and He introduced it with the conjunction *wa* (and). This conveys coordination with something not mentioned before, meaning the sense is: "Do not flee from the causes of death, but stand firm in the places of hardship. ﴿And fight﴾." He expressed it with the preposition *fi* (in), indicating the adverbial sense of enclosure, to show that they must be in the fighting, even when conditions become severe, enclosed by the religion and observing it, not departing from it in any way. Thus they are truthful in advancing against those who persist in disbelief, and they hasten to refrain from harming those who have shown submission, and similar observance of the laws of faith. He expressed it with "the way" (*sabil*) to indicate the ease and clarity of the religion, so there is no excuse for departing from any part of it under any circumstances. So He said: ﴿in the way of God﴾, that is, the one for whom there is no equal, as He prescribed it for you, even if you dislike fighting.

When He commanded them, after warning them, He encouraged and frightened them with His saying: ﴿And know﴾, alerting them so that they would lend their ears and bring their minds to what is being addressed to them, ﴿that God﴾, that is, the One who possesses complete power and all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿is All-Hearing﴾ of what you say when you are commanded to what is disliked in fighting, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what you conceal of aversion to it or inclination toward it. So He will reward you for good, in speech, action, and intention. A good deed is multiplied tenfold, up to seventy-fold, up to seven hundred-fold, up to many multiples, while an evil deed is recompensed with its like, if He wills. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

(p-402) Since spending, which is one of the greatest aims of the surah, is the strongest pillar of jihad and the most powerful confirmation of faith and the fulfilment of the pledge to the King, the Dayyan, He repeated the exhortation to it in a manner more eloquent in arousing eagerness than what came before. He said, in the manner of one testing the sincere among those whom He commanded, warned and admonished: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah﴾ from among you, O you who have been prescribed fighting and the expenditure of souls and wealth, ﴿a goodly loan﴾. The One who is singular in greatness is Allah, and "lending" (ilqa') here means causing a loan to take place; therefore He said ﴿a loan﴾. Glorified and exalted is He, who likened the deed to a loan because of the reward hoped for from it: it is like a loan, which is the giving of wealth in expectation of its return in like form. He expressed it thus because it indicates love, for none lends to you except one who loves you, and because its reward is greater than the reward of (p-403) charity. ﴿Goodly﴾ means comprehensive of good-heartedness, sincerity of intention and purity of wealth.

Al-Harali said: The qard (loan) is the cutting off of a part of a thing and severing it from it, as if one cuts off for Him a piece of his wealth so that He may cut off for him portions of His reward, multiplied. A loan between people is a loan for a loan, like for like; whoever takes more has committed riba, and whoever gives more without a contract or covenant has fulfilled it. Thus a loan is equality, and riba is increase. Glorified and exalted is He, who described the loan to which He urged with "goodly", so that the dealing would be a giving in the manner of ihsan, which is the spirit of religion, namely that one deals with Allah in it as if he sees Him. End of quote.

When souls are naturally inclined to stinginess with what they possess unless there is a benefit, He encouraged them by saying, as a consequence of that: ﴿so that He may multiply it for him﴾.

Al-Harali said: Mudaʿafa (multiplying) is a form of mufa'ala from ḍiʿf (with a kasra), which is folding a thing with its like once or several times. He removed the doubt of possibility by saying ﴿for him﴾, that is, in this world and the Hereafter.

(p-404) Al-Harali said: The first indication of this multiplication is that the increase is a doubling and not a fraction of the lender's principal, so that this would not depart from the meaning of fulfilment of repayment. For the borrower sometimes repays more than the principal by a fraction of its weight. "The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ would not borrow a loan without repaying it with an addition," and he said: "The best of people are those who are best in repayment." So Allah, the Exalted, informed that His borrowing is not in this station but in what is above that, for the loan is multiplied by its like and its likes up to what is called abundance. In His words ﴿manifold﴾ there is what indicates that a good deed is ten-fold, and in His words ﴿many﴾ there is what indicates reaching beyond ten and up to a hundred, as if He were the one who explained His words after this: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261], so He connected the specification of this abundance to hundreds, then opened the door of multiplication to what no scholar's knowledge can reach in His words: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whomever He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261]. End of quote.

When Glorified and Exalted He encouraged them to lend to Him, He followed it with a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in "yuḍā'if", combining fear and hope, and He said: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing in knowledge and power, (p-405) ﴿grasps﴾, that is, this attribute belongs to Him, namely causing contraction and restriction for whomever He wills, even if His wealth is great.

Al-Harali said: Qabḍ (grasping) is the complete taking; its origin is grasping with the whole hand, while qabḍ with an unpointed ḍ (ḍ unmarked, i.e., the verb meaning to take with fingertips) is taking with the tips of the fingers, and it is a gathering in contrast to spreading (basṭ). Therefore it is contrasted with ﴿and He spreads﴾, that is, for whomever He wills, even if his state is constricted. Basṭ (spreading) is the widening of what is gathered to a limit of extent. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, physically through resurrection and in meaning in all your affairs; so He will recompense you in both abodes according to what He knows of your intentions.

(p-406) Since the Companions, may God be pleased with them, were wishing in Mecca, the blessed city, for permission to fight the unbelievers so that they might turn them back from their harm, error, and blindness, He marvelled at the state of the Children of Israel, for they asked for the command to fight and then did not act justly when it was commanded, as a warning against the likes of their condition, as a depiction of the wondrous power of Him who overturns resolutions and turns hearts, and as an announcement of the great rank of the Prophets and their firm grounding in divine knowledge. It is also an indication of the conclusion of the verse before it. So He said, turning to the Highest of Creation (ﷺ), as an allusion that the souls have subtle whisperings that only the discerning understand (p-406): ﴿Have you not considered?﴾

Al-Harali said: He showed you in the first [passage] the state of those who fear death, because of the anxiety in the souls against which this Ummah was warned. Then He showed you in this [passage], in contrast to that, the eagerness to seek war, and these are two extremes of deviation in the souls. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not wish to meet the enemy; ask God for well-being. But when you meet them, be patient, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords." In this there is an indication to this Ummah that it should not seek war initiating it, but rather should only defend against those who prevent it from establishing its religion, as the Exalted and Glorious said: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged﴾ [al-Hajj: 39]. The Prophet (ﷺ) also said, upon him be prayer and peace: 

"The polytheists have transgressed against us; whenever they intend sedition, we refuse."

So it is the right of the believer to refuse war and not to seek it, for if he seeks it and is granted it, he will fail, just as those failed when they turned away, except for a few. These stories are not meant as a narrative about past people; rather, they are an announcement of what those who come after will encounter. "It is you I mean, and listen, O neighbour!" Therefore, no one hears the Qur'an who does not take it in its entirety as an address to this Ummah concerning every story of the earlier peoples that it relates. End of quotation.

It is permissible that the address is to everyone who gives ear while being a witness.

Since the failure of a noble person is more reprehensible, He said: ﴿to the chiefs﴾, that is, the nobles.

Al-Harali said: Those who fill the eyes with splendour and the hearts with awe.

Since this was from the sons of the righteous, it was more shameful, so He said: ﴿of the Children of Israel﴾. And since it was from one to whom religion had been established, whose miracles had become clear, and for whom divine matters had become well known, it was more grievous, so He said: ﴿after Moses﴾, that is, the one who brought them signs that covered the earth in abundance and filled the hearts with greatness, and left among them a book that, after the Qur'an, is unmatched among the heavenly scriptures.

Al-Harali said: In this there is a notice that the community declines after its Prophet by what remains of his light during the time of his presence among them. They said: "We did not shake the dust of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from our hands until we denied our hearts." End of quotation.

﴿When they said﴾. Since breaking a promise to the great, especially to the Prophets, is more heinous, He said: ﴿to a prophet of theirs﴾, and He left him indefinite because there is no requirement for his definition.

Al-Harali said: Because their known Prophet who commanded them was Moses, peace be upon him, and after him, up to Jesus, peace be upon them, the prophets were in the position of governors and leaders over them, like the scholars in this Ummah, who implement and know what was revealed to Moses, peace be upon him. So they remained so until the revelation of the Gospel. Thus, just as He related at the beginning of the sura their state with Moses, peace be upon him, He related at its end their state after Moses, so that this Ummah might take a lesson from that concerning its own state with its Prophet (ﷺ) and after him. End of quotation.

Since among them was such hardness that they would not submit except to gain kingship, and since fighting cannot be carried out except under a unifying leader through whom the word is one, they said: ﴿Raise up for us﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿a king﴾, that is, one who will manage the matter of war for us, ﴿and we will fight﴾, that is, under his command, ﴿in the way of God﴾, that is, the Supreme King.

(p-409) Al-Harali said in his explanation: Their taking the command as a matter of the self's own favour, since in their words there appeared no attribution to God, the Exalted and Glorious, through whom deeds are sound only when they are attributed to Him. Whatever is built upon piety succeeds, and whatever is built upon the claim of the self collapses. ﴿He said﴾, that is, that Prophet: ﴿Is it that﴾, the word ﴿hal﴾ indicates the affirmation of the interrogative, and its meaning has been sufficient in place of the hamza. End of quotation.

﴿It may be that you﴾, that is, you are close to. Since the concern was greater for disciplining those who asked in this important matter, he put first the phrase: ﴿if fighting is prescribed﴾, that is, obligated. So they said, and in my view the better meaning, as will be verified God willing in the Sura of Repentance, is that the meaning is: "Do you fear for yourselves?" And since the intent was to alert them to asking for well-being and to keeping away from the exposure to trial, given the gravity of the situation, that once a matter becomes obligatory there is no concession in it, and whoever falls short in it is ruined, he placed between "it may be" and its complement the phrase: ﴿upon you is fighting﴾, as an obligatory duty. He built the verb in the passive to protect the subject from an opposition that might be expected from their negligence: ﴿that you will not fight﴾, for that would lead you into disobedience.

Al-Harali said: The kasra and the fatha of ʿasā are two dialects. It is the custom of the grammarians not to seek the difference of meanings from the middles and beginnings of forms. But in understanding the language and verifying it there is i'rab (grammatical inflection) in the middles and beginnings, just as the i'rab of the endings is well known among the general grammarians. So the kasra, wherever it appears, indicates a manifest weakness and brokenness, and the fatha, which is inflected, indicates a manifest strength and steadiness. End of quotation.

It is as if he (ﷺ) understood that some of them would abandon fighting out of weakness, and some would abandon it out of strength. For this reason he negated the act and did not say: "that you would be incapable."

Al-Harali said: So He informed them of what their matter would lead to, but they did not turn away from it, argued with him, and answered him with the same prior statement. In his phrasing there is information about what they were upon of coarseness of natures and slowness to awareness. End of quotation.

Since the content of this interrogation was: "I fear for you that you will sit out from fighting," God informed us of their answer by His saying: ﴿They said﴾, that is, to Moses in opposition, and the conjunction over an unmentioned element indicates that the implied meaning is: "What compels us to sit out? We do not fear that for ourselves; rather we are resolved that we will fight the fiercest fighting!" He joined to them their saying: ﴿And what is it for us﴾, that is, what is the matter with us, ﴿that we should not fight﴾. Since the soul is most eager and most ready for what is for God, they said: (p-412) ﴿in the way of God﴾, that is, the One who has no equal, as an incitement and stirring up, ﴿while﴾, that is, the state being that, ﴿we have been driven out﴾, a term general enough to include whether it was with expulsion of banishment or not. It is built in the passive because the cause of the displacement and expulsion is the expulsion itself, not an attribution to a specific party. ﴿from our homes﴾, which are for our bodies as our bodies are for our spirits.

Since in ﴿driven out﴾ there is the meaning of "exiled," He joined to it ﴿and our children﴾. Thus they mixed what is for God with what is for other than Him, while He is the most self-sufficient of partners and accepts only what is pure.

Al-Harali said: God, the Exalted and Glorious, informed that they attributed this to the anger of the selves over the expulsion, whereas one fights in the way of God only when he fights so that the word of God may be the highest. End of quotation.

Since breaking a promise soon after it was made is more shameful, He said: ﴿Then when﴾, with the fa' that indicates immediate sequence, ﴿was prescribed for them﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿fighting﴾, that is, what they had asked for, just as it was prescribed for you after you had been wishing for it while you were in Mecca, as God, the Exalted, will make clear, God willing, in the Women, at His saying: ﴿Have you not considered those who were told: "Restrain your hands"﴾ [al-Nisa': 77] (p-413). ﴿They turned away﴾, hastening to retreat after the intensity of that eagerness, ﴿except a few of them﴾, that is, they fought, and God is Knowing of them. ﴿And God﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs the encompassing of every perfection, ﴿is Knowing﴾ of ﴿those who turned away﴾. This is how the original would have been, but He said: ﴿of the wrongdoers﴾, informing that they had asked for trial, whereas it was their duty to ask for well-being. Then, when they were granted what they asked for, they turned away from it: they held back where advancing was called for, and they advanced where holding back was called for, so they disobeyed God, who had made it obligatory upon them. Thus they combined the shame of breaking a promise, the disgrace of disobedience, the humiliation of drawing back from their peers, and the ugliness of abandoning their brothers.

(p-٤١٤) When the conjunction, referring to something unmentioned, pointed to the implied meaning, "Then their prophet said to them: Did I not tell you, 'Do not ask for trial, and do not hasten the decree of destiny, for most of what the soul says is false and most of its wishes are vain, while the command of God, once it manifests, must come to pass'?", he followed it with ﴿And he said to them﴾, meaning privately, with no one else among them, so that their reply, which was not fitting, would not be attributed to others. He stated the intended meaning explicitly, lest it be thought that the speaker was God and that they had confronted Him with objection. Then he said ﴿their prophet﴾, meaning the one previously mentioned as the one they had asked, emphasized, honored, and affirmed with the particle of expectation, because their request made through a prophet implies the expectation of an answer. ﴿Indeed God﴾, meaning in His majesty and the might of His perfection, ﴿has indeed﴾. Since clothing a person with the honor of kingship is like giving honor to inert matter by breathing life into it, the expression of this by "sending" (ba'atha) was more fitting, so he said ﴿has sent for you﴾, meaning specifically (p-٤١٥) for the sake of your request, ﴿Ṭālūt﴾, the name of a king from the Children of Israel, from a tribe in which kingship had never been, ﴿as king﴾, to whose command you would look in directing war.

Al-Ḥarālī said: "The first thing they were tested with was that a king was appointed over them who was not from the house of kingship among them. Thus the first of their trials was that they asked for a king, and they were answered, but they were not content with what was sent to them." End quote.

When he granted them what they had asked for, one of the first signs of their crudeness was their objection to the command of the Sovereign, the Judge, which He sent to them by His greatest name, which indicates all perfection of majesty and beauty, so that they would be more worthy of accepting His command and stopping at His restraint. Their objection was introduced as the answer to one who seems to have asked: "What did they do when He granted them what they had requested?" So he said: ﴿They said﴾, meaning they themselves, not others, ﴿How can he have kingship over us, when we﴾, meaning while we, in fact, ﴿are more entitled to kingship than he is﴾, because among us there is one who is of the lineage of kings, not he.

Al-Ḥarālī said: "So they doubled their objection with something worse (p-٤١٧), which is boasting, by claiming the right to kingship over the one whom God had made king over them. There was in this a share of the pride of Iblīs, when he said, when he was commanded to prostrate to Ādam: ﴿I am better than him﴾ [al-A'rāf 7:12]." End quote.

﴿And he has not been given abundance of wealth﴾, meaning, while in fact he has not been given, ﴿abundance of wealth﴾. Thus there were two obstacles for him: first, that he was not from the house of rule, and second, that he was poor, while a king must have wealth to support him.

Al-Ḥarālī said: "In this third objection there was the trial of idolizing wealth, as if kingship is established by it, whereas kingship is only by God's granting it. So in this third trial there was ignorance and shirk, and the forms of their trials multiplied in what they pursued from their own selves." End quote.

Since all creatures are equal in the basic fact of being bodies, and the preference of some over others comes only from God, and He is the one on whom all depends, He attached the matter to Himself in His words ﴿He said﴾, meaning the Prophet, not anyone else, emphasizing it because of their denial and honoring the truth before them (p-٤١٨) by repeating the greatest name, ﴿Indeed God﴾, meaning the One to whom all command belongs, so there is no objection to Him, and He knows best what is in the interest of people, ﴿has chosen him﴾.

Al-Ḥarālī said: "Iṣṭifā' (choosing) means taking the best."

Since this implies his having kingship, the verb was followed by ﴿over you﴾. Then He added what God had placed in him that required this, so He said: ﴿And He has increased him﴾, meaning over you, ﴿in breadth of knowledge﴾, by which one attains the capacity to direct and to carry out every matter. This indicates that knowledge is a condition of kingship, and by mentioning it first, it shows that the soul's virtues are nobler than bodily and other qualities, and that kingship is not by inheritance, ﴿and in stature﴾, by which one is enabled to overcome those brave men who challenge him and those rivals who approach him.
