Then He explained what this clause contains, by His saying, rejecting the idea of one who might imagine that something goes outside His command and so is not exclusively His: "Who is it that can intercede (yashfa'u) with Him" [meaning: of what the disbelievers claimed as intercession, and others] "except by His permission" [meaning: by His enabling], [p-32] because no one can oppose Him, and it is clear that everything is in His grip. All of this is evidence of His singularity in divinity.

Al-Harrali said: The reality of intercession (shafa'ah) is a bond between the intercessor and the one for whom intercession is made, owing to a special connection between the intercessor and the one interceded for with Him. So permission within the inner reality of intercession is a portion of the removal of what belongs to the intercessors, so that in reality intercession belongs only to Allah, glorified and exalted, with Allah, glorified and exalted. Thus He, exalted, is in reality the One who interceded with Himself by Himself. By concealing His intercession within the intercession of the intercessors, He was the intercessor at the beginning from behind a veil, since His manifestation is entirely in veil, and His return is without veil. For this reason He, glorified and exalted, is the Seal of the Intercessors, as He says, as is related in the report: "The prophets and messengers interceded, and none remained except the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting." End.

Then He explained all that has passed by His saying: "He knows what is before them" [meaning: whatever is in the two horizons of those whose intercession was claimed, and others] "and what is behind them." Al-Harrali said: That is, what has reached them of His knowledge concerning their own selves and others, since what is before a person is encompassed by his perception, and what he knows is also, as it were, before his heart, encompassed by his knowledge. "And what is behind them" is what their knowledge has not attained, because "behind" is what perception does not reach. He thus informed that His knowledge, from behind their knowledge, encompasses their knowledge, in what they know and what they do not know. End.

Since He had made clear His subjugation of them through His knowledge, He made clear their inability regarding anything of His knowledge except what He bestowed upon them by His forbearance [p-33], so He said: "And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills." This makes clear what preceded, because whoever has all-encompassing knowledge, while no one else knows except what he has made known to them, has complete power. Thus everything is in His grip. He is exalted above any equal and transcendent above every incapacity and ignorance. He is such that no one else can speak except by His permission, because He causes whatever prevents what He does not will.

Then he explained what this sentence contains of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the completeness of His power, by depicting His greatness, the completeness of His knowledge, His majesty and His power in the manner people are accustomed to with their kings: ﴿His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth﴾. The root *k-r-s* revolves around strength, gathering and greatness, and the *kirs* (dung and dried dung, compacted) is derived from this. Al-Asfahani said: the *kursi* is that upon which one sits, and it does not exceed the seat of the one sitting. Al-Harali said: the meaning of *kirs* is gathering, so whatever is more complete in gathering is more deserving of this meaning. It is also used for the step leading up to a throne, on which the one ascending places his foot when he climbs and when he descends, and when he sits firmly, if he wills: a *kursi*. Then he said: the *kursi* contains the forms of all things, just as the sign of it appears in the earth (p. 35), in which all existing things are found. There is no form in the earth except that it has a counterpart in the *kursi*. What is established in the throne is established in its examples in the *kursi*, and what is established in the heavens has its form in the earth. Thus existence is doubled, just as the Qur'an is *mathani* (oft-repeated), both in summary and in detail: in the Qur'an as ink and letters, and in the cosmos as forms. This noble verse therefore gathers the detail of the detailed things and the indeterminacy of the forms of the ink-like things, according to the proportion between the heavens and what is in them. He made the encompassing of the *kursi* a single encompassing when He said: ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, and there were not two encompassings, because the earth is within the heavens, the heavens within the *kursi*, the *kursi* within the throne, and the throne within the air. End of quotation. From this it becomes clear what precedes it, because whoever has this greatness in this firm governance and perfect craftsmanship has this knowledge and this power which nothing burdens. For this reason He said: ﴿and it does not weary Him﴾, that is, burden Him. Al-Harali said: from *al-awd*, meaning reaching the limit of exertion (p. 36), and its counterpart is the letter *ya'* from the word *yad* (hand), meaning power. The original meaning, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that the height of His power does not make Him incapable of it. This is why the linguists explain it with the word "burden." ﴿Their preservation﴾ within His self-subsistence, just as it burdens others, or makes them incapable of preserving what they create. Rather, it is easy for Him, because if it burdened Him, the affairs of both would be disrupted, even slightly, and another would have power, even for a single day, over other than what He wills. Preservation, said al-Harali, is the care of what is by nature falling apart, so its holding together is by the care that keeps it from what weakens or nullifies it. End of quotation. Since His loftiness and greatness are not confined to domination, authority and the perfection of encompassing, which were mentioned before, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And He﴾, that is, despite all of that, the One uniquely described as ﴿the Most High﴾, meaning there is no rank except that it is lower than His rank, ﴿the Most Great﴾, as the opening of the verse with the supreme proper name, which gathers all the meanings of the Most Beautiful Names in loftiness and greatness, indicates, and in which understandings fall short, because of what imaginings dominate them. The arrangement of the two names in this way indicates that by greatness is meant the loftiness of rank and the remoteness of attainment from the comprehension of intellects (p. 37). The verse ends with what it began with, although its beginning with greatness, as al-Harali said, was with the name "Allah" as a hint, and its ending with that is a clear statement of what was mentioned: that the beginning is from behind a veil and the return is without a veil. Likewise the Qur'an was revealed: the start of the address is a hint and its conclusion is a clear statement, so that revelation and the cosmos correspond in the correspondence of the one who stands and the one who is standing in place of him. ﴿Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. And because height carries manifestness, while greatness carries concealment for the place of encompassing, since the great is that which pervades, just as a great body pervades all regions. ﴿And His is the highest description﴾ [al-Rum: 27]. This is when the apparent loftiness is His majesty, to which His great creation bears witness. The Exalted said, in what His Prophet ﷺ reported of Him: "Majesty is My cloak, and greatness is My waist-wrapper." The cloak is what is over the outside, and the waist-wrapper is what covers the inside and the lower part. So in the heavens is His majesty, in the earth is His greatness, in the throne is His loftiness, and in the *kursi* is His greatness. His greatness is most hidden where there is detail, and His majesty and loftiness are most manifest where there is generality and indeterminacy. By this meaning the high rank of this verse becomes clear, in that it has risen over faith as the loftiness of faith rises over disbelief, and because of what it has shown to understandings of His self-subsistence, loftiness, greatness, and the annihilation of everything else such that anything could be attributed to them. For when He, the Exalted, becomes manifest, whatever else is, is annihilated. In the manifestation of this noble, lofty, great verse is the establishment of the religion of Islam, which is the religion of surrender, just as in what preceded in the opening of the surah was the establishment of the religion of the upright (p. 38), for they were only commanded to worship Him sincerely as people of pure faith, to establish prayer and to give zakat. This is why the mention of the religion of Islam occurs in the surah of Al 'Imran, which discloses the meanings of this surah, after His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. End of quotation.

It is known from this explanation that every sentence that is introduced as a new sentence is a reason for what precedes it, and that the last one explains the necessary consequence of all-encompassing knowledge, which is complete power, the proof of whose necessity I established in Ta-Ha. Whoever claims a partner, let him preserve this universe even for one year of years, and let him make known what he will do in that year, so that his statement "And how can he have that, and how?!" holds true.

It has also become clear, through what has been established about His loftiness and greatness, that the one who disbelieves in Him is the wrongdoer, that on the Day when He manifests Himself for judgment there will be no intercession and no friendship, and as for trade, they are in the most preoccupied state concerning it. If by it is meant ransom, it is known that there is no path to it and no way to it.

By these secrets it becomes clear the saying of the Chosen Master ﷺ (p. 39): "This verse is the master of the verses of the Qur'an." This is because it includes the names of the Essence, the Attributes and the Acts, the negation of deficiency and the affirmation of perfection, and it fulfils the proofs of monotheism in the most complete manner, in the most sound order and the most wonderful style, being wholly devoted to that. The excellence of remembrance and knowledge follows what is remembered and known. It contains explicitly the seven attributes: life, knowledge, power, [will], and speech, since permission cannot occur except through speech and will; and hearing and sight follow from "To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth," and from "the Living," because the intended meaning is complete life. The noble names are repeated in it, both explicit and implicit, seventeen times, rather, twenty-one times. No other verse in the Book of Allah contains this collection, and it consists of fifty words, corresponding to the number of the prayers first commanded in that presence, the heaven of the throne and the *kursi* above the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and corresponding to the degree of reward at the end. It is as if it were ladders for the spirit of its reciter to that supreme station, the place to which the angels and the Spirit ascend in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years (p. 40). Perhaps this is the secret of what is established: that no devil comes near the one who recites it at bedtime, because whoever is in the presence of the Most Merciful is exalted above the whisperings of the devil. And Allah the Exalted is the Granter of success.

[And] When the proofs became clear to every scholar and ignorant person alike, religion reached a state in which the fair-minded person, for his own sake, has no need of compulsion in it. So He said: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾. Al-Harrali (d. 638 AH) said: When He, glorified and exalted, moved the level of address from the address of command, prohibition, and legal limits, and what the affairs of this world are built upon, to the religion of the upright (dīn al-qayyima), which hid from them the matter of the greatness and dominion that overpowers the inhabitants of the realm of sovereignty and kingship, in which they are turned about, and raised it to the level of the religion of God, the accepted one, in which there is no confusion, no veil over it, and no crookedness in it. This is His, glorified and exalted, making His servant aware of His self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya), which is manifest in every manifestation, within every manifestation, over every manifestation, and more manifest than every manifestation, and of His hidden greatness, which no name points to and no mark can express, and which is the ink of every ink. He, glorified and exalted, made clear and announced, by placing hidden compulsion in its proper position within the religion of the upright, the aspect in which it compels souls against their dislike concerning what He has prescribed for them, which is the knowledge of their punishment and the sign of their torment. Thus the awareness of God's command in His self-subsistence and greatness removed the soul's aversion (kurh al-nafs), through its witnessing all that flows over it of what is for it and against it. (p. 41) Then those [who have this awareness], God will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, because of what their hearts have perceived of the water of tawhid (monotheism) flowing beneath the various fruits of their actions. Thus its sweet and its bitter both became sweet through that tawhid, as is said of the red sulphur (al-kibrit al-aḥmar, an alchemical substance believed to transmute the essences of base things into the state of the most noble) that it converts the essences of base things into the state of the most exalted. End of quote.

Then He explained the absence of compulsion by His saying: ﴿The right course has become clear from error﴾. Al-Harrali said: Rushd is good management of affairs and steadfastness in them according to what is lasting and enduring, ﴿from error﴾, which is ghayy, bad management of a thing and carrying it out in a way whose consequence is evil. End of quote. That is: every person of intellect now knows that Islam is entirely good and everything else is entirely evil, because of the proofs that have become clear, and he reaches a state in which everyone who wants the benefit of his own soul hastens toward it, and the most tyrannical of tyrants submits before it. So, because of the strength of its manifestation and the dominance of its light, compulsion has been entirely removed from it (p. 42), because compulsion is driving someone toward what the benefit of which has not become apparent. Nothing remains that prevents it except the wicked share of the soul in its bestial and satanic desires. ﴿Whoever﴾, that is, this being the cause, ﴿disbelieves in al-Ṭāghūt﴾, which is the soul itself and whatever it calls to and inclines toward by its base nature. Al-Harrali said: It is what exceeds in transgressing the limit that restrains from ruin; it is an intensive form and an increase in extremity of that from which transgression (ṭughyān) arises. End of quote.

﴿And believes in God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, inclining toward Him with the intellect, which is entirely good, because by its light it saw the decisive evidences and the shining proofs. He persisted in this, as the imperfect form in ﴿disbelieves﴾ and ﴿believes﴾ indicates. ﴿Then he has grasped﴾ with insight ﴿the most trustworthy handhold﴾, that is, the one about which there is no doubt that it is the most secure means for his salvation, by what he has put his hand to, and has submitted to his Lord.

﴿And whoever submits his face to God﴾ [Luqmān: 22]. The 'urwa (handhold) is what is used to tie bundles and the like, by their interlacing one into another, so that part of it cannot be separated from another except by severing its end. If one handhold of it is severed, all of it is severed. The wuthqā is the form fu'lā for intensification, from thiqa (trust), with the intensity of what its weakness is feared. Then He explained its firmness by His saying: ﴿There is no severing for it﴾, that is, no yielding to untying, breaking, or going away. Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said: fasamtu al-shay' means I split the thing; ʿaqda means I untied the knot; and al-shay' ʿanhu means it departed from it. Al-Harrali said: from fasm, which is the coming out of the links from one another. That is, this handhold has no dissolution at all. This is an illustration of what is known by reflection, and an argument from what is observed and perceived, so that the listener conceives of it as if he were looking at it with his own eye, so that his belief in it is firmly established and his contentment with it is complete. From this it is known that no obstacle remains to entering this religion except predestination and decree (al-qaḍāʾ wal-qadar). Whoever has been preceded by happiness, God, glorified and exalted, facilitates for him the means by which He brings him out from darkness into light. Whoever has been overcome by wretchedness, He lets the devils prevail over him, and they bring him out from the light of the natural disposition (fiṭra) into the darknesses of disbelief and confusion.

Since each of the faith and disbelief mentioned earlier is in speech, action, and belief, He said, encouraging the one and warning against abandoning the other: ﴿And God﴾, who possesses the attributes of perfection (p. 44), ﴿is All-Hearing﴾, that is, of what is said that indicates faith, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, that is, of what is done or concealed of disbelief and transgression, and will requite for it. Perhaps in the verse there is a turning (iltifāt) toward what was mentioned at the beginning of the surah about the disbelievers, that it is the same for them whether you warn them or not, and toward the hypocrites and the condemnation of what they are upon, which is in the utmost opposition to that whose proofs have become clearer than the sun. It also indicates permission to turn away from the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 257:

When He had established that, and the context had guided to something which eloquence required to be concealed, as a guidance to keeping far from it and fleeing from it because of its ugliness and the evil of its outcome, namely "and whoever believes in the Taghut (false deities/transgressors) and disbelieves in God, then he has grasped the most secure handhold that has no breaking, and God is Hearing and Knowing" was not the case; rather, the meaning is: whoever believes in the Taghut and disbelieves in God, then no handhold is held for him, and God casts him down into the Blazing Fire. As if it were said: Who then delivers the soul from the darkness of desire, lust, and the whisperings of Satan? So He said, beginning anew: ﴿God﴾, that is, with what He has of greatness and the Most Beautiful Names (p-45) ﴿is the Protector of those who believe﴾, that is, He takes charge of their affairs. For this reason He explained His protection by His saying: ﴿He brings them out of the darkness﴾ [that is, the immaterial (ma'nawiyyah)] — the plural of ẓulmah (darkness), which is that which obscures what is apparent to the senses or to meaning. He used the plural because the paths of misguidance are many, for disbelief has kinds. ﴿into the light﴾, that is, the immaterial light, which is that which makes manifest what is apparent to the senses or to meaning — so said al-Ḥarālī. He used the singular because the Straight Path is one: ﴿And do not follow the (other) ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am: 153]. Among the good interpretations is that the plural refers to what arises from ignorance concerning the faculties about which He reported the sealing, so that the sight becomes bereft of reflection, the hearing empty of understanding and insight, and the heart turned away from contemplation and consideration; and the singular in "light" refers to the soundness of the heart, for it is responsible for bringing every delight and repelling every harm. The light, which is the intellect and the primordial nature (fiṭrah), has one direction, which is the truth, whereas the darkness arising from the self (nafs) has many directions that are in the utmost divergence.

(p-46) When He mentioned His sincere servants, He mentioned the worshippers of desires, and said: ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾, that is, they concealed by their desires what the proofs of reason first and of transmitted texts second indicate; ﴿their protectors are the Taghut﴾ from among their desires and what those desires led to of following every transgressor among the devils and clinging to idols and other than that. Then He explained their domination over them by His saying: ﴿they bring them out﴾, and attributing it to the plural pronoun supports that the plurality of darkness is due to the multiplicity of kinds of disbelief, ﴿from the light﴾, that is, the natural (fiṭrī) light, ﴿into the darkness﴾. Al-Ḥarālī said: In it is an explanation of the equality of all creation in the reality of the first light, toward the spirit disposed to the uniform primordial nature: "Every child is born upon the fiṭrah." End of quotation.

(p-47) When He mentioned the domination of desires over them, the caller to them being recklessness and levity arising from the element of fire, which is a branch of Satan, He explained that their recompense is of the same kind as their deed, and said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, those who dwell in the place of distance and hatred, ﴿are the companions of the Fire﴾. Al-Ḥarālī said: Those who followed it without perceiving, inasmuch as the companion is one who follows his companion. End of quotation. Since their lasting therein was understood from the mention of companionship, He stated it explicitly for emphasis, saying, specifying their exclusive belonging to it: ﴿they therein abide forever﴾, that is, exclusively, for an endless duration. Al-Ḥarālī said: He made eternity a description of them, indicating that they are in it while they are in their worldly life. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 258:

When He (glorified and exalted is He) mentioned His all-encompassing power and greatness, and followed it with the matter of faith and His support of its party, and the matter of disbelief and His abandonment of its people, He began to illustrate this through the story of the one who argued with the Friend (Khalil, Abraham) and the one who passed by the town, recalling the story of those to whom He said, "Die," then brought them to life, all in the context of marvelling at that audacity. Al-Harrali said: Since what Truth had manifested in the verse of His greatness and what was connected to it was specific to His chosen servants, this address was singled out for the Prophet (ﷺ), because the meaning of its purpose is too lofty for anyone other than him. End of quotation. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not considered﴾, that is, know, by what We inform you of (p-48), a knowledge that is with you like direct witnessing, because of your perfect insight and because of the luminous meanings We have deposited in you. Since this arguer was far from correctness and thick in veiling, He indicated his remoteness with the particle of limit (ilá, "to"), saying: ﴿to the one who argued with Abraham﴾, that is, the one who is the father of the Arabs, and they are most worthy of [the people] to follow him, ﴿concerning his Lord﴾. The pronoun may refer to either of the two, that is, concerning what is specific to his Creator, the Nurturer who bestows His kindness upon him, after the clarity of these proofs and the establishment of these demonstrations. This indicates that He (glorified is He) made His command clear on the tongue of every prophet and explained His greatness and His station, even though He had fixed that in all natural dispositions and led them, with the slightest reflection, to the oceans of His majesty. Thus Nimrod, who argued with the Friend, was among those whom the devils brought out from light into darkness (p-49). Since this was a striking and astonishing matter, He explained that its cause was the arrogance which wretched Iblis, saying: ﴿because﴾, that is, for the reason that ﴿Allah had given him﴾, that is, the Supreme King, by the overflow of His grace, ﴿the kingdom﴾, which is transient in the lowly world. He placed in the position of the gratitude that was due from him for that kingdom his argument concerning it and his arrogance, which he claimed over it. He defined him (as one who was given the kingdom) to indicate his perfection in relation to humans, by his rule over all the earth. Al-Harrali said: In its implication is that kingship is a trial and a affliction for the one who is given it. End of quotation. So he became arrogant with what Allah had granted him in it over the servants of Allah, and they obeyed him because of the means Allah had enabled for him, until his foot became firmly fixed in the arrogance that belongs specifically to the Greatest King, Owner of the kingdom and Destroyer of kings, so he wrongly supposed that he was worthy of it.

When He (glorified and exalted is He) informed us of his argument, He explained what it was, as a confirmation of the verse ﴿Then Allah said to them, "Die," then He brought them to life﴾ [al-Baqarah: 243], as evidence of resurrection for a Day in which there is no trade, no friendship, and no intercession. So He said: ﴿when﴾, that is, he argued with him at the time when ﴿Abraham said: "My Lord"﴾, that is, the One who has been good to me by creating me and continuing guidance for me (p-50), ﴿is the One who gives life and causes death﴾, that is, alone. This expression indicates that a previous statement had been made on this subject and that someone had claimed a share in this attribute.

Since it was as if it were said: "This is an evident matter agreed upon, so what is it that the arguer argues about?" he was answered with His saying: ﴿He said﴾, that is, that arguer, with boldness and without reflection, because of what he was accustomed to of people's humiliation before him and their submission to his tyranny: ﴿"I too﴾, that is, also ﴿give life and cause death"﴾, by pardoning whoever deserves execution and executing whoever does not deserve execution.

When Abraham (peace be upon him) saw that he had dared against a great matter, and that his argument about giving life itself might be obscure or prolonged, he resolved to hasten his refutation together with an explanation of his baseness by something clearer than that. In this there is an indication that he was far below what he claimed by several degrees, because giving life is the outpouring of spirit upon a form after its existence from non-existence, by (p-51) ﴿Abraham said﴾. Al-Harrali said: Since it is part of good argumentation to abandon contention by following up an obscuring proof, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an apparent argument﴾ [al-Kahf: 22], he transferred the arguer from the proof that is within souls to the proof that is in the horizons, by its greatest luminary, the sun. ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [Fussilat: 53]. So in the apparent meaning of the argument there is a shift, but within it (the text reads "in its folds") there is a confirmation of the first, because the spirit is the sun of the body. It is thus as if a parable were struck: giving life is nothing but bringing the sun of the spirit back from the place where it set, so it was in its apparent sense and in its facing a decisive proof, while its inner sense completes the first proof. End of quotation. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then indeed﴾, with the fa' that links the two statements, indicating that the first proof is completed by the second. End of quotation. That is: this follows from your claim, or I say to you: indeed ﴿Allah﴾, with the greatness and majesty He possesses, by combining all attributes of perfection, ﴿brings the sun﴾, that is, He who brought it into being ﴿from the east﴾, that is, every day, from before you existed, by ages ﴿so bring it﴾, you, ﴿from the west﴾, even for one day.

(p-52) Al-Harrali said: To show that the return of the whole world is to one, and that the one who sustains human beings in giving life and causing death is the one who sustains the horizons in the rising and setting of the sun. In its implication there is an indication that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, must bring the sun from the west, so that in this there is a manifestation of His control over it, where He wills, so that He causes it to rise from where it set, just as He brings the spirit out from where it was taken, so that the rising of the sun from its west becomes a sign of the approach of the Hour and the rising of spirits from their bodies. End of quotation.

﴿So he was confounded﴾. Al-Harrali said: From bahth (confusion, astonishment), which is the thing remaining in its state and form without changing from it, because of a matter that overwhelms it with its impact. That is: as a result of that, he was confounded. ﴿The one who disbelieved﴾, that is, disbelief came about for him through that claim, to which his denial of the exclusive power of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, over that bound him, and his claim of partnership for himself. So the Friend (peace be upon him) explained to him, [by this example], that he is incapable of transforming a form which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had fashioned and placed in one direction [to] a direction other than that. How then could he bring a form into being from non-existence? How then could he (bring it) then? How then (could he bring) the outpouring of spirit upon it? How then (could he bring) a sensitive spirit? How then a rational spirit! More on this matter will come in surah al-Shu'ara'. How exalted are the stations of the prophets! How pure are their insights! How lofty are their ranks and how pure are their elements! Upon them all from me are the greatest blessings and peace, and the highest (p-53) greetings and honour. Al-Harrali said: So He defined him, that is, in His saying "disbelieved", by the attribute from the aspect through which confusion entered upon him from it. End of quotation. That is: because he concealed what he knew of his own incapacity and the power of his Creator, so Allah, glorified and exalted is He, through the tongue of His Friend (ﷺ), uncovered the veil that he had let down, with a clear uncovering, and tore it with a great exposition, a disgracing tearing.

Since the implication was: because he did wrong in his claim and in the respect in which he claimed it, through the killing of the innocent and the sparing of the audacious, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One with whom no one's command exists, ﴿does not guide the people﴾, that is, those to whom He gave the strength to resist matters, ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, in general, because they place things, by His will and decree, in other than their proper places. For He darkened their hearts and made them darker than the pitch-black night, so He left them no firm ground to hold to. So where is guidance for them, when they have become many stages away from the abodes of the people of care? The restriction of the act of guiding is to convey generality. Al-Imam said: He abbreviated the expression to convey an increase in meaning, and this is one of the subtle features of the Qur'an.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on Surah 2, Verse 259:**

Since giving life and causing death are among the most manifest signs of divine lordship and the most specific to it, God, glorified and exalted, displayed His jealousy over them. He did so at times by refuting the one who claims a share in them, at times by making the one who finds it far-fetched, in himself and in others, witness the deed of his Lord, and at times by making the one seeking guidance witness it through himself. In each case He expressed what the speaker's state required and what his question indicated. He used *ilā* (إلى, "to") regarding the unbeliever, indicating that he was in a place distant from the addressee (ﷺ). Regarding the one who was astonished, He dropped it, thereby dropping that distance. Regarding the seeker of guidance who inquires, He used *idh* (إذ, "when"), as is the constant practice among people of purity, love and fidelity. Thus He followed the expression of wonder at the state of the disputant with wonder also at the state of the one who magnified God's giving life to that town.

Since the meaning of ﴿Have you not considered﴾ [2:258] is "Have you seen?", because *hal* (هَلْ, the interrogative particle), as al-Radi and others mention, is specific in that it conveys the sense of negation, so that *illā* (إلّا, "except") may follow it for affirmation, as in His saying ﴿Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?﴾ [55:60] and His saying ﴿Is this anything but a human like you?﴾ [21:3], it was as if it were said: "Have you seen the one who argued with Abraham?" or "﴿or﴾ have you seen ﴿like the one who﴾?" It is also possible that the estimate is: "Because the reports of the earlier peoples are only admonitions for us: is your people like this disputant in their greatest refusal? For they say that the giving of life is not in its true sense of resurrection after death." Or the estimate is: "or they are like the one who ﴿passed by﴾." Al-Harrali said: "[From *al-murūr*, passing by], which is placing a thing on a path toward another, while turning toward it along its course." ﴿Upon a town﴾, which is the one from which thousands went out, or Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿And it was in ruins﴾, i.e. collapsed, its walls fallen. ﴿Upon its roofs﴾, i.e. its ceilings, or empty while its ceilings remained standing. Al-Harrali said: "From *khawā*, which is the emptiness of a thing from what should sustain it, sensibly or in meaning. *ʿUrūsh* is the plural of *ʿarsh*, from the sense of *ʿarīsh*, which is a structure erected in haste, that repels the heat and cold but does not protect fully, unlike a solid building. Thus the solid building is in reality an *ʿarīsh*, given the frailty of the world in its entirety in the eye of insight." End.

Since it was as if it were said, "What in his state is astonishing?", it was said: ﴿He said: How will God bring this to life﴾, i.e. the town, ﴿God﴾, i.e. the One to whom all command belongs, ﴿after its death﴾, i.e. after its ruin and the departure of its people, so that He restores it to what it had been, populated and inhabited. Al-Harrali said: "In the word *annā* (أنّى) is included the meanings of *kayfa* (how), *ḥaythu* (where) and *matā* (when). His denial was of the revival in its manner, place and time. The source of this denial is only that the soul burdens itself by seeking to know the modality of what its knowledge cannot reach." End.

Since this one who finds it far-fetched fell short of the rank of the Friend (al-Khalīl), upon him be prayers and peace, in readiness for tranquility, and since his certainty about the manner depended, in wisdom, on leaving him in the unseen realm for the period appointed for his remaining dead, so that this would be like leavening in clay and his soul would be prepared to know it and be certain of it, He said: ﴿So He caused him to die﴾, i.e. it thus resulted that God caused him to die, ﴿God﴾, i.e. the One who has no equal, so that whatever He willed was [for his certainty in knowing that, a care from God for him]. ﴿A hundred﴾. Since the intended meaning is that the period of his death was long, so that he would have decayed during it, making resurrection more possible in terms of power, regarding what the Arabs find far-fetched, and that this time was good and pleasant for accepting revival and resettlement, He expressed it with a word denoting abundance, so He said: ﴿years﴾, until his donkey had decayed while his food and drink were preserved from change. This realized the perfection of power by preserving what is subject to change, changing what is subject to permanence, and restoring what had perished.

Al-Harrali said: "He specified a hundred because it is complete in the threefold counting of units and tens, and its tenth is the odd of the even, because what is complete at the third makes what exceeds it a repetition for which three suffices. ﴿Then He raised him﴾, in its explanation, indicates that his body had not changed or decayed as his donkey had, since it had not been ... [then He roused him]. And God knows best, as He said: ﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him﴾ [80:22]." End.

Since it was known that this action was for the sake of his certainty in God's power, the soul yearned to know what happened to him after the resurrection, so it was answered with His saying, alerting him and every listener to what is wondrous in his story: ﴿He said﴾, i.e. God said to him, or whoever He wills of those whose address arises from Him: ﴿How long did you remain?﴾, i.e. in this sleep of yours. ﴿He said﴾, looking at the soundness of his food and drink: ﴿I remained a day﴾. Then his assumption changed according to the sun or something else, so he said: ﴿or part of a day﴾. It seems he hastened with this answer, as is human habit, before looking at his donkey. ﴿He said﴾, i.e. the One who addressed him, turning away from his answer as a clarification that it is a manifest error: ﴿Rather you remained a hundred years﴾, expressing the year with a word that revolves around the meanings of abundance, extension and length, [and guiding him] to that and to the perfection of power by His saying: ﴿Look at your food and drink﴾, i.e. which was with you when you slept, and it is among the swiftest things to spoil: figs and grape juice. ﴿Not gone stale﴾, from *sanah* (year), i.e. not changed by the passing of years over their long course and the strength of their turnings and effects. The meaning of the reading with *hāʾ al-sakt* (هاء السكت, the pausal *hāʾ*, added at a pause) is that the report of this is a decisive command, convincing, with no doubt or hesitation at all. ﴿And look at your donkey﴾, bleached and crumbled bones. Thus God, glorified and exalted, combined the two signs: the moist in its preservation and the dry in its disintegration.

Since the estimate was: "We did that so as to make it a sign for you of complete power, or so that you would know Our power," He joined to it His saying: ﴿and that We may make you a sign for the people﴾, i.e. in the totality of your report, ﴿for the people﴾, i.e. all of them. So His command was a sign of persistence and affirmation in the present world, regarding what will be in the matter of the Hereafter: the Hour, resurrection and rising, as al-Harrali said.

Since He commanded him to look at what He had made a sign for him of his remaining that long time, He commanded him to look at what He had made a sign for him of His power to give life however He wills, so He said: ﴿And look at the bones﴾, i.e. of your donkey. They are the plural of *ʿaẓm* (bone), which is the pillar of the body on which its form is sustained, ﴿how We raise them﴾. Al-Harrali said: "With the *rāʾ*, from *nashr* (spreading out), which is the return of the perishable to its former form. With a *ḍamma*, it is making and transforming toward it. With the *zāy*, from *nashz* (elevation), which is manifesting and raising a thing, from the rising ground that rises up and appears." End. Some of them are joined to others as they were, arranging all of that. ﴿Then We clothe them with flesh﴾. Al-Harrali said: "He made his revival a resurrection and the donkey's life a rising, and He showed him the spreading out and the flesh that was laid upon the bones until they became one form, so that the matter of the Hour would be clear to sight, making it a proof against the unbeliever and the one who finds it far-fetched." ﴿So when it became clear to him﴾, i.e. this extraordinary, dazzling matter indicating what He described Himself with, may He be exalted, in the verse of the Throne. Al-Harrali said: "In the form *tafaʿʿala* (تَفَعَّلَ) there is an indication of his wavering in looking between the two signs until what he had been informed of became firmly settled in him and what he had estimated dissolved." ﴿He said: I know﴾, in the verbal form, based on himself, and in the imperative form (*iʿlam*, "know"), for the benefit of others, what he knew, so that both readings show that he knew and was taught, because knowledge is only complete when it reaches one who does not know [thus combining the excellence of knowing and of teaching]. End. It is permissible that the present-tense expression *aʿlamu* (أعلم, "I know") indicates that he has always been characterized by this knowledge, without reference to a state or to the future. This would also be an excuse for his using in the expression of wonder a phrase that indicates far-fetchedness: he said it only as finding it far-fetched that power should be linked to that, not as a claim of power over it. ﴿That God﴾, i.e. because of what I know of His greatness, ﴿is over all things﴾, i.e. of this and of other things, ﴿All-Powerful﴾.

Al-Harrali said: "In its indication is the binding of insights to witness God's power, glorified and exalted, in its determination within the wise causes through which sights are bound. It attaches what lies below the sign of giving life and causing death to its command, so that in knowledge it is equal that the One who gives you life is the One who turns you. Just as your life is by His power, so too your action is by His power. Thus the detailed assignment of power to God is consistent with what preceded of the display of preservation by God and of greatness for God. They are as comprehensive and detailed, all demanding that God's command, glorified and exalted, encompasses the totality of what was summarized and the minutiae of what was detailed." End.

In the verse there is an explanation of the way the unbeliever deceived those of his people who made light of him in the disputation with the Friend, upon him be the blessings and peace of God: that the giving of life by which the king deserves divinity is this real giving of life, not merely releasing one who deserved execution.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 260 (part 1 of 2):

Since faith in the Resurrection, and indeed certainty about it, is among the great aims of this surah, and it has reached this context, which serves to firm up the pillars of the power to revive, despite the divergence of methods and the variety of paths, He first made clear, by refuting the disbeliever, what necessitates faith, and by calling the one who marvels to witness, what seals certainty. He rose above that explanation to the story of the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and then to what establishes tranquility. Glorified and exalted is He, He has established the matter of the Resurrection in this surah, after the Opening (al-Fatihah) had alluded to it with "the Day of Judgment," in the best of establishments. He scattered its stars throughout its skies of verses, and dispersed its traces across its regions, among its proofs and clear signs, in the manner of the Wise One who delivers what He wills gradually, neither hastily nor negligently. So Glorified and Exalted is He repeated its mention, sometimes with the Hereafter, sometimes with reviving, sometimes in this world and sometimes in the Hereafter, as in His words:

﴿And in the Hereafter they are certain.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 4] ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28] ﴿Then We revived you after your death.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 56] ﴿Thus Allah gives life to the dead.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 73] ﴿Allah said to them, "Die," then He revived them.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 243] and what resembles these, their parallels and forms, in those modes which are generally intended for their own sake and for something else. Thus the souls of those who deny it became familiar with it, and they became prepared to hear the argument for it, until He brought to them the matter of His Friend, upon whom be blessings, peace, greetings and honor. It was as if it were said: O you who deny the Resurrection, who express wonder at it, and who follow your fathers in its matter by reports most of which are false! Listen to the story of your father Ibrahim (ﷺ), in which the argument for the Resurrection, the gathering of the scattered, and the restoration of life was delivered to you, by the testimony of one who is not accused, namely the Qur'an, which has rendered you unable to produce anything like it. So its testimony is the testimony of Allah, so that you may attain from it knowledge of certainty, indeed the very eye of certainty. Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿And when﴾ connecting to what is like "remember," what was recited to you of the matter of the Resurrection, and "remember the story of your father Ibrahim," in what the word "when" indicates.

Al-Harrali said: Since the matter of the one who sent down the Qur'an was to establish the religion with its written text and limits, He, Exalted, brought it to its end, then arranged by it what He arranged of its outward aspect in the Verse of the Throne, and ordered upon that the religion of Islam, which is a casting, like the casting of the hand at death. By it He gathered the matter of the return, in which the servants have no role. So Glorified and Exalted is He arranged the mention of the Return in three states: the state of the denier, whose end reached [utter denial], then the state of the one who considers it far-fetched, whose end reached [knowledge and faith], and He brought the address to the state of the believer, whose state reached certainty, tranquility, and the vision of the dominion within the dominion of the earth. End of quote. So He, Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim said﴾. The arrangement and expression in these three verses have attained the furthest limit of beauty. For it began with one who wished to conceal what the proofs had made clear about the matter of God in reviving, by claiming for himself a share in reviving through a metaphorical sense, deceiving with a word that points to his distance, his being cursed, and his expulsion. Then it [moved] to the one who considered the reviving of the town far-fetched, and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, showed him the real manner of reviving as a sign for him and as a completion of the reply to that, while turning toward him with direct address and the pleasure of gentleness. Then [it moved] to the one who asked Allah, Exalted, for the honor of being shown how He gives life, so he was firmly established, then [his certainty] was confirmed, then it was strengthened. The correspondence among the three is that they concern reviving bodies by spirits [p-63], corresponding to what came before it, which concerns reviving spirits by the secrets of righteousness, which is a most sublime correspondence. So the purpose is to warn against the state of the first, and to urge ascent from the level of the second to the station of the third, whose reality is truthfulness in faith, in hope of attaining what he was honored with. For this reason He expressed in his story with the words "and when," and did not place it in the manner of wonder as with the first. ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, O You who have been good to me, ﴿show me how You give life to the dead.﴾ Al-Harrali said: He asked for what He is worthy of, by what He, Exalted, said:

﴿And thus We showed Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ [al-An'am: 75] And from the dominion of the earth is the reviving. So He, Glorified and Exalted, confirmed him in establishing the beginning of his state from the firmness of faith. He said, beginning anew: ﴿He said﴾. Since the implied sense is: "Do you not know that I am able to revive, because I am able over all things?", He joined to it His words: ﴿Do you not believe?﴾ for faith comprises all of that. ﴿He said, "Yes."﴾ Thus it became clear that his request for the manner of reviving was not from any remnant of wavering in faith. In this there is an indication that most of those who seek the "how" in matters seek it out of weakness in their faith. And whoever seeks it for the firming of faith, when the signs short of the "how" were sufficient for him, does not benefit from the sign for his faith, because its sufficiency lies in what is below it, and he has not been raised to certainty, since his faith lacks the full measure of its limit. So when faith is complete, by the judgment of its signs that are in the existing wisdom of Allah in [p-64] this world, its clear proofs, the vision of the dominion of the witnessed world attains the rank of certainty, as the seekers of unveiling among the truthful found by experience in the matter of Allah, since it bequeathed to them certainty. Whenever a weak believer shares with them in something of the vision of unveiling or the miracles, he seeks an interpretation for it, and it may become a trial for him that diminishes him from whatever share of faith he had, until perhaps hypocrisy infiltrates him, from which he cannot be free unless Allah rescues him. For this reason, Exalted is He, displayed the address of confirming His Friend, upon whom be blessings, to establish faith, so that the ascent from it to the rank of certainty would be sound. This is like what preceded in the absolute words of His, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. It was mentioned about the Friend, upon whom be blessings and peace, that he looked at the body of an animal that was scattered among the sea creatures, the land creatures, and the birds of the air, and he marvelled at it and said: O Lord! I know You will gather them, so show me how You revive them, that I may witness that. For the certainty of direct witnessing is built upon the establishment of faith. ﴿But﴾ I want the witnessing ﴿so that my heart may be at rest﴾, from [tuma'nina] tranquility, which is calm and stillness, upon the soundness of creation and the balance of disposition. ﴿my heart﴾: whoever is created to attain a thing is disposed to yearn for it. So when Ibrahim, upon whom be blessings and peace, was prepared [p-65] to receive tranquility, the seeking of it was cast into his heart, and Allah answered him with what He had prepared for him. Glorified and Exalted is He set forth for him a parable that He showed him, making it the course of witnessing, clear in certainty. This is because Allah, Glorified is He, is the One who is not counted and not limited, and it was among the descent of His manifestation to His servants that He is the one God, and the One is free of counting. So the first appearance of creation was the first appearance of counting, and the first of counting is two. ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49]. Two is a count, for the creation of each of the two is one, so He made two, each of which is two, so that duality is in it as a whole and as a part, and it becomes a pair from a pair. That count was four. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, made it a root for His creatures, so their total became His odd number. He made the sustenances from four ﴿and He determined in it its sustenances in four days﴾ [Fussilat: 10]. He made the elements from which He created the forms of creatures four. He made the regions four, He made the lifespans four, and the Prayer and peace of Allah be upon him said: "The best of companions are four, the best of expeditions are forty, the best of detachments are four hundred, and the best of armies are four thousand." The quadrupled things in the origins of creation are many; the scholars traced them and the wise came to know them. ﴿He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2], the verse. And since the creation of Adam and all created things was from the ink of the elements, which are water, earth, air and fire, from which He fashioned the forms, ﴿and He fashioned you and perfected your forms﴾ [al-Taghabun: 3]. Then Glorified and Exalted He displayed His subjugation by causing death and the annihilation of their forms: "Every son of Adam is consumed by the earth except the coccyx; from it he was created and in it he will be reassembled." So He scattered them in four directions: east, west, north and south. He showed His Friend, upon whom be blessings and peace, how He calls His creation from the four horizons of His regions after their dispersal and mixing, and the reassembling of their parts in other than their former arrangement. It is said that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, struck a clay vessel with his hand and said: How much of it is a smooth cheek and a kohl-lined eye! ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them﴾ [Qaf: 4]. So Exalted is He showed His Friend, upon whom be blessings and peace, an example from the totality of that. ﴿He said, "Then take"﴾ with the particle "fa" confirming his statement, affirming what was established in his faith, and showing that he deserves certainty and tranquility through the firm establishment of his faith. ﴿four birds﴾: it is a collective noun derived from the meaning of that from which flying comes, which is lightness after the weight of what is not by nature meant to rise in the air. He, Exalted, made the example from birds because the elements gathered in bodies are birds that fly to their nests and their centers, which Allah, Exalted, appointed for them as a making in them, not as an obligatory nature from them. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Wise who made wisdom. So whoever makes Him witnessed in wisdom and witnesses that He is its maker, he is its wise one; and whoever witnesses worldly wisdom but does not witness that He is its maker, he is ignorant of it. So wisdom is witnessing wisdom as made by Allah, every quiddity made to have a form, every meaning made to have a sense, every reality made real. So nature and what is in it is a making from Allah; whoever ignores it deviates, and whoever realizes it sets a limit. Likewise the intelligible and what is in it is an illumination from Allah and a showing of the command of Allah. Whoever binds himself to it and believes in it does not cease to attribute limits to nature, and he needs a refuge from the trials of interpretation in the unseen of the Law. Everything other than the Truth is posited, given a portion and a limit, attaining what it has been given and unable to reach beyond it. The intellects have a limit where they stop and do not pass. Therefore He, Exalted, made them birds which the cage of form and the completeness of proportion subdue, and their cohesion is shown by the breathing of the spirit. End of quote. And His words, Glorified and Exalted:

﴿So incline them to you﴾, that is, gather them to you, ﴿so that you may know their forms﴾, so that this may be more firm regarding their matter. Al-Harrali said: It is from [al-sawr], which is winning hearts by kindness until the one who is inclined leans and turns toward the one who wins him. Its implication indicates, and Allah knows best, that Ibrahim, upon whom be blessings and peace, raised them and nourished them until they knew him, so that this would be an example of what belongs to Allah, Glorified and Exalted, in His creation, of raising them by creating them and providing for them, until they knew Him by what they needed. They found Him to be a knowledge of their inability to attain Him, not a knowledge of attaining Him. So whenever He called them from the horizons of the regions, they answered Him in the manner of these birds answering His Friend, [with a] small share of His raising them. And if these four are responsive to the Friend, upon whom be peace, with this small share of forms and inclination, how then will the response of the whole be to the Majestic, the Mighty, the Wise! Exalted is He said: ﴿Then place﴾, connected with the particle of delay, going beyond their raising, from their slaughter, their dismemberment and their mixing, until they became one flesh in which no part of the forms that have departed can be distinguished, just as creatures become dust when they die and scatter, one earthen form, so that the likeness and the thing likened correspond in complete correspondence, and beyond that there is a passing of lesson and reflection. ﴿upon every mountain﴾ of the mountains near to you, ﴿a portion of them﴾. A portion is a part of a whole that resembles it, like a piece of gold or the like. So He made the mountains like the regions, and they are, by their height, more visible for sight and further from confusion.

(p-69) ﴿It will be but a single blast, and behold, they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Yasin: 53]. ﴿It will be but a single cry﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 13], ﴿and behold, they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 14]. What was done with the Cry and the Cry-like call (zajra) in the case of the one being resurrected (al-mamthul) was done with the summons (al-du'a') in the case of the likeness (al-mithl), just as what was done with creation and provision in the case of the one being resurrected was done with the sur (the Trumpet) in the case of the likeness. He made it a part, in that its parts resemble one another. ﴿Then call them, and they will come to you running﴾. Sa'y is running and purposeful hastening, which occurs in the sensible realm. The meaning of the bird coming as a bird is a share of its majesty, and the meaning of its coming running is a share of its humility. For this reason he summoned them to himself running, in the state of one who humbles himself, seeking provision and security, from the hand from which he was accustomed to receive provision and from the side from which he was familiar with security. Thus the likeness matched the resurrected form, and its goal was the sight of the eye, so he became certain and at rest. This is no more marvelous than the stones walking at one time and the trees and their branches at another, to serve his chosen son (ﷺ). "And likewise the reattaching of the hand of Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra' after it had been cut off, and he came carrying it, as is mentioned in the biographies (al-siyar) in the expedition of Badr, so it became like its sister," among other things of this kind. Moreover, he (ﷺ) had the raising of the dead, which I will mention in Al 'Imran. And for the individual members of his community there was of this what al-Bayhaqi mentioned in the Dala'il (Dala'il al-Nubuwwah), a large number. But such things did not multiply at his hand (ﷺ) because he was sent to a people who did not acknowledge the resurrection, and the seat of faith is belief in the unseen. Had such occurrences multiplied for him (ﷺ), (p-70) the veil would have been lifted, and once the veil is lifted, those who refuse faith would be hastened with punishment, while he is the Prophet of mercy (ﷺ). As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, he was among a people who believed in the Hereafter, so his doing this was to display the miracle in a form higher than what they could reach through medicine. Moreover, there is no difference, in displaying the supernatural, between one instance and many. And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the one who grants success.

When He, glory be to Him and exalted, showed him the malakut (the unseen dominion) of the earth, that vision became a sign of the might of Allah beyond the malakut, in the station of the jabarut (the realm of absolute sovereignty). So He said: ﴿And know that Allah﴾, i.e., the one who encompasses all by knowledge and power, ﴿is Mighty﴾. Since might has an overpowering force before which the natures of the originators cannot stand, Allah, exalted is He, brought the address down to the place of His wisdom, so He said: ﴿Wise﴾. In this there is an indication that He, glory be to Him and exalted, made some things come into being from others, and made some move toward others with intent, [and made some of that group return] ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth once more﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55]. And this [is the] wisdom indicated by His name the Wise: a malakutic wisdom that joins the connection between the wisdom of this world and the wisdom of the Hereafter. For the truly wise is not one whom Allah has taught the wisdom of this world while making him confused about its being attributed to Him; rather, that person is ignorant of it, as was previously explained. The wise one is rather the one whom Allah has made witness to the wisdom of this world: the earth, the spheres, the stars, the horizons, births and reproduction, and whom He has made witness that He is its wise one. He blended for him the knowledge of the wisdom of the existence of this world with the knowledge of the wisdom of the existence of the Hereafter, and showed him how the two wisdoms interlock, some within others, and the outcome of some returning to others, until he witnesses the revolving of things, within the wisdom of the matter of the Hereafter, which is the unseen of this world, toward the visible wisdom of this world, and then toward the visible wisdom of the Hereafter, thus returning to the beginning and beginning from the return, in the manifestation of the unseen of origination toward its visible form and in the return of its visible form to its unseen. ﴿They will say: Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice﴾ [Ghafir: 11]. Thus it continues to the greatest human return: ﴿On the Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾ [al-Taghabun: 9]. This is the Wise One in the middle station of wisdom. Beyond that there is another matter from above the command of Allah, in His most exalted manifestations through names and attributes, which exalts itself and magnifies itself for the believers, blesses itself, and makes itself manifest to the certain, the monotheists. So to Him, glory be to Him and exalted, belongs might in His creation and command, and to Him belongs wisdom in His creation and command, and behind these is His word, whose detailed wisdoms never run out: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾ [al-Kahf: 109]. And His words cannot be limited or counted, (p-72) ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea [were ink]...﴾ [Luqman: 27]. So He is the Mighty, the Wise, the Exalted, the Great. End of quotation. It is higher than precious jewels.

By this it has become clear that the aim of the Friend (al-Khalil), upon him be the best of prayers and peace, was to move from ilm al-yaqin (knowledge of certainty) to 'ayn al-yaqin (eye-witnessing certainty), indeed to haqq al-yaqin (truth of certainty). It is as if he regarded the lower degree of tranquility as nothing in comparison with the higher. It has been said: rather, his intent in asking was the vision of the Giver of Life, but he sought it allusively, so he was answered with a refusal of it through the attribute of might, allusively. As for Musa, peace be upon him, when he asked explicitly, he was answered explicitly. The question of the Friend, peace be upon him, was not out of doubt. The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "We have more right to doubt than Ibrahim," points to this, because he (ﷺ) did not doubt, and if doubt is negated from the one with the greater right, it is negated from others all the more. And even if we grant it, the meaning is that he did what the doubter does, using the name of the cause for the effect in a general sense. As for doubt itself, the Qur'an has negated it of him (ﷺ) explicitly with his saying "Yes" (bala), and allusively by this verse coming right after the verse of his argument with the one who was confounded. It is reported (p-73) that Shaykh Ahmad, brother of Hujjat al-Islam al-Ghazali, was asked: which is higher, the Ibrahimic station in asking for tranquility, or the exalted station of the one who said: "If the veil were lifted, I would not increase in certainty"? He said: the Ibrahimic station, because of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

(p-74) When the answer to the question about the King, before whom no intercession avails without His permission, nor friendship nor anything else, and what follows from that, had been completed, until He concluded with the story of the birds that inclined to the Intimate Friend (al-Khalil, Abraham) through being fed and treated kindly, He turned the discourse back to the command to spend before that Day on which intermediaries avail nothing except in the manner He has prescribed. This followed His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan, so that He may multiply it for him?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245]. This was by looking back to the beginning of the surah, as a reminder of the attributes of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), urging them to it. So He struck for this purpose clear parables for its multiplication, and the general command to it was included within it, as the absolute is included within the restricted. Its allusion, which is among the things referred to, is by way of wisdom with modesty. He declared that the spending commanded is among the treasures of that Day, on which nothing avails except what He has prescribed, and it is of the sublime might. He framed it in a way that includes the reviving of the dead, which is the most fitting of things (p-74) to what precedes it of the raising of the dead. Thus it is an allusion to establishing the resurrection by a perceptible matter, and that is of the subtle wisdom. It is as if He, glorified and exalted, were saying: My Intimate Friend, upon him be prayers and peace, when he was among the firmly rooted in the rank of faith, I qualified him to mount a degree higher than the degree of certainty, by breaking the customary order in lifting the veils at his hand, concerning the reviving of birds. And I established a pattern of that for the general creation, folded within the reviving of plants in a customary manner. Whoever takes lesson from it sees, and whoever is blind to it has his state reversed and turns away.

So He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿The parable of﴾. It was as if it were said: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245] and ﴿O you who believe, spend﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254]. Its parable is that of ﴿those who spend﴾, that is, who give ﴿their wealth﴾ with a contented heart ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿like a grain﴾ of what the farmer sowed, the likeness of what they spend. Al-Harrali said: Of grain, which is the completed plant, reaching the state of being fit to be food for the human being, who is the most complete of creation. The grain is more perfect as food than the fruit is as a condiment. ﴿That has grown﴾, that is, by what Allah, glorified and exalted, placed in it of the power to grow, through the goodness of its soil and the moderation of its watering. ﴿Seven spikes﴾, by which seven branches sprout from it, each branch bearing one ear (sunbulah). It is from al-sunbul. Al-Harrali said: It is the gathering place of the grain in its husks, as if it were a sign of the worthiness of the gathering of the people of that provision in their cooperating in their affairs, and an indication that the grain is gathered together and not by its unity alone. ﴿In every ear a hundred grains﴾, so the grain became seven hundred grains through Allah's multiplying it. Al-Harrali said: He struck the parable for spending in the way of Allah, and mentioned the seven because of what it contains of completeness through tillage, which is the alchemy of His servants, witnessed in its fruiting, where the grain becomes a root, the root produces ears, and in each ear there are numbers of grains. So what He mentioned, exalted is He, is the first of spending in the way of Allah. He mentioned the seven because of what it contains of completeness and of what it admits of increase. For what grows more than seven, when increase is intended, is indicated by the seven, since the Arabs use it to multiply whatever is less or more than it. So He made the least of spending in the way of Allah seven hundredfold. Then Allah, exalted is He, opened the door of multiplication beyond what counting can reach. End of quotation. The verse therefore employs al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one element is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, each omission being indicated by the mention of the other). Its estimated sense is: the parable of those who spend and their spending is like the parable of a grain and its sower. The mention of the spender first is evidence of the omission of the sower second, and the mention of the grain second is evidence of the omission of the spending first.

(p-76) Since the estimated sense was: just as Allah, glorified and exalted, multiplied the grain for the sower, so He multiplies the spending for the spender, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾, by what He has of the vastness of power and every beautiful attribute. ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, by what He has of perfection in every attribute, ﴿is All-Encompassing﴾, not limited in any of His attributes from which His acts proceed, ﴿All-Knowing﴾. So He multiplies for the people of spending according to the measure of what He knows of their intentions. Since He concluded the first of the verses of these parables with these two attributes, He concluded the last of them with the same, as an indication that His vastness has encompassed all existing things, so He is worthy of reward in both abodes, and that His knowledge has included every object of knowledge, so He does not fear that He will neglect any deed.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 2, verse 262:

Since a person may cultivate for others what is meant to be theirs, He explained that this (wealth) belongs to them on a condition, so He said: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾. Al-Harrali (al-Ḥarrālī) said: [wa] since spending for the sake of the caliphate (khilafah) has a special place in the soul, in ways that reduce the multiplication (of reward) or nullify it, like what befalls the field that was used as the example, whose growth is diminished or uprooted, He (Exalted is He) drew attention to what nullifies it. End of quote. So He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, said: ﴿who spend﴾, and He encouraged them to improve it and warned them against corrupting it by attributing it to them, saying: ﴿their wealth﴾. He urged sincerity in His words: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong the Most Beautiful Names.

Since the soul is inclined to mention its own merit, and it is very unlikely that it would give this up, He drew attention to this with the particle of distance (thumma), to inform (the reader) of the greatness of its merit. So He said: ﴿Then they do not follow what they have spent﴾ with that which they strive against their own selves, ﴿with reminders (mann)﴾. Al-Harrali said: this is mentioning it to the one to whom one has given, so it cuts off the connection (of kindness) with overlooking him, because the original meaning of mann is cutting. ﴿Nor (with) injury (adha)﴾, which is mentioning it to others so as to hurt them, by exalting oneself over them through one's giving. End of quote. Likewise is saying to someone who shared in a good deed: "If I had not been present, it would not have been completed." The repetition of ﴿nor﴾ is a reminder that the absence of each of these two is a condition for obtaining the reward. ﴿For them﴾: He did not link it with the particle of consequence (fa), to inform that it is, from the outset, a gift from Allah, glorifying its magnitude and magnifying its status, since He did not make it a result of their spending. ﴿Their reward﴾, that is, the one He mentioned regarding the multiplication (of reward). This indicates that if it is accompanied by what is forbidden, it will not be for them. Then He increased them in eagerness by His words: ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to them by nurturing them, who takes what is accepted of their expenditures and preserves and increases it until it reaches a magnitude beyond description. ﴿No fear shall be upon them﴾ of any loss befalling them, ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾ over anything lost, because their Lord, glory be to Him and exalted is He, has not left out any of the bounty fitting for them without delivering it to them.

(p-78) When he had made clear this, namely the expenditure that is not conditioned by a stipulation, the soul yearned to understand the reality of the matter, so he stated it explicitly in His words: ﴿Kind speech﴾. Al-Harrali said: it is that which does not wound the heart of the one who asks, according to his state and the state of the speaker. Since the petitioner may insist and become angry at refusal, even when the refusal is in kind words, and thus anger the one asked, He said: ﴿and forgiveness﴾ toward the petitioner if he angers the one who refused him, ﴿is better than charity﴾, which is the act through which the truthfulness of faith in the unseen becomes apparent, since provision is unseen; the one who is certain spends, affirming belief in the replacement [declaring the greatness of its virtue], ﴿followed by injury﴾ through reproach or otherwise, because then he has combined a benefit with a harm, and perhaps the reward of the benefit does not outweigh the punishment of the harm. ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, while the situation is that the King, than whom none is greater, ﴿is Rich﴾, so He does not accept what He has not permitted. Since He instilled fear in the giver through the attribute of being Rich, He encouraged forbearance toward the one who angers Him by ingratitude for the favour, or by bad speech at refusal, by responding with what is good, so He said: ﴿Forbearing﴾, that is, He does not hasten to punish the one who disobeys Him, but provides for him and supports him while he disobeys and disbelieves in Him.

[p-79] When He had stipulated a condition for its acceptance and had weakened what lacks it, He followed this with an explicit prohibition against neglecting it and an express statement that it nullifies and annuls charity. For this He set forth an example, and He set forth an example for that example as an intensification in warning against it. He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., who have professed this, make true your profession, [by] ﴿not invalidating your charities with reminders and injury﴾. Al-Harrali (the commentator) said: "He made clear that what He had stipulated for the unconditional reward invalidates the spending." [End of quotation.]

﴿with reminders and injury﴾. Perhaps their punishment equals or exceeds the reward of the charity, so it becomes like an annulment of its beginning, leaving no reward at all. Al-Harrali said: "He thus joined the work of sincerity with the affliction of what follows it, [joining it] to what is built on the root of showing off." [End of quotation.] Then He said: ﴿like one who spends his wealth﴾ for other than Allah, spending it only ﴿to be seen by people﴾, i.e., with the aim that they see it. Al-Harrali said: "It is the act intended to be seen by creation, out of heedlessness of seeing the Truth and blindness to it."

When He likened the one who reminds and injures to the one who shows off, because the show-off is the lowest of people, the most meager in aspiration, the worst in judgment, and the most blind in heart, people of lofty aspirations, especially the Arabs, are the most repelled by him and the farthest from him. Such a person has two states, and He attached him to the worse of the two. So He said: ﴿and does not believe in Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses the attribute of perfection, ﴿nor the Last Day﴾, on which the recompense occurs after the examination of deeds, the good from the bad. Al-Harrali said: "When He set forth an example for the growth of expenditure by means of tillage, He set forth an example for its annulment through the error of the farmer in tilling. So He said: ﴿Then his example﴾ in his spending, accompanied by what corrupts it, and the example of his expenditure ﴿is like the example of a smooth rock﴾ and what is sown on it. It is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālaghah) from ṣafā, meaning hard, smooth stones that do not admit the splitting of plants." [End of quotation.]

﴿upon which is dust﴾. Some ignorant people were deceived by it and sowed upon it.

Since removing the dust from what has settled on it, right after it settles, is most fitting while it is still whole, especially if it is a smooth stone, He said, for emphasis in the nullification of showing off in works: ﴿then a heavy rain struck it﴾, i.e., right after the dust settled on it without any delay. This differs from what comes later about the elevated ground (rabwah), for that is a lasting quality; if rain followed it, it would last with its lastingness and corrupt it. ﴿A heavy rain﴾, i.e., abundant rain, ﴿removed the dust from it﴾, ﴿and left it bare﴾, i.e., a rock that accepts no plant in any way, rather whoever hopes in it is disappointed, as one says "the tinder became bare" (aṣlada al-zand) when it does not produce a spark. He made the heart of the one who injures and reminds like the smooth rock that was struck by heavy rain, which removes the remnant of its expenditure, just as the heavy rain, whose nature is to improve seed, removed the farmer's seed from the rock. Al-Harrali said this, and there is some free adaptation in it.

When the invalidity of the action became clear through the example and what it illustrates, He concluded with: ﴿they have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾, i.e., those represented by the example and those for whom it is set forth. The verse is of the type called ihtibāk (a device of mutual omission, where each part of a pair is implied by the other). Since the one who sows on such ground is astonishingly misguided and foolish, and the intended meaning is: "Indeed Allah does not accept the work of those who injure, just as He does not accept the work of those who show off," He added a clause informing that He blinds the perceptive about the clearest matters whenever He wills, and does whatever He wishes, saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide﴾, i.e., to the path of any benefit, He who possesses all wisdom. Since each of the one who injures and the one who shows off has covered the goodness of his deed with the evil it has drawn to him, He said: ﴿the disbelieving people﴾. Mentioning this phrase alone, in this way, is a most intense warning to the giver who gives in this manner.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 265:

When he finished with the parable of the one who gives without condition (ʿārī ʿan al-sharṭ), he set forth a parable for the one who pairs giving with the condition, alerting thereby to the fact that others' giving is not sought for the sake of God's Face. So He said: ﴿And the likeness﴾. Al-Harrali said: it is conjoined (ʿaṭfan) to ﴿like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264] and ﴿does not believe in God and the Last Day﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264] as a conjunction of opposition (ʿaṭf muqābalah), and to ﴿the likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261] as a conjunction of correspondence (ʿaṭf munāsabah). End.
