And by what they are of the first remembrance, and what lies between them of apparent difference between scriptural comprehension and divine comprehension, therefore Surah al-Baqarah was its hump (sanam), and the hump is the highest part of the kneeling animal and its most beautiful as a whole, which is the camel; and Surah Al 'Imran was the crown of the Qur'an, and the crown is the highest of (p. 192) created beings, the standing creature established on earth as vicegerent, whose outward form and whose whole existence is comprehended. So the joining of these two surahs fell in a manner similar to the joining of verses, where the explicitness of a verse connects with the hint of the preceding one, as was pointed out in several places. End. The secret of arranging the surah of the hump in this order is that when God, glorified and exalted is He, opened it by classifying the people who are for religion like the legs bearing the one with the hump, so that it stood upright, the beginning of the intended matter began by mentioning the nearest of the hump to the understanding of those who stand, so He said, addressing all the categories He had mentioned earlier: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21], and it continued until the matter became clear to the utmost clarity. Then He began to mention His blessings, glorified is He, upon the people commanded to worship, by what He bestowed upon them of creating all that exists for them, with what He honored their father Adam with, peace be upon him. Then He singled out the Arabs and those who followed them with the statement of the favor upon them in the argument with the Children of Israel and their rebuke. He, glorified and exalted is He, affirms every little thing of the matter of Lordship and monotheism through worship, without mentioning any of the rulings except what the Children of Israel had departed from; so He mentioned it as a favor to the Arabs and a rebuke to the Children of Israel for abandoning it, not as (p. 193) a matter intended in itself. So when they purified themselves and ascended and became fit for the kinds of knowledge, He said, elevating them from the ascents of Lordship to the ladders of Divinity:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 2, verse 286 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Your God is one God; there is no god but Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163]. When they had ascended this height of nobility, He taught them the acts of worship that purify, and cleansed their pure spirits for them. He mentioned the mother-acts (ummahat al-a'mal), both roots and branches: the five pillars (al-da'a'im al-khams) and the enclosure (al-hazira), and what follows from these limits concerning food, drink, marriage, and other matters of welfare. So they prepared themselves with these, and [knew] that they are the bright sources from the Lord of Majesty. Then He said, raising them toward the unseen presence of His lofty court, [mentioning] the name that encompasses all names: ﴿God—there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

Since one who reaches the highest station of freedom must, in the view of the people (al-qawm), return to the bond of servitude, He mentioned to them some of the acts fitting for them. He urged them to things most of which belong to the valley of excellence (al-ihsan), which is the station of the people of gnosis (al-'irfan). He mentioned the example of spending (al-nafaqah), which is one of the foundations of the surah, right after mentioning the station of tranquility (al-tuma'nina) (p. 194), signaling that this is the trait of one who is at rest. He encouraged it, indicating that there is no hope of arrival except by stripping oneself of the whole world. He stressed much the seeking of wholesome food, without which no state can endure. He forbade usury (riba) most strongly, indicating contentment with the least sufficiency, and forbade excess in general for the elite and every prohibited thing for the common people. He guided them to the etiquette of the religion, which requires trust in what is with God, which in turn demands true reliance (tawakkul), which yields help from God, glory be to Him and exalted, and guidance to that.

The Prophet (ﷺ) died while still engaged in this. God, glory be to Him and exalted, built each third of these thirds upon an introduction affirming His command, and directed each toward a conclusion warning against neglect of it. He added to the third part, because it is the conclusion and blessing of completion, that after His conclusion He stressed to them belief in everything contained in the surah. He ended with an indication that the mainstay of all this is jihad, which is for those of error and obstinacy, and that reliance in it is upon the Owner of dominion and the King of the servants. That is the path of the people of right guidance, of direction and rectitude. And God, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One who grants success to what is correct.
